verses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
verses.transliterated: bis'mi l-lahi l-raḥmāni l-raḥīm
verses.english: In the name of GOD, Most Gracious, Most Merciful.
verses.footnote: The first verse in the Quran represents the foundation upon which a superhuman 19-based mathematical miracle is built. This important statement consists of 19 Arabic letters, and every word in it occurs in the whole Quran in multiples of 19 (see Appendices 1 & 29 for the details).

1981.english: In the name of God, most gracious, most merciful.
1981.footnote:
This opening statement of Quran is the foundation upon which a miraculous numerical code is built. This code, which remained a divinely guarded secret for 1400 years, presents to the world the first physical, touchable, and utterly indisputable proof that this Quran is a divine scripture. The Quran’s miraculous numerical code is so intricate that it leaves no doubt that the Quran is the word of God, and that it has been perfectly protected from the slightest distortion, addition, or loss. Yet it is so simple that any person can fully appreciate its significance. There is no greater acknowledgement than God’s own description of this Quranic code as “one of the greatest miracles” (74:35). It was the will of the Almighty to bless this very translation with the exclusive discovery of this profound miracle, as a clear sign of divine approval and authorization.

The opening statement (verse 1 of sura 1) consists of 19 Arabic letters, and this is the number upon which the Quran’s numerical code is based (see Appendix 1 for details). Every word in the opening statement is mentioned throughout the Quran a number of times which is consistently a multiple of 19. Thus, the first word (Ism=name) is found in the Quran exactly 19 times; the second word (Allah=God) is mentioned 2,698 times (19x142); the third word (Al-Rahman=most gracious) is mentioned 57 times (19x3); and the last word (Al-Raheem=most merciful) is mentioned 114 times (19x6). The reader, therefore, is handed at the outset physical proof that Quran is God’s message to humanity. Of the millions of books in existence, how many will exhibit this elaborate phenomenon; that the opening statement consists of an “X” number of letters, and every word in the statement is mentioned throughout the book a multiple of “X”? Although this unique phenomenon is a minute portion of the Quran’s numerical miracle, the renowned journal “SCIENTIFIC AMERICAN” described it as “an ingenious study of Quran.” (September 1980, pp 22-24).

1989.english: Most Gracious, Most Merciful.*
1989.footnote: This verse, known as the “Basmalah,” occupies a special position in the Quran. It is the opening statement of every sura, ex cept Sura 9, and it constitutes the foundation upon which the Quran’s 19-based mathematical miracle is built (App. 1). The Basmalah consists of 19 Arabic letters, and its constituent words [Bism Allah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem] occur in the Quran in multiples of 19: 19, 2698, 57, and 114 times, respectively. Thus, the reader is handed at the outset tangible proof that this is not a human-made book. Numerous mathematical phenomena are connected with this verse. For example, the absence of Basmalah from Sura 9 is com pensated for 19 suras later; Sura 27 contains two Basmalahs (see Appendix 29 and Footnote 27:30). Thus, the count of all Basmalahs is restored to 114, 19x6. Additionally, when we add the sura numbers from the missing Basmalah (Sura 9) to the extra Bas malah (Sura 27) [9+10+11+.... +27], the total comes to 342, 19x18. This total, remarkably, is also the number of words between the two Basmalahs of Sura 27. As detailed in Appendix 1, the Quran’s mathematical code is so vast, and so intricate that no force on earth could possibly imitate it, let alone manufacture it (17:88).

verses.arabic: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
verses.arabicClean: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين
verses.transliterated: ṣirāṭa alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim ghayri l-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim walā l-ḍālīn
verses.english: the path of those whom You blessed; not of those who have deserved wrath, nor of the strayers.
verses.footnote:
Sura 1 is God's gift to us to establish contact with Him through the daily Contact Prayers. This fact is supported by an earth-shattering, simple-to-understand-but-impossible-to-imitate mathematical composition that challenges the greatest mathematicians on earth, and stumps them; it is far beyond human capabilities:

(1) The sura number, followed by the numbers of verses, next to each other, give 1 1 2 3 4 5 6 7. This number is a multiple of 19.

(2) If we substitute the number of letters per verse in place of verse numbers, we get 1 19 17 12 11 19 18 43. This number is also a multiple of 19.

(3) If we insert the total gematrical value of every verse, we get 1 19 786 17 581 12 618 11 241 19 836 18 1072 43 6009. This number is a multiple of 19.

(4) The number shown above includes all parameters of Sura 1, and consists of 38 digits (19x2).

(5) It is noteworthy that this 38-digit number is still divisible by 19 when we write its components backwards, from right to left as practiced by the Arabs. Thus, 6009 43 1072 18 836 19 241 11 618 12 581 17 786 19 1 is also a multiple of 19.

(6) The mathematical representations mentioned above participate in numerous extraordinary mathematical phenomena to confirm all details of the five daily Contact Prayers (Appendix 15).

(7) Many more astounding phenomena are given in Appendix One. Thus, the reader is handed at the outset tangible proof that this is God's message to the world.

1981.english: the path of those whom You blessed; not of those who deserve wrath, nor the strayers.

1989.english: the path of those whom You blessed; not of those who have deserved wrath, nor the strayers.

verses.arabic: الٓمٓ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الم
verses.transliterated: alif-lam-meem
verses.english: A. L. M.
verses.footnote: These initials remained a divinely guarded secret for 1400 years. Now we recognize them as a major component of the Quran's mathematical miracle (see Appendices 1, 2, 24, and 26). The meaning of A.L.M. is pointed out in Verse 2: "This scripture is infallible." This is incontrovertibly proven by the fact that the frequencies of occurrence of these three initials in this sura are 4502, 3202, and 2195, respectively. The sum of these numbers is 9899, or 19x521. Thus, these most frequent letters of the Arabic language are mathematically placed according to a super-human pattern. These same initials also prefix Suras 3, 29, 30, 31, and 32, and their frequencies of occurrence add up to multiples of 19 in each one of these suras.

1981.english: A.L.M.
1981.footnote: The meaning or significance of these Quranic initials remained unknown for 1400 years, since the revelation of Quran. Now we recognize them as a part of the Quran’s numerical miracle. These letters, as it turned out, provide the proof that this scripture is the infallible word of God (see Appendix 1).

1989.english: A.L.M.*
1989.footnote: These initials remained a divinely guarded secret for 1400 years. Hundreds of Muslim and Orientalist scholars tried in vain to decipher their significance. Ob viously, the Almighty author of the Quran has willed that the decoding of these initials shall be reserved for a specific per son, in a specific place, at a specific time (see Appendicies 1, 2, and 26). Now we recognize these initials as a major component of the Quran’s extraordinary mathematical code. The meaning of A.L.M. is pointed out in Verse 2: “This scripture is infallible.” This is incontrovertibly proven by the fact that the frequencies of occurrence of these three initials in this sura are 4502, 3202, and 2195, respectively. The sum of these numbers is 9899, or 19x521. Thus, these most frequent letters of the Arabic language did not suffer any distortion, addition, or loss. These same initials also prefix Suras 3, 29, 30, 31, and 32. Their frequencies of occurrence add up to multiples of 19 in each one of these suras.

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ

1989.english: This scripture is infallible; a beacon for the righteous; (1) The Righteous.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين يؤمنون بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون
verses.transliterated: alladhīna yu'minūna bil-ghaybi wayuqīmūna l-ṣalata wamimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūn
verses.english: who believe in the unseen, observe the Contact Prayers (Salat), and from our provisions to them, they give to charity.
verses.subtitle: Three Categories of People (1) The Righteous
verses.footnote:
Since the Contact Prayers are decreed five times a day, they constitute the prime source of nourishment for our souls. Along with all other practices in Submission, the Contact Prayers were originally revealed through Abraham (21:73, 22:78). Although these five daily prayers were practiced before the revelation of the Quran, each Contact Prayer is specifically mentioned in the Quran (24:58, 11:114, 17:78, & 2:238). Appendices 1 & 15 provide physical evidence supporting all the details of the Contact Prayers, including the number of units (Rak'aas) and the numbers of bowings, prostrations, and Tashahhuds in each prayer.

±±2:3 When God uses the plural tense, this indicates that other entities, usually the angels, are involved. When God spoke to Moses, the singular form was used (20:12- 14). See Appendix 10.

1981.english: who believe in the unseen,* observe the **salat** prayers,* and from our provisions to them, they give;
1981.footnote: The word “**salat**” designates a specific set of actions, including bowing, prostrating, and reciting specific words. The **salat** prayers must be observed at five specific times each day. The word “prayer” alone is not sufficient to describe this important religious duty.

1989.english: who believe in the unseen, even when alone in their privacy, observe the contact prayers (Salat),* and from our** provisions to them, they give to charity.
1989.subtitle: Three Categories of People
1989.footnote: See Appendix 10.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ وَبِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك وبالآخرة هم يوقنون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna yu'minūna bimā unzila ilayka wamā unzila min qablika wabil-ākhirati hum yūqinūn
verses.english: And they believe in what was revealed to you, and in what was revealed before you, and with regard to the Hereafter, they are absolutely certain.
verses.footnote: Despite severe distortions that afflicted the previous scriptures, God's truth can still be found in them. Both the Old Testament and the New Testament still advocate absolute devotion to God ALONE (Deuteronomy 6:4-5, Mark 12:29-30). All distortions are easily detectable.

1981.english: and they believe in what was revealed to you, and in what was revealed before you; and they are positively certain about the hereafter.

1989.english: And they believe in what was revealed to you, and in what was revealed before you. With regard to the Hereafter, they are certain.

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ

verses.transliterated: ulāika ʿalā hudan min rabbihim wa-ulāika humu l-muf'liḥūn
verses.english: These are guided by their Lord; these are the winners.

1981.english: They have followed the guidance from their Lord; they are the winners.

1989.english: These are guided by their Lord; these are the winners.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن الذين كفروا سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: inna alladhīna kafarū sawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūn
verses.english: As for those who disbelieve, it is the same for them; whether you warn them, or not warn them, they cannot believe.
verses.subtitle: (2) The Disbelievers
verses.footnote: Those who make a decision to reject God are helped in that direction; they are prevented by God from seeing any proof or guidance for as long as they maintain such a decision. The consequences of such a disastrous decision are spelled out in Verse 7.

1981.english: As for those who disbelieve, it will be the same for them; whether you warn them or not, they can not believe.
1981.subtitle: (2) The Disbelievers

1989.english: As for those who disbelieved, it is the same for them; whether you warn them, or not warn them, they cannot believe.
1989.subtitle: (2) The Disbelievers.

verses.arabic: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ غِشَٰوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم ۖ وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة ۖ ولهم عذاب عظيم
verses.transliterated: khatama l-lahu ʿalā qulūbihim waʿalā samʿihim waʿalā abṣārihim ghishāwatun walahum ʿadhābun ʿaẓīmu
verses.english: GOD seals their minds and their hearing, and their eyes are veiled. They have incurred severe retribution.

1981.english: (That is because) God seals their hearts, and their hearing, and places veils upon their eyes. They have deserved terrible retribution.

1989.english: GOD has sealed their hearts, and their hearing, and their eyes are veiled. They have incurred severe retribution.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤْمِنِينَ

verses.transliterated: wamina l-nāsi man yaqūlu āmannā bil-lahi wabil-yawmi l-ākhiri wamā hum bimu'minīn
verses.english: Then there are those who say, "We believe in GOD and the Last Day," while they are not believers.
verses.subtitle: (3) The Hypocrites

1981.english: Then there are those who say, “We believe in God and the last day,” while they are not believers.
1981.subtitle: (3) The Hypocrites

1989.english: Then there are those who say, “We believe in GOD and the Last Day,” when in fact they are not believers.
1989.subtitle: (3) The Hypocrites.

verses.arabic: يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ

verses.transliterated: yukhādiʿūna l-laha wa-alladhīna āmanū wamā yakhdaʿūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūn

1981.english: In attempting to deceive God and the believers, they only deceive themselves without perceiving.

1989.english: In attempting to deceive GOD and those who believed, they only deceive themselves without perceiving.

verses.arabic: فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا ۖ ولهم عذاب أليم بما كانوا يكذبون
verses.transliterated: fī qulūbihim maraḍun fazādahumu l-lahu maraḍan walahum ʿadhābun alīmun bimā kānū yakdhibūn
verses.english: In their minds there is a disease. Consequently, GOD augments their disease. They have incurred a painful retribution for their lying.

1981.english: In their hearts is a disease, and consequently, God augments their disease. They have deserved painful retribution for their lying.

1989.english: In their hearts is a disease. Consequently, GOD augments their disease. They have incurred a painful retribution for their lying.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا قيل لهم لا تفسدوا في الأرض قالوا إنما نحن مصلحون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā qīla lahum lā tuf'sidū fī l-arḍi qālū innamā naḥnu muṣ'liḥūn

1981.english: When they are told, “Do not corrupt the earth,” they say, “But we are righteous.”

1989.english: When they are told, “Do not commit evil,” they say, “But we are working righteousness!”

verses.arabic: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ألا إنهم هم المفسدون ولكن لا يشعرون
verses.transliterated: alā innahum humu l-muf'sidūna walākin lā yashʿurūn

1981.english: In fact, they are corruptors, but they do not perceive.

1989.english: In fact, they are evildoers, but they do not perceive.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ ءَامِنُوا۟ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ

verses.transliterated: wa-idhā qīla lahum āminū kamā āmana l-nāsu qālū anu'minu kamā āmana l-sufahāu alā innahum humu l-sufahāu walākin lā yaʿlamūn

1981.english: When they are told, “Believe as the people have believed,” they say, “Shall we believe as the fools have believed?” In fact, it is they who are fools, but they do not know.

1989.english: When they are told, “Believe as the people have believed,” they say, “Shall we believe as the fools have believed?” In fact, it is they who are fools, but they do not know.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا لَقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا إنا معكم إنما نحن مستهزئون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā laqū alladhīna āmanū qālū āmannā wa-idhā khalaw ilā shayāṭīnihim qālū innā maʿakum innamā naḥnu mus'tahziūn
verses.english: When they meet the believers, they say, "We believe," but when alone with their devils, they say, "We are with you; we were only mocking."

1981.english: When they meet the believers, they say, “We believe,” but when alone with their devils, they say, “We are with you. We were only mocking.”

1989.english: When they meet the believers, they say, “We believe,” but when alone with their devils, they say, “We are still with you; we were only mocking.”

verses.arabic: ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِى طُغْيَٰنِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الله يستهزئ بهم ويمدهم في طغيانهم يعمهون
verses.transliterated: al-lahu yastahzi-u bihim wayamudduhum fī ṭugh'yānihim yaʿmahūn
verses.english: GOD mocks them, and leads them on in their transgressions, blundering.

1981.english: God mocks them, by allowing them to continue their transgressions, blundering.

1989.english: GOD mocks them, by leaving them in their transgressions, blundering.

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُهْتَدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين
verses.transliterated: ulāika alladhīna ish'tarawū l-ḍalālata bil-hudā famā rabiḥat tijāratuhum wamā kānū muh'tadīn
verses.english: It is they who bought the straying, at the expense of guidance. Such trade never prospers, nor do they receive any guidance.

1981.english: They have chosen the straying instead of guidance and thus, their trade never prospers, nor are they ever guided.

1989.english: It is they who bought the straying, at the expense of guidance. Such trade never prospers, nor do they receive any guidance.

verses.arabic: مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِى ظُلُمَٰتٍ لَّا يُبْصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات لا يبصرون
verses.transliterated: mathaluhum kamathali alladhī is'tawqada nāran falammā aḍāat mā ḥawlahu dhahaba l-lahu binūrihim watarakahum fī ẓulumātin lā yub'ṣirūn
verses.english: Their example is like those who start a fire, then, as it begins to shed light around them, GOD takes away their light, leaving them in darkness, unable to see.

1981.english: Their allegory is that of one who starts a fire, then, as it begins to shed light around him, God takes away their light, leaving them in total darkness, unable to see.

1989.english: Their example is like those who start a fire, then, as it begins to shed light for them, GOD takes away their light, leaving them in darkness, unable to see.

verses.arabic: صُمٌّۢ بُكْمٌ عُمْىٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون
verses.transliterated: ṣummun buk'mun ʿum'yun fahum lā yarjiʿūn
verses.english: Deaf, dumb, and blind; they fail to return.

1981.english: Deaf, dumb, and blind; they can never return.

1989.english: Deaf, dumb, and blind; they fail to return.

verses.arabic: أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: أو كصيب من السماء فيه ظلمات ورعد وبرق يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم من الصواعق حذر الموت ۚ والله محيط بالكافرين
verses.transliterated: aw kaṣayyibin mina l-samāi fīhi ẓulumātun waraʿdun wabarqun yajʿalūna aṣābiʿahum fī ādhānihim mina l-ṣawāʿiqi ḥadhara l-mawti wal-lahu muḥīṭun bil-kāfirīn
verses.english: Another example: a rainstorm from the sky in which there is darkness, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears, to evade death. GOD is fully aware of the disbelievers.

1981.english: Or like a storm from the sky, with darkness, thunder, and lightning. They place their fingers in their ears as if to evade death by lightning. God thus encompasses the disbelievers.

1989.english: Or, like a storm from the sky, with darkness, thunder, and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears, to evade the lightning bolts, and death. GOD thus surrounds the disbelievers.

verses.arabic: يَكَادُ ٱلْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَٰرَهُمْ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوْا۟ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا۟ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: يكاد البرق يخطف أبصارهم ۖ كلما أضاء لهم مشوا فيه وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا ۚ ولو شاء الله لذهب بسمعهم وأبصارهم ۚ إن الله على كل شيء قدير
verses.transliterated: yakādu l-barqu yakhṭafu abṣārahum kullamā aḍāa lahum mashaw fīhi wa-idhā aẓlama ʿalayhim qāmū walaw shāa l-lahu ladhahaba bisamʿihim wa-abṣārihim inna l-laha ʿalā kulli shayin qadīru
verses.english: The lightning almost snatches away their eyesight. When it lights for them, they move forward, and when it turns dark, they stand still. If GOD wills, He can take away their hearing and their eyesight. GOD is Omnipotent.
verses.subtitle: The Light of Faith
verses.footnote: "He" and "she" do not necessarily imply natural gender in Arabic (Appendix 4).

1981.english: The lightning is so bright, it almost blinds them. Whenever it lights for them, they move forward. And when it turns dark, they stand still. Had God willed, He* could have taken away their hearing and their eyesight. God is omnipotent.
1981.subtitle: The Light of Faith
1981.footnote: “He” does not imply gender in the Arabic language. God Almighty is neither male nor female. Is this why Arabic was chosen for the final scripture? See Appendix 3.

1989.english: The lightning almost snatches away their eyesight; whenever it lights for them, they move forward, and when it turns dark, they stand still. If GOD willed, He* could have taken away their hearing and their eyesight. GOD is Omnipotent.
1989.subtitle: The Light of Faith
1989.footnote: “He” and “she” do not necessarily imply natural gender in Arabic (Appendix 4).

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون
verses.transliterated: yāayyuhā l-nāsu uʿ'budū rabbakumu alladhī khalaqakum wa-alladhīna min qablikum laʿallakum tattaqūn
verses.english: O people, worship only your Lord—the One who created you and those before you—that you may be saved.

1981.english: O people, you shall worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may attain salvation.

1989.english: O people, worship your Lord—the One who created you and those before you—that you may be saved.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ فِرَٰشًا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءً وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزْقًا لَّكُمْ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًا وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم ۖ فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون
verses.transliterated: alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa firāshan wal-samāa bināan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhraja bihi mina l-thamarāti riz'qan lakum falā tajʿalū lillahi andādan wa-antum taʿlamūn
verses.english: The One who made the earth habitable for you, and the sky a structure. He sends down from the sky water, to produce all kinds of fruits for your sustenance. You shall not set up idols to rival GOD, now that you know.

1981.english: He is the one who made the earth habitable for you; He is the one who constructed the sky. He sends down water from the sky to produce fruits for your sustenance. Therefore, you shall not set up idols besides God, despite this knowledge.

1989.english: He is the One who made the earth habitable for you, and the sky a structure. He sends down water from the sky to produce all kinds of fruits for your sustenance. You shall not set up idols to rival GOD, now that you know.

verses.arabic: وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين
verses.transliterated: wa-in kuntum fī raybin mimmā nazzalnā ʿalā ʿabdinā fatū bisūratin min mith'lihi wa-id'ʿū shuhadāakum min dūni l-lahi in kuntum ṣādiqīn
verses.english: If you have any doubt regarding what we revealed to our servant, then produce one sura like these, and call upon your own witnesses against GOD, if you are truthful.
verses.subtitle: Mathematical Challenge
verses.footnote: The Quran's miraculous mathematical code provides numerous proofs as it spells out the name "Rashad Khalifa" as God's servant mentioned here. Some literary giants, including Al-Mutanabby and Taha Hussein, have answered the literary challenge, but they had no awareness of the Quran's mathematical composition. It is the Quran's mathematical code, revealed through God's Messenger of the Covenant, Rashad Khalifa, that is the real challenge—for it can never be imitated. See Appendices 1, 2, 24, & 26 for the detailed proofs.

1981.english: If you have any doubts concerning this revelation to our servant, then produce one sura like these, and ask your idols, whom you set up besides God, to do the same, if you are truthful.

1989.english: If you have any doubt regarding what we revealed to our servant,* then produce one sura like these, and ask the idols you had set up besides GOD (to do the same), if you are truthful.
1989.subtitle: Mathematical Challenge
1989.footnote: The Quran’s inimitable mathematical code points to Rashad Khalifa as God’s servant mentioned here. Many literary giants, including Al-Mutanabby and Taha Hussein, have answered the literary challenge. Therefore, it is the Quran’s mathematical code revealed through Rashad Khalifa that is the real challenge; it can never be imitated. See Appendices 1, 2, 24, and 26 for the proof.

verses.arabic: فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُوا۟ وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلْحِجَارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة ۖ أعدت للكافرين
verses.transliterated: fa-in lam tafʿalū walan tafʿalū fa-ittaqū l-nāra allatī waqūduhā l-nāsu wal-ḥijāratu uʿiddat lil'kāfirīn
verses.english: If you cannot do this—and you can never do this—then beware of the Hellfire, whose fuel is people and rocks; it awaits the disbelievers.
verses.subtitle: Allegorical Description of Hell

1981.english: If you fail to do this, and most certainly you will fail, then beware of the hellfire whose fuel is people and rocks; it awaits the disbelievers.
1981.subtitle: Heaven and Hell Allegorically Described

1989.english: If you cannot do this—and you can never do this—then beware of the Hellfire, whose fuel is people and rocks; it awaits the disbelievers.
1989.footnote: See Appendix 5.

verses.arabic: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا۟ مِنْهَا مِن ثَمَرَةٍ رِّزْقًا قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ وَأُتُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُتَشَٰبِهًا وَلَهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَٰجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أن لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ۖ كلما رزقوا منها من ثمرة رزقا ۙ قالوا هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل ۖ وأتوا به متشابها ۖ ولهم فيها أزواج مطهرة ۖ وهم فيها خالدون
verses.transliterated: wabashiri alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru kullamā ruziqū min'hā min thamaratin riz'qan qālū hādhā alladhī ruziq'nā min qablu wa-utū bihi mutashābihan walahum fīhā azwājun muṭahharatun wahum fīhā khālidūn
verses.english: Give good news to those who believe and lead a righteous life that they will have gardens with flowing streams. When provided with a provision of fruits therein, they will say, "This is what was provided for us previously." Thus, they are given allegorical descriptions. They will have pure spouses therein, and they abide therein forever.
verses.subtitle: Allegorical Description of Paradise

1981.english: And give good news to those who believe and work righteousness that they have deserved gardens with flowing streams. When given a fruit therein, they would say, “This is what was given to us before.” They will be given the same kind. They will have pure spouses therein, and abide therein forever.

1989.english: And give good news to those who believe and lead a righteous life that they have deserved gardens with flowing streams. When provided with a provision of fruits therein, they say, “This is what was provided for us previously.” Thus, they are given allegorical descriptions. They will have pure spouses therein, and they abide therein forever.
1989.footnote: See Appendix 5.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦٓ أَن يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَّا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِى بِهِۦ كَثِيرًا وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة فما فوقها ۚ فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم ۖ وأما الذين كفروا فيقولون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا ۘ يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا ۚ وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين
verses.transliterated: inna l-laha lā yastaḥyī an yaḍriba mathalan mā baʿūḍatan famā fawqahā fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū fayaʿlamūna annahu l-ḥaqu min rabbihim wa-ammā alladhīna kafarū fayaqūlūna mādhā arāda l-lahu bihādhā mathalan yuḍillu bihi kathīran wayahdī bihi kathīran wamā yuḍillu bihi illā l-fāsiqīn
verses.english: GOD does not shy away from citing any kind of allegory, from the tiny mosquito and greater. As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did GOD mean by such an allegory?" He misleads many thereby, and guides many thereby. But He never misleads thereby except the wicked,
verses.footnote: See Appendix 5 for further discussion of Heaven and Hell.

1981.english: Thus, God does not shy away from any kind of allegory, from down to a mosquito and higher. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord, while the disbelievers would say, “What did God mean by such an allegory?” He misleads many thereby, and guides many thereby; but He never misleads except the wicked;

1989.english: GOD does not shy away from citing any kind of allegory,* from the tiny mosquito and higher. Those who believed know that this is the truth from their Lord, while those who disbelieved say, “What did GOD mean by such an allegory?” He guides many thereby, and misleads many thereby; but He never misleads thereby except the wicked
1989.footnote: See Appendix 5.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض ۚ أولئك هم الخاسرون
verses.transliterated: alladhīna yanquḍūna ʿahda l-lahi min baʿdi mīthāqihi wayaqṭaʿūna mā amara l-lahu bihi an yūṣala wayuf'sidūna fī l-arḍi ulāika humu l-khāsirūn
verses.english: who violate GOD's covenant after pledging to uphold it, sever what GOD has commanded to be joined, and commit evil. These are the losers.

1981.english: who violate God’s covenant after pledging to keep it, disregard what God has ordered upheld, and corrupt the earth. These are the losers.

1989.english: who violate GOD covenant after pledging to uphold it, sever what GOD commanded to be joined, and commit evil. These are the losers. Two Deaths and Two Lives*

verses.arabic: كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ۖ ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم إليه ترجعون
verses.transliterated: kayfa takfurūna bil-lahi wakuntum amwātan fa-aḥyākum thumma yumītukum thumma yuḥ'yīkum thumma ilayhi tur'jaʿūn
verses.english: How can you disbelieve in GOD when you were dead and He gave you life, then He puts you to death, then He brings you back to life, then to Him you ultimately return?
verses.subtitle: Two Deaths and Two Lives for the Disbelievers
verses.footnote: The righteous do not really die; they go straight to Heaven. When their interim on this earth comes to an end, the angels of death simply invite them to go to the same Paradise where Adam and Eve once lived (2:154, 3:169, 8:24, 22:58, 16:32, 36:20-27, 44:56, 89:27-30). Thus, while the righteous experience only the first death following our original sin, the unrighteous go through two deaths (40:11). At the time of death, the disbelievers know their miserable fate (8:50, 47:27), then they suffer a continuous nightmare that lasts until Hell is created (40:46, 89:23, Appendix 17).

1981.english: How could you disbelieve in God, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will put you to death, then bring you back to life? To Him is your ultimate return.
1981.subtitle: Two Deaths and Two Lives

1989.english: How can you disbelieve in GOD when you were dead and He gave you life, then He puts you to death, then He is the One who brings you back to life, then to Him you ultimately return?
1989.footnote: Consistently throughout the Quran, our Creator informs us that we go through two deaths and two lives (see 40:11).

verses.arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات ۚ وهو بكل شيء عليم
verses.transliterated: huwa alladhī khalaqa lakum mā fī l-arḍi jamīʿan thumma is'tawā ilā l-samāi fasawwāhunna sabʿa samāwātin wahuwa bikulli shayin ʿalīmu
verses.english: He is the One who created for you everything on earth, then turned to the sky and perfected seven universes therein, and He is fully aware of all things.
verses.footnote: Our universe with its billion galaxies, spanning distances of billions of light years, is the smallest and innermost of seven universes (Appendix 6). Please look up 41:10-11.

1981.english: He is the one who created for you everything on earth, then turned to the sky and designed seven heavens therein.* He is fully aware of all things.
1981.subtitle: Creation of the Heavens and the Earth
1981.footnote: Our immediate universe includes 100 billion galaxies and a billion trillion stars, at distances of millions of light years. All this incredible vastness is only part of the lowest and smallest “heaven.” Six more larger heavens surround our innermost, small heaven, and all seven heavens are within God’s “right hand.” (see Appendix 5, and 39:67). Yet some people are ignorant enough to idolize such minute and powerless mortals as Jesus, Muhammad, and various saints.

1989.english: He is the One who created for you everything on earth, then turned to the sky and created seven universes therein,* and He is fully aware of all things.
1989.footnote: Our universe with its billion galaxies, spanning distances of billions of light years, is the smallest and innermost of the seven universes (Appendix 6).

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة ۖ قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك ۖ قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qāla rabbuka lil'malāikati innī jāʿilun fī l-arḍi khalīfatan qālū atajʿalu fīhā man yuf'sidu fīhā wayasfiku l-dimāa wanaḥnu nusabbiḥu biḥamdika wanuqaddisu laka qāla innī aʿlamu mā lā taʿlamūn
verses.english: Recall that your Lord said to the angels, "I am placing a representative (a temporary god) on Earth." They said, "Will You place therein one who will spread evil therein and shed blood, while we sing Your praises, glorify You, and uphold Your absolute authority?" He said, "I know what you do not know."
verses.subtitle: Satan: A Temporary "god"
verses.footnote: These verses answer such crucial questions as: "Why are we here?" (See Appendix 7).

1981.english: Then your Lord said to the angels, “I am placing a representative on earth.” They said, “Shall you place therein one who would corrupt therein, and shed blood, while we praise Your glory and hold You sacred?” He said, “I know what you do not know.”
1981.subtitle: Creation of Man
1981.footnote: What is the purpose behind our creation? Why are we here? See Appendix 6.

1989.english: Your Lord said to the angels, “I am placing a representative (a temporary god) on Earth.” They said, “Will You place therein one who will commit evil therein and shed blood, while we praise You, glorify You, and uphold Your absolute authority?” He said, “I know what you do not know.”
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين
verses.transliterated: waʿallama ādama l-asmāa kullahā thumma ʿaraḍahum ʿalā l-malāikati faqāla anbiūnī bi-asmāi hāulāi in kuntum ṣādiqīn
verses.english: He taught Adam all the names then presented them to the angels, saying, "Give Me the names of these, if you are right."
verses.subtitle: The Test Begins
verses.footnote: These are the names of the animals, the automobile, the submarine, the space satellite, the VCR, and all other objects to be encountered by the human beings on Earth.

1981.english: And He taught Adam all the names, then presented them to the angels, saying, “Tell Me the names of these, if you are right.”

1989.english: He taught Adam all the names, then presented them to the angels, saying, “Give me the names of these, if you are truthful.”
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا ۖ إنك أنت العليم الحكيم
verses.transliterated: qālū sub'ḥānaka lā ʿil'ma lanā illā mā ʿallamtanā innaka anta l-ʿalīmu l-ḥakīm
verses.english: They said, "Be You glorified, we have no knowledge, except that which You have taught us. You are the Omniscient, Most Wise."

1981.english: They said, “Glory be to You. We have no knowledge, except that which You taught us. You are the omniscient, the wise.”

1989.english: They said, “Be You glorified, we have no knowledge, except what You have taught us. You are the Omniscient, Most Wise.”
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال يا آدم أنبئهم بأسمائهم ۖ فلما أنبأهم بأسمائهم قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون
verses.transliterated: qāla yāādamu anbi'hum bi-asmāihim falammā anba-ahum bi-asmāihim qāla alam aqul lakum innī aʿlamu ghayba l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wa-aʿlamu mā tub'dūna wamā kuntum taktumūn
verses.english: He said, "O Adam, tell them their names." When he told them their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the secrets of the heavens and the earth? I know what you declare, and what you conceal."

1981.english: He said, “O Adam, tell them their names.” When he told them their names, He said, “Did I not tell you that I know the secrets of the heavens and the earth, and I know everything you declare and everything you conceal?”
1981.footnote: See Appendix 6 for the details of satan’s fall from angelhood.

1989.english: He said, “O Adam, give them their names.” When he told them their names, He said, “Did I not tell you that I know the secrets of the heavens and the earth? I know whatever you reveal, and whatever you conceal.”
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى واستكبر وكان من الكافرين
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qul'nā lil'malāikati us'judū liādama fasajadū illā ib'līsa abā wa-is'takbara wakāna mina l-kāfirīn
verses.english: When we said to the angels, "Fall prostrate before Adam," they fell prostrate, except Satan; he refused, was too arrogant, and a disbeliever.

1981.english: Then we said to the angels, “Fall prostrate before Adam.” They fell prostrate, except Iblis (satan); he refused, turned arrogant, and thus, he became a rebel.

1989.english: We said to the angels, “Fall prostrate before Adam.” They fell prostrate, except Satan; he refused, was too proud, and turned unappreciative.
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة وكلا منها رغدا حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين
verses.transliterated: waqul'nā yāādamu us'kun anta wazawjuka l-janata wakulā min'hā raghadan ḥaythu shi'tumā walā taqrabā hādhihi l-shajarata fatakūnā mina l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: We said, "O Adam, live with your wife in Paradise, and eat therefrom generously, as you please, but do not approach this tree, lest you sin."

1981.english: Then we said, “O Adam, live with your wife in paradise, and eat generously therefrom as you please. But do not approach this one tree, lest you become sinners.”

1989.english: We said, “O Adam, live with your wife in Paradise, and eat, generously, anything you like, but do not approach this one tree, lest you become transgressors.”
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: فأزلهما الشيطان عنها فأخرجهما مما كانا فيه ۖ وقلنا اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ۖ ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين
verses.transliterated: fa-azallahumā l-shayṭānu ʿanhā fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīhi waqul'nā ih'biṭū baʿḍukum libaʿḍin ʿaduwwun walakum fī l-arḍi mus'taqarrun wamatāʿun ilā ḥīni
verses.english: But the devil duped them, and caused their eviction therefrom. We said, "Go down as enemies of one another. On Earth shall be your habitation and provision for awhile."

1981.english: But the devil duped them out of it, causing their eviction therefrom. We said, “Go down as enemies to each other, and on earth will be your habitation and sustenance for awhile.”

1989.english: But the devil duped them, and caused their eviction therefrom. Consequently, we said, “Go down as enemies of one another. On Earth shall be your settlement and provisions for awhile.”
1989.footnote: These verses provide us with the answers to such crucial questions as: “Why are we here?” and “What is the purpose of our life?” See Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه ۚ إنه هو التواب الرحيم
verses.transliterated: fatalaqqā ādamu min rabbihi kalimātin fatāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa l-tawābu l-raḥīm
verses.english: Then, Adam received from his Lord words, whereby He redeemed him. He is the Redeemer, Most Merciful.
verses.subtitle: Specific Words
verses.footnote: Similarly, God has given us specific, mathematically coded words, the words of Sura 1, to establish contact with Him (see Footnote 1:1 and Appendix 15).

1981.english: Then Adam received from his Lord words, whereby He redeemed him. He is the redeemer, the merciful.

1989.english: Then, Adam received from his Lord words* whereby He redeemed him. He is the Redeemer, Most Merciful.
1989.footnote: Similarly, God gives us specific words, the words of Sura 1, in order to establish contact with Him during our contact prayers (Appendix 15).

verses.arabic: قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قلنا اهبطوا منها جميعا ۖ فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون
verses.transliterated: qul'nā ih'biṭū min'hā jamīʿan fa-immā yatiyannakum minnī hudan faman tabiʿa hudāya falā khawfun ʿalayhim walā hum yaḥzanūn
verses.english: We said, "Go down therefrom, all of you. When guidance comes to you from Me, those who follow My guidance will have no fear, nor will they grieve.

1981.english: We said, “Go down therefrom, all of you; and when guidance comes to you from Me, those who follow My guidance have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve.”

1989.english: We said, “Go down therefrom, all of you, and when guidance comes to you from Me, those who follow My guidance will have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار ۖ هم فيها خالدون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna kafarū wakadhabū biāyātinā ulāika aṣḥābu l-nāri hum fīhā khālidūn
verses.english: As for those who disbelieve and reject our revelations, they will be dwellers of Hell, wherein they abide forever.

1981.english: As for those who disbelieve and reject our* revelations, they have deserved hell; they abide therein forever.
1981.footnote: God speaks frequently in the plural. This invariably indicates participation of the angels, and God’s will to give them credit for their participation. For example, God’s revelations to us were brought down by the angel Gabriel, hence the statement “our revelations.” On the other hand, God speaks in the singular where the action is exclusively His, such as worship (see 20:14, 21:25, 21:92, 29:56, and 36:61). When God spoke to Moses (20:12-14) without the mediation of any angels, we find that God speaks in the singular.

1989.english: “As for those who disbelieve and reject our revelations, they will incur Hell, wherein they abide forever.” The Children of Israel

verses.arabic: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِعَهْدِىٓ أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱرْهَبُونِ
verses.arabicClean: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم وإياي فارهبون
verses.transliterated: yābanī is'rāīla udh'kurū niʿ'matiya allatī anʿamtu ʿalaykum wa-awfū biʿahdī ūfi biʿahdikum wa-iyyāya fa-ir'habūn
verses.english: O Children of Israel, remember My favor, which I bestowed upon you, and fulfill your part of the covenant, that I fulfill My part of the covenant, and reverence Me.
verses.subtitle: Divine Commandments to All Jews: "You Shall Believe in This Quran."

1981.english: O children of Israel, appreciate the blessings I have bestowed upon you, and uphold My covenant, that I uphold your covenant; and reverence Me.
1981.subtitle: The Children of Israel
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: O Children of Israel, remember the favors I bestowed upon you, and fulfill your part of My covenant, that I fulfill My part of the covenant, and reverence Me.

verses.arabic: وَءَامِنُوا۟ بِمَآ أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍۭ بِهِۦ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِى ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱتَّقُونِ
verses.arabicClean: وآمنوا بما أنزلت مصدقا لما معكم ولا تكونوا أول كافر به ۖ ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا وإياي فاتقون
verses.transliterated: waāminū bimā anzaltu muṣaddiqan limā maʿakum walā takūnū awwala kāfirin bihi walā tashtarū biāyātī thamanan qalīlan wa-iyyāya fa-ittaqūn
verses.english: You shall believe in what I have revealed herein, confirming what you have; do not be the first to reject it. Do not trade away My revelations for a cheap price, and observe Me.

1981.english: And believe in what is revealed herein confirming what you have, and do not be the first to reject it. Do not trade away My revelations for a cheap price; and observe Me.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Believe in what I have sent down herein, confirming what you have— do not be the first to reject it. Do not trade away My revelations for a cheap price, and observe Me.

verses.arabic: وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولا تلبسوا الحق بالباطل وتكتموا الحق وأنتم تعلمون
verses.transliterated: walā talbisū l-ḥaqa bil-bāṭili wataktumū l-ḥaqa wa-antum taʿlamūn
verses.english: Do not confound the truth with falsehood, nor shall you conceal the truth, knowingly.

1981.english: Do not confound the truth with falsehood, nor shall you conceal the truth knowingly.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Do not confound the truth with falsehood, nor shall you conceal the truth, knowingly.

verses.arabic: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرْكَعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واركعوا مع الراكعين
verses.transliterated: wa-aqīmū l-ṣalata waātū l-zakata wa-ir'kaʿū maʿa l-rākiʿīn
verses.english: You shall observe the Contact Prayers (Salat) and give the obligatory charity (Zakat), and bow down with those who bow down.

1981.english: You shall observe the **salat** prayers and **zakat** charity; you shall bow down with those who bow down.
1981.footnote: Just as the **salat** prayers are a specific set of practices, the **zakat** charity is a specific proportion of one’s properties to be given to the needy on regular basis. In Islam, **zakat**, is 2% of one’s capital possessions annually.

1989.english: You shall observe the contact prayers (Salat) and the obligatory charity (Zakat), and bow down with those who bow down.

verses.arabic: أَتَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب ۚ أفلا تعقلون
verses.transliterated: atamurūna l-nāsa bil-biri watansawna anfusakum wa-antum tatlūna l-kitāba afalā taʿqilūn
verses.english: Do you exhort the people to be righteous, while forgetting yourselves, though you read the scripture? Do you not understand?

1981.english: Would you enjoin righteousness upon the people, and forget yourselves, though you read the scripture? Do you not understand?
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people, and forget yourselves, though you read the scripture? Do you not understand?

verses.arabic: وَٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلْخَٰشِعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة ۚ وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين
verses.transliterated: wa-is'taʿīnū bil-ṣabri wal-ṣalati wa-innahā lakabīratun illā ʿalā l-khāshiʿīn
verses.english: You shall seek help through steadfastness and the Contact Prayers (Salat). This is difficult indeed, but not so for the reverent,

1981.english: Seek help through steadfastness and **salat**; this is difficult indeed, but not for the reverent;
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Seek help through steadfastness and the contact prayers (Salat). This is difficult indeed, but not so for the reverent

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُوا۟ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم وأنهم إليه راجعون
verses.transliterated: alladhīna yaẓunnūna annahum mulāqū rabbihim wa-annahum ilayhi rājiʿūn
verses.english: who believe that they will meet their Lord; that to Him they ultimately return.

1981.english: who realize that they will meet their Lord; that to Him they ultimately return.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: who believe that they will meet their Lord; that to Him they ultimately return.

verses.arabic: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين
verses.transliterated: yābanī is'rāīla udh'kurū niʿ'matiya allatī anʿamtu ʿalaykum wa-annī faḍḍaltukum ʿalā l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you, and that I blessed you more than any other people.

1981.english: O children of Israel, appreciate the blessings I have bestowed upon you, and that I set you apart from all the people.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: O Children of Israel, remember the favors I bestowed upon you, and that I blessed you more than any other people.

verses.arabic: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِى نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَٰعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها شفاعة ولا يؤخذ منها عدل ولا هم ينصرون
verses.transliterated: wa-ittaqū yawman lā tajzī nafsun ʿan nafsin shayan walā yuq'balu min'hā shafāʿatun walā yu'khadhu min'hā ʿadlun walā hum yunṣarūn
verses.english: Beware of the day when no soul can avail another soul, no intercession will be accepted, no ransom can be paid, nor can anyone be helped.

1981.english: Beware of the day when no one can avail another, no intercession will be accepted,* and no one can be helped.
1981.footnote: The myth of “intercession” is prevalent in both Christianity and Islam. The Christians claim that Jesus will intercede on their behalf, and the Muslims claim that Muhammad will intercede on their behalf. The divine truth, as shown throughout the Quran, is that neither Jesus nor Muhammad, nor anyone else, will possess the power of intercession. See Appendix 7 for details.

1989.english: Beware of the day when no soul can avail another, no intercession is accepted, no ransom can be paid, and no one can be helped.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ نجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم ۚ وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم
verses.transliterated: wa-idh najjaynākum min āli fir'ʿawna yasūmūnakum sūa l-ʿadhābi yudhabbiḥūna abnāakum wayastaḥyūna nisāakum wafī dhālikum balāon min rabbikum ʿaẓīmu
verses.english: Recall that we saved you from Pharaoh's people who inflicted upon you the worst persecution, slaying your sons and sparing your daughters. That was an exacting test from your Lord.

1981.english: Recall that we delivered you from Pharaoh's people who inflicted disastrous persecution upon you, slaughtering your sons and sparing your daughters. It was an exacting trial from your Lord.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that we saved you from Pharaoh’s people who inflicted the worst persecution upon you, slaying your sons, and sparing your daughters. That was an exacting test from your Lord.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ فرقنا بكم البحر فأنجيناكم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وأنتم تنظرون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh faraqnā bikumu l-baḥra fa-anjaynākum wa-aghraqnā āla fir'ʿawna wa-antum tanẓurūn
verses.english: Recall that we parted the sea for you; we saved you and drowned Pharaoh's people before your eyes.

1981.english: Recall that we parted the sea for you; we thus saved you and drowned the Pharaoh’s people before your eyes.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that we parted the sea for you; we thus saved you, and drowned Pharaoh’s people as you looked.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ وَٰعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذْتُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلة ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh wāʿadnā mūsā arbaʿīna laylatan thumma ittakhadhtumu l-ʿij'la min baʿdihi wa-antum ẓālimūn
verses.english: Yet, when we summoned Moses for forty nights, you worshiped the calf in his absence, and turned wicked.
verses.footnote: This incident reflects the humans' idolatrous tendency. Despite the profound miracles, Moses' followers worshiped the calf in his absence, and Moses ended up with only two believers (5:23). As pointed out in the Introduction, the humans are rebels whose egos are their gods.

1981.english: Recall that we summoned Moses for forty nights, then you idolized the calf in his absence and turned wicked.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that we summoned Moses for forty nights, then you worshiped the calf in his absence, and you turned wicked.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم عفونا عنكم من بعد ذلك لعلكم تشكرون
verses.transliterated: thumma ʿafawnā ʿankum min baʿdi dhālika laʿallakum tashkurūn
verses.english: Still, we pardoned you thereafter that you may be appreciative.

1981.english: Yet we pardoned you thereafter, that you may be thankful.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Yet, we pardoned you thereafter that you may be appreciative.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْفُرْقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ آتينا موسى الكتاب والفرقان لعلكم تهتدون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba wal-fur'qāna laʿallakum tahtadūn
verses.english: Recall that we gave Moses scripture and the statute book, that you may be guided.

1981.english: Recall that we gave Moses the scripture and the statute book, that you may be guided.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that we gave Moses the scripture and the statute book, that you may be guided.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم إنكم ظلمتم أنفسكم باتخاذكم العجل فتوبوا إلى بارئكم فاقتلوا أنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم عند بارئكم فتاب عليكم ۚ إنه هو التواب الرحيم
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qāla mūsā liqawmihi yāqawmi innakum ẓalamtum anfusakum bi-ittikhādhikumu l-ʿij'la fatūbū ilā bāri-ikum fa-uq'tulū anfusakum dhālikum khayrun lakum ʿinda bāri-ikum fatāba ʿalaykum innahu huwa l-tawābu l-raḥīm
verses.english: Recall that Moses said to his people, "O my people, you have wronged your souls by worshiping the calf. You must repent to your Creator. You shall kill your egos. This is better for you in the sight of your Creator." He did redeem you. He is the Redeemer, Most Merciful.
verses.subtitle: Kill Your Ego
verses.footnote: It is the ego that led to Satan's fall. It is the ego that caused our exile to this world, and it is the ego that is keeping most of us from redemption to God's Kingdom.

1981.english: Recall that Moses said to his people, “O my people, you have wronged your souls by idolizing the calf. You shall repent to your initiator.” God did redeem you, for He is the redeemer, the merciful.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that Moses said to his people, “O my people, you have wronged your souls by worshiping the calf. You shall repent to your Creator, and kill your egos. This is better for you, in the sight of your Creator.” He did redeem you, for He is the Redeemer, Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qul'tum yāmūsā lan nu'mina laka ḥattā narā l-laha jahratan fa-akhadhatkumu l-ṣāʿiqatu wa-antum tanẓurūn
verses.english: Recall that you said, "O Moses, we will not believe unless we see GOD, physically." Consequently, the lightning struck you, as you looked.
verses.subtitle: Physical Evidence
verses.footnote: It is noteworthy that the word "GOD" in this verse is the 19th occurrence, and this is the verse where the people demanded "physical evidence." The Quran's mathematical code, based on the number 19, provides such physical evidence. Note also that 2+55=57=19x3.

1981.english: And when you said, “O Moses, we will not believe unless we see God physically,” the lightning struck you as you looked.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that you said, “O Moses, we will not believe, unless we see GOD, physically.” Consequently, the lightning struck you, as you looked.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون
verses.transliterated: thumma baʿathnākum min baʿdi mawtikum laʿallakum tashkurūn
verses.english: We then revived you, after you had died, that you may be appreciative.

1981.english: Then we resurrected you from death, that you may be appreciative.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Then we resurrected you, after you had died, that you may be appreciative. In Sinai

verses.arabic: وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وظللنا عليكم الغمام وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى ۖ كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ۖ وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون
verses.transliterated: waẓallalnā ʿalaykumu l-ghamāma wa-anzalnā ʿalaykumu l-mana wal-salwā kulū min ṭayyibāti mā razaqnākum wamā ẓalamūnā walākin kānū anfusahum yaẓlimūn
verses.english: We shaded you with clouds (in Sinai), and sent down to you manna and quails: "Eat from the good things we provided for you." They did not hurt us (by rebelling); they only hurt their own souls.

1981.english: We shaded you with clouds, and sent down to you manna and quails. Eat from the good things we provided for you. They did no harm to us (by rebelling); it is their own souls that they harmed.
1981.subtitle: In Sinai
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: We shaded you with clouds, and we sent down to you manna and quails: “Eat from the good things we provided for you.” They never wronged us; they only wronged their own souls.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ٱدْخُلُوا۟ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا۟ حِطَّةٌ نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَٰيَٰكُمْ وَسَنَزِيدُ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قلنا ادخلوا هذه القرية فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغدا وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم ۚ وسنزيد المحسنين
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qul'nā ud'khulū hādhihi l-qaryata fakulū min'hā ḥaythu shi'tum raghadan wa-ud'khulū l-bāba sujjadan waqūlū ḥiṭṭatun naghfir lakum khaṭāyākum wasanazīdu l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: Recall that we said, "Enter this town, where you will find as many provisions as you like. Just enter the gate humbly, and treat the people nicely. We will then forgive your sins, and increase the reward for the pious."
verses.subtitle: Lack of Confidence in God: They Refuse to Enter Jerusalem

1981.english: Recall that we said, “Enter this village and eat therefrom as you please, generously. Enter the gate humbly, and speak amicably. We will then forgive your sins, and increase the reward for the righteous.”
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that we said, “Enter this town, and eat therefrom as you please, generously. Enter the gate humbly, and speak amicably. We will then forgive your sins, and increase the reward for the pious.”

verses.arabic: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ قَوْلًا غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِى قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ رِجْزًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْسُقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فبدل الذين ظلموا قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأنزلنا على الذين ظلموا رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون
verses.transliterated: fabaddala alladhīna ẓalamū qawlan ghayra alladhī qīla lahum fa-anzalnā ʿalā alladhīna ẓalamū rij'zan mina l-samāi bimā kānū yafsuqūn
verses.english: But the wicked among them carried out commands other than the commands given to them. Consequently, we sent down upon the transgressors condemnation from the sky, due to their wickedness.

1981.english: But the wicked distorted the commandments given to them, and consequently, we sent down upon them a curse from the sky; because of their wickedness.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: But the wicked among you substituted other words in place of the words given to them. Consequently, we sent down upon the transgressors condemnation from the sky, due to their wickedness.

verses.arabic: وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ استسقى موسى لقومه فقلنا اضرب بعصاك الحجر ۖ فانفجرت منه اثنتا عشرة عينا ۖ قد علم كل أناس مشربهم ۖ كلوا واشربوا من رزق الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين
verses.transliterated: wa-idhi is'tasqā mūsā liqawmihi faqul'nā iḍ'rib biʿaṣāka l-ḥajara fa-infajarat min'hu ith'natā ʿashrata ʿaynan qad ʿalima kullu unāsin mashrabahum kulū wa-ish'rabū min riz'qi l-lahi walā taʿthaw fī l-arḍi muf'sidīn
verses.english: Recall that Moses sought water for his people. We said, "Strike the rock with your staff." Whereupon, twelve springs gushed out therefrom. The members of each tribe knew their own water. Eat and drink from GOD's provisions, and do not roam the earth corruptingly.
verses.subtitle: More Miracles

1981.english: And when Moses sought water for his people, we said, “Strike the rock with your staff.” Whereupon, twelve springs gushed out therefrom, and thus, each tribe had their own water. Eat and drink from God's provisions, and do not corrupt the earth.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that Moses sought water for his people, and we said, “Strike the rock with your staff.” Whereupon, twelve springs gushed out therefrom. Thus, each tribe knew their own water: “Eat and drink from GOD’s provisions, and do not roam the earth corruptingly.”
1989.subtitle: More Miracles

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَٰحِدٍ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها وقثائها وفومها وعدسها وبصلها ۖ قال أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير ۚ اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم ۗ وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله ۗ ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق ۗ ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qul'tum yāmūsā lan naṣbira ʿalā ṭaʿāmin wāḥidin fa-ud'ʿu lanā rabbaka yukh'rij lanā mimmā tunbitu l-arḍu min baqlihā waqithāihā wafūmihā waʿadasihā wabaṣalihā qāla atastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā bi-alladhī huwa khayrun ih'biṭū miṣ'ran fa-inna lakum mā sa-altum waḍuribat ʿalayhimu l-dhilatu wal-maskanatu wabāū bighaḍabin mina l-lahi dhālika bi-annahum kānū yakfurūna biāyāti l-lahi wayaqtulūna l-nabiyīna bighayri l-ḥaqi dhālika bimā ʿaṣaw wakānū yaʿtadūn
verses.english: Recall that you said, "O Moses, we can no longer tolerate one kind of food. Call upon your Lord to produce for us such earthly crops as beans, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions." He said, "Do you wish to substitute that which is inferior for that which is good? Go down to Egypt, where you can find what you asked for." They have incurred condemnation, humiliation, and disgrace, and brought upon themselves wrath from GOD. This is because they rejected GOD's revelations, and killed the prophets unjustly. This is because they disobeyed and transgressed.
verses.subtitle: Israel Rebels

1981.english: Then you said, “O Moses, we can no longer tolerate one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to produce for us such earthly crops as beans, cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onions.” He said, “Do you wish to substitute that which is inferior for that which is good? Maybe you should go back to Egypt where you had such things!” They were condemned to humiliation and poverty, and they incurred wrath from God. That is because they rejected God’s revelations, and slew the prophets unjustly; they disobeyed and transgressed.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Recall that you said, “O Moses, we can no longer tolerate one kind of food. Call upon your Lord to produce for us such earthly crops as beans, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, and onions.” He said, “Do you wish to substitute that which is inferior for that which is good? Maybe you should go back to Egypt, where you can find what you asked for.” They were condemned to humiliation and disgrace, and they incurred GOD’s wrath. That is because they used to disbelieve in GOD’s revelations, and killed the prophets unjustly. That is because they disobeyed and transgressed.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والنصارى والصابئين من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون
verses.transliterated: inna alladhīna āmanū wa-alladhīna hādū wal-naṣārā wal-ṣābiīna man āmana bil-lahi wal-yawmi l-ākhiri waʿamila ṣāliḥan falahum ajruhum ʿinda rabbihim walā khawfun ʿalayhim walā hum yaḥzanūn
verses.english: Surely, those who believe, those who are Jewish, the Christians, and the converts; anyone who (1) believes in GOD, and (2) believes in the Last Day, and (3) leads a righteous life, will receive their recompense from their Lord. They have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve.
verses.subtitle: Unity of All Submitters

1981.english: Those who believe, those who are Jewish, the Christians, and the converts; any of them who believe in God and the last day, and lead a righteous life, have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve.
1981.subtitle: Minimum Requirement for Salvation
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: Surely, those who believe, those who are Jewish, the Christians, and the converts; anyone who (1) believes in GOD (2) and the Last Day, and (3) leads a righteous life, will receive their recompense from their Lord. They have nothing to fear, nor will they grieve.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh akhadhnā mīthāqakum warafaʿnā fawqakumu l-ṭūra khudhū mā ātaynākum biquwwatin wa-udh'kurū mā fīhi laʿallakum tattaqūn
verses.english: We made a covenant with you, as we raised Mount Sinai above you: "You shall uphold what we have given you strongly, and remember its contents, that you may be saved."
verses.subtitle: Covenant with Israel

1981.english: Recall that we made a covenant with you, as we raised Mount Sinai over you. You shall uphold this covenant strongly, and remember its tenets, that you may attain salvation.
1981.subtitle: The Covenant
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: We made a covenant with you, as we raised Mount Sinai above you: “You shall uphold what we have given you, strongly, and remember what is in it, that you may be saved.”
1989.subtitle: Covenant with Israel

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُۥ لَكُنتُم مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم توليتم من بعد ذلك ۖ فلولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لكنتم من الخاسرين
verses.transliterated: thumma tawallaytum min baʿdi dhālika falawlā faḍlu l-lahi ʿalaykum waraḥmatuhu lakuntum mina l-khāsirīn
verses.english: But you turned away thereafter, and if it were not for GOD's grace towards you and His mercy, you would have been doomed.

1981.english: You turned back thereafter, and if it were not for God’s indulgence towards you, and His mercy, you would have been destroyed.
1981.footnote: Why are the children of Israel so frequently mentioned throughout the Quran? See footnote 4:153 for the parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad.

1989.english: But you turned away after that! If it were not for GOD’s compassion towards you, and His mercy, you would have been losers.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱعْتَدَوْا۟ مِنكُمْ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا۟ قِرَدَةً خَٰسِـِٔينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد علمتم الذين اعتدوا منكم في السبت فقلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين
verses.transliterated: walaqad ʿalim'tumu alladhīna iʿ'tadaw minkum fī l-sabti faqul'nā lahum kūnū qiradatan khāsiīn
verses.english: You have known about those among you who desecrated the Sabbath. We said to them, "Be you as despicable as apes."

1981.english: You have known about those among you who desecrated the Sabbath; we said to them, “Be you despicable apes.”
