1981.english: (The angels) said, "O Lot, we are messengers from your Lord, and they can never harm you. Move during the night with your family, and do not look behind, except your wife; she is doomed with the others. Their appointed time is the morning; is not the morning soon enough?"

1989.english: (The angels) said, “O Lot, we are your Lord’s messengers. These people cannot touch you. You shall leave with your family during the night, and let not anyone of you look back, except your wife; she is condemned along with those who are condemned. Their appointed time is the morning. Is the morning not soon enough?”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا جَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِّن سِجِّيلٍ مَّنضُودٍ
verses.arabicClean: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود
verses.transliterated: falammā jāa amrunā jaʿalnā ʿāliyahā sāfilahā wa-amṭarnā ʿalayhā ḥijāratan min sijjīlin manḍūdi
verses.english: When our judgment came, we turned it upside down, and we showered it with hard, devastating rocks.
verses.subtitle: Sodom & Gomorrah Destroyed

1981.english: When our judgment came, we turned it upside down, and showered them with a barrage of solid rocks.

1989.english: When our judgment came, we turned it upside down. We showered it with hard, devastating rocks.

verses.arabic: مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ وَمَا هِىَ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ
verses.arabicClean: مسومة عند ربك ۖ وما هي من الظالمين ببعيد
verses.transliterated: musawwamatan ʿinda rabbika wamā hiya mina l-ẓālimīna bibaʿīdi
verses.english: Such rocks were designated by your Lord to strike the transgressors.

1981.english: Trained by your Lord, (the rocks) struck directly at the wicked.

1989.english: Such rocks were marked by your Lord to strike the transgressors. Shu'aib

verses.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًا قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ وَلَا تَنقُصُوا۟ ٱلْمِكْيَالَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكُم بِخَيْرٍ وَإِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ مُّحِيطٍ
verses.arabicClean: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا ۚ قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره ۖ ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان ۚ إني أراكم بخير وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط
verses.transliterated: wa-ilā madyana akhāhum shuʿayban qāla yāqawmi uʿ'budū l-laha mā lakum min ilāhin ghayruhu walā tanquṣū l-mik'yāla wal-mīzāna innī arākum bikhayrin wa-innī akhāfu ʿalaykum ʿadhāba yawmin muḥīṭi
verses.english: To Midyan we sent their brother Shu'aib. He said, "O my people, worship GOD; you have no other god beside Him. Do not cheat when you measure or weigh. I see that you are prosperous, and I fear for you the retribution of an overwhelming day.
verses.subtitle: Shu'aib: One and the Same Message

1981.english: To Midyan (we sent) their brother Shu'aib. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no other god besides Him, and do not cheat when you measure or weigh. I see that you are prosperous, and I fear lest you suffer the retribution of an overwhelming day.
1981.subtitle: Shu'aib

1989.english: To Midyan we sent their brother Shu‘aib. He said, “O my people, worship GOD; you have no other god besides Him. Do not cheat when you measure or weigh. I see that you are prosperous, and I fear for you the retribution of an overwhelming day.

verses.arabic: وَيَٰقَوْمِ أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْمِكْيَالَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ويا قوم أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط ۖ ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين
verses.transliterated: wayāqawmi awfū l-mik'yāla wal-mīzāna bil-qis'ṭi walā tabkhasū l-nāsa ashyāahum walā taʿthaw fī l-arḍi muf'sidīn
verses.english: "O my people, you shall give full measure and full weight, equitably. Do not cheat the people out of their rights, and do not roam the earth corruptingly.

1981.english: "O my people, give full measure, and full weight, equitably. Do not cheat the people out of their things, and do not corrupt the earth.

1989.english: “O my people, you shall give full measure and full weight, equitably. Do not cheat the people out of their rights, and do not roam the earth corruptingly.

verses.arabic: بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ عَلَيْكُم بِحَفِيظٍ
verses.arabicClean: بقيت الله خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين ۚ وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ
verses.transliterated: baqiyyatu l-lahi khayrun lakum in kuntum mu'minīna wamā anā ʿalaykum biḥafīẓi
verses.english: "Whatever GOD provides for you, no matter how small, is far better for you, if you are really believers. I am not a guardian over you."

1981.english: "A smaller provision from God would be better for you, if you are really believers. I am not a guardian over you."

1989.english: “Whatever GOD provides for you, no matter how small, is far better for you, if you are really believers. I am not a guardian over you.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰشُعَيْبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَن نَّتْرُكَ مَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلْحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء ۖ إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد
verses.transliterated: qālū yāshuʿaybu aṣalatuka tamuruka an natruka mā yaʿbudu ābāunā aw an nafʿala fī amwālinā mā nashāu innaka la-anta l-ḥalīmu l-rashīd
verses.english: They said, "O Shu'aib, does your religion dictate upon you that we must abandon our parents' religion, or running our businesses in any manner we choose? Surely, you are known for being clement, wise."

1981.english: They said, "O Shu'aib, does your faith enjoin us from idolizing what our parents have idolized, and from doing whatever we want with our money? Surely, you are too clement, and too wise!"

1989.english: They said, “O Shu‘aib, does your religion dictate upon you that we must abandon our parents’ religion, or running our commerce in any manner we choose? Surely, you are known for being clement, wise.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّى وَرَزَقَنِى مِنْهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلْإِصْلَٰحَ مَا ٱسْتَطَعْتُ وَمَا تَوْفِيقِىٓ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ
verses.arabicClean: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا ۚ وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه ۚ إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت ۚ وما توفيقي إلا بالله ۚ عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب
verses.transliterated: qāla yāqawmi ara-aytum in kuntu ʿalā bayyinatin min rabbī warazaqanī min'hu riz'qan ḥasanan wamā urīdu an ukhālifakum ilā mā anhākum ʿanhu in urīdu illā l-iṣ'lāḥa mā is'taṭaʿtu wamā tawfīqī illā bil-lahi ʿalayhi tawakkaltu wa-ilayhi unīb
verses.english: He said, "O my people, what if I have solid proof from my Lord; what if He has provided me with a great blessing? It is not my wish to commit what I enjoin you from. I only wish to correct as many wrongs as I can. My guidance depends totally on GOD; I have put my trust in Him. To Him I have totally submitted.

1981.english: He said, "O my people, what if I have proof from my Lord, and good blessings? I do not wish to impose any hardship upon you, through my prohibitions; I only seek to reform as much I can. My success depends completely on God; I trust in Him, and I submit to Him.

1989.english: He said, “O my people, what if I have positive proof from my Lord; what if He has provided me with a great blessing? It is not my wish to commit what I enjoin you from. I only wish to correct as many wrongs as I can. My guidance depends totally on GOD; I have put my trust in Him. To Him I have totally submitted.

verses.arabic: وَيَٰقَوْمِ لَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شِقَاقِىٓ أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثْلُ مَآ أَصَابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ صَٰلِحٍ وَمَا قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدٍ
verses.arabicClean: ويا قوم لا يجرمنكم شقاقي أن يصيبكم مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح ۚ وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد
verses.transliterated: wayāqawmi lā yajrimannakum shiqāqī an yuṣībakum mith'lu mā aṣāba qawma nūḥin aw qawma hūdin aw qawma ṣāliḥin wamā qawmu lūṭin minkum bibaʿīdi
verses.english: "And, O my people, do not be provoked by your opposition to me into incurring the same disasters as the people of Noah, or the people of Hûd, or the people of Sãleh; and the people of Lot are not too far from you.

1981.english: "And, O my people, let not your hatred of me provoke you into suffering the same fate as the people of Noah, or the people of Hood, or the people of Saalih; and the people of Lot are not too far from you.

1989.english: “And, O my people, do not be provoked by your opposition to me into incurring the same disasters as the people of Noah, or the people of Hood, or the people of Saaleh; and the people of Lot are not too far from you.

verses.arabic: وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ إِنَّ رَبِّى رَحِيمٌ وَدُودٌ
verses.arabicClean: واستغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه ۚ إن ربي رحيم ودود
verses.transliterated: wa-is'taghfirū rabbakum thumma tūbū ilayhi inna rabbī raḥīmun wadūdu
verses.english: "You shall implore your Lord for forgiveness, then repent to Him. My Lord is Most Merciful, Kind."

1981.english: "You shall ask forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is merciful, kind."

1989.english: “You shall implore your Lord for forgiveness, then repent to Him. My Lord is Most Merciful, Kind.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰشُعَيْبُ مَا نَفْقَهُ كَثِيرًا مِّمَّا تَقُولُ وَإِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِينَا ضَعِيفًا وَلَوْلَا رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْنَٰكَ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْنَا بِعَزِيزٍ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا شعيب ما نفقه كثيرا مما تقول وإنا لنراك فينا ضعيفا ۖ ولولا رهطك لرجمناك ۖ وما أنت علينا بعزيز
verses.transliterated: qālū yāshuʿaybu mā nafqahu kathīran mimmā taqūlu wa-innā lanarāka fīnā ḍaʿīfan walawlā rahṭuka larajamnāka wamā anta ʿalaynā biʿazīzi
verses.english: They said, "O Shu'aib, we do not comprehend many of the things you are telling us, and we see that you are powerless among us. If it were not for your tribe, we would have stoned you. You have no value for us."

1981.english: They said, "O Shu'aib, we do not comprehend most of what you say, and we see that you are feeble. If it were not for your tribe, we would have stoned you; we do not care about you."

1989.english: They said, “O Shu'aib, we do not comprehend many of the things you are telling us, and we see that you are powerless among us. If it were not for your tribe, we would have stoned you. You have no power over us.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَرَهْطِىٓ أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَرَآءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا إِنَّ رَبِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا ۖ إن ربي بما تعملون محيط
verses.transliterated: qāla yāqawmi arahṭī aʿazzu ʿalaykum mina l-lahi wa-ittakhadhtumūhu warāakum ẓih'riyyan inna rabbī bimā taʿmalūna muḥīṭu
verses.english: He said, "O my people, does my tribe command a greater respect than GOD? Is this why you have been heedless of Him? My Lord is fully aware of everything you do.

1981.english: He said, "O my people, is my tribe more respectable to you than God? Is this why you disregard Him? Indeed, my Lord is fully aware of everything you do.

1989.english: He said, “O my people, is my tribe more powerful in your eyes than GOD? Is this why you have been heedless of Him? My Lord is fully aware of everything you do.

verses.arabic: وَيَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْمَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنِّى عَٰمِلٌ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن يَأْتِيهِ عَذَابٌ يُخْزِيهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ كَٰذِبٌ وَٱرْتَقِبُوٓا۟ إِنِّى مَعَكُمْ رَقِيبٌ
verses.arabicClean: ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل ۖ سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب ۖ وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب
verses.transliterated: wayāqawmi iʿ'malū ʿalā makānatikum innī ʿāmilun sawfa taʿlamūna man yatīhi ʿadhābun yukh'zīhi waman huwa kādhibun wa-ir'taqibū innī maʿakum raqību
verses.english: "O my people, go on doing what you wish, and so will I. You will certainly find out which of us will incur shameful retribution; you will find out who the liar is. Just wait in anticipation, and I will wait in anticipation along with you."

1981.english: "And, O my people, do what you wish, and so will I. You will find out which of us suffers humiliating retribution, and which of us is the liar. Keep watching, and I am a watcher with you."

1989.english: “O my people, go on doing what you wish, and so will I. You will certainly find out which of us will incur shameful retribution; you will find out who the liar is. Just wait in anticipation, and I will wait in anticipation along with you.”

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا شُعَيْبًا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنَّا وَأَخَذَتِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ فِى دِيَٰرِهِمْ جَٰثِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين
verses.transliterated: walammā jāa amrunā najjaynā shuʿayban wa-alladhīna āmanū maʿahu biraḥmatin minnā wa-akhadhati alladhīna ẓalamū l-ṣayḥatu fa-aṣbaḥū fī diyārihim jāthimīn
verses.english: When our judgment came, we saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him, by mercy from us. As for the evil ones, they were struck by a disaster that left them dead in their homes.

1981.english: When our judgment came, we saved Shu'aib and those who believed, with mercy from us, and the wicked were struck by disaster; they were left dead in their homes.

1989.english: When our judgment came, we saved Shu‘aib and those who believed with him, by mercy from us. As for the evil ones, they were struck by a disaster that left them dead in their homes.

verses.arabic: كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا۟ فِيهَآ أَلَا بُعْدًا لِّمَدْيَنَ كَمَا بَعِدَتْ ثَمُودُ
verses.arabicClean: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ۗ ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود
verses.transliterated: ka-an lam yaghnaw fīhā alā buʿ'dan limadyana kamā baʿidat thamūd
verses.english: It was as though they never existed. Thus, Midyan perished, just like Thamûd had perished before that.

1981.english: It was as though they never existed. Behold, Midyan perished, just as Thamud had perished.

1989.english: It was as though they never existed. Thus, Midyan perished, just like Thamoud had perished.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين
verses.transliterated: walaqad arsalnā mūsā biāyātinā wasul'ṭānin mubīni
verses.english: We sent Moses with our signs and a profound authority.
verses.subtitle: Moses

1981.english: And we sent Moses with our miracles and manifest authorization;
1981.subtitle: Moses

1989.english: We sent Moses with our signs and a profound authority—
1989.subtitle: Moses

verses.arabic: إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦ فَٱتَّبَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَآ أَمْرُ فِرْعَوْنَ بِرَشِيدٍ
verses.arabicClean: إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون ۖ وما أمر فرعون برشيد
verses.transliterated: ilā fir'ʿawna wamala-ihi fa-ittabaʿū amra fir'ʿawna wamā amru fir'ʿawna birashīdi
verses.english: To Pharaoh and his elders. But they followed the command of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh's command was not wise.

1981.english: to Pharaoh and his elders. But they followed Pharaoh's orders; and Pharaoh's orders were not wise.

1989.english: to Pharaoh and his elders. But they followed the command of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh’s command was not wise.

verses.arabic: يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْوِرْدُ ٱلْمَوْرُودُ
verses.arabicClean: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار ۖ وبئس الورد المورود
verses.transliterated: yaqdumu qawmahu yawma l-qiyāmati fa-awradahumu l-nāra wabi'sa l-wir'du l-mawrūd
verses.english: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection, all the way to Hell; what a miserable abode to live in!

1981.english: He will lead his people on the day of resurrection, plunging them into hell, what a miserable abode to plunge in.

1989.english: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection, all the way to Hell. What a miserable abode to enter!

verses.arabic: وَأُتْبِعُوا۟ فِى هَٰذِهِۦ لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ بِئْسَ ٱلرِّفْدُ ٱلْمَرْفُودُ
verses.arabicClean: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة ۚ بئس الرفد المرفود
verses.transliterated: wa-ut'biʿū fī hādhihi laʿnatan wayawma l-qiyāmati bi'sa l-rif'du l-marfūd
verses.english: They have incurred condemnation in this life, as well as on the Day of Resurrection; what a miserable path to follow!

1981.english: They were accursed in this life, as well as on the day of resurrection; what a miserable fate to be attained.

1989.english: They have incurred condemnation in this (life), as well as on the Day of Resurrection. What a miserable path to follow!

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّهُۥ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهَا قَآئِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ
verses.arabicClean: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك ۖ منها قائم وحصيد
verses.transliterated: dhālika min anbāi l-qurā naquṣṣuhu ʿalayka min'hā qāimun waḥaṣīdu
verses.english: This is news from the past communities that we narrate to you. Some are still standing, and some have vanished.
verses.subtitle: Lessons to be Learned

1981.english: This is history from the past communities that we narrate to you; some of them are still standing, while others were wiped out.

1989.english: This is news from the (past) communities that we narrate to you. Some are still standing, and some have vanished.
1989.subtitle: Lessons to be Learned

verses.arabic: وَمَا ظَلَمْنَٰهُمْ وَلَٰكِن ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ فَمَآ أَغْنَتْ عَنْهُمْ ءَالِهَتُهُمُ ٱلَّتِى يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ لَّمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَمَا زَادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ
verses.arabicClean: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم ۖ فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك ۖ وما زادوهم غير تتبيب
verses.transliterated: wamā ẓalamnāhum walākin ẓalamū anfusahum famā aghnat ʿanhum ālihatuhumu allatī yadʿūna min dūni l-lahi min shayin lammā jāa amru rabbika wamā zādūhum ghayra tatbībi
verses.english: We never wronged them; they wronged their own souls. Their gods, whom they invoked beside GOD, could not help them in the least when the judgment of your Lord came. In fact, they only ensured their doom.

1981.english: We were not unjust towards them; it was they who were unjust to themselves. The idols they had set up besides God never helped them, when God's judgment came. They only augmented their plight.

1989.english: We never wronged them; they wronged their own souls. Their gods, whom they invoked besides GOD, could not help them in the least when the judgment of your Lord came. In fact, they only ensured their doom.

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَآ أَخَذَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَهِىَ ظَٰلِمَةٌ إِنَّ أَخْذَهُۥٓ أَلِيمٌ شَدِيدٌ
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة ۚ إن أخذه أليم شديد
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika akhdhu rabbika idhā akhadha l-qurā wahiya ẓālimatun inna akhdhahu alīmun shadīdu
verses.english: Such was the retribution enforced by your Lord when the communities transgressed. Indeed, His retribution is painful, devastating.

1981.english: Thus does your Lord punish the wicked communities; indeed, His punishment is painful, severe.

1989.english: Such was the retribution enforced by your Lord when the communities transgressed. Indeed, His retribution is painful, devastating.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً لِّمَنْ خَافَ عَذَابَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَّجْمُوعٌ لَّهُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَّشْهُودٌ
verses.arabicClean: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ۚ ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود
verses.transliterated: inna fī dhālika laāyatan liman khāfa ʿadhāba l-ākhirati dhālika yawmun majmūʿun lahu l-nāsu wadhālika yawmun mashhūdu
verses.english: This should be a lesson for those who fear the retribution of the Hereafter. That is a day when all the people will be summoned—a day to be witnessed.

1981.english: This should be a lesson for any one who dreads the retribution of the hereafter. This is a day on which all the people will be gathered; this is a day that will be witnessed (by all).

1989.english: This should be a lesson for those who fear the retribution of the Hereafter. For that is a day when all the people will be summoned— a day to be witnessed (by all).

verses.arabic: وَمَا نُؤَخِّرُهُۥٓ إِلَّا لِأَجَلٍ مَّعْدُودٍ
verses.arabicClean: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود
verses.transliterated: wamā nu-akhiruhu illā li-ajalin maʿdūdi
verses.english: We have appointed a specific time for it to take place.

1981.english: We have it delayed until a predetermined time.

1989.english: We have appointed a specific time for it to happen.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِىٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ
verses.arabicClean: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه ۚ فمنهم شقي وسعيد
verses.transliterated: yawma yati lā takallamu nafsun illā bi-idh'nihi famin'hum shaqiyyun wasaʿīdu
verses.english: The day it comes to pass, no soul will utter a single word, except in accordance with His will. Some will be miserable, and some will be happy.

1981.english: The day it comes, no one will speak, except with God's permission; some will be miserable, and (some will be) happy.

1989.english: The day it comes to pass, no soul will utter a single word, except in accordance with His will. Some will be miserable, and (some will be) happy.

verses.arabic: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُوا۟ فَفِى ٱلنَّارِ لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ
verses.arabicClean: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق
verses.transliterated: fa-ammā alladhīna shaqū fafī l-nāri lahum fīhā zafīrun washahīqu
verses.english: As for the miserable ones, they will be in Hell, wherein they sigh and wail.

1981.english: As for those destined for misery, they abide in hell, wherein they sigh and wail.

1989.english: As for those who transgressed, they will be in Hell, wherein they sigh and wail.

verses.arabic: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ
verses.arabicClean: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك ۚ إن ربك فعال لما يريد
verses.transliterated: khālidīna fīhā mā dāmati l-samāwātu wal-arḍu illā mā shāa rabbuka inna rabbaka faʿʿālun limā yurīd
verses.english: Eternally they abide therein, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, in accordance with the will of your Lord. Your Lord is doer of whatever He wills.

1981.english: Eternally they stay therein, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, in accordance with the will of your Lord. Your Lord's will is done.

1989.english: Eternally they abide therein, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, in accordance with the will of your Lord. Your Lord is doer of whatever He wills.

verses.arabic: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا۟ فَفِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ
verses.arabicClean: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك ۖ عطاء غير مجذوذ
verses.transliterated: wa-ammā alladhīna suʿidū fafī l-janati khālidīna fīhā mā dāmati l-samāwātu wal-arḍu illā mā shāa rabbuka ʿaṭāan ghayra majdhūdhi
verses.english: As for the fortunate ones, they will be in Paradise. Eternally they abide therein, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, in accordance with the will of your Lord—an everlasting reward.

1981.english: As for those destined for happiness, they abide in Paradise. Eternally they stay therein, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, in accordance with the will of your Lord; an everlasting gift.

1989.english: As for those who deserved happiness, they will be in Paradise. Eternally they abide therein, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, in accordance with the will of your Lord—an everlasting reward.

verses.arabic: فَلَا تَكُ فِى مِرْيَةٍ مِّمَّا يَعْبُدُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُهُم مِّن قَبْلُ وَإِنَّا لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ غَيْرَ مَنقُوصٍ
verses.arabicClean: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ۚ ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل ۚ وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص
verses.transliterated: falā taku fī mir'yatin mimmā yaʿbudu hāulāi mā yaʿbudūna illā kamā yaʿbudu ābāuhum min qablu wa-innā lamuwaffūhum naṣībahum ghayra manqūṣi
verses.english: Do not have any doubt regarding what these people worship; they worship exactly as they found their parents worshiping. We will requite them their due share fully, without reduction.
verses.subtitle: Following Our Parents Blindly A Great Human Tragedy

1981.english: You should have no question about the idol worship that these people practice; they are following their parents' footsteps. We will pay them their full share, without the least reduction.

1989.english: Do not have any doubt regarding what these people worship; they worship exactly as they found their parents worshiping. We will pay them their due share fully, without reduction.
1989.subtitle: Following Our Parents Blindly A Great Human Tragedy

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ فَٱخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَقُضِىَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِى شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ مُرِيبٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ۚ ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم ۚ وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب
verses.transliterated: walaqad ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba fa-ukh'tulifa fīhi walawlā kalimatun sabaqat min rabbika laquḍiya baynahum wa-innahum lafī shakkin min'hu murībi
verses.english: We have given Moses the scripture, but it was disputed, and if it were not for a predetermined word decreed by your Lord, they would have been judged immediately. They are full of doubt about this, suspicious.

1981.english: We have given Moses the scripture, and it was disputed. If it were not for a predetermined decision by your Lord, they would have been judged. Similarly, these people are doubtful about the Quran.

1989.english: We have given Moses the scripture, but it was disputed. If it were not for a word already decreed by your Lord, they would have been judged. Indeed, they are doubtful about it, suspicious.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ كُلًّا لَّمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ رَبُّكَ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم ۚ إنه بما يعملون خبير
verses.transliterated: wa-inna kullan lammā layuwaffiyannahum rabbuka aʿmālahum innahu bimā yaʿmalūna khabīru
verses.english: Your Lord will surely recompense everyone for their works. He is fully Cognizant of everything they do.

1981.english: And surely, God will pay each of them fully for their works; He is fully cognizant of everything they do.

1989.english: Your Lord will surely pay everyone for their works. He is fully Cognizant of everything they do.

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَقِمْ كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ وَمَن تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا۟ إِنَّهُۥ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا ۚ إنه بما تعملون بصير
verses.transliterated: fa-is'taqim kamā umir'ta waman tāba maʿaka walā taṭghaw innahu bimā taʿmalūna baṣīru
verses.english: Therefore, continue on the path you have been enjoined to follow, together with those who repented with you, and do not transgress. He is Seer of everything you do.

1981.english: You shall follow the straight path pointed out to you, along with those who have repented with you, and do not transgress. God is seer of everything you do.
1981.subtitle: Important Commandments

1989.english: Therefore, continue on the path you have been enjoined to follow, together with those who repented with you, and do not transgress. He is Seer of everything you do.

verses.arabic: وَلَا تَرْكَنُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ فَتَمَسَّكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَآءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون
verses.transliterated: walā tarkanū ilā alladhīna ẓalamū fatamassakumu l-nāru wamā lakum min dūni l-lahi min awliyāa thumma lā tunṣarūn
verses.english: Do not lean towards those who have transgressed, lest you incur Hell, and find no allies to help you against GOD, then end up losers.

1981.english: And do not ally yourselves with those who wrong their souls, lest you deserve hell, and find no allies besides God, nor any help.

1989.english: Do not join those who transgress, lest you incur Hell, and find no allies to help you against GOD, then end up defeated.

verses.arabic: وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَىِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ إِنَّ ٱلْحَسَنَٰتِ يُذْهِبْنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ ذَٰلِكَ ذِكْرَىٰ لِلذَّٰكِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل ۚ إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ۚ ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين
verses.transliterated: wa-aqimi l-ṣalata ṭarafayi l-nahāri wazulafan mina al-layli inna l-ḥasanāti yudh'hib'na l-sayiāti dhālika dhik'rā lildhākirīn
verses.english: You shall observe the Contact Prayers (Salat) at both ends of the day, and during the night. The righteous works wipe out the evil works. This is a reminder for those who would take heed.
verses.subtitle: Three of the Five Prayers

1981.english: You shall observe the **salat** prayers at both ends of the day, and during the night. The righteous works nullify the evil works. This is a message for those who take heed.

1989.english: You shall observe the contact prayers (Salat) at both ends of the day, and during the night. The righteous works wipe out the evil works. This is a reminder for those who would take heed.
1989.subtitle: Three of the Five Prayers

verses.arabic: وَٱصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين
verses.transliterated: wa-iṣ'bir fa-inna l-laha lā yuḍīʿu ajra l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: You shall steadfastly persevere, for GOD never fails to recompense the righteous.

1981.english: You shall be steadfast; for God never fails to reward the righteous.

1989.english: You shall steadfastly persevere, for GOD never fails to reward the righteous.

verses.arabic: فَلَوْلَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ أُو۟لُوا۟ بَقِيَّةٍ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْفَسَادِ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّنْ أَنجَيْنَا مِنْهُمْ وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مَآ أُتْرِفُوا۟ فِيهِ وَكَانُوا۟ مُجْرِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم ۗ واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين
verses.transliterated: falawlā kāna mina l-qurūni min qablikum ulū baqiyyatin yanhawna ʿani l-fasādi fī l-arḍi illā qalīlan mimman anjaynā min'hum wa-ittabaʿa alladhīna ẓalamū mā ut'rifū fīhi wakānū muj'rimīn
verses.english: If only some of those among the previous generations possessed enough intelligence to forbid evil! Only a few of them deserved to be saved by us. As for the transgressors, they were preoccupied with their material luxuries; they were guilty.

1981.english: If only the previous generations had some intelligent people who enjoined them from corruption, they would have been saved. But we saved a few of them, while the rest pursued their material things, and became sinners.

1989.english: If only some of those among the previous generations possessed enough intelligence to forbid evil! Only a few of them deserved to be saved by us. As for the transgressors, they were preoccupied with their material luxuries—they were guilty.

verses.arabic: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون
verses.transliterated: wamā kāna rabbuka liyuh'lika l-qurā biẓul'min wa-ahluhā muṣ'liḥūn
verses.english: Your Lord never annihilates any community unjustly, while its people are righteous.

1981.english: Your Lord never destroys any community unjustly, while the people are righteous.

1989.english: Your Lord never annihilates any community unjustly, while its people are righteous.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً وَلَا يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ۖ ولا يزالون مختلفين
verses.transliterated: walaw shāa rabbuka lajaʿala l-nāsa ummatan wāḥidatan walā yazālūna mukh'talifīn
verses.english: Had your Lord willed, all the people would have been one congregation (of believers). But they will always dispute (the truth).
verses.subtitle: Why Were We Created

1981.english: Had your Lord willed, He could have made all the people one congregation. But they will always dispute.

1989.english: Had your Lord willed, all the people would have been one {believing) congregation. But they will always dispute {the truth).
1989.subtitle: Why Were We Created

verses.arabic: إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَ وَلِذَٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إلا من رحم ربك ۚ ولذلك خلقهم ۗ وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين
verses.transliterated: illā man raḥima rabbuka walidhālika khalaqahum watammat kalimatu rabbika la-amla-anna jahannama mina l-jinati wal-nāsi ajmaʿīn
verses.english: Only those blessed with mercy from your Lord (will not dispute the truth). This is why He created them. The judgment of your Lord has already been issued: "I will fill Hell with jinns and humans, all together."
verses.footnote:
The Most Merciful has created us on this earth to give us yet another chance to denounce our original crime and to be redeemed (see the Introduction and Appendix 7).

±±11:119 God does not put a single person in Hell; they choose and insist upon going to Hell.

1981.english: Only those endowed with mercy from your Lord (will not dispute), and this is what He created them for. Your Lord's decision has already been made; that I will fill Gehenna of both jinns and humans.

1989.english: Except for those redeemed by your Lord. This is why He created them.* The decision of your Lord has already been issued: “I will fill Hell with jinns and humans, all together.”
1989.footnote: The Most Merciful has created us on this earth to give us a chance to denounce our original crime and to be redeemed (see the Introduction and Appendix 7)

verses.arabic: وَكُلًّا نَّقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلرُّسُلِ مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ وَجَآءَكَ فِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك ۚ وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين
verses.transliterated: wakullan naquṣṣu ʿalayka min anbāi l-rusuli mā nuthabbitu bihi fuādaka wajāaka fī hādhihi l-ḥaqu wamawʿiẓatun wadhik'rā lil'mu'minīn
verses.english: We narrate to you enough history of the messengers to strengthen your heart. The truth has come to you herein, as well as enlightenments and reminders for the believers.

1981.english: We have narrated to you the history of previous messengers, in order to strengthen your heart. The truth has come to you herein, and enlightenment, and a reminder for the believers.

1989.english: We narrate to you enough history of the messengers to strengthen your heart. The truth has come to you herein, and enlightenment, and a reminder for the believers.

verses.arabic: وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ ٱعْمَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنَّا عَٰمِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون
verses.transliterated: waqul lilladhīna lā yu'minūna iʿ'malū ʿalā makānatikum innā ʿāmilūn
verses.english: Say to those who disbelieve, "Do whatever you can, and so will we.

1981.english: And say to those who do not believe, "Keep doing what you are doing, and we will.

1989.english: Say to those who disbelieve, “Do whatever you can, and so will we.

verses.arabic: وَٱنتَظِرُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مُنتَظِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون
verses.transliterated: wa-intaẓirū innā muntaẓirūn
verses.english: "Then wait; we too will wait."

1981.english: "Then wait, and we will wait."

1989.english: “Then wait; we too will wait.”

verses.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ ٱلْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُۥ فَٱعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه ۚ وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون
verses.transliterated: walillahi ghaybu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wa-ilayhi yur'jaʿu l-amru kulluhu fa-uʿ'bud'hu watawakkal ʿalayhi wamā rabbuka bighāfilin ʿammā taʿmalūn
verses.english: To GOD belongs the future of the heavens and the earth, and all matters are controlled by Him. You shall worship Him and trust in Him. Your Lord is never unaware of anything you do.

1981.english: To God belongs the future of the heavens and the earth. He is in full control of all things. You shall worship Him, and trust in Him. Your Lord is never unaware of anything you do.

1989.english: To GOD belongs the future of the heavens and the earth; all matters will be returned to Him. Therefore, you shall worship Him and put your trust in Him. Your Lord is never unaware of anything you do.

verses.arabic: الٓر تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الر ۚ تلك آيات الكتاب المبين
verses.transliterated: alif-lam-ra til'ka āyātu l-kitābi l-mubīn
verses.english: A. L. R. These (letters) are proofs of this profound scripture.
verses.footnote: The Quranic initials constitute a major component of a great miracle (App. 1).

1981.english: A.L.R. These (letters) are the miracles of this manifest scripture.
1981.footnote: See Appendix 1 for details of the Quran's miraculous secret numerical code involving these letters. One of the miraculous features of Quran is the use of multiple-meaning words. One such word is "Ayat." This word has at least three different meanings, namely, "sign" (see for example 2:164), "verse" (see for example 2:99), and "miracle" (see for example 17:101). In this way, various generations of people can derive the meaning that perfectly suits each one of them. Before the discovery of the Quran's secret numerical code, the word "ayat" in verse 12:1 was understood to mean "verses" and to apply to the verses of Quran in general. However, now that the significance of these letters is unveiled, we find that the suitable meaning of the word "ayat" is "miracles." Two facts pin down the meaning of this verse to what you see in this translation: (1) this expression is used exclusively with Quranic initials such as these A.L.R. (see also 13:1, 15:1, 26:2, 27:1, 28:2, & 31:2), and (2) the Arabic word commonly used for "miracle," namely, "Mu'jizah" is never mentioned in the Quran.

1989.english: A.L.R. These {letters) are miracles of this profound scripture.*
1989.footnote: The Quranic initials constitute a major component of a great miracle (App. 1).

verses.arabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون
verses.transliterated: innā anzalnāhu qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan laʿallakum taʿqilūn
verses.english: We have revealed it an Arabic Quran, that you may understand.
verses.footnote: Why was the Quran revealed in Arabic? See 41:44 and Appendix 4.

1981.english: We have sent it down, an Arabic Quran, that you may understand.
1981.footnote: The word "you" in this verse applies to all the people of the world, regardless of their mother tongue. See Appendix 3 for details.

1989.english: We have revealed it, an Arabic Quran, that you may understand.*
1989.footnote: Why was the Quran revealed in Arabic? See 41:44 and Appendix 4.

verses.arabic: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلْغَٰفِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين
verses.transliterated: naḥnu naquṣṣu ʿalayka aḥsana l-qaṣaṣi bimā awḥaynā ilayka hādhā l-qur'āna wa-in kunta min qablihi lamina l-ghāfilīn
verses.english: We narrate to you the most accurate history through the revelation of this Quran. Before this, you were totally unaware.

1981.english: We narrate to you the best narrations, by revealing this Quran to you. Before this, you were unaware.

1989.english: We narrate to you the most accurate history through the revelation of this Quran. Before this, you were totally unaware.

verses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَٰجِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين
verses.transliterated: idh qāla yūsufu li-abīhi yāabati innī ra-aytu aḥada ʿashara kawkaban wal-shamsa wal-qamara ra-aytuhum lī sājidīn
verses.english: Recall that Joseph said to his father, "O my father, I saw eleven planets, and the sun, and the moon; I saw them prostrating before me."

1981.english: Recall that Joseph said to his father, "O my father, I saw eleven planets and the sun and the moon, prostrating before me."

1989.english: Joseph said to his father, “O my father, I saw eleven planets, and the sun, and the moon; I saw them prostrating before me.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا ۖ إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين
verses.transliterated: qāla yābunayya lā taqṣuṣ ru'yāka ʿalā ikh'watika fayakīdū laka kaydan inna l-shayṭāna lil'insāni ʿaduwwun mubīnu
verses.english: He said, "My son, do not tell your brothers about your dream, lest they plot and scheme against you. Surely, the devil is man's worst enemy.

1981.english: He said, "O my son, do not mention your dream to your brothers, lest they become jealous of you. Surely, the devil is man's most ardent enemy.

1989.english: He said, “O my son, do not tell your brothers about your dream, lest they plot and scheme against you. Surely, the devil is man’s worst enemy.”

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق ۚ إن ربك عليم حكيم
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika yajtabīka rabbuka wayuʿallimuka min tawīli l-aḥādīthi wayutimmu niʿ'matahu ʿalayka waʿalā āli yaʿqūba kamā atammahā ʿalā abawayka min qablu ib'rāhīma wa-is'ḥāqa inna rabbaka ʿalīmun ḥakīmu
verses.english: "Your Lord has thus blessed you, and has given you good news through your dream. He has perfected His blessings upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He did for your ancestors Abraham and Isaac before that. Your Lord is Omniscient, Most Wise."

1981.english: "Your Lord thus chooses you, and teaches you the correct interpretation of things, and fulfills His favors upon you, and upon the family of Jacob, as He had fulfilled them upon your forefathers Abraham and Isaac. Your Lord is omniscient, wise."

1989.english: Your Lord has thus blessed you (O Joseph), and delivered to you good news through your dream. He has perfected His blessings upon you and the family of Jacob, as He did for your ancestors Abraham and Isaac before that. Your Lord is Omniscient, Most Wise.

verses.arabic: لَّقَدْ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتٌ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين
verses.transliterated: laqad kāna fī yūsufa wa-ikh'watihi āyātun lilssāilīn
verses.english: In Joseph and his brothers there are lessons for the seekers.

1981.english: Surely, in Joseph and his brothers there are lessons for those who seek.

1989.english: In Joseph and his brothers there are for

verses.arabic: إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين
verses.transliterated: idh qālū layūsufu wa-akhūhu aḥabbu ilā abīnā minnā wanaḥnu ʿuṣ'batun inna abānā lafī ḍalālin mubīni
verses.english: They said, "Joseph and his brother are favored by our father, and we are in the majority. Indeed, our father is far astray.

1981.english: They said, "Joseph and his brother are more beloved by our father than we are, and there are more of us. Our father is making a big mistake.

1989.english: They said, “Joseph and his brother are favored by our father, and we are the majority. Indeed, our father is far astray.

verses.arabic: ٱقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ قَوْمًا صَٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين
verses.transliterated: uq'tulū yūsufa awi iṭ'raḥūhu arḍan yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum watakūnū min baʿdihi qawman ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: "Let us kill Joseph, or banish him, that you may get some attention from your father. Afterwards, you can be righteous people."
verses.subtitle: Joseph's Fate Already Decided by God
verses.footnote: We learn from Joseph's dream that he was destined for a bright future. Thus, while his brothers met to decide his fate, his fate was already decided by God. Everything is done by God (8:17), and is already recorded (57:22).

1981.english: "Let us kill Joseph or banish him to gain your father's undivided attention. Later, you can be righteous people."

1989.english: “Let us kill Joseph, or banish him, that you may get some attention from your father. Afterwards, you can be righteous people.”*
1989.subtitle: Joseph’s Fate Already Decided by God
1989.footnote: We learn from Joseph’s dream that he was destined for a bright future. Thus, while his brothers met to decide his fate, his fate was already decided by God. Everything is done by God (8:17), and is already recorded (57:22).

verses.arabic: قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين
verses.transliterated: qāla qāilun min'hum lā taqtulū yūsufa wa-alqūhu fī ghayābati l-jubi yaltaqiṭ'hu baʿḍu l-sayārati in kuntum fāʿilīn
verses.english: One of them said, "Do not kill Joseph; let us throw him into the abyss of the well. Perhaps some caravan can pick him up, if this is what you decide to do."

1981.english: One of them said, "Do not kill Joseph. Instead, throw him in the darkness of the well. Some caravan may pick him up if you do this."

1989.english: One of them said, “Let us not kill Joseph; let us throw him into the abyss of the well. Perhaps some caravan can pick him up, if this is what you decide to do.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَنَٰصِحُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون
verses.transliterated: qālū yāabānā mā laka lā tamannā ʿalā yūsufa wa-innā lahu lanāṣiḥūn
verses.english: They said, "Our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph? We will take good care of him.

1981.english: They said, "O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph? We will take care of him.

1989.english: They said, “Our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph? We can take care of him.

verses.arabic: أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون
verses.transliterated: arsil'hu maʿanā ghadan yartaʿ wayalʿab wa-innā lahu laḥāfiẓūn
verses.english: "Send him with us tomorrow to run and play. We will protect him."

1981.english: "Send him with us tomorrow to run and play. We will protect him."

1989.english: “Send him with us tomorrow to run and play. We will protect him.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَٰفِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون
verses.transliterated: qāla innī layaḥzununī an tadhhabū bihi wa-akhāfu an yakulahu l-dhi'bu wa-antum ʿanhu ghāfilūn
verses.english: He said, "I worry lest you go away with him, then the wolf may devour him while you are not watching him."

1981.english: He said, "It worries me to see you go away with him; I worry that the wolf may eat him while you are not watching him."

1989.english: He said, “I worry lest you take him, then the wolf may devour him while you are not watching him.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون
verses.transliterated: qālū la-in akalahu l-dhi'bu wanaḥnu ʿuṣ'batun innā idhan lakhāsirūn
verses.english: They said, "Indeed, if the wolf devours him, with so many of us around, then we are really losers."

1981.english: They said, "If the wolf eats him while there are so many of us, then we are really losers."

1989.english: They said, “Indeed, if the wolf devoured him, with so many of us around, then we are really losers.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب ۚ وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون
verses.transliterated: falammā dhahabū bihi wa-ajmaʿū an yajʿalūhu fī ghayābati l-jubi wa-awḥaynā ilayhi latunabbi-annahum bi-amrihim hādhā wahum lā yashʿurūn
verses.english: When they went away with him, and unanimously decided to throw him into the abyss of the well, we inspired him: "Some day, you will tell them about all this, while they have no idea."
verses.subtitle: Believers are Blessed with God's Assurances

1981.english: Then, when they took him away, they unanimously agreed to place him in the darkness of the well. Meanwhile, we inspired him that, "You will remind them someday of all this, when they least expect it."
1981.footnote: This is a classic example of the perfect happiness and contentment of God's sincere servants. In this example, Joseph appears to the outsiders to be in deep trouble. But inside, he had received his Lord's assurances that everything will be allright.

1989.english: When they went away with him, and unanimously decided to throw him into the abyss of the well, we assured him: “(Do not worry.) Some day, you will tell them about all this, while they have no idea.”

verses.arabic: وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمْ عِشَآءً يَبْكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون
verses.transliterated: wajāū abāhum ʿishāan yabkūn
verses.english: They came back to their father in the evening, weeping.

1981.english: They came to their father in the evening weeping.

1989.english: They came back to their father in the evening, weeping.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب ۖ وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين
verses.transliterated: qālū yāabānā innā dhahabnā nastabiqu wataraknā yūsufa ʿinda matāʿinā fa-akalahu l-dhi'bu wamā anta bimu'minin lanā walaw kunnā ṣādiqīn
verses.english: They said, "Our father, we went racing with each other, leaving Joseph with our equipment, and the wolf devoured him. You will never believe us, even if we were telling the truth."

1981.english: They said, "Our father, we went racing, leaving Joseph with our things, and the wolf ate him. You will never believe us, even if we are telling the truth."

1989.english: They said, “Our father, we went racing with each other, leaving Joseph with our equipment, and the wolf devoured him. You will never believe us, even if we are telling the truth.”

verses.arabic: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب ۚ قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا ۖ فصبر جميل ۖ والله المستعان على ما تصفون
verses.transliterated: wajāū ʿalā qamīṣihi bidamin kadhibin qaala bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amran faṣabrun jamīlun wal-lahu l-mus'taʿānu ʿalā mā taṣifūn
verses.english: They produced his shirt with fake blood on it. He said, "Indeed, you have conspired with each other to commit a certain scheme. All I can do is resort to a quiet patience. May GOD help me in the face of your conspiracy."

1981.english: They produced his shirt with false blood thereon. He said, "No, it is you who carried out some conspiracy. I can only resort to a quiet patience. God is the only helper against your claims."

1989.english: They produced his shirt with fake blood on it. He said, “Indeed, you have conspired with each other to commit a certain scheme. All I can do is resort to a quiet patience. May GOD help me in the face of your conspiracy.”

verses.arabic: وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُۥ قَالَ يَٰبُشْرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَٰعَةً وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه ۖ قال يا بشرى هذا غلام ۚ وأسروه بضاعة ۚ والله عليم بما يعملون
verses.transliterated: wajāat sayyāratun fa-arsalū wāridahum fa-adlā dalwahu qāla yābush'rā hādhā ghulāmun wa-asarrūhu biḍāʿatan wal-lahu ʿalīmun bimā yaʿmalūn
verses.english: A caravan passed by, and soon sent their waterer. He let down his bucket, then said, "How lucky! There is a boy here!" They took him along as merchandise, and GOD was fully aware of what they did.
verses.subtitle: Joseph is Taken to Egypt

1981.english: When a caravan came, they sent their waterer to the well, and he sent down his bucket. He said, "What a good fortune. This is a boy." They took him as part of their merchandise. God was fully aware of everything they did.

1989.english: A caravan passed by, and soon sent their waterer. He let down his bucket, then said, “How lucky! There is a boy here!” They took him along as merchandise, and GOD was fully aware of what they did.
1989.subtitle: Joseph is Taken to Egypt

verses.arabic: وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍۭ بَخْسٍ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ وَكَانُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين
verses.transliterated: washarawhu bithamanin bakhsin darāhima maʿdūdatin wakānū fīhi mina l-zāhidīn
verses.english: They sold him for a cheap price— a few Dirhams—for they did not have any need for him.

1981.english: They sold him for a cheap price -- a few dirhams. They were eager to get rid of him.

1989.english: They sold him for a cheap price, a few Dirhams; for they did not have any need for him.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لِٱمْرَأَتِهِۦٓ أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُۥ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا ۚ وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث ۚ والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: waqāla alladhī ish'tarāhu min miṣ'ra li-im'ra-atihi akrimī mathwāhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fī l-arḍi walinuʿallimahu min tawīli l-aḥādīthi wal-lahu ghālibun ʿalā amrihi walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: The one who bought him in Egypt said to his wife, "Take good care of him. Maybe he can help us, or maybe we can adopt him." We thus established Joseph on earth, and we taught him the interpretation of dreams. GOD's command is always done, but most people do not know.

1981.english: The one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Take good care of him. Perhaps he may help us, or we may adopt him." We thus provided Joseph with a home in the new land, and we taught him the interpretation of dreams. God's commands are always carried out, but most people do not know.

1989.english: The one who bought him in Egypt said to his wife, “Take good care of him. Maybe he can help us, or maybe we can adopt him.” We thus established Joseph on earth; and we taught him the interpretation of dreams. GOD’s command is always done, but most people do not know.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما ۚ وكذلك نجزي المحسنين
verses.transliterated: walammā balagha ashuddahu ātaynāhu ḥuk'man waʿil'man wakadhālika najzī l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: When he reached maturity, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the righteous.

1981.english: When he grew up, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the righteous.

1989.english: When he reached maturity, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the righteous.

verses.arabic: وَرَٰوَدَتْهُ ٱلَّتِى هُوَ فِى بَيْتِهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلْأَبْوَٰبَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ رَبِّىٓ أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَاىَ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك ۚ قال معاذ الله ۖ إنه ربي أحسن مثواي ۖ إنه لا يفلح الظالمون
verses.transliterated: warāwadathu allatī huwa fī baytihā ʿan nafsihi waghallaqati l-abwāba waqālat hayta laka qāla maʿādha l-lahi innahu rabbī aḥsana mathwāya innahu lā yuf'liḥu l-ẓālimūn
verses.english: The lady of the house where he lived tried to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "I am all yours." He said, "May GOD protect me. He is my Lord, who gave me a good home. The transgressors never succeed."
verses.subtitle: God Protects the Believers From Sin
verses.footnote: Joseph worded this statement in such a way that the governor's wife thought that he was talking about her husband, when in fact he was talking about God.

1981.english: The lady of the house tried to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "I am all yours." He said, "God forbid. He is my Lord who took good care of me.* Surely, the wicked never succeed."
1981.footnote: Note the incredibly clever answer that bears a double meaning. To the lady, it sounded as if Joseph was talking about her husband. But Joseph was talking about God. This is one example of the Quran's superb and extraordinary literary style.

1989.english: The lady of the house where he lived tried to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, “I am all yours.” He said, “May GOD protect me. He is my Lord, who gave me a good home.* The transgressors never succeed.”
1989.subtitle: God Protects the Believers From Sin
1989.footnote: Joseph worded this statement in such a way that the governor’s wife thought that he was talking about her husband, when in fact he was talking about God.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِۦ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرْهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد همت به ۖ وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه ۚ كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء ۚ إنه من عبادنا المخلصين
verses.transliterated: walaqad hammat bihi wahamma bihā lawlā an raā bur'hāna rabbihi kadhālika linaṣrifa ʿanhu l-sūa wal-faḥshāa innahu min ʿibādinā l-mukh'laṣīn
verses.english: She almost succumbed to him, and he almost succumbed to her, if it were not that he saw a proof from his Lord. We thus diverted evil and sin away from him, for he was one of our devoted servants.

1981.english: She almost succumbed to him, and he almost succumbed to her, if it were not that he saw a sign from his Lord. We thus diverted from him evil and vice. For he was one of our devoted servants.

1989.english: She almost succumbed to him, and he too almost succumbed to her, if it were not that he saw a sign from his Lord. We thus diverted evil and sin away from him, for he was one of our devoted servants.

verses.arabic: وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُۥ مِن دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلْبَابِ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب ۚ قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم
verses.transliterated: wa-is'tabaqā l-bāba waqaddat qamīṣahu min duburin wa-alfayā sayyidahā ladā l-bābi qālat mā jazāu man arāda bi-ahlika sūan illā an yus'jana aw ʿadhābun alīmu
verses.english: The two of them raced towards the door, and, in the process, she tore his garment from the back. They found her husband at the door. She said, "What should be the punishment for one who wanted to molest your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?"

1981.english: As they raced towards the door, she grabbed and tore his shirt from behind; and they found her husband by the door. She said, "What is the punishment for one who wanted to hurt your family, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?"

1989.english: The two of them raced towards the door, and, in the process, she tore his garment from the back. They found her husband at the door. She said, “What should be the punishment for one who wanted to molest your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي ۚ وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين
verses.transliterated: qāla hiya rāwadatnī ʿan nafsī washahida shāhidun min ahlihā in kāna qamīṣuhu qudda min qubulin faṣadaqat wahuwa mina l-kādhibīn
verses.english: He said, "She is the one who tried to seduce me." A witness from her family suggested: "If his garment is torn from the front, then she is telling the truth and he is a liar.

1981.english: He said, "She is the one who tried to seduce me." A witness testified from her family saying, "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is a liar."

1989.english: He said, “She is the one who tried to seduce me.” A witness from her family suggested: “If his garment is torn from the front, then she is telling the truth and he is a liar.

verses.arabic: وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين
verses.transliterated: wa-in kāna qamīṣuhu qudda min duburin fakadhabat wahuwa mina l-ṣādiqīn
verses.english: "And if his garment is torn from the back, then she lied, and he is telling the truth."

1981.english: "And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is truthful."

1989.english: “And if his garment is torn from the back, then she lied, and he is telling the truth.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَءَا قَمِيصَهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ مِن كَيْدِكُنَّ إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن ۖ إن كيدكن عظيم
verses.transliterated: falammā raā qamīṣahu qudda min duburin qāla innahu min kaydikunna inna kaydakunna ʿaẓīmu
verses.english: When her husband saw that his garment was torn from the back, he said, "This is a woman's scheme. Indeed, your scheming is formidable.

1981.english: Thus, when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said to her, "This is deceit on your part, and the women's deceit is mighty indeed.

1989.english: When her husband saw that his garment was torn from the back, he said, “This is women’s scheming. Indeed, your scheming is formidable.

verses.arabic: يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَا وَٱسْتَغْفِرِى لِذَنۢبِكِ إِنَّكِ كُنتِ مِنَ ٱلْخَاطِـِٔينَ
verses.arabicClean: يوسف أعرض عن هذا ۚ واستغفري لذنبك ۖ إنك كنت من الخاطئين
verses.transliterated: yūsufu aʿriḍ ʿan hādhā wa-is'taghfirī lidhanbiki innaki kunti mina l-khāṭiīn
verses.english: "Joseph, disregard this incident. As for you (my wife), you should seek forgiveness for your sin. You have committed an error."

1981.english: "As for you Joseph, you can forget the whole thing. And you, my wife, shall ask forgiveness for your sin. You are certainly wrong."

1989.english: “O Joseph, disregard this incident. As for you {my wife), you should seek forgiveness for your sin. You have committed an error.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ تُرَٰوِدُ فَتَىٰهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰهَا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه ۖ قد شغفها حبا ۖ إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين
verses.transliterated: waqāla nis'watun fī l-madīnati im'ra-atu l-ʿazīzi turāwidu fatāhā ʿan nafsihi qad shaghafahā ḥubban innā lanarāhā fī ḍalālin mubīni
verses.english: Some women in the city gossiped: "The governor's wife is trying to seduce her servant. She is deeply in love with him. We see that she has gone astray."

1981.english: Some women in the city gossiped, "The governor's wife is trying to seduce her servant. She is madly in love with him. What she is doing is really gross."

1989.english: Some women in the city gossiped: “The governor’s wife is trying to seduce her servant,” they said, “she is deeply in love with him. We see that she is far astray.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـًٔا وَءَاتَتْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةٍ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وَقَالَتِ ٱخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُۥٓ أَكْبَرْنَهُۥ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن ۖ فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم
verses.transliterated: falammā samiʿat bimakrihinna arsalat ilayhinna wa-aʿtadat lahunna muttaka-an waātat kulla wāḥidatin min'hunna sikkīnan waqālati ukh'ruj ʿalayhinna falammā ra-aynahu akbarnahu waqaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunna waqul'na ḥāsha lillahi mā hādhā basharan in hādhā illā malakun karīmu
verses.english: When she heard of their gossip, she invited them, prepared for them a comfortable place, and gave each of them a knife. She then said to him, "Enter their room." When they saw him, they so admired him, that they cut their hands. They said, "Glory be to GOD, this is not a human being; this is an honorable angel."
verses.footnote: This is the same word used in 5:38 regarding the hand of the thief, and the sum of sura and verse numbers (12+31 and 5+38) are the same. Therefore, the thief 's hand should be marked, not severed as practiced by the corrupted Islam (see Footnote 5:38).

1981.english: When she heard of their gossip, she sent for them and prepared a feast. After she gave each one of them a knife, she said to him, "Go out to them." When they saw him, they so admired him that they cut their hands and said, "By God, this is not a human being; he is a handsome angel."

1989.english: When she heard of their gossip, she invited them, prepared for them a comfortable place, gave each of them a knife, then said to him, “Enter their room.” When they saw him, they so admired him, that they cut their hands. They said, “GOD forbid, this is not a human; this is an honorable angel.”

verses.arabic: قَالَتْ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِى لُمْتُنَّنِى فِيهِ وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ فَٱسْتَعْصَمَ وَلَئِن لَّمْ يَفْعَلْ مَآ ءَامُرُهُۥ لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونًا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ۖ ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ۖ ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين
verses.transliterated: qālat fadhālikunna alladhī lum'tunnanī fīhi walaqad rāwadttuhu ʿan nafsihi fa-is'taʿṣama wala-in lam yafʿal mā āmuruhu layus'jananna walayakūnan mina l-ṣāghirīn
verses.english: She said, "This is the one you blamed me for falling in love with. I did indeed try to seduce him, and he refused. Unless he does what I command him to do, he will surely go to prison, and will be debased."

1981.english: She said, "This is the one about whom you blame me, and I did try to seduce him, but he refused. Unless he does what I command him to do, he will be imprisoned and debased."

1989.english: She said, “This is the one you blamed me for falling in love with. I did indeed try to seduce him, and he refused. Furthermore, unless he does what I command him to do, he will surely go to prison, and will be debased.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَيْهِ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّى كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه ۖ وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi l-sij'nu aḥabbu ilayya mimmā yadʿūnanī ilayhi wa-illā taṣrif ʿannī kaydahunna aṣbu ilayhinna wa-akun mina l-jāhilīn
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, the prison is better than giving in to them. Unless You divert their scheming from me, I may desire them and behave like the ignorant ones."

1981.english: He said, "My Lord, the prison is better for me than what they invite me to do. Unless you divert their evil from me, I may desire them and behave like the ignorant."

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, the prison is better than (disobeying You and) giving in to them. Unless You protect me from their schemes, I may desire them and be like the ignorant ones.”

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن ۚ إنه هو السميع العليم
verses.transliterated: fa-is'tajāba lahu rabbuhu faṣarafa ʿanhu kaydahunna innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīm
verses.english: His Lord answered his prayer and diverted their scheming from him. He is the Hearer, the Omniscient.

1981.english: His Lord answered his prayer and diverted their evil from him. He is the hearer, the omniscient.

1989.english: His Lord answered his prayer and protected him from their schemes. He is the Hearer, the Omniscient.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين
verses.transliterated: thumma badā lahum min baʿdi mā ra-awū l-āyāti layasjununnahu ḥattā ḥīni
verses.english: Later, they saw to it, despite the clear proofs, that they should imprison him for awhile.

1981.english: They later decided, in spite of all the signs, to imprison him for awhile.

1989.english: Later, they saw to it, despite the clear proof (of his innocence), that they should put him in prison for awhile.

verses.arabic: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ ٱلْءَاخَرُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِى خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦٓ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ودخل معه السجن فتيان ۖ قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا ۖ وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه ۖ نبئنا بتأويله ۖ إنا نراك من المحسنين
verses.transliterated: wadakhala maʿahu l-sij'na fatayāni qāla aḥaduhumā innī arānī aʿṣiru khamran waqāla l-ākharu innī arānī aḥmilu fawqa rasī khub'zan takulu l-ṭayru min'hu nabbi'nā bitawīlihi innā narāka mina l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: Two young men were in the prison with him. One of them said, "I saw (in my dream) that I was making wine," and the other said, "I saw myself carrying bread on my head, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of the interpretation of these dreams. We see that you are righteous."

1981.english: Two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, "I saw myself in a dream pressing wine." The other one said, "I saw myself carrying bread on my head, from which the birds were eating. Tell us the interpretation of these dreams. We see that you are a righteous person."

1989.english: Two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, “I saw (in my dream) that I was making wine,” and the other said, “I saw myself carrying bread on my head, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of the interpretation of these dreams. We see that you are righteous.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِۦٓ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتِيَكُمَا ذَٰلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِى رَبِّىٓ إِنِّى تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَهُم بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ۚ ذلكما مما علمني ربي ۚ إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون
verses.transliterated: qāla lā yatīkumā ṭaʿāmun tur'zaqānihi illā nabbatukumā bitawīlihi qabla an yatiyakumā dhālikumā mimmā ʿallamanī rabbī innī taraktu millata qawmin lā yu'minūna bil-lahi wahum bil-ākhirati hum kāfirūn
verses.english: He said, "If any food is provided to you, I can inform you about it before you receive it. This is some of the knowledge bestowed upon me by my Lord. I have forsaken the religion of people who do not believe in GOD, and with regard to the Hereafter, they are really disbelievers.

1981.english: He said, "I have been telling you of every food that came to you as provision, even before it came to you. This is what my Lord has taught me, for I have forsaken the religion of people who disbelieve in God and the hereafter.

1989.english: He said, “I can inform you of any food provision you may receive, even before you receive it. This is some of the knowledge bestowed upon me by my Lord, for I have forsaken the religion of people who do not believe in GOD, and with regard to the Hereafter, they are really disbelievers.

verses.arabic: وَٱتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَآءِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نُّشْرِكَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ ذَٰلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ۚ ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ۚ ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون
verses.transliterated: wa-ittabaʿtu millata ābāī ib'rāhīma wa-is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba mā kāna lanā an nush'rika bil-lahi min shayin dhālika min faḍli l-lahi ʿalaynā waʿalā l-nāsi walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yashkurūn
verses.english: "And I followed instead the religion of my ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. We never set up any idols beside GOD. Such is the blessing from GOD upon us and upon the people, but most people are unappreciative.

1981.english: "I follow the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. We never worship anything besides God. This is but grace from God upon us, and upon the people, but most people are not appreciative.

1989.english: “And I followed instead the religion of my ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. We never set up any idols besides GOD. Such is the blessing from GOD upon us and upon the people, but most people are unappreciative.

verses.arabic: يَٰصَىٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ
verses.arabicClean: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار
verses.transliterated: yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni a-arbābun mutafarriqūna khayrun ami l-lahu l-wāḥidu l-qahār
verses.english: "O my prison mates, are several gods better, or GOD alone, the One, the Supreme?

1981.english: "O my prison companions, is it better to have several idols, or one God, the most powerful?

1989.english: “O my prison mates, is it better to worship several gods, or GOD alone, the One, the Supreme?”

verses.arabic: مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَٰنٍ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان ۚ إن الحكم إلا لله ۚ أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ۚ ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: mā taʿbudūna min dūnihi illā asmāan sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi amara allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu dhālika l-dīnu l-qayimu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: "You do not worship beside Him except innovations that you have made up, you and your parents. GOD has never authorized such idols. All ruling belongs to GOD, and He has ruled that you shall not worship except Him. This is the perfect religion, but most people do not know.

1981.english: "You only idolize besides Him idols that you make up, you and your parents. God never places any power in them. Kingship belongs to God. He commanded that you shall not worship except Him. This is the perfect religion, but most people do not know.
1981.subtitle: You Shall Not Worship Except God
1981.footnote: See footnote 11:2.

1989.english: You do not worship besides Him except innovations that you have made up, you and your parents. GOD has never placed any power in such idols. All ruling belongs to GOD, and He has ruled that you shall not worship except Him. This is the perfect religion, but most people do not know.

verses.arabic: يَٰصَىٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا ٱلْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِن رَّأْسِهِۦ قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ
verses.arabicClean: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا ۖ وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه ۚ قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان
verses.transliterated: yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni ammā aḥadukumā fayasqī rabbahu khamran wa-ammā l-ākharu fayuṣ'labu fatakulu l-ṭayru min rasihi quḍiya l-amru alladhī fīhi tastaftiyān
verses.english: "O my prison mates, one of you will be the wine butler for his lord, while the other will be crucified— the birds will eat from his head. This settles the matter about which you have inquired."

1981.english: "O my prison companions, one of you will be the king's wine butler. As for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. This is the opinion concerning your inquiry."

1989.english: “O my prison mates, one of you will be the wine butler for his lord, while the other will be crucified—the birds will eat from his head. This finishes the matter about which you inquired.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين
verses.transliterated: waqāla lilladhī ẓanna annahu nājin min'humā udh'kur'nī ʿinda rabbika fa-ansāhu l-shayṭānu dhik'ra rabbihi falabitha fī l-sij'ni biḍ'ʿa sinīn
verses.english: He then said to the one to be saved "Remember me at your lord." Thus, the devil caused him to forget his Lord, and, consequently, he remained in prison a few more years.
verses.footnote: When Joseph begged his companion to intercede with the king on his behalf, he exhibited dependence on other than God to be saved from the prison. This does not befit a true believer, and such a serious slip cost Joseph a few years in the prison. We learn from the Quran that only God can relieve any hardship that might befall us. A true believer trusts in God and depends totally on Him alone (1:5, 6:17, 8:17, 10:107).
