1981.english: He then said to the one to be saved, "Remember me at your lord." But the devil made him forget to remember him at his lord, and Joseph remained in prison a few more years.

1989.english: He then said to the one to be saved “Remember me at your lord.”* Thus, the devil caused him to forget his Lord, and, consequently, he remained in prison a few more years.
1989.footnote: When Joseph begged his companion to intercede with the king on his behalf, he exhibited dependence on other than God to be saved from the prison. This does not befit a true believer, and such a serious slip cost Joseph a few more years in the prison. We learn from the Quran that only God can relieve any hardship that might befall us. A true believer trusts in God and depends totally on Him alone (1:5, 6:17, 8:17, 10:107).

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات ۖ يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون
verses.transliterated: waqāla l-maliku innī arā sabʿa baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿa sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin yāayyuhā l-mala-u aftūnī fī ru'yāya in kuntum lilrru'yā taʿburūn
verses.english: The king said, "I saw seven fat cows being devoured by seven skinny cows, and seven green spikes (of wheat), and others shriveled. O my elders, advise me regarding my dream, if you know how to interpret the dreams."
verses.subtitle: The King's Dream

1981.english: The king said, "I saw seven fat cows being devoured by seven skinny cows; and seven green spikes of wheat, and seven dry spikes. O you elders, explain my dream to me if you can interpret the dreams."
1981.subtitle: The King's Dream

1989.english: The king said, “I saw seven fat cows being devoured by seven skinny cows, and seven green spikes (of wheat), and others dry. O my elders, explain this dream to me, if you know how to explain the dreams.”
1989.subtitle: The King’s Dream

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحْلَٰمِ بِعَٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا أضغاث أحلام ۖ وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين
verses.transliterated: qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin wamā naḥnu bitawīli l-aḥlāmi biʿālimīn
verses.english: They said, "Nonsense dreams. When it comes to the interpretation of dreams, we are not knowledgeable."

1981.english: They said, "This is probably a nonsense dream. We know nothing about the interpretation of dreams."

1989.english: They said, “Nonsense dreams. When it comes to the explanation of dreams, we are not knowledgeable.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۠ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرْسِلُونِ
verses.arabicClean: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون
verses.transliterated: waqāla alladhī najā min'humā wa-iddakara baʿda ummatin anā unabbi-ukum bitawīlihi fa-arsilūn
verses.english: The one who was saved (from the prison) said, now that he finally remembered, "I can tell you its interpretation, so send me (to Joseph)."

1981.english: Then the one who had been saved remembered after such a long time and said, "I can tell you the interpretation thereof if you send me."

1989.english: The one who was saved (from the prison) said, now that he finally remembered, “I can tell you the explanation thereof, if you send me (to Joseph)”

verses.arabic: يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون
verses.transliterated: yūsufu ayyuhā l-ṣidīqu aftinā fī sabʿi baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿi sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin laʿallī arjiʿu ilā l-nāsi laʿallahum yaʿlamūn
verses.english: "Joseph my friend, inform us about seven fat cows being devoured by seven skinny cows, and seven green spikes, and others shriveled. I wish to go back with some information for the people."
verses.subtitle: Joseph Interprets the King's Dream

1981.english: "Joseph, my friend, explain to us seven fat cows being devoured by seven skinny ones; and seven green spikes of wheat and seven dry spikes, that I may return to the people, and let them know."

1989.english: “Joseph my friend, inform us about seven fat cows being devoured by seven skinny cows, and seven green spikes, and others dry. I wish to go back with some information for the people.”
1989.subtitle: Joseph Interprets the King’s Dream

verses.arabic: قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون
verses.transliterated: qāla tazraʿūna sabʿa sinīna da-aban famā ḥaṣadttum fadharūhu fī sunbulihi illā qalīlan mimmā takulūn
verses.english: He said, "What you cultivate during the next seven years, when the time of harvest comes, leave the grains in their spikes, except for what you eat.

1981.english: He said, "You will produce good crops for seven consecutive years. When you harvest, you should store them in their spikes, except for a minimum that you eat.

1989.english: He said, “What you cultivate during seven years, you shall store in their spikes, with the exception of what you eat.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون
verses.transliterated: thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika sabʿun shidādun yakul'na mā qaddamtum lahunna illā qalīlan mimmā tuḥ'ṣinūn
verses.english: "After that, seven years of drought will come, which will consume most of what you stored for them.

1981.english: "Then seven bad years will follow, and will exhaust what you had advanced for them, except for a little that may be left.

1989.english: “After that, seven years of drought will come, which will consume most of what you stored for them.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون
verses.transliterated: thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika ʿāmun fīhi yughāthu l-nāsu wafīhi yaʿṣirūn
verses.english: "After that, a year will come that brings relief for the people, and they will, once again, press juice."

1981.english: "After that, a year will come in which the people will prosper, and will again press (wine and oil)."

1989.english: “After that, a year will come that brings relief for the people; they will, once again, press juice.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسْـَٔلْهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسْوَةِ ٱلَّٰتِى قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّى بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وقال الملك ائتوني به ۖ فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن ۚ إن ربي بكيدهن عليم
verses.transliterated: waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi falammā jāahu l-rasūlu qāla ir'jiʿ ilā rabbika fasalhu mā bālu l-nis'wati allātī qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunna inna rabbī bikaydihinna ʿalīmu
verses.english: The king said, "Bring him to me." When the messenger came to him, he said, "Go back to your lord and ask him to investigate the women who cut their hands. My Lord is fully aware of their schemes."

1981.english: The king said, "Bring him to me." When the messenger went to him, Joseph said, "Go back to your lord and ask him about the women who cut their hands. My Lord is fully aware of their schemes."

1989.english: The king said, “Bring him to me.” When the messenger came to him, he said, “Go back to your lord and ask him to investigate the women who cut their hands. My Lord is fully aware of their schemes.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَٰوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ قُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوٓءٍ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْـَٰٔنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَا۠ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه ۚ قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء ۚ قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين
verses.transliterated: qāla mā khaṭbukunna idh rāwadttunna yūsufa ʿan nafsihi qul'na ḥāsha lillahi mā ʿalim'nā ʿalayhi min sūin qālati im'ra-atu l-ʿazīzi l-āna ḥaṣḥaṣa l-ḥaqu anā rāwadttuhu ʿan nafsihi wa-innahu lamina l-ṣādiqīn
verses.english: (The king) said (to the women), "What do you know about the incident when you tried to seduce Joseph?" They said, "GOD forbid; we did not know of anything evil committed by him." The wife of the governor said, "Now the truth has prevailed. I am the one who tried to seduce him, and he was the truthful one.

1981.english: The king said, "What happened when you tried to seduce Joseph?" They said, "God forbid, we have not known of anything bad about him." The governor's wife said, "Now the truth is manifest. I am the one who tried to seduce him. He told the truth.

1989.english: (The king) said (to the women), “What was wrong with you, when you tried to seduce Joseph?” They said, “GOD forbid; we did not know of anything bad about him.” The wife of the governor said, “Now the truth has prevailed. I am the one who tried to seduce him. He was the truthful one.

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى كَيْدَ ٱلْخَآئِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين
verses.transliterated: dhālika liyaʿlama annī lam akhun'hu bil-ghaybi wa-anna l-laha lā yahdī kayda l-khāinīn
verses.english: "I hope that he will realize that I never betrayed him in his absence, for GOD does not bless the schemes of the betrayers.

1981.english: "Now he should know that I did not betray him in his absence. God does not bless the schemes of the betrayers."

1989.english: “I hope he realizes that I never betrayed him in his absence, for GOD does not bless the schemes of the betrayers.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وما أبرئ نفسي ۚ إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي ۚ إن ربي غفور رحيم
verses.transliterated: wamā ubarri-u nafsī inna l-nafsa la-ammāratun bil-sūi illā mā raḥima rabbī inna rabbī ghafūrun raḥīmu
verses.english: "I do not claim innocence for myself. The self is an advocate of vice, except for those who have attained mercy from my Lord. My Lord is Forgiver, Most Merciful."

1981.english: "I claim no innocence for myself. Surely, the self advocates evil, except for those blessed by my Lord. My Lord is forgiver, merciful."

1989.english: “I do not claim innocence for myself. The self is an advocate of vice. I only hope for my Lord’s mercy; my Lord is Forgiver, Most Merciful.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦٓ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِى فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُۥ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي ۖ فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين
verses.transliterated: waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi astakhliṣ'hu linafsī falammā kallamahu qāla innaka l-yawma ladaynā makīnun amīnu
verses.english: The king said, "Bring him to me, so I can hire him to work for me." When he talked with him, he said, "Today, you have a prominent position with us."
verses.subtitle: Joseph Attains Prominence

1981.english: The king said, "Bring him to me, to have him work for me." When he talked to him he said, "As of now, you are our trusted confidant."

1989.english: The king said, “Bring him to me, so I can hire him to work for me.” When he talked with him, he said, “Today, you have a prominent position with us.”
1989.subtitle: Joseph Attains Prominence

verses.arabic: قَالَ ٱجْعَلْنِى عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلْأَرْضِ إِنِّى حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض ۖ إني حفيظ عليم
verses.transliterated: qāla ij'ʿalnī ʿalā khazāini l-arḍi innī ḥafīẓun ʿalīmu
verses.english: He said, "Make me the treasurer, for I am experienced in this area and knowledgeable."

1981.english: He said, "Put me in charge of the treasury. I am an experienced treasurer."

1989.english: He said, “Make me the treasurer; I am experienced and knowledgeable.”

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَآءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء ۚ نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ۖ ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fī l-arḍi yatabawwa-u min'hā ḥaythu yashāu nuṣību biraḥmatinā man nashāu walā nuḍīʿu ajra l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: We thus established Joseph on earth, ruling as he wished. We shower our mercy upon whomever we will, and we never fail to recompense the righteous.

1981.english: We thus established Joseph in the land, ruling therein as he pleases. We endow with our mercy whomever we will, and we never neglect to reward the righteous.

1989.english: We thus established Joseph on earth, ruling as he wished. We shower our mercy upon whomever we will, and we never fail to reward the righteous (in this life).

verses.arabic: وَلَأَجْرُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ يَتَّقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون
verses.transliterated: wala-ajru l-ākhirati khayrun lilladhīna āmanū wakānū yattaqūn
verses.english: Additionally, the reward in the Hereafter is even better for those who believe and lead a righteous life.

1981.english: The reward of the hereafter is even better for those who believe and maintain righteousness.

1989.english: And the reward in the Hereafter is even better for those who believed and led a righteous life.

verses.arabic: وَجَآءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون
verses.transliterated: wajāa ikh'watu yūsufa fadakhalū ʿalayhi faʿarafahum wahum lahu munkirūn
verses.english: Joseph's brothers came; when they entered, he recognized them, while they did not recognize him.

1981.english: Joseph's brothers came to obtain grain. When they entered, Joseph recognized them, while they did not recognize him.

1989.english: Joseph’s brothers came to obtain grain. When they entered, he recognized them, while they did not recognize him.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ٱئْتُونِى بِأَخٍ لَّكُم مِّنْ أَبِيكُمْ أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّىٓ أُوفِى ٱلْكَيْلَ وَأَنَا۠ خَيْرُ ٱلْمُنزِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ۚ ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين
verses.transliterated: walammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim qāla i'tūnī bi-akhin lakum min abīkum alā tarawna annī ūfī l-kayla wa-anā khayru l-munzilīn
verses.english: After he provided them with their provisions, he said, "Next time, bring with you your half-brother. Do you not see that I give full measure, and treat you generously?

1981.english: After he provided them with their provisions he said, "Next time bring your step brother with you. Do you not see that I give you generous measures, and I am being a charitable host?

1989.english: And when he provided them with their provisions, he said, “Bring that brother of yours, your half-brother. Do you not see that I give a good measure, and treat you generously?

verses.arabic: فَإِن لَّمْ تَأْتُونِى بِهِۦ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِندِى وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ
verses.arabicClean: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون
verses.transliterated: fa-in lam tatūnī bihi falā kayla lakum ʿindī walā taqrabūn
verses.english: "If you fail to bring him to me, you will get no share from me; you will not even come close."

1981.english: "If you do not bring him next time, you will get no grain, nor will you even come close."

1989.english: “If you fail to bring him with you, you will get nothing from me; you will not even come close.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ سَنُرَٰوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَٰعِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون
verses.transliterated: qālū sanurāwidu ʿanhu abāhu wa-innā lafāʿilūn
verses.english: They said, "We will negotiate with his father about him. We will surely do this."

1981.english: They said, "We will try to induce his father to part with him. We will surely do this."

1989.english: They said, “We will negotiate with his father about him. We will surely do this.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَٰنِهِ ٱجْعَلُوا۟ بِضَٰعَتَهُمْ فِى رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون
verses.transliterated: waqāla lifit'yānihi ij'ʿalū biḍāʿatahum fī riḥālihim laʿallahum yaʿrifūnahā idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihim laʿallahum yarjiʿūn
verses.english: He then instructed his assistants: "Put their goods back in their bags. When they find them upon their return to their family, they may come back sooner."

1981.english: Joseph said to his assistants, "Put their goods back in their bags. When they find them upon arrival to their home, this will encourage them to come back."

1989.english: He then instructed his assistants: “Put their goods back in their bags, so that they find them when they return to their family; perhaps they come back soon.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا ٱلْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون
verses.transliterated: falammā rajaʿū ilā abīhim qālū yāabānā muniʿa minnā l-kaylu fa-arsil maʿanā akhānā naktal wa-innā lahu laḥāfiẓūn
verses.english: When they returned to their father, they said, "Our father, we can no longer get any provisions, unless you send our brother with us. We will take good care of him."

1981.english: When they returned to their father they said, "O our father, we are prevented from future shares, unless you send with us our brother. We will take care of him."

1989.english: When they returned to their father, they said, “Our father, we can no longer get any provisions, unless you send our brother with us. We will take good care of him.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ هَلْ ءَامَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَٰفِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل ۖ فالله خير حافظا ۖ وهو أرحم الراحمين
verses.transliterated: qāla hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā kamā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qablu fal-lahu khayrun ḥāfiẓan wahuwa arḥamu l-rāḥimīn
verses.english: He said, "Shall I trust you with him, as I trusted you with his brother before that? GOD is the best Protector, and, of all the merciful ones, He is the Most Merciful."

1981.english: He said, "Shall I trust him to you any more than I trusted his brother previously? God is the best protector; He is the most merciful."

1989.english: He said, “Shall I trust you with him, as I trusted you with his brother before that? GOD is the best Protector, and, of all the merciful ones, He is the Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا۟ مَتَٰعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا۟ بِضَٰعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِى هَٰذِهِۦ بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذَٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم ۖ قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي ۖ هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ۖ ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ۖ ذلك كيل يسير
verses.transliterated: walammā fataḥū matāʿahum wajadū biḍāʿatahum ruddat ilayhim qālū yāabānā mā nabghī hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā wanamīru ahlanā wanaḥfaẓu akhānā wanazdādu kayla baʿīrin dhālika kaylun yasīru
verses.english: When they opened their bags, they found their goods returned to them. They said, "Our father, what more can we ask for? Here are our goods returned to us. We can thus provide for our family, protect our brother, and receive one more camel-load. This is certainly a profitable deal."

1981.english: When they opened their bags, they found their goods returned to them. They said, "O our father, what more can we wish for? Here are our goods returned to us. We will thus provide for our family, and protect our brother. We can get one more camel load on account of our brother. This will be an easy share to get."

1989.english: When they opened their bags, they found their goods returned to them. They said, “Our father, what more can we ask for? Here are our goods returned to us. We can easily provide for our family, protect our brother, and receive one more camel-load. This is certainly a profitable deal.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُۥ مَعَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِى بِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم ۖ فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل
verses.transliterated: qāla lan ur'silahu maʿakum ḥattā tu'tūni mawthiqan mina l-lahi latatunnanī bihi illā an yuḥāṭa bikum falammā ātawhu mawthiqahum qāla l-lahu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīlu
verses.english: He said, "I will not send him with you, unless you give me a solemn pledge before GOD that you will bring him back, unless you are utterly overwhelmed." When they gave him their solemn pledge, he said, "GOD is witnessing everything we say."

1981.english: He said, "I will not send him with you unless you give me a solemn pledge before God that you will bring him back to me, unless you are completely overwhelmed." When they gave him their pledge, he said, "God is witness to what we say."

1989.english: He said, “I will not send him with you, unless you give me a solemn pledge before GOD that you will bring him back, unless you are overwhelmed.” When they gave him their solemn pledge, he said, “GOD is witnessing everything we say.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ يَٰبَنِىَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ مِنۢ بَابٍ وَٰحِدٍ وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبٍ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍ وَمَآ أُغْنِى عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة ۖ وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء ۖ إن الحكم إلا لله ۖ عليه توكلت ۖ وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون
verses.transliterated: waqāla yābaniyya lā tadkhulū min bābin wāḥidin wa-ud'khulū min abwābin mutafarriqatin wamā ugh'nī ʿankum mina l-lahi min shayin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi ʿalayhi tawakkaltu waʿalayhi falyatawakkali l-mutawakilūn
verses.english: And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one door; enter through separate doors. However, I cannot save you from anything that is predetermined by GOD. To GOD belongs all judgments. I trust in Him, and in Him shall all the trusters put their trust."

1981.english: He said, "O my sons, do not enter from one door; you shall always enter from separate doors. However, I cannot avail you at all against God's will."
1981.footnote: A myth that still dominates the Middle East is known as "the evil eye." Jacob was afraid that if his eleven sons entered from one door, they may be stricken by the "evil eye." According to this legend, the "evil eye" can kill its victim. Tourists who visit certain areas of the Middle East may be aware of the natives' wariness of people who admire or praise their children and/or properties.

1989.english: And he said, “O my sons, do not enter from one door; you shall enter from separate doors. However, I cannot save you from anything that is predetermined by GOD. To GOD belongs all judgments. I trust in Him, and in Him shall all the trusters put their trust.”

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِى عَنْهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِى نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَا وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِّمَا عَلَّمْنَٰهُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها ۚ وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: walammā dakhalū min ḥaythu amarahum abūhum mā kāna yugh'nī ʿanhum mina l-lahi min shayin illā ḥājatan fī nafsi yaʿqūba qaḍāhā wa-innahu ladhū ʿil'min limā ʿallamnāhu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: When they went (to Joseph), they entered in accordance with their father's instructions. Although this could not change anything decreed by GOD, Jacob had a private reason for asking them to do this. For he possessed certain knowledge that we taught him, but most people do not know.
verses.subtitle: Jacob Senses Joseph

1981.english: They entered as their father had instructed them, though this could not avail them at all against God's will. But it was a personal wish that Jacob had expressed. He possessed certain knowledge from us, but most people do not know.

1989.english: When they went {to Joseph), they entered in accordance with their father’s instructions. Although this could not change anything decreed by GOD, Jacob had a private reason for asking them to do this. For he possessed certain knowledge that we taught him, but most people do not know.
1989.subtitle: Jacob Senses Joseph

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه ۖ قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون
verses.transliterated: walammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi akhāhu qāla innī anā akhūka falā tabta-is bimā kānū yaʿmalūn
verses.english: When they entered Joseph's place, he brought his brother closer to him and said, "I am your brother; do not be saddened by their actions."
verses.subtitle: Back in Egypt

1981.english: When they entered to Joseph, he confided to his brother, saying, "I am your brother, so do not be saddened by their actions."

1989.english: When they entered Joseph’s place, he brought his brother closer to him and said, “I am your brother; do not be saddened by their actions.”
1989.subtitle: Back in Egypt

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِى رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَٰرِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون
verses.transliterated: falammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim jaʿala l-siqāyata fī raḥli akhīhi thumma adhana mu-adhinun ayyatuhā l-ʿīru innakum lasāriqūn
verses.english: When he provided them with their provisions, he placed the drinking cup in his brother's bag, then an announcer announced: "The owners of this caravan are thieves."
verses.subtitle: Joseph Keeps His Brother

1981.english: When he supplied them with their grains, he slipped the cup into his brother's bag. Then an announcer announced that "You, the people of this caravan, are thieves."

1989.english: When he provided them with their provisions, he placed the cup in his brother’s bag, then an announcer announced: “This caravan belongs to thieves.”
1989.subtitle: Joseph Keeps His Brother

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ وَأَقْبَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِم مَّاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون
verses.transliterated: qālū wa-aqbalū ʿalayhim mādhā tafqidūn
verses.english: They said, as they came towards them, "What did you lose?"

1981.english: They said, as they returned, "What did you lose?"

1989.english: They said, as they came towards them, “What did you lose?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلْمَلِكِ وَلِمَن جَآءَ بِهِۦ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا۠ بِهِۦ زَعِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم
verses.transliterated: qālū nafqidu ṣuwāʿa l-maliki waliman jāa bihi ḥim'lu baʿīrin wa-anā bihi zaʿīmu
verses.english: They said, "We lost the king's cup. Anyone who returns it will receive an extra camel-load; I personally guarantee this."

1981.english: They said, "We lost the king's cup; anyone who recovers it will get a camel's load; I guarantee this."

1989.english: They said, “We lost the king’s cup. Anyone who returns it will receive an extra camel-load; I personally guarantee this.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَٰرِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين
verses.transliterated: qālū tal-lahi laqad ʿalim'tum mā ji'nā linuf'sida fī l-arḍi wamā kunnā sāriqīn
verses.english: They said, "By GOD, you know full well that we did not come here to commit evil, nor are we thieves."

1981.english: They said, "By God, you know well that we did not come to corrupt the earth; we are not thieves."

1989.english: They said, “By GOD, you know full well that we did not come here to commit evil, nor are we thieves.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ فَمَا جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين
verses.transliterated: qālū famā jazāuhu in kuntum kādhibīn
verses.english: They said, "What is the punishment for the thief, if you are liars?"

1981.english: "What then should be the punishment if you are liars?"

1989.english: They said, “What is the punishment for the thief, if you are liars?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥ مَن وُجِدَ فِى رَحْلِهِۦ فَهُوَ جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه ۚ كذلك نجزي الظالمين
verses.transliterated: qālū jazāuhu man wujida fī raḥlihi fahuwa jazāuhu kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: They said, "The punishment, if it is found in his bag, is that the thief belongs to you. We thus punish the guilty."

1981.english: They said, "If you find the cup in any person's bag, then this person becomes your slave. This is our law."

1989.english: They said, “The punishment, if it is found in his bag, is that the thief belongs to you. This is our law.”

verses.arabic: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ قَبْلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ كَذَٰلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِى دِينِ ٱلْمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٍ مَّن نَّشَآءُ وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِى عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه ۚ كذلك كدنا ليوسف ۖ ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله ۚ نرفع درجات من نشاء ۗ وفوق كل ذي علم عليم
verses.transliterated: fabada-a bi-awʿiyatihim qabla wiʿāi akhīhi thumma is'takhrajahā min wiʿāi akhīhi kadhālika kid'nā liyūsufa mā kāna liyakhudha akhāhu fī dīni l-maliki illā an yashāa l-lahu narfaʿu darajātin man nashāu wafawqa kulli dhī ʿil'min ʿalīmu
verses.english: He then started by inspecting their containers, before getting to his brother's container, and he extracted it out of his brother's container. We thus perfected the scheme for Joseph; he could not have kept his brother if he applied the king's law. But that was the will of GOD. We exalt whomever we choose to higher ranks. Above every knowledgeable one, there is one who is even more knowledgeable.

1981.english: He started looking in their bags, before his brother's bag, then he took it out of his brother's bag. He thus planned for Joseph, for he could not take his brother according to the king's law. This was God's will. We raise whomever we will to higher ranks. Over any possessor of knowledge, there is one who knows more.

1989.english: (Joseph) started by inspecting their containers, before getting to his brother’s container. Then he got it out of his brother’s container. We thus perfected the scheme for Joseph; he could not keep his brother if he applied the king’s law. But that was the will of GOD. We exalt whomever we choose to higher ranks. Above every knowledgeable one, there is one who is even more knowledgeable.

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِى نَفْسِهِۦ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ قَالَ أَنتُمْ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل ۚ فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم ۚ قال أنتم شر مكانا ۖ والله أعلم بما تصفون
verses.transliterated: qālū in yasriq faqad saraqa akhun lahu min qablu fa-asarrahā yūsufu fī nafsihi walam yub'dihā lahum qāla antum sharrun makānan wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā taṣifūn
verses.english: They said, "If he stole, so did a brother of his in the past." Joseph concealed his feelings in himself, and did not give them any clue. He said (to himself), "You are really bad. GOD is fully aware of your accusations."

1981.english: They said, "If he has stolen, a brother of his had committed the same crime." Joseph noted this remark, and concealed it in himself, saying, "You are far worse, and God knows the falsehoods you utter."

1989.english: They said, “If he stole, so did a brother of his in the past.” Joseph hid it in himself. He did not give them any clue, as he said, “You are truly bad. GOD is fully aware of your accusations.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُۥٓ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُۥٓ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه ۖ إنا نراك من المحسنين
verses.transliterated: qālū yāayyuhā l-ʿazīzu inna lahu aban shaykhan kabīran fakhudh aḥadanā makānahu innā narāka mina l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: They said, “O you noble one, he has a father who is elderly; would you take one of us in his place? We see that you are a kind man."

1981.english: They said, "O you honorable one, his father is an old man. Would you take one of us in his place? We see that you are charitable."

1989.english: They said, “O you noble one, he has a father who is elderly; would you take anyone of us in his place? We see that you are righteous.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ أَن نَّأْخُذَ إِلَّا مَن وَجَدْنَا مَتَٰعَنَا عِندَهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّظَٰلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون
verses.transliterated: qāla maʿādha l-lahi an nakhudha illā man wajadnā matāʿanā ʿindahu innā idhan laẓālimūn
verses.english: He said, "GOD forbid that we should take other than the one in whose possession we found our goods. Otherwise, we would be unjust."

1981.english: He said, "God forbid that we should take other than the guilty person. We would then be unjust."

1989.english: He said, “GOD forbid that we should take other than the one in whose possession we found our goods. Otherwise, we would be unjust.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسُوا۟ مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا۟ نَجِيًّا قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُم مَّوْثِقًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمْ فِى يُوسُفَ فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ ٱلْأَرْضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْذَنَ لِىٓ أَبِىٓ أَوْ يَحْكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِى وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا ۖ قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف ۖ فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي ۖ وهو خير الحاكمين
verses.transliterated: falammā is'tayasū min'hu khalaṣū najiyyan qāla kabīruhum alam taʿlamū anna abākum qad akhadha ʿalaykum mawthiqan mina l-lahi wamin qablu mā farraṭtum fī yūsufa falan abraḥa l-arḍa ḥattā yadhana lī abī aw yaḥkuma l-lahu lī wahuwa khayru l-ḥākimīn
verses.english: When they despaired of changing his mind, they conferred together. Their eldest said, "Do you realize that your father has taken a solemn pledge from you before GOD? In the past you lost Joseph. I am not leaving this place until my father gives me permission, or until GOD judges for me; He is the best Judge.

1981.english: When they gave up on him, they conferred with each other. The oldest one said, "Did you not give your father a solemn pledge before God? Also, you have lost Joseph previously. I will not leave this land until my father gives me permission, or until God rules for me. He is the best ruler."

1989.english: When they despaired of changing his mind, they conferred together. Their eldest said, “Do you realize that your father has taken a solemn pledge from you before GOD, and in the past you lost Joseph? I am not leaving this place until my father gives me permission, or until GOD judges for me; He is the best Judge.

verses.arabic: ٱرْجِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّ ٱبْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدْنَآ إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حَٰفِظِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين
verses.transliterated: ir'jiʿū ilā abīkum faqūlū yāabānā inna ib'naka saraqa wamā shahid'nā illā bimā ʿalim'nā wamā kunnā lil'ghaybi ḥāfiẓīn
verses.english: "Go back to your father and tell him...'Our father, your son has committed a theft. We know for sure, because this is what we have witnessed. This was an unexpected occurrence.
verses.subtitle: Back In Palestine

1981.english: "Go back to your father, and say, 'O our father, your son has stolen and we bear witness to what we know for sure. We could not foretell the future.

1989.english: “Go back to your father and tell him...” ‘Our father, your son has committed a theft, and we know that he did because this is what we have witnessed. This was an unexpected occurrence.

verses.arabic: وَسْـَٔلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ ٱلَّتِى كُنَّا فِيهَا وَٱلْعِيرَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَقْبَلْنَا فِيهَا وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها ۖ وإنا لصادقون
verses.transliterated: wasali l-qaryata allatī kunnā fīhā wal-ʿīra allatī aqbalnā fīhā wa-innā laṣādiqūn
verses.english: You may ask the community where we were, and the caravan that came back with us. We are telling the truth.'"

1981.english: 'You may ask the community where we were, and the caravan in which we came. We are telling the truth.' "

1989.english: ‘You may ask the community where we were, and the caravan that came back with us. We are telling the truth.’ ”
1989.subtitle: Back In Palestine

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَنِى بِهِمْ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا ۖ فصبر جميل ۖ عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا ۚ إنه هو العليم الحكيم
verses.transliterated: qāla bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amran faṣabrun jamīlun ʿasā l-lahu an yatiyanī bihim jamīʿan innahu huwa l-ʿalīmu l-ḥakīm
verses.english: He said, "Indeed, you have conspired to carry out a certain scheme. Quiet patience is my only recourse. May GOD bring them all back to me. He is the Omniscient, Most Wise."

1981.english: He said, "It is you who plotted a conspiracy. I can only resort to quiet patience. May God bring them back to me. He is the omniscient, the wise."

1989.english: He said, “Indeed, you have conspired to carry out a certain scheme. Quiet patience is my only recourse. May GOD bring them all back to me. He is the Knower, the Most Wise.”

verses.arabic: وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَسَفَىٰ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَٱبْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم
verses.transliterated: watawallā ʿanhum waqāla yāasafā ʿalā yūsufa wa-ib'yaḍḍat ʿaynāhu mina l-ḥuz'ni fahuwa kaẓīmu
verses.english: He turned away from them, saying, "I am grieving over Joseph." His eyes turned white from grieving so much; he was truly sad.

1981.english: He turned away from them saying, "How do I grieve for Joseph!" His eyes became white from weeping, and he became depressed.

1989.english: He turned away from them, saying, “I am grieving over Joseph.” His eyes turned white from grieving so much; he was truly sad.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا۟ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْهَٰلِكِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين
verses.transliterated: qālū tal-lahi tafta-u tadhkuru yūsufa ḥattā takūna ḥaraḍan aw takūna mina l-hālikīn
verses.english: They said, "By GOD, you will keep on grieving over Joseph until you become ill, or until you die."

1981.english: They said, "By God, you will continue to think of Joseph until you ruin your health or until you die."

1989.english: They said, “By GOD, you will keep on grieving over Joseph until you become crippled, or until you die.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُوا۟ بَثِّى وَحُزْنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون
verses.transliterated: qāla innamā ashkū bathī waḥuz'nī ilā l-lahi wa-aʿlamu mina l-lahi mā lā taʿlamūn
verses.english: He said, "I simply complain to GOD about my dilemma and grief, for I know from GOD what you do not know.

1981.english: He said, "I only complain of my sorrow and my grief to God, and I know from God what you do not know.
1981.footnote: Jacob knew from Joseph's dream in 12:4 that the family will be reunited some day.

1989.english: He said, “I simply complain to GOD about my dilemma and grief, for I know from GOD what you do not know.

verses.arabic: يَٰبَنِىَّ ٱذْهَبُوا۟ فَتَحَسَّسُوا۟ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله ۖ إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون
verses.transliterated: yābaniyya idh'habū fataḥassasū min yūsufa wa-akhīhi walā tāy'asū min rawḥi l-lahi innahu lā yāy'asu min rawḥi l-lahi illā l-qawmu l-kāfirūn
verses.english: "O my sons, go fetch Joseph and his brother, and never despair of GOD's grace. None despairs of GOD's grace except the disbelieving people.

1981.english: "O my sons, go fetch Joseph and his brother, and never despair of God's grace; only the disbelievers despair of God's grace."

1989.english: “O my sons, go fetch Joseph and his brother, and never despair of GOD’s grace. None despairs of GOD’s grace except the disbelieving people.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَٰعَةٍ مُّزْجَىٰةٍ فَأَوْفِ لَنَا ٱلْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجْزِى ٱلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا ۖ إن الله يجزي المتصدقين
verses.transliterated: falammā dakhalū ʿalayhi qālū yāayyuhā l-ʿazīzu massanā wa-ahlanā l-ḍuru waji'nā bibiḍāʿatin muz'jātin fa-awfi lanā l-kayla wataṣaddaq ʿalaynā inna l-laha yajzī l-mutaṣadiqīn
verses.english: When they entered (Joseph's) quarters, they said, "O you noble one, we have suffered a lot of hardship, along with our family, and we have brought inferior goods. But we hope that you will give us full measure and be charitable to us. GOD rewards the charitable."
verses.subtitle: Israel Goes to Egypt

1981.english: When they later returned to Joseph they said, "Your honor, we have suffered hardship, our whole family, and we bring with us humble goods. Give us a generous share and treat us kindly. God rewards those who are charitable."

1989.english: When they entered (Joseph ’5) quarters, they said, “O you noble one, we have suffered a lot, along with our family, and we have brought excellent goods. So give us full measure and be charitable towards us. GOD rewards the charitable.”
1989.subtitle: Israel Goes to Egypt

verses.arabic: قَالَ هَلْ عَلِمْتُم مَّا فَعَلْتُم بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذْ أَنتُمْ جَٰهِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون
verses.transliterated: qāla hal ʿalim'tum mā faʿaltum biyūsufa wa-akhīhi idh antum jāhilūn
verses.english: He said, "Do you recall what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"

1981.english: He said, "Are you aware of what you have done to Joseph and his brother, when you were ignorant?"

1989.english: He said, “Do you recall what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ أَءِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ يُوسُفُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ يُوسُفُ وَهَٰذَآ أَخِى قَدْ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف ۖ قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي ۖ قد من الله علينا ۖ إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين
verses.transliterated: qālū a-innaka la-anta yūsufu qāla anā yūsufu wahādhā akhī qad manna l-lahu ʿalaynā innahu man yattaqi wayaṣbir fa-inna l-laha lā yuḍīʿu ajra l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: They said, "You must be Joseph." He said, "I am Joseph, and here is my brother. GOD has blessed us. That is because if one leads a righteous life, and steadfastly perseveres, GOD never fails to reward the righteous."

1981.english: They said, "You must be Joseph." He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. God has been gracious to us. If anyone works righteousness and steadfastly persevere, then God never neglects to reward the righteous."

1989.english: They said, “You must be Joseph.” He said, “I am Joseph, and here is my brother. GOD has blessed us. If one leads a righteous life, and steadfastly perseveres, GOD never fails to reward the righteous.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين
verses.transliterated: qālū tal-lahi laqad ātharaka l-lahu ʿalaynā wa-in kunnā lakhāṭiīn
verses.english: They said, "By GOD, GOD has truly preferred you over us. We were definitely wrong."

1981.english: They said, "Indeed, God has preferred you over us, and we were really wrong."

1989.english: They said, “By GOD, GOD has truly preferred you over us. We were really wrong.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم ۖ يغفر الله لكم ۖ وهو أرحم الراحمين
verses.transliterated: qāla lā tathrība ʿalaykumu l-yawma yaghfiru l-lahu lakum wahuwa arḥamu l-rāḥimīn
verses.english: He said, "There is no blame upon you today. May GOD forgive you. Of all the merciful ones, He is the Most Merciful.

1981.english: He said, "There is no blame on you today. May God forgive you. Of those who are merciful, He is the most merciful.
1981.subtitle: Israel's Family Moves to Egypt

1989.english: He said, “There is no blame on you today. May GOD forgive you. Of all the merciful ones, He is the Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: ٱذْهَبُوا۟ بِقَمِيصِى هَٰذَا فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِ أَبِى يَأْتِ بَصِيرًا وَأْتُونِى بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين
verses.transliterated: idh'habū biqamīṣī hādhā fa-alqūhu ʿalā wajhi abī yati baṣīran watūnī bi-ahlikum ajmaʿīn
verses.english: "Take this shirt of mine; when you throw it on my father's face, his vision will be restored. Bring your whole family and come back to me."
verses.footnote: This marks the beginning of the Children of Israel in Egypt. Moses led them out of Egypt a few centuries later.

1981.english: "Take this shirt of mine, and throw it on my father's face; he will then recover his eyesight, and bring all your family to me."

1989.english: “Take this shirt of mine; when you throw it on my father’s face, his vision will be restored. Bring your whole family and come back to me.”*
1989.footnote: This marks the beginning of the Children of Israel in Egypt. Moses led them out of Egypt a few centuries later.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ ٱلْعِيرُ قَالَ أَبُوهُمْ إِنِّى لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ لَوْلَآ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ
verses.arabicClean: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف ۖ لولا أن تفندون
verses.transliterated: walammā faṣalati l-ʿīru qāla abūhum innī la-ajidu rīḥa yūsufa lawlā an tufannidūn
verses.english: Even before the caravan arrived, their father said, "I can sense the smell of Joseph. Will someone enlighten me?"

1981.english: When the caravan arrived, their father said, "I sense the smell of Joseph. Can you deny?"

1989.english: Before the caravan arrived, their father said, “I can sense the smell of Joseph. Will someone enlighten me?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَفِى ضَلَٰلِكَ ٱلْقَدِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم
verses.transliterated: qālū tal-lahi innaka lafī ḍalālika l-qadīm
verses.english: They said, "By GOD, you are still in your old confusion."

1981.english: They said, "By God, you are still in your old imaginations."

1989.english: They said, “By GOD, you are still in your old confusion.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلْبَشِيرُ أَلْقَىٰهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦ فَٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا ۖ قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون
verses.transliterated: falammā an jāa l-bashīru alqāhu ʿalā wajhihi fa-ir'tadda baṣīran qāla alam aqul lakum innī aʿlamu mina l-lahi mā lā taʿlamūn
verses.english: When the bearer of good news arrived, he threw (the shirt) on his face, whereupon his vision was restored. He said, "Did I not tell you that I knew from GOD what you did not know?"

1981.english: Then, when the bearer of good news came, he threw the shirt on his face, whereupon he recovered his eyesight. He said, "Did I not tell you that I knew from God what you do not know?"
1981.footnote: See footnote 12:86.

1989.english: When the bearer of good news arrived, he threw (the shirt) on his face, whereupon his vision was restored. He said, “Did I not tell you that I knew from GOD what you did not know?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا ٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا خَٰطِـِٔينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين
verses.transliterated: qālū yāabānā is'taghfir lanā dhunūbanā innā kunnā khāṭiīn
verses.english: They said, "Our father, pray for our forgiveness; we were wrong indeed."

1981.english: They said, "O our father, pray for forgiveness of our sins; we have been really wrong."

1989.english: They said, “Our father, pray for our forgiveness; we were wrong indeed.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّىٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي ۖ إنه هو الغفور الرحيم
verses.transliterated: qāla sawfa astaghfiru lakum rabbī innahu huwa l-ghafūru l-raḥīm
verses.english: He said, "I will implore my Lord to forgive you; He is the Forgiver, Most Merciful."

1981.english: He said, "I will ask my Lord to forgive you. He is the forgiver, the merciful."

1989.english: He said, “I will implore my Lord to forgive you; He is the Forgiver, Most Merciful.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ وَقَالَ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِصْرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين
verses.transliterated: falammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi abawayhi waqāla ud'khulū miṣ'ra in shāa l-lahu āminīn
verses.english: When they entered Joseph's quarters, he embraced his parents, saying, "Welcome to Egypt. GOD willing, you will be safe here."
verses.subtitle: In Egypt

1981.english: When they arrived at Joseph, he hugged his parents and said, "You will live in Egypt, God willing, in peace."

1989.english: When they entered Joseph’s quarters, he embraced his parents, saying, “Welcome to Egypt. GOD willing, you will be safe here.”
1989.subtitle: In Egypt

verses.arabic: وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا۟ لَهُۥ سُجَّدًا وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُءْيَٰىَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّا وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِىٓ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْبَدْوِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِىٓ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا ۖ وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا ۖ وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي ۚ إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء ۚ إنه هو العليم الحكيم
verses.transliterated: warafaʿa abawayhi ʿalā l-ʿarshi wakharrū lahu sujjadan waqāla yāabati hādhā tawīlu ru'yāya min qablu qad jaʿalahā rabbī ḥaqqan waqad aḥsana bī idh akhrajanī mina l-sij'ni wajāa bikum mina l-badwi min baʿdi an nazagha l-shayṭānu baynī wabayna ikh'watī inna rabbī laṭīfun limā yashāu innahu huwa l-ʿalīmu l-ḥakīm
verses.english: He raised his parents upon the throne. They fell prostrate before him. He said, "O my father, this is the fulfillment of my old dream. My Lord has made it come true. He has blessed me, delivered me from the prison, and brought you from the desert, after the devil had driven a wedge between me and my brothers. My Lord is Most Kind towards whomever He wills. He is the Knower, the Most Wise."

1981.english: He honored his parents by hosting them in the mansion, and they fell prostrate all together before him. He then said, "O my father, this is the realization of my old dream; my Lord has made it come true. He has been most gracious to me, by saving me from the prison, and bringing me from the desert, after the devil interfered between me and my brothers. My Lord is kind towards whatever He wills; He is the knower, the wise."

1989.english: He raised his parents upon the throne. They fell prostrate before him, and he said, “O my father, this is the fulfillment of my old dream. My Lord has made it come true. He has blessed me, delivered me from the prison, and brought you from the desert, after the devil had driven a wedge between me and my brothers. My Lord is Most Kind towards whomever He wills. He is the Knower, the Most Wise.”

verses.arabic: رَبِّ قَدْ ءَاتَيْتَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِى مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَنتَ وَلِىِّۦ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ تَوَفَّنِى مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث ۚ فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة ۖ توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين
verses.transliterated: rabbi qad ātaytanī mina l-mul'ki waʿallamtanī min tawīli l-aḥādīthi fāṭira l-samāwāti wal-arḍi anta waliyyī fī l-dun'yā wal-ākhirati tawaffanī mus'liman wa-alḥiq'nī bil-ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: "My Lord, You have given me kingship and taught me the interpretation of dreams. Initiator of the heavens and the earth; You are my Lord and Master in this life and in the Hereafter. Let me die as a submitter, and count me with the righteous."

1981.english: "My Lord, you have bestowed some kingship on me, and taught me the interpretation of dreams. O creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my master in this life, and in the hereafter. Let me die as a Muslim, and count me with the righteous."

1989.english: “My Lord, You have given me kingship and taught me the interpretation of dreams. You are the Initiator of the heavens and the earth. You are my Lord and Master in this life and in the Hereafter. Let me die as a Muslim, and count me with the righteous.”

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ أَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك ۖ وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون
verses.transliterated: dhālika min anbāi l-ghaybi nūḥīhi ilayka wamā kunta ladayhim idh ajmaʿū amrahum wahum yamkurūn
verses.english: This is news from the past that we reveal to you. You were not present when they made their unanimous decision (to throw Joseph in the well), as they conspired together.

1981.english: This is history from the past that we narrate to you. You were not present when they made their unanimous decision, or when they plotted and schemed.

1989.english: This is news from the past that we reveal to you. You were not present when they made their unanimous decision, as they conspired together.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين
verses.transliterated: wamā aktharu l-nāsi walaw ḥaraṣta bimu'minīn
verses.english: Most people, no matter what you do, will not believe.
verses.subtitle: The Majority of People Do Not Believe

1981.english: The majority of people, no matter what you do, will not believe.
1981.subtitle: The Majority of People Will Not Believe

1989.english: Most people, no matter what you do, will not believe.
1989.subtitle: The Majority of People Do Not Believe

verses.arabic: وَمَا تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر ۚ إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين
verses.transliterated: wamā tasaluhum ʿalayhi min ajrin in huwa illā dhik'run lil'ʿālamīn
verses.english: You are not asking them for any money; you simply deliver this reminder for all the people.

1981.english: Even though you do not ask them for any wage; for this is a message to all the people.

1989.english: Even though you are not asking them for any money. This is a reminder for all the people.

verses.arabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّنْ ءَايَةٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون
verses.transliterated: waka-ayyin min āyatin fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi yamurrūna ʿalayhā wahum ʿanhā muʿ'riḍūn
verses.english: So many proofs in the heavens and the earth are given to them, but they pass by them, heedlessly!

1981.english: (And even though) the heavens and the earth are full of signs. They pass by them totally heedless.

1989.english: So many signs are in the heavens and the earth—they pass by them, heedlessly

verses.arabic: وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُم بِٱللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُم مُّشْرِكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون
verses.transliterated: wamā yu'minu aktharuhum bil-lahi illā wahum mush'rikūn
verses.english: The majority of those who believe in GOD do not do so without committing idol worship.
verses.subtitle: The Majority of Believers Destined for Hell

1981.english: And the majority of those who believe, fall into idol worship.
1981.subtitle: Minority of the Minority Attain Salvation
1981.footnote: The majority of Jews follow the Talmud instead of the Torah; the majority of Christians idolize Jesus instead of God; and the majority of Muslims follow "Hadith" instead of the Quran.

1989.english: The majority of those who believe in GOD do not do so without committing idol worship.
1989.subtitle: The Majority of Believers Destined for Hell

verses.arabic: أَفَأَمِنُوٓا۟ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ غَٰشِيَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون
verses.transliterated: afa-aminū an tatiyahum ghāshiyatun min ʿadhābi l-lahi aw tatiyahumu l-sāʿatu baghtatan wahum lā yashʿurūn
verses.english: Have they guaranteed that an overwhelming retribution from GOD will not strike them, or the Hour will not come to them suddenly, when they least expect it?

1981.english: Have they guaranteed that overwhelming retribution will not come to them from God? Have they guaranteed that the Hour will not come to them suddenly, when they least expect it?

1989.english: Have they guaranteed that an overwhelming retribution from GOD will not strike them, or the Hour will not come to them suddenly, when they least expect it?

verses.arabic: قُلْ هَٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى وَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله ۚ على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني ۖ وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين
verses.transliterated: qul hādhihi sabīlī adʿū ilā l-lahi ʿalā baṣīratin anā wamani ittabaʿanī wasub'ḥāna l-lahi wamā anā mina l-mush'rikīn
verses.english: Say, "This is my path: I invite to GOD, on the basis of a clear proof, and so do those who follow me. GOD be glorified. I am not an idol worshiper."

1981.english: Say, "This is my way; I invite to God on the basis of positive knowledge; me and those who follow me. God be glorified; I will never set up idols."

1989.english: Say, “This is my path: I invite to GOD, on the basis of a clear proof, and so do those who follow me. GOD be glorified. I am not an idol worshiper.”

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وَلَدَارُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى ۗ أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ۗ ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا ۗ أفلا تعقلون
verses.transliterated: wamā arsalnā min qablika illā rijālan nūḥī ilayhim min ahli l-qurā afalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim waladāru l-ākhirati khayrun lilladhīna ittaqaw afalā taʿqilūn
verses.english: We did not send before you except men whom we inspired, chosen from the people of various communities. Did they not roam the earth and see the consequences for those before them? The abode of the Hereafter is far better for those who lead a righteous life. Would you then understand?

1981.english: We have not sent before you except humans from among the communities, whom we inspired. Do they not travel the earth, and see the fate of those before them? Indeed, the abode of the hereafter is far better for those who observe piety. Do you not understand?

1989.english: We did not send before you except men whom we inspired, chosen from the people of various communities. Did they not roam the earth and see the consequences for those before them? The abode of the Hereafter is far better for those who lead a righteous life. Would you then understand?

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ٱسْتَيْـَٔسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا۟ جَآءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا فَنُجِّىَ مَن نَّشَآءُ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ۖ ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā is'tayasa l-rusulu waẓannū annahum qad kudhibū jāahum naṣrunā fanujjiya man nashāu walā yuraddu basunā ʿani l-qawmi l-muj'rimīn
verses.english: Just when the messengers despair, and think that they had been rejected, our victory comes to them. We then save whomever we choose, while our retribution for the guilty people is unavoidable.
verses.subtitle: Victory, Ultimately, Belongs to the Believers

1981.english: Just as the messengers reach the point of despair, and imagine that they have failed, our victory comes to them. We then save whomever we will, while the guilty can never evade our retribution.

1989.english: Just when the messengers despair, and think that they had been rejected, our victory comes to them. We then save whomever we choose, while our retribution for the guilty people is unavoidable.
1989.subtitle: Victory, Ultimately, Belongs to the Believers

verses.arabic: لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ۗ ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: laqad kāna fī qaṣaṣihim ʿib'ratun li-ulī l-albābi mā kāna ḥadīthan yuf'tarā walākin taṣdīqa alladhī bayna yadayhi watafṣīla kulli shayin wahudan waraḥmatan liqawmin yu'minūn
verses.english: In their history, there is a lesson for those who possess intelligence. This is not fabricated Hadith; this (Quran) confirms all previous scriptures, provides the details of everything, and is a beacon and mercy for those who believe.
verses.subtitle: The Quran is All We Need

1981.english: Their history offers lessons for those who possess intelligence. This is not fabricated "Hadith" (narration). It is a confirmation of previous scriptures; it details everything; it is a guide and mercy for those who believe.

1989.english: In their history, there is a lesson for those who possess intelligence. This is not a fabricated Hadith; this (Quran) confirms all previous scriptures, and provides the details of everything. It is a beacon and mercy for those who believe.
1989.subtitle: The Quran is All We Need

verses.arabic: الٓمٓر تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم المر ۚ تلك آيات الكتاب ۗ والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: alif-lam-meem-ra til'ka āyātu l-kitābi wa-alladhī unzila ilayka min rabbika l-ḥaqu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yu'minūn
verses.english: A. L. M. R. These (letters) are proofs of this scripture. What is revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
verses.footnote: These initials constitute a major component of the Quran's built-in proof of divine authorship, the miraculous mathematical code. See Appendix 1.

1981.english: A.L.M.R.* These (letters) constitute the miracles of this scripture. They prove that these revelations from your Lord are the truth, but most people do not believe.
1981.footnote: The word "Ayat" is used in each one of these verses to illustrate another miraculous feature of Quran, namely, the use of multi-meaning words. In 13:1, the word "Ayat" means "miracles or verses," and in 13:3-4 it means "signs or lessons." Thus, the generations of people who lived before the discovery of the Quran's secret numerical code, were content with the meaning "verses" for the word "Ayat." This makes the Quran suitable for all generations. Please see also footnote 10:1, and note that the standard word for "miracle," namely, "Mu'jizah" is NEVER used in Quran.

1989.english: A. L. M. R.* These (letters) are miracles of this scripture, proving that these revelations to you from your Lord are the truth. However, most people do not know.
1989.footnote: These initials constitute a major component of the Quran’s built-in proof oi divine authorship, the miraculous mathematical code. See Appendix 1.

verses.arabic: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى يُدَبِّرُ ٱلْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ۖ ثم استوى على العرش ۖ وسخر الشمس والقمر ۖ كل يجري لأجل مسمى ۚ يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون
verses.transliterated: al-lahu alladhī rafaʿa l-samāwāti bighayri ʿamadin tarawnahā thumma is'tawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi wasakhara l-shamsa wal-qamara kullun yajrī li-ajalin musamman yudabbiru l-amra yufaṣṣilu l-āyāti laʿallakum biliqāi rabbikum tūqinūn
verses.english: GOD is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then assumed all authority. He committed the sun and the moon, each running (in its orbit) for a predetermined period. He controls all things, and explains the revelations, that you may attain certainty about meeting your Lord.

1981.english: God is the one who raised the heavens without visible pillars, then assumed all authority. He committed the sun and the moon (in your service), each running for a specified period. He controls everything. He explains the revelations,* that you may be certain about meeting your Lord.
1981.footnote: The word "Ayat" is used in each one of these verses to illustrate another miraculous feature of Quran, namely, the use of multi-meaning words. In 13:1, the word "Ayat" means "miracles or verses," and in 13:3-4 it means "signs or lessons." Thus, the generations of people who lived before the discovery of the Quran's secret numerical code, were content with the meaning "verses" for the word "Ayat." This makes the Quran suitable for all generations. Please see also footnote 10:1, and note that the standard word for "miracle," namely, "Mu'jizah" is NEVER used in Quran.

1989.english: GOD is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then assumed all authority. He committed the sun and the moon (to serve you), each running (in its orbit) for a specific period. He controls all things, and explains the revelations, that you may attain certainty about meeting your Lord.

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَدَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَأَنْهَٰرًا وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ يُغْشِى ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ۖ ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين ۖ يغشي الليل النهار ۚ إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī madda l-arḍa wajaʿala fīhā rawāsiya wa-anhāran wamin kulli l-thamarāti jaʿala fīhā zawjayni ith'nayni yugh'shī al-layla l-nahāra inna fī dhālika laāyātin liqawmin yatafakkarūn
verses.english: He is the One who constructed the earth and placed on it mountains and rivers. And from the different kinds of fruits, He made them into pairs—males and females. The night overtakes the day. These are solid proofs for people who think.

1981.english: And He is the one who constructed the earth, and placed stabilizers and rivers therein. Of all the fruits, He designated two kinds. The night covers the day. In all these, there are signs for people who reflect.
1981.footnote: The word "Ayat" is used in each one of these verses to illustrate another miraculous feature of Quran, namely, the use of multi-meaning words. In 13:1, the word "Ayat" means "miracles or verses," and in 13:3-4 it means "signs or lessons." Thus, the generations of people who lived before the discovery of the Quran's secret numerical code, were content with the meaning "verses" for the word "Ayat." This makes the Quran suitable for all generations. Please see also footnote 10:1, and note that the standard word for "miracle," namely, "Mu'jizah" is NEVER used in Quran.

1989.english: He is the One who constructed the earth and placed on it mountains and rivers, and all kinds of fruits— which He rendered as males and females. The night overtakes the day. These are sure signs for those who think.

verses.arabic: وَفِى ٱلْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَٰوِرَٰتٌ وَجَنَّٰتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَٰبٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَٰنٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَٰنٍ يُسْقَىٰ بِمَآءٍ وَٰحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِى ٱلْأُكُلِ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل ۚ إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون
verses.transliterated: wafī l-arḍi qiṭaʿun mutajāwirātun wajannātun min aʿnābin wazarʿun wanakhīlun ṣin'wānun waghayru ṣin'wānin yus'qā bimāin wāḥidin wanufaḍḍilu baʿḍahā ʿalā baʿḍin fī l-ukuli inna fī dhālika laāyātin liqawmin yaʿqilūn
verses.english: On earth, there are adjacent lots that produce orchards of grapes, crops, palm trees—dioecious and non-dioecious. Although they are irrigated with the same water, we prefer some of them over others in eating. These are solid proofs for people who understand.

1981.english: And on earth, adjoining pieces of land produce gardens of grapes, crops, date palms, dioecious and non-dioecious. Although they are watered with the same water, we prefer some of them over others in eating. In all these, there are lessons for people who understand.
1981.footnote: The word "Ayat" is used in each one of these verses to illustrate another miraculous feature of Quran, namely, the use of multi-meaning words. In 13:1, the word "Ayat" means "miracles or verses," and in 13:3-4 it means "signs or lessons." Thus, the generations of people who lived before the discovery of the Quran's secret numerical code, were content with the meaning "verses" for the word "Ayat." This makes the Quran suitable for all generations. Please see also footnote 10:1, and note that the standard word for "miracle," namely, "Mu'jizah" is NEVER used in Quran.

1989.english: On earth, there are adjacent lots that produce orchards of grapes, crops, palm trees—dioecious and non-dioecious. Although they are watered with the same water, we prefer some of them over others in eating. These are sure signs for people who understand.

verses.arabic: وَإِن تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًا أَءِنَّا لَفِى خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِرَبِّهِمْ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلْأَغْلَٰلُ فِىٓ أَعْنَٰقِهِمْ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد ۗ أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم ۖ وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم ۖ وأولئك أصحاب النار ۖ هم فيها خالدون
verses.transliterated: wa-in taʿjab faʿajabun qawluhum a-idhā kunnā turāban a-innā lafī khalqin jadīdin ulāika alladhīna kafarū birabbihim wa-ulāika l-aghlālu fī aʿnāqihim wa-ulāika aṣḥābu l-nāri hum fīhā khālidūn
verses.english: If you ever wonder, the real wonder is their saying: "After we turn into dust, do we get recreated anew?" These are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord. These are the ones who have incurred shackles around their necks. These are the ones who have incurred Hell, wherein they abide forever.
verses.subtitle: Belief in the Hereafter Required For Salvation

1981.english: If you ever wonder, you should wonder about their saying, "After we are dust, are we going to be recreated?" These are the ones who disbelieve in their Lord; these are the ones whose necks will be chained; these are the ones who have deserved hell; they abide therein for ever.

1989.english: If you ever wonder, you should wonder abour their saying: “After we turn into dust, do we get recreated anew?” These are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord. These are the ones who incur shackles around their necks. These are the ones who incur Hell, wherein they abide forever.
1989.subtitle: Belief in the Hereafter Required For Salvation

verses.arabic: وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ ٱلْمَثُلَٰتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ
verses.arabicClean: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات ۗ وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم ۖ وإن ربك لشديد العقاب
verses.transliterated: wayastaʿjilūnaka bil-sayi-ati qabla l-ḥasanati waqad khalat min qablihimu l-mathulātu wa-inna rabbaka ladhū maghfiratin lilnnāsi ʿalā ẓul'mihim wa-inna rabbaka lashadīdu l-ʿiqāb
verses.english: They challenge you to bring doom upon them, rather than turning righteous! Sufficient precedents have been set for them in the past. Indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness towards the people, in spite of their transgressions, and your Lord is also strict in enforcing retribution.

1981.english: They challenge you to bring doom upon them, instead of following the righteous path, even though the examples have been set before them. Indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness towards the people, despite their wickedness; and indeed, your Lord is most strict in imposing retribution.

1989.english: They challenge you to bring doom upon them, rather than turning righteous! Sufficient examples have been set for them in the past. Indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness towards the people, in spite of their transgressions. You Lord is also strict in enforcing retribution.

verses.arabic: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ
verses.arabicClean: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه ۗ إنما أنت منذر ۖ ولكل قوم هاد
verses.transliterated: wayaqūlu alladhīna kafarū lawlā unzila ʿalayhi āyatun min rabbihi innamā anta mundhirun walikulli qawmin hādi
verses.english: Those who disbelieved say, "If only a miracle could come down to him from his Lord (we will then believe)." You are simply a warner—every community receives a guiding teacher.

1981.english: Those who disbelieved say, "How come no miracle came down to him from his Lord?" You are no more than a warner; for every community, we appoint a guide.

1989.english: Those who disbelieved say, “If only a miracle could come down to him from his Lord (we will then believe)." You are simply a warner— every community receives a guiding teacher.

verses.arabic: ٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ وَكُلُّ شَىْءٍ عِندَهُۥ بِمِقْدَارٍ
verses.arabicClean: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد ۖ وكل شيء عنده بمقدار
verses.transliterated: al-lahu yaʿlamu mā taḥmilu kullu unthā wamā taghīḍu l-arḥāmu wamā tazdādu wakullu shayin ʿindahu bimiq'dāri
verses.english: GOD knows what every female bears, and what every womb releases, or gains. Everything He does is perfectly measured.

1981.english: God knows what any female bears, and whatever comes out of the wombs, and whatever grows inside them. Everything is designed by Him in exact measure.
1981.subtitle: God Only Worthy of Worship

1989.english: GOD knows what every female bears, and what every womb releases, or gains. Everything He does is perfectly measured.*
1989.footnote: A specific number of persons (souls) are destined to come to this world, and receive this final chance to be redeemed. See the INTRODUCTION and Appendix 7.

verses.arabic: عَٰلِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ ٱلْكَبِيرُ ٱلْمُتَعَالِ
verses.arabicClean: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال
verses.transliterated: aleemun alghaybi washuhaadati alkayru almuta'aala
verses.english: The Knower of all secrets and declarations; the Supreme, the Most High.

1981.english: The knower of all secrets and declarations; the magnificent, the most exalted.

1989.english: (He is) the Knower of all secrets and declarations; the Supreme, the Most High.

verses.arabic: سَوَآءٌ مِّنكُم مَّنْ أَسَرَّ ٱلْقَوْلَ وَمَن جَهَرَ بِهِۦ وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍۭ بِٱلَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌۢ بِٱلنَّهَارِ
verses.arabicClean: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار
verses.transliterated: sawāon minkum man asarra l-qawla waman jahara bihi waman huwa mus'takhfin bi-al-layli wasāribun bil-nahār
verses.english: It is the same whether you conceal your thoughts, or declare them, or hide in the darkness of the night, or act in the daylight.

1981.english: Thus, it is the same whether you conceal your thoughts or declare them, and whether you hide in the darkness of night, or appear during the day.

1989.english: It is the same whether you conceal your thoughts, or declare them, or hide in the darkness of the night, or act in the daylight.

verses.arabic: لَهُۥ مُعَقِّبَٰتٌ مِّنۢ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِۦ يَحْفَظُونَهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا۟ مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ وَإِذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوٓءًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَالٍ
