1989.english: We informed you that your Lord fully controls all the people. But we rendered the vision that we showed you, including the tree that is accursed in the Quran, only a test for the people.* We showed them (miracles), but this only augmented their defiance.
1989.footnote: Muhammad’s journey to the seventh heaven, to receive the Quran, as stated in

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ قَالَ ءَأَسْجُدُ لِمَنْ خَلَقْتَ طِينًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qul'nā lil'malāikati us'judū liādama fasajadū illā ib'līsa qāla a-asjudu liman khalaqta ṭīna
verses.english: When we said to the angels, "Fall prostrate before Adam," they fell prostrate, except Satan. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one You created from mud?"
verses.subtitle: Satan Dupes the People

1981.english: When we said to the angels, "Bow down to Adam," they bowed down, except Iblees (Satan). He said, "Shall I bow down to one You created from clay?"
1981.subtitle: The Beginning of Satan

1989.english: When we said to the angels, “Fall prostrate before Adam,” they fell prostrate, except Satan. He said, “Shall I prostrate to one You created from mud?”
1989.subtitle: Satan Dupes the People

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَرَءَيْتَكَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كَرَّمْتَ عَلَىَّ لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا
verses.transliterated: qāla ara-aytaka hādhā alladhī karramta ʿalayya la-in akhartani ilā yawmi l-qiyāmati la-aḥtanikanna dhurriyyatahu illā qalīla
verses.english: He said, "Since You have honored him over me, if You respite me till the Day of Resurrection, I will possess all his descendants, except a few."

1981.english: Satan said, "Just watch this, whom You exalt above me; if You respite me till the day of resurrection, I will possess his descendants, except a few."

1989.english: He said, “Since You have honored him over me, if You respite me till the Day of Resurrection, I will possess all his descendants, except for a few.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ ٱذْهَبْ فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَآؤُكُمْ جَزَآءً مَّوْفُورًا
verses.arabicClean: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا
verses.transliterated: qāla idh'hab faman tabiʿaka min'hum fa-inna jahannama jazāukum jazāan mawfūra
verses.english: He said, "Then go; you and those who follow you will end up in Hell as your requital; an equitable requital.

1981.english: God said, "Go ahead; if any of them follow you, then hell will be sufficient as retribution.

1989.english: He said, “Go; you and those who follow you will end up in Hell as your just retribution.

verses.arabic: وَٱسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتَ مِنْهُم بِصَوْتِكَ وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِم بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ وَشَارِكْهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَوْلَٰدِ وَعِدْهُمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا
verses.arabicClean: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم ۚ وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا
verses.transliterated: wa-is'tafziz mani is'taṭaʿta min'hum biṣawtika wa-ajlib ʿalayhim bikhaylika warajilika washārik'hum fī l-amwāli wal-awlādi waʿid'hum wamā yaʿiduhumu l-shayṭānu illā ghurūra
verses.english: "You may entice them with your voice, and mobilize all your forces and all your men against them, and share in their money and children, and promise them. Anything the devil promises is no more than an illusion.

1981.english: "Entice whomever you can with your voice, and mobilize your horses and men against them, and share their wealth and children, and promise them. The devil's promises are no more than illusions.

1989.english: “Go ahead and entice them with your voice, mobilize all your forces and all your men against them, and take a share of their money and children, and promise them. Anything the devil promises is no more than an illusion.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ عِبَادِى لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَٰنٌ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان ۚ وكفى بربك وكيلا
verses.transliterated: inna ʿibādī laysa laka ʿalayhim sul'ṭānun wakafā birabbika wakīla
verses.english: "As for My servants, you have no power over them." Your Lord suffices as an advocate.

1981.english: "As for My servants, you will have no power over them. Your Lord suffices as guardian."

1989.english: “As for My servants, you have no power over them.” Your Lord suffices as a protector.

verses.arabic: رَّبُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُزْجِى لَكُمُ ٱلْفُلْكَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ لِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا
verses.arabicClean: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله ۚ إنه كان بكم رحيما
verses.transliterated: rabbukumu alladhī yuz'jī lakumu l-ful'ka fī l-baḥri litabtaghū min faḍlihi innahu kāna bikum raḥīma
verses.english: Your Lord is the One who causes the ships to float on the ocean, that you may seek His bounties. He is Most Merciful towards you.
verses.footnote: We now learn from physics and physical chemistry that water possesses unique qualities that render it perfectly suitable for serving our various needs.

1981.english: Your Lord is the one who causes the ships to float in the sea, that you may seek His bounties. He is merciful towards you.

1989.english: Your Lord is the One who causes the ships to float on the ocean,* that you may seek His bounties. He is Most Merciful towards you.
1989.footnote: We now learn from physics and physical chemistry that water possesses unique qualities that render it perfectly suitable for serving our various needs.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ كَفُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه ۖ فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم ۚ وكان الإنسان كفورا
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā massakumu l-ḍuru fī l-baḥri ḍalla man tadʿūna illā iyyāhu falammā najjākum ilā l-bari aʿraḍtum wakāna l-insānu kafūra
verses.english: If you are afflicted in the middle of the sea, you forget your idols and sincerely implore Him alone. But as soon as He saves you to the shore, you revert. Indeed, the human being is unappreciative.
verses.subtitle: Bad Weather Friends

1981.english: And when adversity touches you at sea, all your idols abandon you, but God does not. Then, when He saves you to the shore, you turn away. Indeed, man is unappreciative.

1989.english: If you are afflicted in the middle of the sea, you forget your idols and sincerely implore Him. But as soon as He saves you to the shore, you revert. Indeed, the human being is unappreciative.
1989.subtitle: Bad Weather Friends

verses.arabic: أَفَأَمِنتُمْ أَن يَخْسِفَ بِكُمْ جَانِبَ ٱلْبَرِّ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا۟ لَكُمْ وَكِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا
verses.transliterated: afa-amintum an yakhsifa bikum jāniba l-bari aw yur'sila ʿalaykum ḥāṣiban thumma lā tajidū lakum wakīla
verses.english: Have you guaranteed that He will not cause the land, on shore, to swallow you? Or, that He will not send upon you a tempest, then you find no protector?

1981.english: Have you guaranteed that He will not destroy you on shore, or send a hurricane against you? You will then find no protector.

1989.english: Have you guaranteed that He will not cause the land on shore, to swallow you? Or, that He will not send upon you a tempest, then you find no protector?

verses.arabic: أَمْ أَمِنتُمْ أَن يُعِيدَكُمْ فِيهِ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ فَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ قَاصِفًا مِّنَ ٱلرِّيحِ فَيُغْرِقَكُم بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُوا۟ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا بِهِۦ تَبِيعًا
verses.arabicClean: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ۙ ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا
verses.transliterated: am amintum an yuʿīdakum fīhi tāratan ukh'rā fayur'sila ʿalaykum qāṣifan mina l-rīḥi fayugh'riqakum bimā kafartum thumma lā tajidū lakum ʿalaynā bihi tabīʿa
verses.english: Have you guaranteed that He will not return you to the sea another time, then send upon you a storm that drowns you because of your disbelief? Once this happens, we will not give you another chance.

1981.english: Or, have you guaranteed that He will not send you back into the sea, then afflict you with a storm, and drown you for your disbelief? You will then have no ally against us.

1989.english: Have you guaranteed that He will not return you to the sea, then send upon you a storm that drowns you because of your disbelief, without getting a second chance?

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا
verses.transliterated: walaqad karramnā banī ādama waḥamalnāhum fī l-bari wal-baḥri warazaqnāhum mina l-ṭayibāti wafaḍḍalnāhum ʿalā kathīrin mimman khalaqnā tafḍīla
verses.english: We have honored the children of Adam, and provided them with rides on land and in the sea. We provided for them good provisions, and we gave them greater advantages than many of our creatures.

1981.english: We honored the children of Adam, and we carried them on land and in the sea, and we provided them with good provisions, and we endowed them more than many other creations, generously.

1989.english: We have honored the children of Adam, and carried them on land and in the sea. We provided for them good provisions, and we honored them high above many of our creatures.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا۟ كُلَّ أُنَاسٍۭ بِإِمَٰمِهِمْ فَمَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يَقْرَءُونَ كِتَٰبَهُمْ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم ۖ فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا
verses.transliterated: yawma nadʿū kulla unāsin bi-imāmihim faman ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi fa-ulāika yaqraūna kitābahum walā yuẓ'lamūna fatīla
verses.english: The day will come when we summon every people, together with their record. As for those who are given a record of righteousness, they will read their record and will not suffer the least injustice.

1981.english: The day will come when we summon all the people with their records. Thus, whoever is given his record in his right hand, these will read their records, and will not suffer misery in the least.

1989.english: The day will come when we summon every people, together with their record. As for those who are given a record of righteousness, they will read their record and will not suffer the least injustice.

verses.arabic: وَمَن كَانَ فِى هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَعْمَىٰ فَهُوَ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَعْمَىٰ وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا
verses.transliterated: waman kāna fī hādhihi aʿmā fahuwa fī l-ākhirati aʿmā wa-aḍallu sabīla
verses.english: As for those who are blind in this life, they will be blind in the Hereafter; even a lot worse.

1981.english: As for him who was blind in this life, he will be blind in the hereafter, and in worse shape.

1989.english: As for those who are blind in this life they will be blind in the Hereafter; even a lot worse.

verses.arabic: وَإِن كَادُوا۟ لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ لِتَفْتَرِىَ عَلَيْنَا غَيْرَهُۥ وَإِذًا لَّٱتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره ۖ وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا
verses.transliterated: wa-in kādū layaftinūnaka ʿani alladhī awḥaynā ilayka litaftariya ʿalaynā ghayrahu wa-idhan la-ittakhadhūka khalīla
verses.english: They almost diverted you from the revelations we have given you. They wanted you to fabricate something else, in order to consider you a friend.
verses.subtitle: God Strengthens the Messenger

1981.english: They almost diverted you (Muhammad) from our revelations to you, and pressured you to invent something else. In that case, they would have considered you a friend.
1981.subtitle: The Quran, the Whole Quran, and Nothing But the Quran

1989.english: They almost diverted you from the commandments we revealed to you. They wanted you to fabricate something else, in order to consider you a friend.
1989.subtitle: God Strengthens the Messenger

verses.arabic: وَلَوْلَآ أَن ثَبَّتْنَٰكَ لَقَدْ كِدتَّ تَرْكَنُ إِلَيْهِمْ شَيْـًٔا قَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا
verses.transliterated: walawlā an thabbatnāka laqad kidtta tarkanu ilayhim shayan qalīla
verses.english: If it were not that we strengthened you, you almost leaned towards them just a little bit.

1981.english: If it were not that we strengthened you, you almost leaned towards them a little bit.

1989.english: If it were not that we strengthened you, you almost leaned towards them a little bit.

verses.arabic: إِذًا لَّأَذَقْنَٰكَ ضِعْفَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ وَضِعْفَ ٱلْمَمَاتِ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ عَلَيْنَا نَصِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا
verses.transliterated: idhan la-adhaqnāka ḍiʿ'fa l-ḥayati waḍiʿ'fa l-mamāti thumma lā tajidu laka ʿalaynā naṣīra
verses.english: Had you done that, we would have doubled the retribution for you in this life, and after death, and you would have found no one to help you against us.

1981.english: Had you done so, we would have doubled the punishment for you in this life, and after death, and you would have found no helper against us.

1989.english: Had you done that, we would have doubled the retribution for you in this life, and after death, and you would have found no one to help you against us.

verses.arabic: وَإِن كَادُوا۟ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنْهَا وَإِذًا لَّا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلَٰفَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها ۖ وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا
verses.transliterated: wa-in kādū layastafizzūnaka mina l-arḍi liyukh'rijūka min'hā wa-idhan lā yalbathūna khilāfaka illā qalīla
verses.english: They almost banished you from the land to get rid of you, so they could revert as soon as you left.

1981.english: They also wanted to banish you from the land, in order to revert freely to their old ways.

1989.english: They almost banished you from the land to get rid of you, so they could revert as soon as you left.

verses.arabic: سُنَّةَ مَن قَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَا وَلَا تَجِدُ لِسُنَّتِنَا تَحْوِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ۖ ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا
verses.transliterated: sunnata man qad arsalnā qablaka min rusulinā walā tajidu lisunnatinā taḥwīla
verses.english: This has been consistently the case with all the messengers that we sent before you, and you will find that our system never changes.

1981.english: This has been the case with all the previous messengers, and you will find that our system is never changeable.

1989.english: This has been consistently the case with all the messengers that we sent before you, and you will find that our system never changes.

verses.arabic: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَقُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا
verses.arabicClean: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر ۖ إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا
verses.transliterated: aqimi l-ṣalata lidulūki l-shamsi ilā ghasaqi al-layli waqur'āna l-fajri inna qur'āna l-fajri kāna mashhūda
verses.english: You shall observe the Contact Prayer (Salat) when the sun declines from its highest point at noon, as it moves towards sunset. You shall also observe (the recitation of) the Quran at dawn. (Reciting) the Quran at dawn is witnessed.
verses.subtitle: The Noon Prayer

1981.english: You shall observe the **salat** prayers from sunrise to the darkness of night. And recite the Quran at dawn; the recitation of Quran at dawn is witnessed.
1981.subtitle: Attainment of the Highest Ranks

1989.english: You shall observe the contact prayer (Salat) when the sun declines from its highest point at noon, as it moves towards sunset. You shall also observe (the recitation of) the Quran at dawn. (Reciting) the Quran at dawn is witnessed.
1989.subtitle: The Noon Prayer

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةً لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَّحْمُودًا
verses.arabicClean: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا
verses.transliterated: wamina al-layli fatahajjad bihi nāfilatan laka ʿasā an yabʿathaka rabbuka maqāman maḥmūda
verses.english: During the night, you shall meditate for extra credit, that your Lord may raise you to an honorable rank.
verses.subtitle: Meditation

1981.english: During the night, you shall worship and meditate for extra credit, that your Lord may resurrect you in an exalted rank.

1989.english: During the night, you shall meditate for extra credit, that your Lord may raise you to an honorable rank.
1989.subtitle: Meditation

verses.arabic: وَقُل رَّبِّ أَدْخِلْنِى مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِى مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَٱجْعَل لِّى مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلْطَٰنًا نَّصِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا
verses.transliterated: waqul rabbi adkhil'nī mud'khala ṣid'qin wa-akhrij'nī mukh'raja ṣid'qin wa-ij'ʿal lī min ladunka sul'ṭānan naṣīra
verses.english: And say, "My Lord, admit me an honorable admittance, and let me depart an honorable departure, and grant me from You a powerful support."

1981.english: And say, "My Lord, grant me an honorable entry, and an honorable exit, and provide me with Your powerful support."

1989.english: And say, “My Lord, admit me an honorable admittance, and let me depart an honorable departure, and grant me from You a powerful support.”

verses.arabic: وَقُلْ جَآءَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلْبَٰطِلُ إِنَّ ٱلْبَٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقًا
verses.arabicClean: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل ۚ إن الباطل كان زهوقا
verses.transliterated: waqul jāa l-ḥaqu wazahaqa l-bāṭilu inna l-bāṭila kāna zahūqa
verses.english: Proclaim, "The truth has prevailed, and falsehood has vanished; falsehood will inevitably vanish."

1981.english: And say, "The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Surely, falsehood is destined to vanish."

1989.english: And proclaim, “The truth has prevailed, and falsehood has vanished; falsehood is destined to vanish.”

verses.arabic: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَا هُوَ شِفَآءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
verses.arabicClean: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ۙ ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا
verses.transliterated: wanunazzilu mina l-qur'āni mā huwa shifāon waraḥmatun lil'mu'minīna walā yazīdu l-ẓālimīna illā khasāra
verses.english: We send down in the Quran healing and mercy for the believers. At the same time, it only increases the wickedness of the transgressors.
verses.subtitle: Healing and Mercy

1981.english: We reveal in the Quran healing and mercy for the believers. As for the wicked, it only augments their wickedness.

1989.english: We send down in the Quran healing and mercy for the believers. At the same time, it only increases the wickedness of the transgressors.
1989.subtitle: Healing and Mercy

verses.arabic: وَإِذَآ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَـَٔا بِجَانِبِهِۦ وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ كَانَ يَـُٔوسًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه ۖ وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā anʿamnā ʿalā l-insāni aʿraḍa wanaā bijānibihi wa-idhā massahu l-sharu kāna yaūsa
verses.english: When we bless the human being, he becomes preoccupied and heedless. But when adversity strikes him, he turns despondent.

1981.english: When we endow the human, he turns away, prevented by his independence. And when adversity afflicts him, he turns desperate.

1989.english: When we bless the human being, he becomes preoccupied and heedless. But when adversity strikes him, he turns despondent.

verses.arabic: قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِۦ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا
verses.transliterated: qul kullun yaʿmalu ʿalā shākilatihi farabbukum aʿlamu biman huwa ahdā sabīla
verses.english: Say, "Everyone works in accordance with his belief, and your Lord knows best which ones are guided in the right path."

1981.english: Say, "Each will work according to his circumstances. Your Lord is fully aware which of you are the guided ones."

1989.english: Say, “Everyone works in accordance with his belief. Your Lord knows best which ones are guided in the right path.”

verses.arabic: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ويسألونك عن الروح ۖ قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا
verses.transliterated: wayasalūnaka ʿani l-rūḥi quli l-rūḥu min amri rabbī wamā ūtītum mina l-ʿil'mi illā qalīla
verses.english: They ask you about the revelation. Say, "The revelation comes from my Lord. The knowledge given to you is minute."
verses.subtitle: Divine Revelation: The Source of All Knowledge

1981.english: They ask you about this revelation. Say, "This revelation is from my Lord, and the knowledge given to you herein is minute."
1981.subtitle: Quran: God's Miraculous Revelation
1981.footnote: Previous translations, and interpretations, have erroneously referred to the word "Rooh" as "soul." The Quran, however, consistently uses this word to refer to divine revelations (see 16:2, 40:15, 58:22, and 97:4). Specifically, the Quran is described as "Rooh" in 42:52. The whole context clearly refers to God's revelation, and the interpretation of "Rooh" as "soul" will be taking it out of context. Verse 88 is a direct reference to the Quran's miraculous numerical code that this translation was exclusively blessed with unveiling. While many human beings did produce literary works as excellent as the Quran, no power on earth can duplicate the Quran's intricate numerical code (see Appendices 1 and 2 for details).

1989.english: They ask you about the revelation. Say, “The revelation comes from my Lord. The knowledge given to you is minute.”
1989.subtitle: Divine Revelation: The Source of All Knowledge

verses.arabic: وَلَئِن شِئْنَا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِۦ عَلَيْنَا وَكِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا
verses.transliterated: wala-in shi'nā lanadhhabanna bi-alladhī awḥaynā ilayka thumma lā tajidu laka bihi ʿalaynā wakīla
verses.english: If we will, we can take back what we revealed to you, then you will find no protector against us.

1981.english: If we will, we can take back what we revealed to you, then you will find no way to reach us.
1981.footnote: Previous translations, and interpretations, have erroneously referred to the word "Rooh" as "soul." The Quran, however, consistently uses this word to refer to divine revelations (see 16:2, 40:15, 58:22, and 97:4). Specifically, the Quran is described as "Rooh" in 42:52. The whole context clearly refers to God's revelation, and the interpretation of "Rooh" as "soul" will be taking it out of context. Verse 88 is a direct reference to the Quran's miraculous numerical code that this translation was exclusively blessed with unveiling. While many human beings did produce literary works as excellent as the Quran, no power on earth can duplicate the Quran's intricate numerical code (see Appendices 1 and 2 for details).

1989.english: If we will, we can take back what we revealed to you, then you will find no protector against us.

verses.arabic: إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ إِنَّ فَضْلَهُۥ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ كَبِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: إلا رحمة من ربك ۚ إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا
verses.transliterated: illā raḥmatan min rabbika inna faḍlahu kāna ʿalayka kabīra
verses.english: This is but mercy from your Lord. His blessings upon you have been great.

1981.english: This is but mercy from your Lord; indeed, His grace has been abundant towards you.
1981.footnote: Previous translations, and interpretations, have erroneously referred to the word "Rooh" as "soul." The Quran, however, consistently uses this word to refer to divine revelations (see 16:2, 40:15, 58:22, and 97:4). Specifically, the Quran is described as "Rooh" in 42:52. The whole context clearly refers to God's revelation, and the interpretation of "Rooh" as "soul" will be taking it out of context. Verse 88 is a direct reference to the Quran's miraculous numerical code that this translation was exclusively blessed with unveiling. While many human beings did produce literary works as excellent as the Quran, no power on earth can duplicate the Quran's intricate numerical code (see Appendices 1 and 2 for details).

1989.english: This is but mercy from your Lord. His blessings upon you have been great.

verses.arabic: قُل لَّئِنِ ٱجْتَمَعَتِ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتُوا۟ بِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِۦ وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا
verses.transliterated: qul la-ini ij'tamaʿati l-insu wal-jinu ʿalā an yatū bimith'li hādhā l-qur'āni lā yatūna bimith'lihi walaw kāna baʿḍuhum libaʿḍin ẓahīra
verses.english: Say, "If all the humans and all the jinns banded together in order to produce a Quran like this, they can never produce anything like it, no matter how much assistance they lent one another."
verses.subtitle: Mathematical Composition of the Quran

1981.english: Say, "If all the humans and all the jinns banded together to produce a Quran like this, they can never produce one like it, no matter how much assistance they lend one another."
1981.footnote: Previous translations, and interpretations, have erroneously referred to the word "Rooh" as "soul." The Quran, however, consistently uses this word to refer to divine revelations (see 16:2, 40:15, 58:22, and 97:4). Specifically, the Quran is described as "Rooh" in 42:52. The whole context clearly refers to God's revelation, and the interpretation of "Rooh" as "soul" will be taking it out of context. Verse 88 is a direct reference to the Quran's miraculous numerical code that this translation was exclusively blessed with unveiling. While many human beings did produce literary works as excellent as the Quran, no power on earth can duplicate the Quran's intricate numerical code (see Appendices 1 and 2 for details).

1989.english: Say, “If all the humans and all the jinns banded together in order to produce a Quran like this, they would surely fail, no matter how much assistance they lent one another.”
1989.subtitle: Mathematical Composition of the Quran

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِى هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا
verses.transliterated: walaqad ṣarrafnā lilnnāsi fī hādhā l-qur'āni min kulli mathalin fa-abā aktharu l-nāsi illā kufūra
verses.english: We have cited for the people in this Quran all kinds of examples, but most people insist upon disbelieving.

1981.english: And we cited for the people in this Quran all kinds of examples. But most people insist on disbelieving.
1981.footnote: Previous translations, and interpretations, have erroneously referred to the word "Rooh" as "soul." The Quran, however, consistently uses this word to refer to divine revelations (see 16:2, 40:15, 58:22, and 97:4). Specifically, the Quran is described as "Rooh" in 42:52. The whole context clearly refers to God's revelation, and the interpretation of "Rooh" as "soul" will be taking it out of context. Verse 88 is a direct reference to the Quran's miraculous numerical code that this translation was exclusively blessed with unveiling. While many human beings did produce literary works as excellent as the Quran, no power on earth can duplicate the Quran's intricate numerical code (see Appendices 1 and 2 for details).

1989.english: We have cited for the people in this Quran all kinds of examples, but most people insist upon disbelieving.

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا
verses.transliterated: waqālū lan nu'mina laka ḥattā tafjura lanā mina l-arḍi yanbūʿa
verses.english: They said, "We will not believe you unless you cause a spring to gush out of the ground.
verses.subtitle: God's Messengers Challenged

1981.english: They said, "We will not believe, unless you cause a spring to gush out of the ground.

1989.english: They said, “We will not believe you unless you cause a spring to gush out of the ground.
1989.subtitle: God’s Messengers Challenged

verses.arabic: أَوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَعِنَبٍ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفْجِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا
verses.transliterated: aw takūna laka jannatun min nakhīlin waʿinabin fatufajjira l-anhāra khilālahā tafjīra
verses.english: "Or unless you own a garden of date palms and grapes, with rivers running through it.

1981.english: "Or unless you acquire a garden of date palms and grapes, with rivers gushing generously therein.

1989.english: “Or unless you own a garden of date palms and grapes, with rivers running through it.

verses.arabic: أَوْ تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا أَوْ تَأْتِىَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا
verses.transliterated: aw tus'qiṭa l-samāa kamā zaʿamta ʿalaynā kisafan aw tatiya bil-lahi wal-malāikati qabīla
verses.english: "Or unless you cause masses from the sky, as you claimed, to fall on us. Or unless you bring GOD and the angels before our eyes.

1981.english: "Or unless you cause the sky to fall on us, as you claim, in masses; or bring God and the angels in a group.

1989.english: “Or unless you cause masses from the sky to fall on us, as you claimed. Or unless you bring GOD and the angels before our eyes.

verses.arabic: أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍ أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَٰبًا نَّقْرَؤُهُۥ قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
verses.arabicClean: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه ۗ قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا
verses.transliterated: aw yakūna laka baytun min zukh'rufin aw tarqā fī l-samāi walan nu'mina liruqiyyika ḥattā tunazzila ʿalaynā kitāban naqra-uhu qul sub'ḥāna rabbī hal kuntu illā basharan rasūla
verses.english: "Or unless you own a luxurious mansion, or unless you climb into the sky. Even if you do climb, we will not believe unless you bring a book that we can read." Say, "Glory be to my Lord. Am I any more than a human messenger?"
verses.footnote: God's Messenger of the Covenant, Rashad Khalifa, was thus challenged, including the challenge to bring a new book, or bring down masses from the sky. Verse 3:81 defines the duties of God's Messenger of the Covenant. Overwhelming proof is detailed in Appendices 2 & 26.

1981.english: "Or unless you possess a luxurious mansion, or climb into the sky. Even if you climb, we will not believe, unless you bring down a book that we can read." Say, "God be glorified; am I any more than a human messenger?"

1989.english: “Or unless you own a luxurious mansion, or unless you climb into the sky. Even if you do, we will not believe unless you bring a new book that we can read.”* Say, “Glory be to my Lord. Am I any more than a human messenger?”
1989.footnote: God’s Messenger of the Covenant, Rashad Khalifa, was thus challenged, including the challenge to bring a new book. Verse 3:81 defines the duties of God’s Messenger of the Covenant. Overwhelming proof is detailed in Appendices 2 & 26.

verses.arabic: وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا
verses.arabicClean: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا
verses.transliterated: wamā manaʿa l-nāsa an yu'minū idh jāahumu l-hudā illā an qālū abaʿatha l-lahu basharan rasūla
verses.english: What prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, is their saying, "Did GOD send a human being as a messenger?"
verses.subtitle: Messengership: An Essential Test

1981.english: Thus, what prevented the people from believing, when the guidance came to them, is their saying, "How could God send a human messenger?"

1989.english: What prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, is their saying, “Did GOD send a human being as a messenger?’
1989.subtitle: Messengership: An Essential Test

verses.arabic: قُل لَّوْ كَانَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَلَكًا رَّسُولًا
verses.arabicClean: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا
verses.transliterated: qul law kāna fī l-arḍi malāikatun yamshūna muṭ'ma-innīna lanazzalnā ʿalayhim mina l-samāi malakan rasūla
verses.english: Say, "If the earth were inhabited by angels, we would have sent down to them from the sky an angel messenger."

1981.english: Say, "If the earth were inhabited by angels, we would have sent down from the sky an angel messenger."

1989.english: Say, “If the earth were inhabited by angels, we would have sent down to them from the sky an angel messenger.”

verses.arabic: قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدًۢا بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًۢا بَصِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ۚ إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا
verses.transliterated: qul kafā bil-lahi shahīdan baynī wabaynakum innahu kāna biʿibādihi khabīran baṣīra
verses.english: Say, "GOD suffices as a witness between me and you. He is fully Cognizant of His worshipers, Seer."
verses.subtitle: God Is My Witness

1981.english: Say, "God suffices as witness between me and you; He is fully cognizant of His servants, seer."

1989.english: Say, “GOD suffices as a witness between me and you. He is fully Cognizant of His worshipers, Seer.”
1989.subtitle: God Is My Witness

verses.arabic: وَمَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلْمُهْتَدِ وَمَن يُضْلِلْ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِهِۦ وَنَحْشُرُهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ عُمْيًا وَبُكْمًا وَصُمًّا مَّأْوَىٰهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَٰهُمْ سَعِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ۖ ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ۖ ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما ۖ مأواهم جهنم ۖ كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا
verses.transliterated: waman yahdi l-lahu fahuwa l-muh'tadi waman yuḍ'lil falan tajida lahum awliyāa min dūnihi wanaḥshuruhum yawma l-qiyāmati ʿalā wujūhihim ʿum'yan wabuk'man waṣumman mawāhum jahannamu kullamā khabat zid'nāhum saʿīra
verses.english: Whomever GOD guides is the truly guided one. And whomever He sends astray, you will never find for them any lords and masters beside Him. We will summon them on the Day of Resurrection forcibly; blind, dumb, and deaf. Their destination is Hell; whenever it cools down, we will increase their fire.

1981.english: Whomever God guides is the truly guided one. As for those whom He sends astray, you will find no allies to help them against Him, and we gather them forcibly on the day of resurrection, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their final abode is hell; whenever it cools down, we re-ignite their fire.

1989.english: Whomever GOD guides is the truly guided one. And whomever He sends astray, you will never find protectors for them. We will summon them on the Day of Resurrection, forcibly, and they will be blind, dumb, and deaf. Their destination is Hell; whenever it cools down, we will increase its fire.

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا وَرُفَٰتًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا
verses.arabicClean: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا
verses.transliterated: dhālika jazāuhum bi-annahum kafarū biāyātinā waqālū a-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman warufātan a-innā lamabʿūthūna khalqan jadīda
verses.english: Such is their just retribution, since they rejected our revelations. They said, "After we turn into bones and fragments, do we get resurrected into a new creation?"
verses.subtitle: Their Innermost Thoughts

1981.english: This is their just retribution, for they rejected our revelations and said, "After we become bones and fragments, do we get created anew?"

1989.english: Such is their just retribution, since they rejected our revelations. They said, “After we turn into bones and fragments, do we get resurrected anew?”

verses.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ قَادِرٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَجَلًا لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَأَبَى ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
verses.arabicClean: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا
verses.transliterated: awalam yaraw anna l-laha alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa qādirun ʿalā an yakhluqa mith'lahum wajaʿala lahum ajalan lā rayba fīhi fa-abā l-ẓālimūna illā kufūra
verses.english: Could they not see that the GOD who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the same creations? He has predetermined for them an irrevocable life span? Yet, the disbelievers insist upon disbelieving.

1981.english: Do they not realize that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the same? And He predetermined an inevitable end for their life; but the wicked insist upon disbelieving.

1989.english: Do they not realize that GOD, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to recreate the same creations? (Also, do they not see that) He has predetermined for them an irrevocable life span? Yet, the disbelievers insist upon disbelieving.

verses.arabic: قُل لَّوْ أَنتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزَآئِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّىٓ إِذًا لَّأَمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ ٱلْإِنفَاقِ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ قَتُورًا
verses.arabicClean: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق ۚ وكان الإنسان قتورا
verses.transliterated: qul law antum tamlikūna khazāina raḥmati rabbī idhan la-amsaktum khashyata l-infāqi wakāna l-insānu qatūra
verses.english: Proclaim, "If you possessed my Lord's treasures of mercy, you would have withheld them, fearing that you might exhaust them. The human being is stingy."

1981.english: Say, "If you take possession of my Lord's treasures of mercy, you would be too stingy to spend therefrom; the human being is parsimonious."

1989.english: Proclaim, “If you possessed my Lord’s treasures of mercy, you would have withheld them, fearing that you might exhaust them The human being is stingy.”

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ فَسْـَٔلْ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ فَقَالَ لَهُۥ فِرْعَوْنُ إِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ مَسْحُورًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات ۖ فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا
verses.transliterated: walaqad ātaynā mūsā tis'ʿa āyātin bayyinātin fasal banī is'rāīla idh jāahum faqāla lahu fir'ʿawnu innī la-aẓunnuka yāmūsā masḥūra
verses.english: We supported Moses with nine profound miracles—ask the Children of Israel. When he went to them, Pharaoh said to him, "I think that you, Moses, are bewitched."
verses.subtitle: Moses and Pharaoh

1981.english: We gave Moses nine miracles, so ask the children of Israel. When he went to them, Pharaoh said to him, "I think you are bewitched, Moses."
1981.subtitle: Muslims and Jews: the Great Parallel
1981.footnote: The frequency of mentioning Moses and his followers throughout the Quran is noteworthy, and points out the great parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad. God gave the Torah to the followers of Moses and asked them to uphold it strongly (2:63). But around A.D. 200, the "scholars and sages" of Judaism invented the Mishnah and the Gemara, which make up the Talmud, and eventually replaced the Torah. Similarly, God gave the Muslims the Quran and asked them to uphold it. But 250 years after Muhammad, the "scholars and sages" of Islam invented the "Hadith" and "Sunna" which replaced and abrogated the Quran (see 24:1-2). This amazing parallel explains the frequency of narration of Israel's history.

1989.english: We supported Moses with nine profound miracles—ask the Children of Israel. When he went to them, Pharaoh said to him, “I think that you, Moses, are bewitched.”
1989.subtitle: Moses and Pharaoh

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ بَصَآئِرَ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰفِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا
verses.arabicClean: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا
verses.transliterated: qāla laqad ʿalim'ta mā anzala hāulāi illā rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi baṣāira wa-innī la-aẓunnuka yāfir'ʿawnu mathbūra
verses.english: He said, "You know full well that no one can manifest these except, obviously, the Lord of the heavens and the earth. I think that you, Pharaoh, are doomed."

1981.english: He said, "You know well that none can manifest these profound miracles except the Lord of the heavens and the earth. I think you are doomed, Pharaoh."

God gave the Torah to the followers of Moses and asked them to uphold it strongly (2:63). But around A.D. 200, the "scholars and sages" of Judaism invented the Mishnah and the Gemara, which make up the Talmud, and eventually replaced the Torah. Similarly, God gave the Muslims the Quran and asked them to uphold it. But 250 years after Muhammad, the "scholars and sages" of Islam invented the "Hadith" and "Sunna" which replaced and abrogated the Quran (see 24:1-2). 1989.english: He said, “You know full well that no one can manifest these except, obviously, the Lord of the heavens and the earth. I think that you, Pharaoh, are doomed.”

verses.arabic: فَأَرَادَ أَن يَسْتَفِزَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا
verses.arabicClean: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا
verses.transliterated: fa-arāda an yastafizzahum mina l-arḍi fa-aghraqnāhu waman maʿahu jamīʿa
verses.english: When he pursued them, as he chased them out of the land, we drowned him, together with those who sided with him, all of them.

1981.english: He then wanted to oppress them throughout the land, but we drowned him and all his troops.

God gave the Torah to the followers of Moses and asked them to uphold it strongly (2:63). But around A.D. 200, the "scholars and sages" of Judaism invented the Mishnah and the Gemara, which make up the Talmud, and eventually replaced the Torah. 1989.english: When he pursued them, as he chased them out of the land, we drowned him, together with those who sided with him, all of them.

verses.arabic: وَقُلْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ لِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱسْكُنُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ جِئْنَا بِكُمْ لَفِيفًا
verses.arabicClean: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا
verses.transliterated: waqul'nā min baʿdihi libanī is'rāīla us'kunū l-arḍa fa-idhā jāa waʿdu l-ākhirati ji'nā bikum lafīfa
verses.english: And we said to the Children of Israel afterwards, "Go live in this land. When the final prophecy comes to pass, we will summon you all in one group."

1981.english: And we said to the children of Israel after him, "Inhabit the land, and when the second prophecy* comes to pass, we will gather you together."
1981.footnote: Could this be the gathering of the Jews into the state of Israel? See 17:4-7.

1989.english: And we said to the Children of Israel afterwards, “Go live in this land. When the final prophecy comes to pass, we will bring you all together.”

verses.arabic: وَبِٱلْحَقِّ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ وَبِٱلْحَقِّ نَزَلَ وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل ۗ وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا
verses.transliterated: wabil-ḥaqi anzalnāhu wabil-ḥaqi nazala wamā arsalnāka illā mubashiran wanadhīra
verses.english: Truthfully, we sent it down, and with the truth it came down. We did not send you except as a bearer of good news, as well as a warner.
verses.subtitle: The Quran Released Slowly To Facilitate Memorization

1981.english: Similarly, we reveal this truthfully, and we reveal the truth herein. We send you (O Muhammad) as no more than a preacher and warner.
1981.footnote: The frequency of mentioning Moses and his followers throughout the Quran is noteworthy, and points out the great parallel between the followers of Moses and the followers of Muhammad. God gave the Torah to the followers of Moses and asked them to uphold it strongly (2:63). But around A.D. 200, the "scholars and sages" of Judaism invented the Mishnah and the Gemara, which make up the Talmud, and eventually replaced the Torah. Similarly, God gave the Muslims the Quran and asked them to uphold it. But 250 years after Muhammad, the "scholars and sages" of Islam invented the "Hadith" and "Sunna" which replaced and abrogated the Quran (see 24:1-2). This amazing parallel explains the frequency of narration of Israel's history.

1989.english: Truthfully, we sent it down, and with the truth it came down. We did not send you except as a bearer of good news, as well as a warner.
1989.subtitle: The Quran Released Slowly To Facilitate Memorization

verses.arabic: وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَٰهُ تَنزِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا
verses.transliterated: waqur'ānan faraqnāhu litaqra-ahu ʿalā l-nāsi ʿalā muk'thin wanazzalnāhu tanzīla
verses.english: A Quran that we have released slowly, in order for you to read it to the people over a long period, although we sent it down all at once.

1981.english: This is a Quran that we decreed to be released to the people by you, over a long period, though we sent it down all at once.
1981.footnote: Muhammad's soul was summoned, and the Quran was given to him all at once, in the same manner as Adam's acquisition of knowledge (2:31). The process of revelation to Muhammad is described in 53:1-18. This verse teaches us that, although the Quran was revealed into Muhammad's heart all at once (16:102), God decreed that it shall be "released" from Muhammad's heart to the people over a long period of time. Please see 2:185, 17:1, 44:3, and 97:1.

1989.english: It is a Quran that we have released slowly, in order for you to read it to the people over a long period, although we sent it down all at once.

verses.arabic: قُلْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِهِۦٓ أَوْ لَا تُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦٓ إِذَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ سُجَّدًا
verses.arabicClean: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا ۚ إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا
verses.transliterated: qul āminū bihi aw lā tu'minū inna alladhīna ūtū l-ʿil'ma min qablihi idhā yut'lā ʿalayhim yakhirrūna lil'adhqāni sujjada
verses.english: Proclaim, "Believe in it, or do not believe in it." Those who possess knowledge from the previous scriptures, when it is recited to them, they fall down to their chins, prostrating.

1981.english: Say, "Believe therein, or disbelieve. Those who possess knowledge before it is recited for them, fall down to their chins prostrating."

1989.english: Proclaim, “Believe in it, or do not believe in it.” Those who possess knowledge from the previous scriptures, when it is recited to them, they immediately fall down on their chins, in prostration.

verses.arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِن كَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّنَا لَمَفْعُولًا
verses.arabicClean: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا
verses.transliterated: wayaqūlūna sub'ḥāna rabbinā in kāna waʿdu rabbinā lamafʿūla
verses.english: They say, "Glory be to our Lord. This fulfills our Lord's prophecy."

1981.english: And they say, "Glory be to our Lord; the promise of our Lord has come true."
1981.footnote: See Deuteronomy 18:15 and 18:18-19, John 14:16-17, and John 16:13.

1989.english: They say, “Glory be to our Lord. Our Lord’s promise is fulfilled.”

verses.arabic: وَيَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ يَبْكُونَ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ خُشُوعًا
verses.arabicClean: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا ۩
verses.transliterated: wayakhirrūna lil'adhqāni yabkūna wayazīduhum khushūʿa
verses.english: They fall down on their chins, prostrating and weeping. For it augments their reverence.

1981.english: They fall down to their chins, weeping, for it increases their reverence.

1989.english: They fall down on their chins, prostrating, as they weep, for it augments their reverence.

verses.arabic: قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ أَيًّا مَّا تَدْعُوا۟ فَلَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَلَا تَجْهَرْ بِصَلَاتِكَ وَلَا تُخَافِتْ بِهَا وَٱبْتَغِ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن ۖ أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ۚ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا
verses.transliterated: quli id'ʿū l-laha awi id'ʿū l-raḥmāna ayyan mā tadʿū falahu l-asmāu l-ḥus'nā walā tajhar biṣalātika walā tukhāfit bihā wa-ib'taghi bayna dhālika sabīla
verses.english: Say, "Call Him GOD, or call Him Most Gracious; whichever name you use, to Him belongs the best names." You shall not utter your Contact Prayers (Salat) too loudly, nor secretly; use a moderate tone.
verses.subtitle: Tone of the Contact Prayers (Salat)

1981.english: Say, "Call Him God, or call Him Al-Rahman (the most gracious); whichever name you call Him by, He possesses the most beautiful names." And do not be too loud when you say your **salat** prayers, nor too low; but use a moderate tone.

1989.english: Say, “Call upon GOD, or call upon the Most Gracious; whichever name you use, to Him belongs the most beautiful names.” Do not utter your contact prayers (Salat) too loudly, nor secretly; you shall use a moderate tone.
1989.subtitle: Tone of the Contact Prayers (Salat)

verses.arabic: وَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِىٌّ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّ وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًۢا
verses.arabicClean: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل ۖ وكبره تكبيرا
verses.transliterated: waquli l-ḥamdu lillahi alladhī lam yattakhidh waladan walam yakun lahu sharīkun fī l-mul'ki walam yakun lahu waliyyun mina l-dhuli wakabbir'hu takbīra
verses.english: And proclaim: "Praise be to GOD, who has never begotten a son, nor does He have a partner in His kingship, nor does He need any ally out of weakness," and magnify Him constantly.

1981.english: And say, "Praise God; who has never taken a son for Himself, nor does He have a partner in kingship, nor does He need any ally out of weakness;" you shall magnify Him constantly.

1989.english: And proclaim: “Praise be to GOD, who has never begotten a son, nor does He have a partner in His kingship, nor does He need any ally out of weakness.” You shall magnify Him constantly. ( >

verses.arabic: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُۥ عِوَجَا
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا ۜ
verses.transliterated: al-ḥamdu lillahi alladhī anzala ʿalā ʿabdihi l-kitāba walam yajʿal lahu ʿiwaj
verses.english: Praise GOD, who revealed to His servant this scripture, and made it flawless.

1981.english: Praise be to God, who sent down the scripture to His servant, and made it flawless.

1989.english: Praise GOD, who revealed to His servant this scripture, and made it flawless.

verses.arabic: قَيِّمًا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا
verses.arabicClean: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا
verses.transliterated: qayyiman liyundhira basan shadīdan min ladun'hu wayubashira l-mu'minīna alladhīna yaʿmalūna l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum ajran ḥasana
verses.english: A perfect (scripture) to warn of severe retribution from Him, and to deliver good news to the believers who lead a righteous life, that they have earned a generous recompense.

1981.english: (He made it) perfect, in order to warn of severe retribution from Him, and to bear good news for the believers who work righteousness, that they have deserved a delightful recompense.

1989.english: A perfect (scripture) to warn of severe retribution from Him, and to deliver good news to the believers who lead a righteous life, that they have earned a beautiful recompense.

verses.arabic: مَّٰكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًا
verses.arabicClean: ماكثين فيه أبدا
verses.transliterated: mākithīna fīhi abada
verses.english: Wherein they abide forever.

1981.english: They abide therein forever.

1989.english: Wherein they abide forever.

verses.arabic: وَيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدًا
verses.arabicClean: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا
verses.transliterated: wayundhira alladhīna qālū ittakhadha l-lahu walada
verses.english: And to warn those who said, "GOD has begotten a son!"

1981.english: And to warn those who claimed that God has taken a son for Himself.

1989.english: And to warn those who said, “GOD has begotten a son!”

verses.arabic: مَّا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلَا لِءَابَآئِهِمْ كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ إِن يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًا
verses.arabicClean: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم ۚ كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم ۚ إن يقولون إلا كذبا
verses.transliterated: mā lahum bihi min ʿil'min walā liābāihim kaburat kalimatan takhruju min afwāhihim in yaqūlūna illā kadhiba
verses.english: They possess no knowledge about this, nor did their parents. What a blasphemy coming out of their mouths! What they utter is a gross lie.

1981.english: They have no real knowledge thereof, nor did their ancestors. Gross indeed is such an utterance, coming out of their mouths. It is a lie.

1989.english: They possess no knowledge about this, nor did their parents. What a blasphemy comes out of their mouths! What they utter is a gross lie.

verses.arabic: فَلَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِهَٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا
verses.arabicClean: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا
verses.transliterated: falaʿallaka bākhiʿun nafsaka ʿalā āthārihim in lam yu'minū bihādhā l-ḥadīthi asafa
verses.english: You may blame yourself on account of their response to this narration, and their disbelieving in it; you may be saddened.

1981.english: Yet, you may blame yourself on their account, that they do not accept this **hadith** (message), and you may be saddened.

1989.english: You may blame yourself on account of them, because they do not believe in this narration, and you may be saddened.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَّهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا
verses.arabicClean: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا
verses.transliterated: innā jaʿalnā mā ʿalā l-arḍi zīnatan lahā linabluwahum ayyuhum aḥsanu ʿamala
verses.english: We have adorned everything on earth, in order to test them, and thus distinguish those among them who work righteousness.
verses.subtitle: The End of the World

1981.english: We created everything on earth, as adornment, in order to test them therewith and distinguish the good doers.

1989.english: We have adorned everything on earth, in order to test them therewith, and distinguish those among them who work righteousness.
1989.subtitle: The End of the World

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّا لَجَٰعِلُونَ مَا عَلَيْهَا صَعِيدًا جُرُزًا
verses.arabicClean: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا
verses.transliterated: wa-innā lajāʿilūna mā ʿalayhā ṣaʿīdan juruza
verses.english: Inevitably, we will wipe out everything on it, leaving it completely barren.
verses.footnote: As it turns out, the history of these Christian believers, the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus, is directly connected with the end of the world as stated in 18:9 & 21. The role of these believers in unveiling the end of the world is detailed in Appendix 25.

1981.english: Inevitably, we will wipe out everything therein, making it a barren land.

1989.english: Inevitably, we will wipe out everything therein, leaving it barren.*
1989.footnote: As it turns out, the history of these Christian believers, the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus, is directly connected with the end of the world as stated in 18:9 & 21. The role of these believers in unveiling the end of the world is detailed in Appendix 25.

verses.arabic: أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا۟ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
verses.arabicClean: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا
verses.transliterated: am ḥasib'ta anna aṣḥāba l-kahfi wal-raqīmi kānū min āyātinā ʿajaba
verses.english: Why else do you think we are telling you about the people of the cave, and the numbers connected with them? They are among our wondrous signs.
verses.subtitle: The Dwellers of the Cave

1981.english: You may consider the people of the cave, and their number, among our wondrous marvels.
1981.subtitle: The Seven Sleepers of Ephesus
1981.footnote: Many variations of this story are found in the various encyclopedias, and the world literature. The Quran sets the record straight. The "Christian" literature generally claims that these youth were running away from the Romans' persecution. But the divine truth herein teaches us that they actually ran away from the Christians who deviated from the teachings of Christ, and idolized him against his will; they wanted to worship God alone and recognized Jesus as a great teacher. Note that the history of these righteous Ephesians coincides with the period of turmoil that resulted in convening the Councils of Nicene, and permanent distortion of Christianity through the Nicene Creed. This is the Creed that invented the Trinity doctrine, according to all recognized encyclopedias, and the Vatican's own encyclopedia. The seven sleepers of Ephesus wanted to practice the true teachings of Christ, and rejected the false doctrines, such as the Trinity. Ephesus was an ancient Turkish city, 35 miles south of today's Izmir, and was famous for its Temple of Artemis, one of the ancient seven wonders of the world. It later became the leading Christian community of Asia. In 1928, an Austrian archeologist called Franz Miltner found a tomb near Ephesus which proved that the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus actually existed, and that their story is a historical fact. The ultimate truth, of course, is narrated here by the almighty creator of the universe.

1989.english: Why else do you think we are telling you about the people of the cave, and the numbers connected with them? They are among our wondrous signs.
1989.footnote: As it turns out, the history of these Christian believers, the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus, is directly connected with the end of the world as stated in 18:9 & 21. The role of these believers in unveiling the end of the world is detailed in Appendix 25.

verses.arabicClean: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا
verses.transliterated: idh awā l-fit'yatu ilā l-kahfi faqālū rabbanā ātinā min ladunka raḥmatan wahayyi lanā min amrinā rashada
verses.english: When the youths took refuge in the cave, they said, "Our Lord, shower us with Your mercy, and bless our affairs with Your guidance."

1981.english: Thus, some youths took refuge in the cave, saying, "Our Lord, grant us mercy from You, and direct us rightly in our affairs."

verses.arabic: فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ فِى ٱلْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدًا

verses.transliterated: faḍarabnā ʿalā ādhānihim fī l-kahfi sinīna ʿadada
verses.english: We then sealed their ears in the cave for a predetermined number of years.

verses.arabicClean: وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم ليعلموا أن وعد الله حق وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها إذ يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم ۖ فقالوا ابنوا عليهم بنيانا ۖ ربهم أعلم بهم ۚ قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika aʿtharnā ʿalayhim liyaʿlamū anna waʿda l-lahi ḥaqqun wa-anna l-sāʿata lā rayba fīhā idh yatanāzaʿūna baynahum amrahum faqālū ib'nū ʿalayhim bun'yānan rabbuhum aʿlamu bihim qāla alladhīna ghalabū ʿalā amrihim lanattakhidhanna ʿalayhim masjida
verses.english: We caused them to be discovered, to let everyone know that GOD's promise is true, and to remove all doubt concerning the end of the world. The people then disputed among themselves regarding them. Some said, "Let us build a building around them." Their Lord is the best knower about them. Those who prevailed said, "We will build a place of worship around them."
verses.subtitle: Connection With the End of the World
verses.footnote: As detailed in Appendix 25, this story helped pinpoint the end of the world.

1981.english: We thus allowed the people to find them, in order for them to realize that God's promise is truth, and that the hour is inevitable. They then conferred with each other about them, and some of them said, "Let us erect a building over them, their Lord knows best about them." Their leaders finally said, "Let us build a place of worship to commemorate them."
1981.footnote: The recognized encyclopedias state that Emperor Theodosius II believed a miracle had taken place, and had a great church built to mark the spot where the seven sleepers of Ephesus had slept.

1989.english: We caused them to be discovered to let them know that GOD’s promise is true and to remove all doubt concerning the end of the world.* The people disputed among themselves regarding them (the dwellers of the cavet They said, “Let us build a building for them. 1989.footnote: As detailed in Appendix 25, this story helped pinpoint the end of the world.

verses.transliterated: sayaqūlūna thalāthatun rābiʿuhum kalbuhum wayaqūlūna khamsatun sādisuhum kalbuhum rajman bil-ghaybi wayaqūlūna sabʿatun wathāminuhum kalbuhum qul rabbī aʿlamu biʿiddatihim mā yaʿlamuhum illā qalīlun falā tumāri fīhim illā mirāan ẓāhiran walā tastafti fīhim min'hum aḥada
verses.english: Some would say, "They were three; their dog being the fourth," while others would say, "Five; the sixth being their dog," as they guessed. Others said, "Seven," and the eighth was their dog. Say, "My Lord is the best knower of their number." Only a few knew the correct number. Therefore, do not argue with them; just go along with them. You need not consult anyone about this.

verses.english: You shall not say that you will do anything in the future,
verses.subtitle: Remembering God Every Chance We Get

verses.arabic: إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ وَقُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّى لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَٰذَا رَشَدًا

verses.arabic: وَلَبِثُوا۟ فِى كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلَٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًا
verses.arabicClean: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا
verses.transliterated: walabithū fī kahfihim thalātha mi-atin sinīna wa-iz'dādū tis'ʿa
verses.english: They stayed in their cave three hundred years, increased by nine.
verses.footnote: The difference between 300 solar years and 300 lunar years is nine years. Thus, discovering the end of the world was predetermined by the Almighty to take place in 1980 AD (1400 AH), 300 years (309 lunar years) before the end of the world (see 72:27 & Appendix 25).

1981.english: They stayed in their cave three hundred years, plus nine.
1981.footnote: Another valuable lesson we learn is that the period of our death will pass like one night of sleep (see Appendix 14 for details, and 2:259).

1989.english: They stayed in their cave three hundred years, increased by nine.*

verses.arabicClean: قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا ۖ له غيب السماوات والأرض ۖ أبصر به وأسمع ۚ ما لهم من دونه من ولي ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا
verses.transliterated: quli l-lahu aʿlamu bimā labithū lahu ghaybu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi abṣir bihi wa-asmiʿ mā lahum min dūnihi min waliyyin walā yush'riku fī ḥuk'mihi aḥada
verses.english: Say, "GOD is the best knower of how long they stayed there." He knows all secrets in the heavens and the earth. By His grace you can see; by His grace you can hear. There is none beside Him as Lord and Master, and He never permits any partners to share in His kingship.

verses.arabic: وَٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِن كِتَابِ رَبِّكَ لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمَٰتِهِۦ وَلَن تَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلْتَحَدًا
verses.arabicClean: واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك ۖ لا مبدل لكلماته ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا
verses.transliterated: wa-ut'lu mā ūḥiya ilayka min kitābi rabbika lā mubaddila likalimātihi walan tajida min dūnihi mul'taḥada
verses.english: You shall recite what is revealed to you of your Lord's scripture. Nothing shall abrogate His words, and you shall not find any other source beside it.

1981.english: You shall recite what is revealed to you from your Lord; nothing shall abrogate His words, and you shall not find any other source besides it.
1981.subtitle: Quran Revealed to All of Us Through Muhammad
1981.footnote: See also 42:51.

1989.english: You shall recite what was revealed to you of your Lord’s scripture. Nothing shall abrogate His words, and you shall not find any other source besides it.

verses.arabicClean: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ۖ ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ۖ ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا
verses.transliterated: wa-iṣ'bir nafsaka maʿa alladhīna yadʿūna rabbahum bil-ghadati wal-ʿashiyi yurīdūna wajhahu walā taʿdu ʿaynāka ʿanhum turīdu zīnata l-ḥayati l-dun'yā walā tuṭiʿ man aghfalnā qalbahu ʿan dhik'rinā wa-ittabaʿa hawāhu wakāna amruhu furuṭa
verses.english: You shall force yourself to be with those who worship their Lord day and night, seeking Him alone. Do not turn your eyes away from them, seeking the vanities of this world. Nor shall you obey one whose heart we rendered oblivious to our message; one who pursues his own desires, and whose priorities are confused.
verses.subtitle: Quranic Study Groups

1981.english: You shall force yourself to stay with those who worship their Lord day and night, seeking only Him, and do not divert your eyes from them, seeking the vanities of this life. And do not obey anyone whose heart we render unaware of our message, and follows his own opinions, and thus his efforts are in vain.

1989.english: You shall force yourself to stay with those who worship their Lord day and night seeking Him alone. Do not turn your eyes away from them, seeking the vanities of this world. Nor shall you obey one whose heart we rendered oblivious to our message; one who pursues his own desires, and whose priorities are confused.
1989.subtitle: Quranic Study Groups

verses.arabic: وَقُلِ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ فَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن وَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ إِنَّآ أَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ نَارًا أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُوا۟ يُغَاثُوا۟ بِمَآءٍ كَٱلْمُهْلِ يَشْوِى ٱلْوُجُوهَ بِئْسَ ٱلشَّرَابُ وَسَآءَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا
verses.arabicClean: وقل الحق من ربكم ۖ فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر ۚ إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها ۚ وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه ۚ بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا
verses.transliterated: waquli l-ḥaqu min rabbikum faman shāa falyu'min waman shāa falyakfur innā aʿtadnā lilẓẓālimīna nāran aḥāṭa bihim surādiquhā wa-in yastaghīthū yughāthū bimāin kal-muh'li yashwī l-wujūha bi'sa l-sharābu wasāat mur'tafaqa
verses.english: Proclaim: "This is the truth from your Lord," then whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve. We have prepared for the transgressors a fire that will completely surround them. When they scream for help, they will be given a liquid like concentrated acid that scalds the faces. What a miserable drink! What a miserable destiny!
verses.subtitle: Absolute Freedom of Religion

1981.english: You shall say, "This is the truth from your Lord," then whoever wishes let him believe, and whoever wishes let him disbelieve. We have prepared for the wicked a fire that surrounds them completely. When they plead for water, they get a drink like lava, that burns their faces. What a miserable drink, and a miserable abode!
1981.subtitle: Freedom to Believe or Disbelieve

1989.english: Proclaim: “This is the truth from your Lord,” then whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve. We have prepared for the transgressors a fire that will completely surround them. When they scream for help, they will be given a liquid like concentrated acid that scalds the faces. 1989.subtitle: Absolute Freedom of Religion

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا
verses.arabicClean: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا
verses.transliterated: inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti innā lā nuḍīʿu ajra man aḥsana ʿamala
verses.english: As for those who believe and lead a righteous life, we never fail to recompense those who work righteousness.

1981.english: As for those who believe and lead a righteous life, we never fail to reward the good doers.

1989.english: As for those who believe and lead a righteous life, we never fail to reward those who work righteousness.

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهِمُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِيَابًا خُضْرًا مِّن سُندُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُّتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا عَلَى ٱلْأَرَآئِكِ نِعْمَ ٱلثَّوَابُ وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا
verses.arabicClean: أولئك لهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتهم الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ويلبسون ثيابا خضرا من سندس وإستبرق متكئين فيها على الأرائك ۚ نعم الثواب وحسنت مرتفقا
verses.transliterated: ulāika lahum jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihimu l-anhāru yuḥallawna fīhā min asāwira min dhahabin wayalbasūna thiyāban khuḍ'ran min sundusin wa-is'tabraqin muttakiīna fīhā ʿalā l-arāiki niʿ'ma l-thawābu waḥasunat mur'tafaqa
verses.english: They have deserved gardens of Eden wherein rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and will wear clothes of green silk and velvet, and will rest on comfortable furnishings. What a wonderful reward; what a wonderful abode!

1981.english: These have deserved the gardens of Eden, where rivers flow beneath them. They will be adorned with bracelets of gold, and wear green garments of silk and velvet. They relax therein on comfortable furnishings. What a beautiful reward, and a beautiful abode!
1981.footnote: See Appendix 4 for details of this allegorical description of heaven.

1989.english: They have deserved gardens of Eden wherein rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and will wear clothes of green silk and velvet, and will rest on comfortable furnishings. What a beautiful reward, and a beautiful abode!

verses.arabic: وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا رَّجُلَيْنِ جَعَلْنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيْنِ مِنْ أَعْنَٰبٍ وَحَفَفْنَٰهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمَا زَرْعًا
verses.arabicClean: واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا
verses.transliterated: wa-iḍ'rib lahum mathalan rajulayni jaʿalnā li-aḥadihimā jannatayni min aʿnābin waḥafafnāhumā binakhlin wajaʿalnā baynahumā zarʿa
verses.english: Cite for them the example of two men: we gave one of them two gardens of grapes, surrounded by date palms, and placed other crops between them.
verses.subtitle: Property as an Idol
verses.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship beside God; they include children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

1981.english: Cite for them the parable of two men; one of them we endowed with two orchards of grapes, surrounded them with date palms, and interspersed them with crops.
1981.subtitle: Do Not Idolize Your Material Properties

1989.english: Cite for them the example of two men: we gave one of them two gardens of grapes, surrounded by date palms, and placed other crops between them.
1989.subtitle: Property as an Idol
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: كِلْتَا ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ ءَاتَتْ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمْ تَظْلِم مِّنْهُ شَيْـًٔا وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرًا
verses.arabicClean: كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها ولم تظلم منه شيئا ۚ وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا
verses.transliterated: kil'tā l-janatayni ātat ukulahā walam taẓlim min'hu shayan wafajjarnā khilālahumā nahara
verses.english: Both gardens produced their crops on time, and generously, for we caused a river to run through them.

1981.english: Both orchards produced generously, and never failed. We had a river gush through them.

1989.english: Both gardens produced their crops generously, for we caused a river to run through them.
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: وَكَانَ لَهُۥ ثَمَرٌ فَقَالَ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَنَا۠ أَكْثَرُ مِنكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا
verses.arabicClean: وكان له ثمر فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا
verses.transliterated: wakāna lahu thamarun faqāla liṣāḥibihi wahuwa yuḥāwiruhu anā aktharu minka mālan wa-aʿazzu nafara
verses.english: Once, after harvesting, he boastfully told his friend: "I am far more prosperous than you, and I command more respect from the people."

1981.english: As he noted the fruits therein, he said to his friend who debated with him, "I am richer than you are and have more children."

1989.english: Once, after harvesting, he was debating with his friend: “I am far more prosperous than you, and I have more children.”
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا
verses.arabicClean: ودخل جنته وهو ظالم لنفسه قال ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا
verses.transliterated: wadakhala jannatahu wahuwa ẓālimun linafsihi qāla mā aẓunnu an tabīda hādhihi abada
verses.english: When he entered his garden, he wronged his soul by saying, "I do not think that this will ever end.

1981.english: And he entered his orchard in a state of wickedness, saying, "I do not think that this can ever vanish.

1989.english: He entered his garden, and wronged his soul by saying, “I am secure for life; I do not think that this will ever end.
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةً وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا مُنقَلَبًا
verses.arabicClean: وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا
verses.transliterated: wamā aẓunnu l-sāʿata qāimatan wala-in rudidttu ilā rabbī la-ajidanna khayran min'hā munqalaba
verses.english: "Moreover, I think this is it; I do not think that the Hour (the Hereafter) will ever come to pass. Even if I am returned to my Lord, I will (be clever enough to) possess an even better one over there."

1981.english: "Nor do I believe that the hour will come to pass. Even if I am returned to my Lord, I am clever enough to possess a better one."

1989.english: “I do not think that the Hour (the Hereafter) will ever come. Even if I am returned to my Lord, I will (be clever enough to) possess an even better one over there.”
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَهُۥ صَاحِبُهُۥ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَكَفَرْتَ بِٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا
verses.arabicClean: قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا
verses.transliterated: qāla lahu ṣāḥibuhu wahuwa yuḥāwiruhu akafarta bi-alladhī khalaqaka min turābin thumma min nuṭ'fatin thumma sawwāka rajula
verses.english: His friend said to him, as he debated with him, "Have you disbelieved in the One who created you from dust, then from a tiny drop, then perfected you into a man?

1981.english: His friend said to him, as he debated him, "Do you disbelieve in the one who created you from dust, then from a drop, then perfected you as a man?

1989.english: His friend said to him, as he debated with him, “Have you disbelieved in the One who created you from dust, then from a tiny drop, then perfected you into a man?
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: لَّٰكِنَّا۠ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّى وَلَآ أُشْرِكُ بِرَبِّىٓ أَحَدًا
verses.arabicClean: لكنا هو الله ربي ولا أشرك بربي أحدا
verses.transliterated: lākinnā huwa l-lahu rabbī walā ush'riku birabbī aḥada
verses.english: "As for me, GOD is my Lord, and I will never set up any other god besides my Lord.

1981.english: "As for me, God is my Lord, and I will never associate any idol with Him.

1989.english: “As for me, GOD is my Lord, and I will never set up any other god besides my Lord.
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: وَلَوْلَآ إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا۠ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا
verses.arabicClean: ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله ۚ إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا
verses.transliterated: walawlā idh dakhalta jannataka qul'ta mā shāa l-lahu lā quwwata illā bil-lahi in tarani anā aqalla minka mālan wawalada
verses.english: "When you entered your garden, you should have said, 'This is what GOD has given me (Mã Shã Allãh). No one possesses power except GOD (Lã Quwwata Ellã Bellãh).' You may see that I possess less money and less children than you.
verses.subtitle: Important Commandment

1981.english: "Whenever you enter your orchard, you should say, 'This is God's giving; I can never possess anything, except by God's leave.' You may see me poorer than you are, with fewer children.

1989.english: “When you entered your garden, you should have said, ‘This is what GOD has given me (Maa Shaa Allah). No one possesses power except GOD (Laa Quwwata Ellaa Bellaah) ' You may see that I possess less money and less children than you.
