1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يُؤْتِيَنِ خَيْرًا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهَا حُسْبَانًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا
verses.arabicClean: فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا
verses.transliterated: faʿasā rabbī an yu'tiyani khayran min jannatika wayur'sila ʿalayhā ḥus'bānan mina l-samāi fatuṣ'biḥa ṣaʿīdan zalaqa
verses.english: "My Lord may grant me better than your garden. He may send a violent storm from the sky that wipes out your garden, leaving it completely barren.

1981.english: "But my Lord may endow me with better orchards than yours, and wipe out your orchards with a storm from the sky, making it a barren land.

1989.english: “My Lord may grant me better than your garden. He may send a violent storm from the sky that wipes out your garden, leaving it completely barren.
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: أَوْ يُصْبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوْرًا فَلَن تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُۥ طَلَبًا
verses.arabicClean: أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا
verses.transliterated: aw yuṣ'biḥa māuhā ghawran falan tastaṭīʿa lahu ṭalaba
verses.english: "Or, its water may sink deeper, out of your reach."

1981.english: "Or its water may sink deeper, beyond your reach."

1989.english: “Or, its water may sink deeper, out of your reach.”
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِۦ فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُشْرِكْ بِرَبِّىٓ أَحَدًا
verses.arabicClean: وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا
verses.transliterated: wa-uḥīṭa bithamarihi fa-aṣbaḥa yuqallibu kaffayhi ʿalā mā anfaqa fīhā wahiya khāwiyatun ʿalā ʿurūshihā wayaqūlu yālaytanī lam ush'rik birabbī aḥada
verses.english: Indeed, his crops were wiped out, and he ended up sorrowful, lamenting what he had spent on it in vain, as his property lay barren. He finally said, "I wish I never set up my property as a god beside my Lord."

1981.english: Subsequently, his crops were wiped out, and he became deeply sorrowful over the efforts he wasted therein, and he said, "Oh I wish I did not idolize my property besides my Lord."

1989.english: His crops were wiped out, and he ended up sorrowful, lamenting what he had spent on it in vain, as his property lay barren. He finally said, “I wish I never set up my property as a god besides my Lord.”
1989.footnote: The Quran cites many examples of the different gods that people worship besides God, such as children (7:190), religious leaders and scholars (9:31), property (18:42), dead saints and prophets (16:20-21, 35:14, & 46:5-6), and the ego (25:43, 45:23).

verses.arabic: وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُۥ فِئَةٌ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا
verses.arabicClean: ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان منتصرا
verses.transliterated: walam takun lahu fi-atun yanṣurūnahu min dūni l-lahi wamā kāna muntaṣira
verses.english: No force on earth could have helped him against GOD, nor was it possible for him to receive any help.

1981.english: There was no army to support him against God, nor was he ever destined to win.

1989.english: No force on earth could have helped him against GOD, nor was he capable of receiving any help.

verses.arabic: هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلَٰيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلْحَقِّ هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ عُقْبًا
verses.arabicClean: هنالك الولاية لله الحق ۚ هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا
verses.transliterated: hunālika l-walāyatu lillahi l-ḥaqi huwa khayrun thawāban wakhayrun ʿuq'ba
verses.english: That is because the only true Lord and master is GOD; He provides the best recompense, and with Him is the best destiny.

1981.english: The true mastership belongs only to God; He provides the best reward, and the best destiny.

1989.english: That is the time when only GOD stands supreme; He provides the best recompense, and with Him is the best destiny.

verses.arabic: وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِۦ نَبَاتُ ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ ٱلرِّيَٰحُ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مُّقْتَدِرًا
verses.arabicClean: واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح ۗ وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا
verses.transliterated: wa-iḍ'rib lahum mathala l-ḥayati l-dun'yā kamāin anzalnāhu mina l-samāi fa-ikh'talaṭa bihi nabātu l-arḍi fa-aṣbaḥa hashīman tadhrūhu l-riyāḥu wakāna l-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin muq'tadira
verses.english: Cite for them the example of this life as water that we send down from the sky to produce plants of the earth, then they turn into hay that is blown away by the wind. GOD is able to do all things.

1981.english: Cite for them the parable of this life as a crop watered from the rain, then it turns into hay, and gets blown away by the wind. God is supreme over all things.
1981.subtitle: Property and Children Can be Distracting Idols

1989.english: Cite for them the example of this life as water that we send down from the sky to produce plants of the earth, then they turn into hay that is blown away by the wind. GOD is able to do all things.

verses.arabic: ٱلْمَالُ وَٱلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًا
verses.arabicClean: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا ۖ والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا
verses.transliterated: al-mālu wal-banūna zīnatu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wal-bāqiyātu l-ṣāliḥātu khayrun ʿinda rabbika thawāban wakhayrun amala
verses.english: Money and children are the joys of this life, but the righteous works provide an eternal recompense from your Lord, and a far better hope.
verses.subtitle: Rearranging Our Priorities

1981.english: Money and children are the vanities of this life, and the eternal righteous works are rewarded by your Lord; they are your only hope.

1989.english: Money and children are the material enjoyments of this life, but the righteous works provide an eternal recompense from your Lord, and a far better hope.
1989.subtitle: Rearranging Our Priorities

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ ٱلْجِبَالَ وَتَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً وَحَشَرْنَٰهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا
verses.arabicClean: ويوم نسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا
verses.transliterated: wayawma nusayyiru l-jibāla watarā l-arḍa bārizatan waḥasharnāhum falam nughādir min'hum aḥada
verses.english: The day will come when we wipe out the mountains, and you will see the earth barren. We will summon them all, not leaving out a single one of them.

1981.english: The day will come when we remove the mountains, and you see the earth level. We will gather them all, leaving out not a single one of them.

1989.english: The day will come when we wipe out the mountains; you will see the earth barren, and we will summon them, without leaving out a single one of them.

verses.arabic: وَعُرِضُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ صَفًّا لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۭ بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّن نَّجْعَلَ لَكُم مَّوْعِدًا
verses.arabicClean: وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة ۚ بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا
verses.transliterated: waʿuriḍū ʿalā rabbika ṣaffan laqad ji'tumūnā kamā khalaqnākum awwala marratin bal zaʿamtum allan najʿala lakum mawʿida
verses.english: They will be presented before your Lord in a row. You have come to us as individuals, just as we created you initially. Indeed, this is what you claimed will never happen.

1981.english: They will be presented before your Lord in a row. Now you have come to us as we created you the first time. Did you not claim that this audience will never take place?

1989.english: They will be presented before your Lord in a row. You have come to us as individuals, just as we created you initially. Indeed, this is what you claimed will never happen.

verses.arabic: وَوُضِعَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيْلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحْصَىٰهَا وَوَجَدُوا۟ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ حَاضِرًا وَلَا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدًا
verses.arabicClean: ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا مال هذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ۚ ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ۗ ولا يظلم ربك أحدا
verses.transliterated: wawuḍiʿa l-kitābu fatarā l-muj'rimīna mush'fiqīna mimmā fīhi wayaqūlūna yāwaylatanā māli hādhā l-kitābi lā yughādiru ṣaghīratan walā kabīratan illā aḥṣāhā wawajadū mā ʿamilū ḥāḍiran walā yaẓlimu rabbuka aḥada
verses.english: The record will be shown, and you will see the guilty fearful of its contents. They will say, "Woe to us. How come this book leaves nothing, small or large, without counting it?" They will find everything they had done brought forth. Your Lord is never unjust towards anyone.

1981.english: The record will then be opened, and you will see the guilty frightened from the contents thereof and say, "Woe to us; this record does not leave out anything small or large, without counting it." They will find everything they had done presented to them. Your Lord never inflicts injustice.

1989.english: The record will be shown, and you will see the guilty fearful of its contents. They will say, “Woe to us. How come this book leaves nothing, small or large, without counting it?” They will find everything they had done brought forth. Your Lord is never unjust towards anyone.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُۥ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِى وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّۢ بِئْسَ لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَدَلًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه ۗ أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو ۚ بئس للظالمين بدلا
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qul'nā lil'malāikati us'judū liādama fasajadū illā ib'līsa kāna mina l-jini fafasaqa ʿan amri rabbihi afatattakhidhūnahu wadhurriyyatahu awliyāa min dūnī wahum lakum ʿaduwwun bi'sa lilẓẓālimīna badala
verses.english: We said to the angels, "Fall prostrate before Adam." They fell prostrate, except Satan. He became a jinn, for he disobeyed the order of His Lord. Will you choose him and his descendants as lords instead of Me, even though they are your enemies? What a miserable substitute!
verses.subtitle: Classification of God's Creatures
verses.footnote: When the great feud in the heavenly society took place (38:69), all creatures became classified into angels, jinns, and humans (Appendix 7).

1981.english: When we said to the angels, "Bow down to Adam," they bowed down, except Iblees (Satan). He became a jinn, as he violated the command of his Lord. Would you then accept him, and his descendants, as masters besides Me, even though they are your enemies? What a miserable substitute for the wicked!
1981.subtitle: Satan Turns From Angel to Jinn

1989.english: We said to the angels, “Fall prostrate before Adam.” They fell prostrate, except Satan. He became a jinn, for he disobeyed the order of His Lord.* Will you choose him and his descendants as lords instead of Me, even though they are your enemies? What a miserable substitute!
1989.subtitle: Classification of God’s Creatures
1989.footnote: When the great feud in the heavenly society took place (38:69), all creatures became classified into angels, jinns, and humans (Appendix 7).

verses.arabic: مَّآ أَشْهَدتُّهُمْ خَلْقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمَا كُنتُ مُتَّخِذَ ٱلْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُدًا
verses.arabicClean: ما أشهدتهم خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا
verses.transliterated: mā ashhadttuhum khalqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍi walā khalqa anfusihim wamā kuntu muttakhidha l-muḍilīna ʿaḍuda
verses.english: I never permitted them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves. Nor do I permit the wicked to work in My kingdom.
verses.footnote: God knew that Satan and his supporters (jinns and humans) were going to make the wrong decision. Hence their exclusion from witnessing the creation process.

1981.english: I never even allowed them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth; nor the creation of themselves. I never accept the misleaders as assistants.

1989.english: I never permitted them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves. Nor do I permit the wicked to be members in My kingdom.*
1989.footnote: God knew that Satan and his supporters (jinns and humans) were going to make the wrong decision. Hence their exclusion from witnessing the creation process.

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نَادُوا۟ شُرَكَآءِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لَهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّوْبِقًا
verses.arabicClean: ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا
verses.transliterated: wayawma yaqūlu nādū shurakāiya alladhīna zaʿamtum fadaʿawhum falam yastajībū lahum wajaʿalnā baynahum mawbiqa
verses.english: The day will come when He says, "Call upon My partners, whom you claimed to be gods beside Me," they will call on them, but they will not respond to them. An insurmountable barrier will separate them from each other.

1981.english: The day will come when He says, "Call upon the idols you set up besides Me." They will call upon them, but they will not respond; we will place a barrier between them.

1989.english: The day will come when He says, “Call upon My partners, whom you claimed to be gods besides Me,” they will call on them, but in vain. A gulf of hatred will separate them from each other.

verses.arabic: وَرَءَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ ٱلنَّارَ فَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُم مُّوَاقِعُوهَا وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ عَنْهَا مَصْرِفًا
verses.arabicClean: ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفا
verses.transliterated: waraā l-muj'rimūna l-nāra faẓannū annahum muwāqiʿūhā walam yajidū ʿanhā maṣrifa
verses.english: The guilty will see Hell, and will realize that they will fall into it. They will have no escape therefrom.

1981.english: The guilty will see hell, and realize that they are doomed therein; they will have no way of evading it.

1989.english: The guilty will see Hell and will realize that they will fall into it; they will have no escape therefrom.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا فِى هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ لِلنَّاسِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَكْثَرَ شَىْءٍ جَدَلًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل ۚ وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا
verses.transliterated: walaqad ṣarrafnā fī hādhā l-qur'āni lilnnāsi min kulli mathalin wakāna l-insānu akthara shayin jadala
verses.english: We have cited in this Quran every kind of example, but the human being is the most argumentative creature.
verses.subtitle: Disbelievers Refuse to Accept the Completeness of the Quran

1981.english: We have cited in this Quran all kinds of parables for the people, but the human being is the most contentious.
1981.subtitle: Quran is Truth; Other Sources Are Falsehood

1989.english: We have cited in this Quran every kind of example, but the human being is the most argumentative creature.
1989.subtitle: Disbelievers Refuse to Accept the Completeness of the Quran

verses.arabic: وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلًا
verses.arabicClean: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ويستغفروا ربهم إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا
verses.transliterated: wamā manaʿa l-nāsa an yu'minū idh jāahumu l-hudā wayastaghfirū rabbahum illā an tatiyahum sunnatu l-awalīna aw yatiyahumu l-ʿadhābu qubula
verses.english: Nothing prevented the people from believing, when the guidance came to them, and from seeking the forgiveness of their Lord, except that they demanded to see the same (kind of miracles) as the previous generations, or challenged to see the retribution beforehand.

1981.english: What prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, and from seeking forgiveness from their Lord, is that they demand to see miracles like previous generations, or challenge the retribution to afflict them in advance.

1989.english: Nothing prevented the people from believing, when the guidance came to them and from seeking the forgiveness of their Lord, except that they demanded to see the same (miracles) as the previous generations, or challenged to see the retribution beforehand.

verses.arabic: وَمَا نُرْسِلُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَيُجَٰدِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا۟ بِهِ ٱلْحَقَّ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِى وَمَآ أُنذِرُوا۟ هُزُوًا
verses.arabicClean: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين ۚ ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق ۖ واتخذوا آياتي وما أنذروا هزوا
verses.transliterated: wamā nur'silu l-mur'salīna illā mubashirīna wamundhirīna wayujādilu alladhīna kafarū bil-bāṭili liyud'ḥiḍū bihi l-ḥaqa wa-ittakhadhū āyātī wamā undhirū huzuwa
verses.english: We only send the messengers as simply deliverers of good news, as well as warners. Those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to defeat the truth, and they take My proofs and warnings in vain.

1981.english: We do not send the messengers except as preachers and warners. Then the disbelievers argue with falsehood, in order to refute the truth. They take My scriptures and warnings in vain.

1989.english: We send the messengers as deliverers of good news, as well as warners. Those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to defeat the truth, and they take My signs and warnings in vain.

verses.arabic: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا وَنَسِىَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِن تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ فَلَن يَهْتَدُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًا
verses.arabicClean: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه فأعرض عنها ونسي ما قدمت يداه ۚ إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا ۖ وإن تدعهم إلى الهدى فلن يهتدوا إذا أبدا
verses.transliterated: waman aẓlamu mimman dhukkira biāyāti rabbihi fa-aʿraḍa ʿanhā wanasiya mā qaddamat yadāhu innā jaʿalnā ʿalā qulūbihim akinnatan an yafqahūhu wafī ādhānihim waqran wa-in tadʿuhum ilā l-hudā falan yahtadū idhan abada
verses.english: Who are more evil than those who are reminded of their Lord's proofs, then disregard them, without realizing what they are doing. Consequently, we place shields on their hearts to prevent them from understanding it (the Quran), and deafness in their ears. Thus, no matter what you do to guide them, they can never ever be guided.
verses.subtitle: Divine Intervention

1981.english: Who is more evil than one who is reminded of his Lord's revelations, then he turns away therefrom, paying no attention to what he commits. Consequently, we place on their hearts shields, to prevent them from understanding this Quran, and in their ears deafness. Therefore, when you invite them to the guidance, they can never be guided
1981.subtitle: The Curse

1989.english: Who are more evil than those who are reminded of their Lord’s revela tions, then disregard them, without realizing what they are doing. Consequently, we place shields on their hearts to prevent them from understanding it (the Quran), and deafness in their ears. Thus, no matter what you do to guide them, they can never ever be guided.
1989.subtitle: Divine Intervention

verses.arabic: وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ذُو ٱلرَّحْمَةِ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُم بِمَا كَسَبُوا۟ لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ بَل لَّهُم مَّوْعِدٌ لَّن يَجِدُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦ مَوْئِلًا
verses.arabicClean: وربك الغفور ذو الرحمة ۖ لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا لعجل لهم العذاب ۚ بل لهم موعد لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا
verses.transliterated: warabbuka l-ghafūru dhū l-raḥmati law yuākhidhuhum bimā kasabū laʿajjala lahumu l-ʿadhāba bal lahum mawʿidun lan yajidū min dūnihi mawila
verses.english: Yet, your Lord is the Forgiver, full of mercy. If He called them to account for their deeds, He would annihilate them right there and then. Instead, He gives them a respite until a specific, predetermined time; then they can never escape.

1981.english: Your Lord is forgiving, full of mercy. If He punishes them for their deeds, He would immediately afflict them with retribution. Instead, they have a specific appointment that they can never evade.

1989.english: Yet, your Lord is the Forgiver, full of mercy. If He called them to account for their deeds, He would have annihilated them right there and then. Instead, He gives them a respite until a specific, predetermined time; then they can never escape.

verses.arabic: وَتِلْكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَهْلَكْنَٰهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا۟ وَجَعَلْنَا لِمَهْلِكِهِم مَّوْعِدًا
verses.arabicClean: وتلك القرى أهلكناهم لما ظلموا وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا
verses.transliterated: watil'ka l-qurā ahlaknāhum lammā ẓalamū wajaʿalnā limahlikihim mawʿida
verses.english: Many a community we annihilated because of their transgressions, we designated a specific time for their annihilation.

1981.english: Thus, those communities we destroyed when they turned wicked, and we set a specific time for their destruction.

1989.english: Many a community we annihilated because of their transgressions. We designated a specific time for their annihilation.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَىٰهُ لَآ أَبْرَحُ حَتَّىٰٓ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِىَ حُقُبًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قال موسى لفتاه لا أبرح حتى أبلغ مجمع البحرين أو أمضي حقبا
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qāla mūsā lifatāhu lā abraḥu ḥattā ablugha majmaʿa l-baḥrayni aw amḍiya ḥuquba
verses.english: Moses said to his servant, "I will not rest until I reach the point where the two rivers meet, no matter how long it takes."
verses.subtitle: Valuable Lessons from Moses and His Teacher

1981.english: Recall that Moses said to his servant, "I have to reach the point where the two rivers meet, even if it takes me ages."
1981.subtitle: A Good Reason For Everything

1989.english: Moses said to his servant, “I will not rest until I reach the point where the two rivers meet, no matter how long it takes.”
1989.subtitle: Valuable Lessons from Moses and His Teacher

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَبًا
verses.arabicClean: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما نسيا حوتهما فاتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا
verses.transliterated: falammā balaghā majmaʿa baynihimā nasiyā ḥūtahumā fa-ittakhadha sabīlahu fī l-baḥri saraba
verses.english: When they reached the point where they met, they forgot their fish, and it found its way back to the river, sneakily.

1981.english: When they reached the point where they meet, they neglected their fish, and it sneaked back into the river.

1989.english: When they reached the point where they met, they lost their fish; it found its way back to the river, sneakily.

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَا قَالَ لِفَتَىٰهُ ءَاتِنَا غَدَآءَنَا لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا
verses.arabicClean: فلما جاوزا قال لفتاه آتنا غداءنا لقد لقينا من سفرنا هذا نصبا
verses.transliterated: falammā jāwazā qāla lifatāhu ātinā ghadāanā laqad laqīnā min safarinā hādhā naṣaba
verses.english: After they passed that point, he said to his servant, "Let us have lunch. All this traveling has thoroughly exhausted us."

1981.english: Then, after they passed that point, he said to his servant, "Bring our lunch; we are certainly exhausted from this travelling."

1989.english: After they passed it, he said to his servant, “Let us have lunch. All this traveling has thoroughly exhausted us.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَرَءَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى ٱلصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّى نَسِيتُ ٱلْحُوتَ وَمَآ أَنسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُۥ وَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا
verses.arabicClean: قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره ۚ واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا
verses.transliterated: qāla ara-ayta idh awaynā ilā l-ṣakhrati fa-innī nasītu l-ḥūta wamā ansānīhu illā l-shayṭānu an adhkurahu wa-ittakhadha sabīlahu fī l-baḥri ʿajaba
verses.english: He said, "Remember when we sat by the rock back there? I paid no attention to the fish. It was the devil who made me forget it, and it found its way back to the river, strangely."

1981.english: He said, "Do you recall when we took refuge by the rock back there? That is where I neglected the fish, and it is the devil that made me forget it. Strangely, it found its way back to the river."

1989.english: He said, “Remember when we sat by the rock back there? I paid no attention to the fish; the devil made me forget it, and it found its way back to the river, strangely.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ فَٱرْتَدَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا
verses.arabicClean: قال ذلك ما كنا نبغ ۚ فارتدا على آثارهما قصصا
verses.transliterated: qāla dhālika mā kunnā nabghi fa-ir'taddā ʿalā āthārihimā qaṣaṣa
verses.english: (Moses) said, "That was the place we were looking for." They traced their steps back.

1981.english: Moses said, "That is exactly the place we are seeking." They traced their footsteps back.

1989.english: (Moses) said, “That was the place we wanted.” They traced their steps back.

verses.arabic: فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًا مِّنْ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْمًا
verses.arabicClean: فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما
verses.transliterated: fawajadā ʿabdan min ʿibādinā ātaynāhu raḥmatan min ʿindinā waʿallamnāhu min ladunnā ʿil'ma
verses.english: They found one of our servants, whom we blessed with mercy, and bestowed upon him from our own knowledge.

1981.english: They found a servant of ours whom we endowed with mercy from us, and taught him from our own knowledge.

1989.english: They found one of our servants, whom we blessed with mercy, and bestowed upon him from our own knowledge.

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًا
verses.arabicClean: قال له موسى هل أتبعك على أن تعلمن مما علمت رشدا
verses.transliterated: qāla lahu mūsā hal attabiʿuka ʿalā an tuʿallimani mimmā ʿullim'ta rush'da
verses.english: Moses said to him, "Can I follow you, that you may teach me some of the knowledge and the guidance bestowed upon you?"

1981.english: Moses said to him, "Can I follow you, so that you teach me from the wisdom you learned?"

1989.english: Moses said to him, “Can I follow you that you may teach me some of the knowledge and the guidance bestowed upon you?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا
verses.transliterated: qāla innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabra
verses.english: He said, "You cannot stand to be with me.

1981.english: He said, "You will not bear to stay with me.

1989.english: He said, “You cannot stand to be with me.”

verses.arabic: وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ خُبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا
verses.transliterated: wakayfa taṣbiru ʿalā mā lam tuḥiṭ bihi khub'ra
verses.english: "How can you stand that which you do not comprehend?"

1981.english: "How can you bear with things you do not understand?"

1989.english: “How can you stand that which you do not comprehend?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرًا وَلَآ أَعْصِى لَكَ أَمْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا
verses.transliterated: qāla satajidunī in shāa l-lahu ṣābiran walā aʿṣī laka amra
verses.english: He said, "You will find me, GOD willing, patient. I will not disobey any command you give me."

1981.english: He said, "You will find me, God willing, patient; and I will not disobey any order you give me."

1989.english: He said, “You will find me, GOD willing, patient. I will not disobey any command you give me.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَإِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتَنِى فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِى عَن شَىْءٍ حَتَّىٰٓ أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا
verses.transliterated: qāla fa-ini ittabaʿtanī falā tasalnī ʿan shayin ḥattā uḥ'ditha laka min'hu dhik'ra
verses.english: He said, "If you follow me, then you shall not ask me about anything, unless I choose to tell you about it."

1981.english: He said, "Then, if you wish to follow me, do not ask me about anything, unless I talk to you about it."

1989.english: He said, “If you follow me, then you shall not ask me about anything, unless I choose to tell you about it.”

verses.arabic: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِى ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا إِمْرًا
verses.arabicClean: فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة خرقها ۖ قال أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها لقد جئت شيئا إمرا
verses.transliterated: fa-inṭalaqā ḥattā idhā rakibā fī l-safīnati kharaqahā qāla akharaqtahā litugh'riqa ahlahā laqad ji'ta shayan im'ra
verses.english: So they went. When they boarded a ship, he bore a hole in it. He said, "Did you bore a hole in it to drown its people? You have committed something terrible."

1981.english: The two of them set out. When they embarked the ship, he bored a hole therein. Moses said, "Did you bore a hole therein to drown the people? You have committed something terrible."

1989.english: So they went. When they boarded a ship, he bore a hole in it. He said, “Did you bore a hole in it to drown its people? You have committed something terrible.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا
verses.transliterated: qāla alam aqul innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabra
verses.english: He said, "Did I not say that you cannot stand to be with me?"

1981.english: He said, "Did I not say that you cannot bear it with me.?"

1989.english: He said, “Did I not say that you cannot stand to be with me?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِى بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِى مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسرا
verses.transliterated: qāla lā tuākhidh'nī bimā nasītu walā tur'hiq'nī min amrī ʿus'ra
verses.english: He said, "I am sorry. Do not punish me for my forgetfulness; do not be too harsh with me."

1981.english: He said, "Please excuse me, for I have forgotten. Do not be too harsh on me."

1989.english: He said, “I am sorry. Do not punish me for my forgetfulness; do not be too harsh with me.”

verses.arabic: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَٰمًا فَقَتَلَهُۥ قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَكِيَّةًۢ بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ لَّقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا نُّكْرًا
verses.arabicClean: فانطلقا حتى إذا لقيا غلاما فقتله قال أقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس لقد جئت شيئا نكرا
verses.transliterated: fa-inṭalaqā ḥattā idhā laqiyā ghulāman faqatalahu qāla aqatalta nafsan zakiyyatan bighayri nafsin laqad ji'ta shayan nuk'ra
verses.english: So they went. When they met a young boy, he killed him. He said, "Why did you kill such an innocent soul, who did not kill another soul? You have committed something horrendous."

1981.english: So they set out. When they met a young boy, he killed them. Moses said, "Why did you kill this innocent soul, who did not kill anyone? You have committed something horrendous."

1989.english: So they went. When they met a young boy, he killed him. He said, “Why did you kill such an innocent soul, who did not kill another soul? You have committed something gross.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال ألم أقل لك إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا
verses.transliterated: qāla alam aqul laka innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabra
verses.english: He said, "Did I not tell you that you cannot stand to be with me?"

1981.english: He said, "Did I not tell you that you will not bear it with me?

1989.english: He said, “Did I not tell you that you cannot stand to be with me?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِن سَأَلْتُكَ عَن شَىْءٍۭ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصَٰحِبْنِى قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّى عُذْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها فلا تصاحبني ۖ قد بلغت من لدني عذرا
verses.transliterated: qāla in sa-altuka ʿan shayin baʿdahā falā tuṣāḥib'nī qad balaghta min ladunnī ʿudh'ra
verses.english: He said, "If I ask you about anything else, then do not keep me with you. You have seen enough apologies from me."

1981.english: "If I ask you about anything else, then you have the right to send me away; I have no more excuses to stay in your company."

1989.english: He said, “If I ask you about anything else, then do not keep me with you. You have seen enough excuses from me.”

verses.arabic: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ أَهْلَهَا فَأَبَوْا۟ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥ قَالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا
verses.arabicClean: فانطلقا حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فأقامه ۖ قال لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا
verses.transliterated: fa-inṭalaqā ḥattā idhā atayā ahla qaryatin is'taṭʿamā ahlahā fa-abaw an yuḍayyifūhumā fawajadā fīhā jidāran yurīdu an yanqaḍḍa fa-aqāmahu qāla law shi'ta lattakhadhta ʿalayhi ajra
verses.english: So they went. When they reached a certain community, they asked the people for food, but they refused to host them. Soon, they found a wall about to collapse, and he fixed it. He said, "You could have demanded a wage for that!"

1981.english: So they set out. When they reached a town, they asked the people there for food, but they refused to host them. Then they found a wall therein that was about to fall down, and he straightened it. Moses said, "You could have charged a wage for this."

1989.english: So they went. When they reached a certain community, they asked the people for food, but they refused to host them. Soon, they found a wall about to collapse, and he fixed it up. He said, “You could have demanded a wage for that!”

verses.arabic: قَالَ هَٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنِكَ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأْوِيلِ مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال هذا فراق بيني وبينك ۚ سأنبئك بتأويل ما لم تستطع عليه صبرا
verses.transliterated: qāla hādhā firāqu baynī wabaynika sa-unabbi-uka bitawīli mā lam tastaṭiʿ ʿalayhi ṣabra
verses.english: He said, "Now we have to part company. But I will explain to you everything you could not stand.
verses.subtitle: There is a Good Reason for Everything

1981.english: He said, "Now, you and I have to part. I will explain to you all the things you could not bear.

1989.english: He said, “Now we have to part company. But I will explain to you everything you could not stand.

verses.arabic: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا
verses.arabicClean: أما السفينة فكانت لمساكين يعملون في البحر فأردت أن أعيبها وكان وراءهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا
verses.transliterated: ammā l-safīnatu fakānat limasākīna yaʿmalūna fī l-baḥri fa-aradttu an aʿībahā wakāna warāahum malikun yakhudhu kulla safīnatin ghaṣba
verses.english: "As for the ship, it belonged to poor fishermen, and I wanted to render it defective. There was a king coming after them, who was confiscating every ship, forcibly.

1981.english: "As for the ship, it belonged to poor fishermen, and I wanted to create a defect therein. A king was coming after them, who confiscated every ship forcibly.

1989.english: “As for the ship, it belonged to poor fishermen, and I wanted to render it defective. There was a king coming behind them, who was confiscating every ship, forcibly.

verses.arabic: وَأَمَّا ٱلْغُلَٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَٰنًا وَكُفْرًا
verses.arabicClean: وأما الغلام فكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا أن يرهقهما طغيانا وكفرا
verses.transliterated: wa-ammā l-ghulāmu fakāna abawāhu mu'minayni fakhashīnā an yur'hiqahumā ṭugh'yānan wakuf'ra
verses.english: "As for the boy, his parents were good believers, and we saw that he was going to burden them with his transgression and disbelief.
verses.footnote: Adolf Hitler was a cute and seemingly innocent child. Had he died as a child, many would have grieved, and many would have even questioned God's wisdom. We learn from these profound lessons that there is a good reason behind everything.

1981.english: "As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we expected him to cause them a great deal of misery through rebellion and disbelief.

1989.english: “As for the boy, his parents were good believers, and we saw that he was going to burden them with his transgression and disbelief.*
1989.footnote: Adolf Hitler was a cute and seemingly innocent child. Had he died as a child, many would have grieved, and many would have even questioned God’s wisdom. We learn from these profound lessons that there is a good reason behind everything.

verses.arabic: فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهُ زَكَوٰةً وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًا
verses.arabicClean: فأردنا أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما
verses.transliterated: fa-aradnā an yub'dilahumā rabbuhumā khayran min'hu zakatan wa-aqraba ruḥ'ma
verses.english: "We willed that your Lord substitute in his place another son; one who is better in righteousness and kindness.

1981.english: "We wanted that their Lord substitutes a better son, who would be righteous and more considerate.

1989.english: “We willed that your Lord substitute in his place another son; one who is better in righteousness and kindness.

verses.arabic: وَأَمَّا ٱلْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَٰمَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُۥ كَنزٌ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَٰلِحًا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُۥ عَنْ أَمْرِى ذَٰلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين يتيمين في المدينة وكان تحته كنز لهما وكان أبوهما صالحا فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما ويستخرجا كنزهما رحمة من ربك ۚ وما فعلته عن أمري ۚ ذلك تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا
verses.transliterated: wa-ammā l-jidāru fakāna lighulāmayni yatīmayni fī l-madīnati wakāna taḥtahu kanzun lahumā wakāna abūhumā ṣāliḥan fa-arāda rabbuka an yablughā ashuddahumā wayastakhrijā kanzahumā raḥmatan min rabbika wamā faʿaltuhu ʿan amrī dhālika tawīlu mā lam tasṭiʿ ʿalayhi ṣabra
verses.english: "As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city. Under it, there was a treasure that belonged to them. Because their father was a righteous man, your Lord wanted them to grow up and attain full strength, then extract their treasure. Such is mercy from your Lord. I did none of that of my own volition. This is the explanation of the things you could not stand."

1981.english: "As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and a treasure was hidden beneath it. Their father was a righteous man, so your Lord wanted them to grow up and excavate their treasure. All these were merciful decisions of your Lord, and I did nothing on my own. This explains all the things you could not bear."

1989.english: “As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city. Under it, there was a treasure that belonged to them. Because their father was a righteous man, your Lord wanted them to grow up and attain full strength, then extract their treasure. Such is mercy from your Lord. I did none of that of my own volition. This is the explanation of the things you could not stand.” Zul-Qamain: The One With the Two Homs

verses.arabic: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَن ذِى ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ قُلْ سَأَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْهُ ذِكْرًا
verses.arabicClean: ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين ۖ قل سأتلو عليكم منه ذكرا
verses.transliterated: wayasalūnaka ʿan dhī l-qarnayni qul sa-atlū ʿalaykum min'hu dhik'ra
verses.english: They ask you about Zul-Qarnain. Say, "I will narrate to you some of his history."
verses.subtitle: Zul-Qarnain: The One With the Two Horns or Two Generations

1981.english: And they ask you about the one with two horns. Say, "I will tell you about him."
1981.subtitle: Gog and Magog

1989.english: They ask you about the one with the two horns. Say, “I will narrate to you some of his history.”

verses.arabic: إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ سَبَبًا
verses.arabicClean: إنا مكنا له في الأرض وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا
verses.transliterated: innā makkannā lahu fī l-arḍi waātaynāhu min kulli shayin sababa
verses.english: We granted him authority on earth, and provided him with all kinds of means.

1981.english: We granted him authority on earth, and we gave him the means to do all kinds of things.

1989.english: We granted him authority on earth, and provided him with all kinds of means.

verses.arabic: فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
verses.arabicClean: فأتبع سببا
verses.transliterated: fa-atbaʿa sababa
verses.english: Then, he pursued one way.

1981.english: Then, he pursued one way.

1989.english: Then, he pursued one way.

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًا قُلْنَا يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا بلغ مغرب الشمس وجدها تغرب في عين حمئة ووجد عندها قوما ۗ قلنا يا ذا القرنين إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā balagha maghriba l-shamsi wajadahā taghrubu fī ʿaynin ḥami-atin wawajada ʿindahā qawman qul'nā yādhā l-qarnayni immā an tuʿadhiba wa-immā an tattakhidha fīhim ḥus'na
verses.english: When he reached the far west, he found the sun setting in a vast ocean, and found people there. We said, "O Zul-Qarnain, you can rule as you wish; either punish, or be kind to them."

1981.english: When he reached the far West, he found the sun setting in a vast ocean, and he found people there. We said, "You can rule as you please, either punishing them, or treating them kindly."

1989.english: When he reached the far west, he found the sun setting in a vast ocean, and found people there. We said, “O you with two horns, you can rule as you wish; either punish, or be kind to them.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًا نُّكْرًا
verses.arabicClean: قال أما من ظلم فسوف نعذبه ثم يرد إلى ربه فيعذبه عذابا نكرا
verses.transliterated: qāla ammā man ẓalama fasawfa nuʿadhibuhu thumma yuraddu ilā rabbihi fayuʿadhibuhu ʿadhāban nuk'ra
verses.english: He said, "As for those who transgress, we will punish them, then, when they return to their Lord, He will commit them to more retribution.

1981.english: He said, "As for him who works evil, we will punish him, then he will be returned to his Lord for an even worse retribution."

1989.english: He said, “As for those who transgress, we will punish them, then, when they return to their Lord, He will commit them to more retribution.

verses.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا
verses.arabicClean: وأما من آمن وعمل صالحا فله جزاء الحسنى ۖ وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا
verses.transliterated: wa-ammā man āmana waʿamila ṣāliḥan falahu jazāan l-ḥus'nā wasanaqūlu lahu min amrinā yus'ra
verses.english: "As for those who believe and lead a righteous life, they receive a good reward; we will treat them kindly."

1981.english: "As for him who believes and works righteousness, he has deserved a good reward, and we will treat him amicably."

1989.english: “As for those who believe and lead a righteous life, they receive a good reward; we will treat them kindly.”

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
verses.arabicClean: ثم أتبع سببا
verses.transliterated: thumma atbaʿa sababa
verses.english: Then he pursued another way.

1981.english: Then he pursued another way.

1989.english: Then he pursued another way.

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًا
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس وجدها تطلع على قوم لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā balagha maṭliʿa l-shamsi wajadahā taṭluʿu ʿalā qawmin lam najʿal lahum min dūnihā sit'ra
verses.english: When he reached the far east, he found the sun rising on people who had nothing to shelter them from it.

1981.english: When he reached the far East, he found the sun rising upon people who had no cover to protect them therefrom.

1989.english: When he reached the far east, he found the sun rising on people who had nothing to shelter them from it.

verses.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ وَقَدْ أَحَطْنَا بِمَا لَدَيْهِ خُبْرًا
verses.arabicClean: كذلك وقد أحطنا بما لديه خبرا
verses.transliterated: kadhālika waqad aḥaṭnā bimā ladayhi khub'ra
verses.english: Naturally, we were fully aware of everything he found out.

1981.english: We have already known about the things he just discovered

1989.english: Naturally, we were fully aware of everything he found out.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
verses.arabicClean: ثم أتبع سببا
verses.transliterated: thumma atbaʿa sababa
verses.english: He then pursued another way.

1981.english: Then he pursued another way.

1989.english: He then pursued another way.

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين وجد من دونهما قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā balagha bayna l-sadayni wajada min dūnihimā qawman lā yakādūna yafqahūna qawla
verses.english: When he reached the valley between two palisades, he found people whose language was barely understandable.

1981.english: When he reached the two palisades, he found people who spoke a different language.

1989.english: When he reached the valley between two palisades, he found people whose language was barely understandable.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا ذا القرنين إن يأجوج ومأجوج مفسدون في الأرض فهل نجعل لك خرجا على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا
verses.transliterated: qālū yādhā l-qarnayni inna yajūja wamajūja muf'sidūna fī l-arḍi fahal najʿalu laka kharjan ʿalā an tajʿala baynanā wabaynahum sadda
verses.english: They said, "O Zul-Qarnain, Gog and Magog are corruptors of the earth. Can we pay you to create a barrier between us and them?"
verses.subtitle: Gog and Magog
verses.footnote: One of my duties as God's Messenger of the Covenant is to state that Gog and Magog, the final sign before the end of the world, will reappear in 2270 AD (1700 AH), just 10 years before the end. Note that Gog and Magog occur in Suras 18 and 21, precisely 17 verses before the end of each sura, representing 17 lunar centuries (see 72:27 and Appendix 25).

1981.english: They said, "O you with the two horns, Gog and Magog are tyrants; can we pay you to build a barrier between us and them?"

1989.english: They said, “O you with the two horns Gog and Magog are corruptors of the earth. Can we pay you to create a barrier between us and them?”
1989.subtitle: Gog and Magog
1989.footnote: One of my duties as God’s Messenger of the Covenant is to state that Gog and Magog; the final sign before the end of the world, will reappear in 2270 AD (170C AH), just 10 years before the end. Note that Gog and Magog occur in Suras 18 and 21, precisely 17 verses before the end of each sura, representing 17 lunar centuries (72:27).

verses.arabic: قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّى فِيهِ رَبِّى خَيْرٌ فَأَعِينُونِى بِقُوَّةٍ أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا
verses.arabicClean: قال ما مكني فيه ربي خير فأعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما
verses.transliterated: qāla mā makkannī fīhi rabbī khayrun fa-aʿīnūnī biquwwatin ajʿal baynakum wabaynahum radma
verses.english: He said, "My Lord has given me great bounties. If you cooperate with me, I will build a dam between you and them.

1981.english: He said, "God has blessed me with great abilities, so help me sufficiently, and I will build an obstruction between you and them.

1989.english: He said, “My Lord has given me great bounties. If you cooperate with me, I will create a dam between you and them.
1989.footnote: One of my duties as God’s Messenger of the Covenant is to state that Gog and Magog; the final sign before the end of the world, will reappear in 2270 AD (170C AH), just 10 years before the end. Note that Gog and Magog occur in Suras 18 and 21, precisely 17 verses before the end of each sura, representing 17 lunar centuries (72:27).

verses.arabic: ءَاتُونِى زُبَرَ ٱلْحَدِيدِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ قَالَ ٱنفُخُوا۟ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَعَلَهُۥ نَارًا قَالَ ءَاتُونِىٓ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا
verses.arabicClean: آتوني زبر الحديد ۖ حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين قال انفخوا ۖ حتى إذا جعله نارا قال آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا
verses.transliterated: ātūnī zubara l-ḥadīdi ḥattā idhā sāwā bayna l-ṣadafayni qāla unfukhū ḥattā idhā jaʿalahu nāran qāla ātūnī uf'righ ʿalayhi qiṭ'ra
verses.english: "Bring to me masses of iron." Once he filled the gap between the two palisades, he said, "Blow." Once it was red hot, he said, "Help me pour tar on top of it."

1981.english: "Bring me blocks of iron." He filled the gap between the two cliffs, then said, "Blow." When it became red hot, he said, "Let us pour tar over it."

1989.english: “Bring to me masses of iron.” He filled the gap between the two palisades, then said, “Blow.” Once it was red hot, he said, “Help me pour tar on top of it.”
1989.footnote: One of my duties as God’s Messenger of the Covenant is to state that Gog and Magog; the final sign before the end of the world, will reappear in 2270 AD (170C AH), just 10 years before the end. Note that Gog and Magog occur in Suras 18 and 21, precisely 17 verses before the end of each sura, representing 17 lunar centuries (72:27).

verses.arabic: فَمَا ٱسْطَٰعُوٓا۟ أَن يَظْهَرُوهُ وَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ لَهُۥ نَقْبًا
verses.arabicClean: فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه وما استطاعوا له نقبا
verses.transliterated: famā is'ṭāʿū an yaẓharūhu wamā is'taṭāʿū lahu naqba
verses.english: Thus, they could not climb it, nor could they bore holes in it.

1981.english: They could neither surmount it, nor could they bore a hole therein.

1989.english: Thus, they could not climb it, nor could they bore holes in it.
1989.footnote: One of my duties as God’s Messenger of the Covenant is to state that Gog and Magog; the final sign before the end of the world, will reappear in 2270 AD (170C AH), just 10 years before the end. Note that Gog and Magog occur in Suras 18 and 21, precisely 17 verses before the end of each sura, representing 17 lunar centuries (72:27).

verses.arabic: قَالَ هَٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّى فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى جَعَلَهُۥ دَكَّآءَ وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى حَقًّا
verses.arabicClean: قال هذا رحمة من ربي ۖ فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء ۖ وكان وعد ربي حقا
verses.transliterated: qāla hādhā raḥmatun min rabbī fa-idhā jāa waʿdu rabbī jaʿalahu dakkāa wakāna waʿdu rabbī ḥaqqa
verses.english: He said, "This is mercy from my Lord. When the prophecy of my Lord comes to pass, He will cause the dam to crumble. The prophecy of my Lord is truth."

1981.english: He said, "This is mercy from my Lord, and it will last until my Lord's promise comes to pass. That is when He wipes it out, for my Lord's promise is truth."

1989.english: He said, “This is mercy from my Lord. When the prophecy of my Lord comes to pass, He will cause the dam to crumble. The prophecy of my Lord is truth.”
1989.footnote: One of my duties as God’s Messenger of the Covenant is to state that Gog and Magog; the final sign before the end of the world, will reappear in 2270 AD (170C AH), just 10 years before the end. Note that Gog and Magog occur in Suras 18 and 21, precisely 17 verses before the end of each sura, representing 17 lunar centuries (72:27).

verses.arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِى بَعْضٍ وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَٰهُمْ جَمْعًا
verses.arabicClean: وتركنا بعضهم يومئذ يموج في بعض ۖ ونفخ في الصور فجمعناهم جمعا
verses.transliterated: wataraknā baʿḍahum yawma-idhin yamūju fī baʿḍin wanufikha fī l-ṣūri fajamaʿnāhum jamʿa
verses.english: At that time, we will let them invade with one another, then the horn will be blown, and we will summon them all together.

1981.english: On that day, we will let them mingle with each other; the horn will be blown, and we will gather them all together.

1989.english: On that day, we will let them mingle with one another, then the horn will be blown, and we will summon them all together.

verses.arabic: وَعَرَضْنَا جَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ عَرْضًا
verses.arabicClean: وعرضنا جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا
verses.transliterated: waʿaraḍnā jahannama yawma-idhin lil'kāfirīna ʿarḍa
verses.english: We will present Hell, on that day, to the disbelievers.

1981.english: On that day, we will present hell to the disbelievers face to face.

1989.english: We will present Hell, on that day, to the disbelievers.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ فِى غِطَآءٍ عَن ذِكْرِى وَكَانُوا۟ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا
verses.arabicClean: الذين كانت أعينهم في غطاء عن ذكري وكانوا لا يستطيعون سمعا
verses.transliterated: alladhīna kānat aʿyunuhum fī ghiṭāin ʿan dhik'rī wakānū lā yastaṭīʿūna samʿa
verses.english: They are the ones whose eyes were too veiled to see My message. Nor could they hear.

1981.english: Their eyes were blind to My message, and they could not hear.

1989.english: They are the ones whose eyes were too veiled to see My message. Nor could they hear.

verses.arabic: أَفَحَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَن يَتَّخِذُوا۟ عِبَادِى مِن دُونِىٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ إِنَّآ أَعْتَدْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ نُزُلًا
verses.arabicClean: أفحسب الذين كفروا أن يتخذوا عبادي من دوني أولياء ۚ إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا
verses.transliterated: afaḥasiba alladhīna kafarū an yattakhidhū ʿibādī min dūnī awliyāa innā aʿtadnā jahannama lil'kāfirīna nuzula
verses.english: Do those who disbelieve think that they can get away with setting up My servants as gods beside Me? We have prepared for the disbelievers Hell as an eternal abode.

1981.english: Did the disbelievers think that they can get away with idolizing My servants besides Me? We prepared hell for the disbelievers as an abode.
1981.subtitle: Idolizing God's Servants

1989.english: Did those who disbelieved think that they could get away with setting up My servants as gods besides Me? We have prepared for the disbelievers Hell as an eternal abode. The Worst Losers

verses.arabic: قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَٰلًا
verses.arabicClean: قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا
verses.transliterated: qul hal nunabbi-ukum bil-akhsarīna aʿmāla
verses.english: Say, "Shall I tell you who the worst losers are?
verses.subtitle: Examine Yourself

1981.english: Say, "Shall we inform you of the worst losers?

1989.english: Say, “Shall I tell you who the worst losers are?

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا
verses.arabicClean: الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا
verses.transliterated: alladhīna ḍalla saʿyuhum fī l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wahum yaḥsabūna annahum yuḥ'sinūna ṣun'ʿa
verses.english: "They are the ones whose works in this life are totally astray, but they think that they are doing good."

1981.english: "It is those who go astray in this life, yet believe that they are right."

1989.english: “They are the ones whose works in this life are totally astray, but they think that they are doing good.”

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَلِقَآئِهِۦ فَحَبِطَتْ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَزْنًا
verses.arabicClean: أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا
verses.transliterated: ulāika alladhīna kafarū biāyāti rabbihim waliqāihi faḥabiṭat aʿmāluhum falā nuqīmu lahum yawma l-qiyāmati wazna
verses.english: Such are the ones who disbelieved in the revelations of their Lord and in meeting Him. Therefore, their works are in vain; on the Day of Resurrection, they have no weight.

1981.english: They rejected the scriptures of their Lord, and disbelieved in meeting Him. Consequently, their works are in vain, and they have no weight with us on the day of resurrection.

1989.english: Such are the ones who disbelieved in the revelations of their Lord and in meeting Him. Therefore, their works are in vain; on the Day of Resurrection, they have no weight.

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَٰتِى وَرُسُلِى هُزُوًا
verses.arabicClean: ذلك جزاؤهم جهنم بما كفروا واتخذوا آياتي ورسلي هزوا
verses.transliterated: dhālika jazāuhum jahannamu bimā kafarū wa-ittakhadhū āyātī warusulī huzuwa
verses.english: Their just requital is Hell, in return for their disbelief, and for mocking My revelations and My messengers.

1981.english: Their just requital is hell, because they disbelieved and scoffed at My scriptures and My messengers.

1989.english: Their just requital is Hell, in return for their disbelief, and for mocking My revelations and My messengers.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلًا
verses.arabicClean: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كانت لهم جنات الفردوس نزلا
verses.transliterated: inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti kānat lahum jannātu l-fir'dawsi nuzula
verses.english: As for those who believe and lead a righteous life they have deserved a blissful Paradise as their abode.

1981.english: As for those who believe and work righteousness, the gardens of bliss will be their abode.

1989.english: As for those who believe and lead a righteous life they have deserved a blissful Paradise as their abode.

verses.arabic: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا
verses.arabicClean: خالدين فيها لا يبغون عنها حولا
verses.transliterated: khālidīna fīhā lā yabghūna ʿanhā ḥiwala
verses.english: Forever they abide therein; they will never want any other substitute.

1981.english: Forever they abide therein, and they will want no substitute.

1989.english: Forever they abide therein; they will never want any other substitute.

verses.arabic: قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ مِدَادًا لِّكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّى لَنَفِدَ ٱلْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَٰتُ رَبِّى وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِۦ مَدَدًا
verses.arabicClean: قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا
verses.transliterated: qul law kāna l-baḥru midādan likalimāti rabbī lanafida l-baḥru qabla an tanfada kalimātu rabbī walaw ji'nā bimith'lihi madada
verses.english: Say, "If the ocean were ink for the words of my Lord, the ocean would run out, before the words of my Lord run out, even if we double the ink supply."
verses.subtitle: The Quran: Everything We Need

1981.english: Say, "If the ocean was ink for the words of my Lord, the ocean would run out before the words of my Lord run out, even if we double the ink supply."
1981.subtitle:
Quran Encompasses Everything We Need
Uphold the Words of God, Not the Words Attributed to Muhammad
1981.footnote: These two verses teach us that there is no shortage of words as far as God is concerned, and therefore, the Quran contains everything we need. Anything left out, such as the way to sleep, or the way to eat, etc. is therefore up to us and our personal preference. We also learn that Muhammad is no more than a human being like us, and that following the inventions attributed to him, or even his personal opinions, is idol worship. Note that the only two verses in Quran describing Muhammad as a human being end up by enjoining us from idolizing him (see also 41:6).

1989.english: Say, “If the ocean were ink for the words of my Lord, the ocean would run out, before the words of my Lord run out, even if we double the ink supply.”
1989.subtitle: The Quran: Everything We Need

verses.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَٰلِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدًۢا
verses.arabicClean: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد ۖ فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا
verses.transliterated: qul innamā anā basharun mith'lukum yūḥā ilayya annamā ilāhukum ilāhun wāḥidun faman kāna yarjū liqāa rabbihi falyaʿmal ʿamalan ṣāliḥan walā yush'rik biʿibādati rabbihi aḥada
verses.english: Say, "I am no more than a human like you, being inspired that your god is one god. Those who hope to meet their Lord shall work righteousness, and never worship any other god beside his Lord."

1981.english: Say (O Muhammad), "I am no more than a human being like you. It was revealed to me that your God is one God. Therefore, whoever looks forward to meeting his Lord shall lead a righteous life, and never idolize anyone besides his Lord."
1981.footnote: These two verses teach us that there is no shortage of words as far as God is concerned, and therefore, the Quran contains everything we need. Anything left out, such as the way to sleep, or the way to eat, etc. is therefore up to us and our personal preference. We also learn that Muhammad is no more than a human being like us, and that following the inventions attributed to him, or even his personal opinions, is idol worship. Note that the only two verses in Quran describing Muhammad as a human being end up by enjoining us from idolizing him (see also 41:6).

1989.english: Say, “I am no more than a human like you, being inspired that your god is one god. Those who hope to meet their Lord shall work righteousness, and never worship any other god besides his Lord.”

verses.arabic: كٓهيعٓصٓ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم كهيعص
verses.transliterated: kaf-ha-ya-ain-saad
verses.english: K. H. Y. 'A. S. (Kãf Hã Yã 'Ayn Sãd)
verses.footnote: This is the maximum number of Quranic Initials, because this sura deals with such crucial matters as the miraculous birth of John and the virgin birth of Jesus, and strongly condemns the gross blasphemy that considers Jesus to be a son of God. The five initials provide a powerful physical evidence to support these issues (See Appendices 1 & 22).

1981.english: K. H. Y. 'A. S.
1981.footnote: These five Quranic initials are part of the Quran's miraculous numerical code that proves to the world the divine source of Quran, and the perfect preservation of every single letter therein. As detailed in Appendix 1, the common denominator of all the Quranic initials is the number 19. As it turned out, this sura contains 137 K's (Kaf), 175 H's (Ha), 343 Y's (Ya), 117 'A's ('Ayn), and 26 S's (Sad) in the Arabic text. The total sum of these 5 Arabic alphabets, in this sura, comes to 798 which is a multiple of 19.

1989.english: K. H. Y. ‘A. S.* (Kaaf Haa Yaa ‘Ayn Saad) Zachariah
1989.footnote: This is the maximum number of Quranic Initials, because this sura deals with such crucial matters as the miraculous birth of John and the virgin birth of Jesus, and strongly condemns the blasphemy of Jesus’ sonship to God. The 5-lettered initials provide powerful physical evidence to support these issues (See Appendices 1 & 22).

verses.arabic: ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُۥ زَكَرِيَّآ
verses.arabicClean: ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا
verses.transliterated: dhik'ru raḥmati rabbika ʿabdahu zakariyy
verses.english: A narration about your Lord's mercy towards His servant Zachariah.
verses.subtitle: Zachariah

1981.english: This is a reminder of your Lord's mercy towards His servant Zechariah.

1989.english: A narration about your Lord’s mercy towards His servant Zachariah.

verses.arabic: إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ نِدَآءً خَفِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا
verses.transliterated: idh nādā rabbahu nidāan khafiyya
verses.english: He called his Lord, a secret call.

1981.english: He called upon his Lord, a secret call.

1989.english: He called his Lord, a secret call.

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَهَنَ ٱلْعَظْمُ مِنِّى وَٱشْتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا وَلَمْ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قال رب إني وهن العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi innī wahana l-ʿaẓmu minnī wa-ish'taʿala l-rasu shayban walam akun biduʿāika rabbi shaqiyya
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, the bones have turned brittle in my body, and my hair is aflame with gray. As I implore You, my Lord, I never despair.

1981.english: He said, "My Lord, my bones have become brittle, and my head aflame with gray hair. I am confident, my Lord, You will not let me down.

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, the bones have turned brittle in my body, and my hair is aflame with gray. As I implore You, my Lord, I never despair.

verses.arabic: وَإِنِّى خِفْتُ ٱلْمَوَٰلِىَ مِن وَرَآءِى وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًا فَهَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي وكانت امرأتي عاقرا فهب لي من لدنك وليا
verses.transliterated: wa-innī khif'tu l-mawāliya min warāī wakānati im'ra-atī ʿāqiran fahab lī min ladunka waliyya
verses.english: "I worry about my dependants after me, and my wife has been sterile. Grant me, from You, an heir.

1981.english: "I worry about my folk after my death, for my wife is sterile. Grant me a successor, as a gift from You.

1989.english: “And I fear for my (female) dependants after me, for my wife has been sterile. Grant me, from You, an heir.

verses.arabic: يَرِثُنِى وَيَرِثُ مِنْ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ وَٱجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب ۖ واجعله رب رضيا
verses.transliterated: yarithunī wayarithu min āli yaʿqūba wa-ij'ʿalhu rabbi raḍiyya
verses.english: "Let him be my heir and the heir of Jacob's clan, and make him, my Lord, acceptable."

1981.english: "Let him inherit me, and of the house of Jacob; and make him, my Lord, acceptable."

1989.english: “Let him be my heir and the heir of Jacob’s clan, and make him, my Lord, acceptable.” John

verses.arabic: يَٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا
verses.transliterated: yāzakariyyā innā nubashiruka bighulāmin us'muhu yaḥyā lam najʿal lahu min qablu samiyya
verses.english: "O Zachariah, we give you good news; a boy whose name shall be John (Yahya). We never created anyone like him before."
verses.subtitle: John

1981.english: O Zechariah, we give you good news; a boy to be named John; a name we never gave to anyone previously.

1989.english: “O Zachariah, we give you good news; a boy whose name shall be John (Yahya). We never created anyone like him before.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi annā yakūnu lī ghulāmun wakānati im'ra-atī ʿāqiran waqad balaghtu mina l-kibari ʿitiyya
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, will I have a son despite my wife's sterility, and despite my old age?"

1981.english: He said, "My Lord, will I have a boy despite my wife's sterility, and my old age?"

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, will I have a son despite my wife’s sterility, and despite my old age?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْـًٔا
verses.arabicClean: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا
verses.transliterated: qāla kadhālika qāla rabbuka huwa ʿalayya hayyinun waqad khalaqtuka min qablu walam taku shaya
verses.english: He said, "Thus said your Lord: 'It is easy for Me to do. I created you before that, and you were nothing.'"

1981.english: (The angel) said, "Thus said your Lord, 'It is easy for Me; I created you previously, and you were nothing.' "

1989.english: He said, “Thus said your Lord: ‘It is easy for Me to do. I created you before that, and you were nothing.’ ”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قال رب اجعل لي آية ۚ قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi ij'ʿal lī āyatan qāla āyatuka allā tukallima l-nāsa thalātha layālin sawiyya
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, give me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three consecutive nights."

1981.english: He said, "My Lord, give me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you do not speak to the people three consecutive nights."

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, give me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three consecutive nights.”

verses.arabic: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا۟ بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا
verses.transliterated: fakharaja ʿalā qawmihi mina l-miḥ'rābi fa-awḥā ilayhim an sabbiḥū buk'ratan waʿashiyya
verses.english: He came out to his family, from the sanctuary, and signaled to them: "Meditate (on GOD) day and night."

1981.english: He came out of the sanctuary, and signaled to his folk, "Glorify God day and night."

1989.english: He came out to his family, from the sanctuary, and signaled to them: “Meditate (on God) day and night.”

verses.arabic: يَٰيَحْيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِقُوَّةٍ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة ۖ وآتيناه الحكم صبيا
verses.transliterated: yāyaḥyā khudhi l-kitāba biquwwatin waātaynāhu l-ḥuk'ma ṣabiyya
verses.english: "O John, you shall uphold the scripture, strongly." We endowed him with wisdom, even in his youth.

1981.english: O John, uphold the scripture strictly. We endowed him with wisdom in his youth.

1989.english: “O John, uphold the scripture, strongly.” We endowed him with wisdom, even in his youth.

verses.arabic: وَحَنَانًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَوٰةً وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة ۖ وكان تقيا
verses.transliterated: waḥanānan min ladunnā wazakatan wakāna taqiyya
verses.english: And (we endowed him with) kindness from us and purity, for he was righteous.

1981.english: And we blessed him with kindness from us, and sanctity, for he was righteous.

1989.english: And (we endowed him with) kindness from us, and purity; he was righteous.

verses.arabic: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا
verses.transliterated: wabarran biwālidayhi walam yakun jabbāran ʿaṣiyya
verses.english: He honored his parents, and was never a disobedient tyrant.

1981.english: He honored his parents, and was never a disobedient rebel.

1989.english: He was kind to his parents, never a disobedient tyrant.

verses.arabic: وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
verses.arabicClean: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا
verses.transliterated: wasalāmun ʿalayhi yawma wulida wayawma yamūtu wayawma yub'ʿathu ḥayya
verses.english: Peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is resurrected back to life.

1981.english: He deserved peace the day he was born, the day of his death, and the day he is resurrected.

1989.english: Peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is resurrected back to life.

verses.arabic: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا
verses.transliterated: wa-udh'kur fī l-kitābi maryama idhi intabadhat min ahlihā makānan sharqiyya
verses.english: Mention in the scripture Mary. She isolated herself from her family, into an eastern location.
verses.subtitle: Mary

1981.english: And mention in the scripture Mary, when she isolated herself in an Eastern chamber.
1981.subtitle: Mary

1989.english: Mention in the scripture Mary. She isolated herself from her family, into an eastern location.
1989.subtitle: Mary

verses.arabic: فَٱتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا فَأَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا
verses.transliterated: fa-ittakhadhat min dūnihim ḥijāban fa-arsalnā ilayhā rūḥanā fatamathala lahā basharan sawiyya
verses.english: While a barrier separated her from them, we sent to her our Spirit. He went to her in the form of a human being.

1981.english: While secluded from her folk, we sent to her our Spirit (Gabriel), and he appeared to her as a perfect human.

1989.english: While a barrier separated her from them, we sent to her our Spirit. He went to her in the form of a perfect man.

verses.arabic: قَالَتْ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا
verses.transliterated: qālat innī aʿūdhu bil-raḥmāni minka in kunta taqiyya
verses.english: She said, "I seek refuge in the Most Gracious, that you may be righteous."

1981.english: She said, "I seek refuge in God from you, in case this means anything to you."

1989.english: She said, “I seek refuge in the Most Gracious, unless you are righteous.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَٰمًا زَكِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا
verses.transliterated: qāla innamā anā rasūlu rabbiki li-ahaba laki ghulāman zakiyya
verses.english: He said, "I am the messenger of your Lord, to grant you a pure son."

1981.english: He said, "I am sent by your Lord, to grant you a pious child."

1989.english: He said, “I am the messenger of your Lord, to grant you a pure child.”

verses.arabic: قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا
verses.transliterated: qālat annā yakūnu lī ghulāmun walam yamsasnī basharun walam aku baghiyya
verses.english: She said, "How can I have a son, when no man has touched me; I have never been unchaste."

1981.english: She said, "How can I have a child, when no man has touched me, and I am not unchaste?"

1989.english: She said, “How can I have a child, when no man has touched me, and I have never been unchaste.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُۥٓ ءَايَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً مِّنَّا وَكَانَ أَمْرًا مَّقْضِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ۖ ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا ۚ وكان أمرا مقضيا
verses.transliterated: qāla kadhāliki qāla rabbuki huwa ʿalayya hayyinun walinajʿalahu āyatan lilnnāsi waraḥmatan minnā wakāna amran maqḍiyya
verses.english: He said, "Thus said your Lord, 'It is easy for Me. We will render him a sign for the people, and mercy from us. This is a predestined matter.'"

1981.english: He said, "Thus said your Lord, 'It is easy for me,' in order to make him a miracle among the people, and a mercy from us; this is the way it will be people, and a mercy from us; this is the way it will be done."

1989.english: He said, “Thus said your Lord, ‘It is easy for Me. We will render him a sign for the people, and mercy from us. This matter is already decided.’ ”

verses.arabic: فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَٱنتَبَذَتْ بِهِۦ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا
verses.transliterated: faḥamalathu fa-intabadhat bihi makānan qaṣiyya
verses.english: When she bore him, she isolated herself to a faraway place.
verses.subtitle: The Birth of Jesus

1981.english: She bore him, and isolated herself to a faraway place.

1989.english: When she bore him, she isolated herself to a faraway place.
1989.subtitle: The Birth of Jesus

verses.arabic: فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَٰلَيْتَنِى مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا
verses.transliterated: fa-ajāahā l-makhāḍu ilā jidh'ʿi l-nakhlati qālat yālaytanī mittu qabla hādhā wakuntu nasyan mansiyya
verses.english: The birth process came to her by the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "(I am so ashamed;) I wish I were dead before this happened, and completely forgotten."

1981.english: When the birth pangs surprised her by the palm tree, she said, "Oh I wish I was dead before this happened, and was completely forgotten."

1989.english: The birth pangs came to her by the trunk of a palm tree. She said, “(7 am so ashamed;) I wish I were dead, and completely forgotten.”

verses.arabic: فَنَادَىٰهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ أَلَّا تَحْزَنِى قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا
verses.transliterated: fanādāhā min taḥtihā allā taḥzanī qad jaʿala rabbuki taḥtaki sariyya
verses.english: (The infant) called her from beneath her, saying, "Do not grieve. Your Lord has provided you with a stream.

1981.english: But (the child) called her from under her, saying, "Do not worry, your Lord has provided you with a running stream.

1989.english: (The infant) called her from beneath her, saying, “Do not grieve. Your Lord has provided you with a stream.

verses.arabic: وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ تُسَٰقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا
verses.transliterated: wahuzzī ilayki bijidh'ʿi l-nakhlati tusāqiṭ ʿalayki ruṭaban janiyya
verses.english: "If you shake the trunk of this palm tree, it will drop ripe dates for you.
verses.footnote: Thus, Jesus was born in late September or early October. This is when dates ripen in the Middle East to the point of falling off the tree.

1981.english: "And if you shake the palm tree, it will drop on you ripe dates.

1989.english: “And if you shake the trunk of this palm tree, it will drop ripe dates for you.*
1989.footnote: Thus, Jesus was born in late September or early October. This is when dates ripen in the Middle East to the point of falling off the tree.

verses.arabic: فَكُلِى وَٱشْرَبِى وَقَرِّى عَيْنًا فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا ۖ فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا
verses.transliterated: fakulī wa-ish'rabī waqarrī ʿaynan fa-immā tarayinna mina l-bashari aḥadan faqūlī innī nadhartu lilrraḥmāni ṣawman falan ukallima l-yawma insiyya
verses.english: "Eat and drink, and be happy. When you see anyone, say, 'I have made a vow of silence; I am not talking today to anyone.' "

1981.english: "So eat and drink and be happy, and when you see anyone, then say, 'I have pledged to God a fast; I will not talk to anyone.' "

1989.english: “Eat and drink, and be happy. When you see anyone, say, ‘I have made a vow of silence; I am not talking, today, to anyone.’ ”

verses.arabic: فَأَتَتْ بِهِۦ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُۥ قَالُوا۟ يَٰمَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْـًٔا فَرِيًّا
verses.arabicClean: فأتت به قومها تحمله ۖ قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا
