verses.arabic: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ۗ ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة ۖ وإلينا ترجعون
verses.transliterated: kullu nafsin dhāiqatu l-mawti wanablūkum bil-shari wal-khayri fit'natan wa-ilaynā tur'jaʿūn
verses.english: Every soul will taste death, after we put you to the test through adversity and prosperity, then to us you ultimately return.

1981.english: Everyone will taste death; you are now being tested through adversity, as well as prosperity, then you will be returned to us.

1989.english: Every soul will taste death, after we put you to the test through adversity, as well as prosperity, then to us you ultimately return.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى يَذْكُرُ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَهُم بِذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā raāka alladhīna kafarū in yattakhidhūnaka illā huzuwan ahādhā alladhī yadhkuru ālihatakum wahum bidhik'ri l-raḥmāni hum kāfirūn
verses.english: When those who disbelieve see you, they ridicule you: "Is this the one who challenges your gods?" Meanwhile, they remain totally heedless of the message from the Most Gracious.
verses.subtitle: All Messengers Ridiculed

1981.english: When the disbelievers see you, they scoff at you, saying, "Is this the one who attacks your idols?" Meanwhile, they reject the message of God most gracious.

1989.english: When those who disbelieved see you, they ridicule you: “Is this the one who talks about your idols?” They totally disregard the message of the Most Gracious.
1989.subtitle: All Messengers Ridiculed

verses.arabic: خُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُو۟رِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِى فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
verses.arabicClean: خلق الإنسان من عجل ۚ سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون
verses.transliterated: khuliqa l-insānu min ʿajalin sa-urīkum āyātī falā tastaʿjilūn
verses.english: The human being is impatient by nature. I will inevitably show you My signs; do not be in such a hurry.

1981.english: The human being is hasty by nature; I will afflict you (disbelievers) with My judgments; do not be in a hurry.

1989.english: The human being is impatient by nature. I will surely show you My signs; do not be in such a hurry.

verses.arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين
verses.transliterated: wayaqūlūna matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīn
verses.english: They challenge: "Where is that (retribution), if you are truthful?"

1981.english: They say, "When will that threat come to pass, if you are truthful?"

1989.english: They challenge: “Where is that (retribution), if you are truthful?”

verses.arabic: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَن وُجُوهِهِمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا عَن ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم ولا هم ينصرون
verses.transliterated: law yaʿlamu alladhīna kafarū ḥīna lā yakuffūna ʿan wujūhihimu l-nāra walā ʿan ẓuhūrihim walā hum yunṣarūn
verses.english: If only those who disbelieve could envision themselves when they try to ward off the fire; off their faces and their backs! No one will help them then.

1981.english: If only the disbelievers realize how they will try to ward off the fire from their faces and their backs! They will have none to help them.

1989.english: If only those who disbelieved could realize how it will be when they try to ward the fire off their faces and their backs! They will receive no help.

verses.arabic: بَلْ تَأْتِيهِم بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: بل تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم فلا يستطيعون ردها ولا هم ينظرون
verses.transliterated: bal tatīhim baghtatan fatabhatuhum falā yastaṭīʿūna raddahā walā hum yunẓarūn
verses.english: Indeed, it will come to them suddenly, and they will be utterly stunned. They can neither avoid it, nor can they receive any respite.

1981.english: Indeed, judgment will afflict them suddenly; it will overwhelm them, so they can neither evade it, nor will they be respited.

1989.english: Indeed, it will come to them so suddenly, they will be utterly stunned. They can neither repel it, nor receive any respite.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدِ ٱسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون
verses.transliterated: walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūn
verses.english: Messengers before you have been ridiculed, and, consequently, those who ridiculed them incurred the retribution for their ridiculing.

1981.english: Messengers before you have been ridiculed, and those who mocked them were doomed because of their ridiculing.

1989.english: Messengers before you have been ridiculed, and those who ridiculed them have incurred the consequence: of their ridiculing.

verses.arabic: قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِم مُّعْرِضُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن ۗ بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون
verses.transliterated: qul man yakla-ukum bi-al-layli wal-nahāri mina l-raḥmāni bal hum ʿan dhik'ri rabbihim muʿ'riḍūn
verses.english: Say, "Who can protect you from the Most Gracious during the night or during the day?" Indeed, they are totally oblivious to the message of their Lord.
verses.subtitle: Priorities Confused

1981.english: Say, "Who can protect you during the night and day besides God most gracious?" Indeed, they are neglecting the message of their Lord.
1981.subtitle: All Power Belongs to God

1989.english: Say, “Who takes care of you during the night and the day, other than the Most Gracious?” Indeed, they are totally disregarding the message of their Lord.
1989.subtitle: Humans’ Priorities Confused

verses.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُم مِّن دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُم مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا ۚ لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون
verses.transliterated: am lahum ālihatun tamnaʿuhum min dūninā lā yastaṭīʿūna naṣra anfusihim walā hum minnā yuṣ'ḥabūn
verses.english: Do they have gods who can protect them from us? They cannot even help themselves. Nor can they accompany one another when they are summoned to face us.

1981.english: Have they found gods who can help them besides us? They cannot even help themselves, nor can they band together against us.

1989.english: Do they have gods who can protect them from us? They cannot even help themselves. Nor can they accompany one another when they face us.

verses.arabic: بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِى ٱلْأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَآ أَفَهُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر ۗ أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها ۚ أفهم الغالبون
verses.transliterated: bal mattaʿnā hāulāi waābāahum ḥattā ṭāla ʿalayhimu l-ʿumuru afalā yarawna annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā afahumu l-ghālibūn
verses.english: We have provided for these people and their ancestors, up until an old age. Do they not see that every day on earth brings them closer to the end? Can they reverse this process?

1981.english: Indeed, we allowed these people, and their parents, to go on for a long life. Do they not realize that every day on earth brings closer to the end? Can they alter this?

1989.english: We have provided for these people and their ancestors, up until an old age. Do they not see that every day on earth brings them closer to the end? Can they reverse this process?

verses.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أُنذِرُكُم بِٱلْوَحْىِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا مَا يُنذَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي ۚ ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون
verses.transliterated: qul innamā undhirukum bil-waḥyi walā yasmaʿu l-ṣumu l-duʿāa idhā mā yundharūn
verses.english: Say, "I am warning you in accordance with divine inspiration." However, the deaf cannot hear the call, when they are warned.

1981.english: Say, "I only warn you according to the revelations." However, the deaf cannot hear the call, when they are warned.

1989.english: Say, “I am warning you in accordance with divine inspiration.” However, the deaf cannot hear the call, when they are warned.

verses.arabic: وَلَئِن مَّسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَٰوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين
verses.transliterated: wala-in massathum nafḥatun min ʿadhābi rabbika layaqūlunna yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīn
verses.english: When a sample of your Lord's retribution afflicts them, they readily say, "We were indeed wicked."

1981.english: Only when afflicted with a touch of your Lord's retribution do the wicked admit, "Woe to us; we were indeed wrong."

1989.english: When a sample of your Lord’s retribution afflicts them, they readily say, “We were indeed wicked.”

verses.arabic: وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْـًٔا وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا ۖ وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها ۗ وكفى بنا حاسبين
verses.transliterated: wanaḍaʿu l-mawāzīna l-qis'ṭa liyawmi l-qiyāmati falā tuẓ'lamu nafsun shayan wa-in kāna mith'qāla ḥabbatin min khardalin ataynā bihā wakafā binā ḥāsibīn
verses.english: We will establish the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection. No soul will suffer the least injustice. Even the equivalent of a mustard seed will be accounted for. We are the most efficient reckoners.

1981.english: We will set up the equitable scales on the day of resurrection. Thus, not a soul will be wronged in the least. Even the equivalent of a mustard seed will be brought by us. We suffice as reckoners.

1989.english: We will establish the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection. No soul will suffer any injustice. Even the equivalent of a mustard seed will be accounted for. We are the most efficient reckoners.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءً وَذِكْرًا لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين
verses.transliterated: walaqad ātaynā mūsā wahārūna l-fur'qāna waḍiyāan wadhik'ran lil'muttaqīn
verses.english: We gave Moses and Aaron the Statute Book, a beacon, and a reminder for the righteous.
verses.subtitle: Prophets Moses and Aaron

1981.english: We have given Moses and Aaron the statute book, and enlightenment, and a message for the righteous;
1981.subtitle: Moses and Aaron

1989.english: We gave Moses and Aaron the Statute Book, and a beacon, and a reminder for the righteous—
1989.subtitle: Prophets Moses and Aaron

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَهُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وهم من الساعة مشفقون
verses.transliterated: alladhīna yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghaybi wahum mina l-sāʿati mush'fiqūn
verses.english: The ones who reverence their Lord, even when alone in their privacy, and they worry about the Hour.

1981.english: Who reverence their Lord in their privacy, and worry about the hereafter.

1989.english: who reverence their Lord, even when alone in their privacy, and they worry about the Hour.

verses.arabic: وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ أَفَأَنتُمْ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه ۚ أفأنتم له منكرون
verses.transliterated: wahādhā dhik'run mubārakun anzalnāhu afa-antum lahu munkirūn
verses.english: This too is a blessed reminder that we sent down. Are you denying it?

1981.english: Similarly, this is a blessed message that we send down; are you going to deny it?

1989.english: This too is a blessed reminder that we have sent down. Are you denying it?

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ رُشْدَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين
verses.transliterated: walaqad ātaynā ib'rāhīma rush'dahu min qablu wakunnā bihi ʿālimīn
verses.english: Before that, we granted Abraham his guidance and understanding, for we were fully aware of him.
verses.subtitle: Abraham
verses.footnote: Was Abraham so smart as to discover God, or, did God grant him the intelligence because He knew that he deserved to be saved? As it turns out, this whole world was created to redeem those among us who deserve redemption. When the angels suggested that all the rebels, humans and jinns, must be banished out of God's kingdom, 'I know what you do not know' (2:30). At the same time, this world proves Satan's incompetence as a god (App. 7).

1981.english: And we gave Abraham his guidance before that; we were fully aware of him.
1981.subtitle: Abraham

1989.english: Before that, we granted Abraham his understanding, for we were fully aware of him.*
1989.subtitle: Abraham
1989.footnote: Was Abraham so smart as to discover God, or, did God grant him the intelligence because He knew that he deserved to be saved? As it turns out, this whole world was created to redeem those among us who deserve redemption. When the angels suggested to throw us all in Hell, God told them, ‘I know what you do not know’ (2:30). At the same time, this world proves Satan’s incompetence as a god (App. 7).

verses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون
verses.transliterated: idh qāla li-abīhi waqawmihi mā hādhihi l-tamāthīlu allatī antum lahā ʿākifūn
verses.english: He said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoting yourselves?"

1981.english: He said to his father and his people, "What are these statues that you worship?"

1989.english: He said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are devoting yourselves?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا وجدنا آباءنا لها عابدين
verses.transliterated: qālū wajadnā ābāanā lahā ʿābidīn
verses.english: They said, "We found our parents worshiping them."

1981.english: They said, "We found our ancestors worshiping them."

1989.english: They said, “We found our parents worshiping them.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: قال لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين
verses.transliterated: qāla laqad kuntum antum waābāukum fī ḍalālin mubīni
verses.english: He said, "Indeed, you and your parents have gone totally astray."

1981.english: He said, "Indeed, you and your ancestors are totally astray."

1989.english: He said, “Indeed, you and your parents have gone completely astray.’

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا أجئتنا بالحق أم أنت من اللاعبين
verses.transliterated: qālū aji'tanā bil-ḥaqi am anta mina l-lāʿibīn
verses.english: They said, "Are you telling us the truth, or are you playing?"

1981.english: They said, "Have you brought the truth, or are you just playing?"

1989.english: They said, “Are you telling us the truth, or are you playing?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمْ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال بل ربكم رب السماوات والأرض الذي فطرهن وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين
verses.transliterated: qāla bal rabbukum rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi alladhī faṭarahunna wa-anā ʿalā dhālikum mina l-shāhidīn
verses.english: He said, "Your only Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them. This is the testimony to which I bear witness.

1981.english: He said, "Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them. This is what I testify to.

1989.english: He said, “Your only Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them. This is my testimony.

verses.arabic: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وتالله لأكيدن أصنامكم بعد أن تولوا مدبرين
verses.transliterated: watal-lahi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum baʿda an tuwallū mud'birīn
verses.english: "I swear by GOD, I have a plan to deal with your statues, as soon as you leave."

1981.english: "By God, I will do something about your statues, as soon as you leave."

1989.english: “I swear by GOD, I have a plan to deal with your statues, as soon as you leave.”

verses.arabic: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون
verses.transliterated: fajaʿalahum judhādhan illā kabīran lahum laʿallahum ilayhi yarjiʿūn
verses.english: He broke them into pieces, except for a big one, that they may refer to it.

1981.english: He broke them into pieces, leaving the biggest among them, that they may refer to it.

1989.english: He broke them into pieces, except for the big one, that they may refer to it.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا من فعل هذا بآلهتنا إنه لمن الظالمين
verses.transliterated: qālū man faʿala hādhā biālihatinā innahu lamina l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: They said, "Whoever did this to our gods is really a transgressor."

1981.english: They said, "Who did this to our gods? He is really wicked."

1989.english: They said, “Whoever did this to our gods is really a transgressor.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم
verses.transliterated: qālū samiʿ'nā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu ib'rāhīm
verses.english: They said, "We heard a youth threaten them; he is called Abraham."

1981.english: They said, "We heard a youth threaten them; his name is Abraham."

1989.english: They said, “We heard a youth threaten them; his name is Abraham.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ فَأْتُوا۟ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا فأتوا به على أعين الناس لعلهم يشهدون
verses.transliterated: qālū fatū bihi ʿalā aʿyuni l-nāsi laʿallahum yashhadūn
verses.english: They said, "Bring him before the eyes of all the people, that they may bear witness."

1981.english: They said, "Then bring him in front of all the people, that they may bear witness."

1989.english: They said, “Bring him before the eyes of all the people; let them bear witness.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا أأنت فعلت هذا بآلهتنا يا إبراهيم
verses.transliterated: qālū a-anta faʿalta hādhā biālihatinā yāib'rāhīm
verses.english: They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"

1981.english: They said, "Did you do this to our gods, Abraham?"

1989.english: They said, “Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال بل فعله كبيرهم هذا فاسألوهم إن كانوا ينطقون
verses.transliterated: qāla bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fasalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn
verses.english: He said, "It is that big one who did it. Go ask them, if they can speak."
verses.subtitle: Abraham Proves His Point

1981.english: He said, "It must be the biggest one who did it. So ask them, if they do speak."

1989.english: He said, “It is that big one who did it. Go ask them, if they can speak.”
1989.subtitle: Abraham Proves His Point

verses.arabic: فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فقالوا إنكم أنتم الظالمون
verses.transliterated: farajaʿū ilā anfusihim faqālū innakum antumu l-ẓālimūn
verses.english: They were taken aback, and said to themselves, "Indeed, you are the ones who have been transgressing."

1981.english: They conferred and said to each other, "Indeed, it is you who are wrong."

1989.english: They were taken aback, and said to themselves, “Indeed, you have been wrong.”

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم نكسوا على رءوسهم لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون
verses.transliterated: thumma nukisū ʿalā ruūsihim laqad ʿalim'ta mā hāulāi yanṭiqūn
verses.english: Yet, they reverted to their old ideas: "You know full well that these cannot speak."

1981.english: Yet, they reverted, against their own common sense, (and said,) "You know well that these cannot speak."

1989.english: Yet, they reverted to their old ideas: “You know full well that these cannot speak.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
verses.arabicClean: قال أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم
verses.transliterated: qāla afataʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi mā lā yanfaʿukum shayan walā yaḍurruku
verses.english: He said, "Do you then worship besides GOD what possesses no power to benefit you or harm you?

1981.english: He said, "Do you then worship besides God what is too powerless to benefit you or harm you?

1989.english: He said, “Do you then worship besides GOD what possesses no power to benefit you or harm you?

verses.arabic: أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله ۖ أفلا تعقلون
verses.transliterated: uffin lakum walimā taʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi afalā taʿqilūn
verses.english: "You have incurred shame by worshiping idols beside GOD. Do you not understand?"

1981.english: "Shame on you and whatever idols you set up besides God. Do you not understand?"

1989.english: “Shame on you and on whatever you worship besides GOD. Do you not understand?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا حرقوه وانصروا آلهتكم إن كنتم فاعلين
verses.transliterated: qālū ḥarriqūhu wa-unṣurū ālihatakum in kuntum fāʿilīn
verses.english: They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if this is what you decide to do."
verses.subtitle: Profound Miracle

1981.english: They said, "Burn him in support of your gods; this is what you should do."

1989.english: They said, “Burn him and support your gods, if this is what you decide to do.”
1989.subtitle: Profound Miracle

verses.arabic: قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
verses.arabicClean: قلنا يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم
verses.transliterated: qul'nā yānāru kūnī bardan wasalāman ʿalā ib'rāhīm
verses.english: We said, "O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham."
verses.footnote: "Cool," without "and safe" would have caused Abraham to freeze.

1981.english: We said, "O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham."

1989.english: We said, “O fire, be cool and safe for Abraham.”

verses.arabic: وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأخسرين
verses.transliterated: wa-arādū bihi kaydan fajaʿalnāhumu l-akhsarīn
verses.english: Thus, they schemed against him, but we made them the losers.

1981.english: They wanted to oppress him, but we made them the losers.

1989.english: Thus, they schemed against him, but we made them the losers.

verses.arabic: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ونجيناه ولوطا إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها للعالمين
verses.transliterated: wanajjaynāhu walūṭan ilā l-arḍi allatī bāraknā fīhā lil'ʿālamīn
verses.english: We saved him, and we saved Lot, to the land that we blessed for all the people.

1981.english: And we saved him, together with Lot, to the land that we blessed for all the people.

1989.english: We saved him, and we saved Lot, to the land that we blessed for all the people.

verses.arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب نافلة ۖ وكلا جعلنا صالحين
verses.transliterated: wawahabnā lahu is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba nāfilatan wakullan jaʿalnā ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: And we granted him Isaac and Jacob as a gift, and we made them both righteous.

1981.english: We granted him Isaac and Jacob as a gift, and we made them righteous.
1981.subtitle: The Origin of Salat Prayers and Zakat Charity

1989.english: And we granted him Isaac and Jacob as a gift, and we made them both righteous.

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلناهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا وأوحينا إليهم فعل الخيرات وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة ۖ وكانوا لنا عابدين
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalnāhum a-immatan yahdūna bi-amrinā wa-awḥaynā ilayhim fiʿ'la l-khayrāti wa-iqāma l-ṣalati waītāa l-zakati wakānū lanā ʿābidīn
verses.english: We made them imams who guided in accordance with our commandments, and we taught them how to work righteousness, and how to observe the Contact Prayers (Salat) and the obligatory charity (Zakat). To us, they were devoted worshipers.
verses.subtitle: Abraham: Delivered All Religious Duties of Submission
verses.footnote: When the Quran was revealed, all religious duties were already established through Abraham (2:128, 16:123, 22:78).

1981.english: We made them imams who guide according to our commandments, and we taught them how to work righteousness, and how to observe the **salat** prayers and **zakat** charity.* To Him, they were worshipers.
1981.footnote: Those who refuse to believe God's repeated assertions that the Quran is complete and perfect (see 6:38, 114, 17:89, 18:54, 30:58, & 39:27), frequently pose a favorite question. They ask, "If the Quran is complete and perfect, where can we find details of **salat** prayers?" This question obviously reveals their ignorance of the Quran. We learn from this verse, as well as many other verses, that **salat** and **zakat** were given originally to Abraham and his family, then transmitted to us generation after generation (see 2:128, 187, 3:68, 16:123, 22:27, 78, and Appendix 8).

1989.english: We made them imams who guided in accordance with our commandments, and we taught them how to work righteousness, and how to observe the contact prayers (Salat) and the obligatory charity (Zakat).* To us, they were devoted worshipers.
1989.subtitle: Abraham: Delivered All Religious Duties of Islam
1989.footnote: When the Quran was revealed, all religious duties were already established through Abraham (2:128, 16:123, 22:78).

verses.arabic: وَلُوطًا ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِى كَانَت تَّعْمَلُ ٱلْخَبَٰٓئِثَ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَٰسِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولوطا آتيناه حكما وعلما ونجيناه من القرية التي كانت تعمل الخبائث ۗ إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فاسقين
verses.transliterated: walūṭan ātaynāhu ḥuk'man waʿil'man wanajjaynāhu mina l-qaryati allatī kānat taʿmalu l-khabāitha innahum kānū qawma sawin fāsiqīn
verses.english: As for Lot, we granted him wisdom and knowledge, and we saved him from the community that practiced abominations; they were wicked and evil people.
verses.subtitle: Lot

1981.english: As for Lot, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge, and we saved him from the community that committed vice. Indeed, they were evil and wicked people.
1981.subtitle: Lot

1989.english: And we granted Lot wisdom and knowledge, and we saved him from the community that practiced abominations; they were wicked and evil people.
1989.subtitle: Lot

verses.arabic: وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأدخلناه في رحمتنا ۖ إنه من الصالحين
verses.transliterated: wa-adkhalnāhu fī raḥmatinā innahu mina l-ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: We admitted him into our mercy, for he was righteous.

1981.english: And we admitted him into our mercy, for he was righteous.

1989.english: We admitted him into our mercy, for he was righteous.

verses.arabic: وَنُوحًا إِذْ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: ونوحا إذ نادى من قبل فاستجبنا له فنجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم
verses.transliterated: wanūḥan idh nādā min qablu fa-is'tajabnā lahu fanajjaynāhu wa-ahlahu mina l-karbi l-ʿaẓīm
verses.english: And, before that, Noah called and we responded to him. We saved him and his family from the great disaster.
verses.subtitle: Noah

1981.english: And when Noah called before that, we responded to him, and saved him and his family from the great disaster.
1981.subtitle: Noah

1989.english: And, before that, Noah called and we responded to him. We saved him and his family from the great disaster.
1989.subtitle: Noah

verses.arabic: وَنَصَرْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ونصرناه من القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا ۚ إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فأغرقناهم أجمعين
verses.transliterated: wanaṣarnāhu mina l-qawmi alladhīna kadhabū biāyātinā innahum kānū qawma sawin fa-aghraqnāhum ajmaʿīn
verses.english: We supported him against the people who rejected our revelations. They were evil people, so we drowned them all.

1981.english: And we supported him against the people who rejected our revelations. Because they were evil people, we drowned them all.

1989.english: We supported him against the people who rejected our revelations. They were evil people, so we drowned them all.

verses.arabic: وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وداوود وسليمان إذ يحكمان في الحرث إذ نفشت فيه غنم القوم وكنا لحكمهم شاهدين
verses.transliterated: wadāwūda wasulaymāna idh yaḥkumāni fī l-ḥarthi idh nafashat fīhi ghanamu l-qawmi wakunnā liḥuk'mihim shāhidīn
verses.english: And David and Solomon, when they once ruled with regard to someone's crop that was destroyed by another's sheep. We witnessed their judgment.
verses.subtitle: David and Solomon

1981.english: And when David and Solomon issued their judgments regarding the sheep that ate some people's crops, we were witnessing their judgments.
1981.subtitle: David and Solomon

1989.english: And David and Solomon once ruled with regard to someone’s crop that was destroyed by another’s sheep. We witnessed their judgment.
1989.subtitle: David and Solomon

verses.arabic: فَفَهَّمْنَٰهَا سُلَيْمَٰنَ وَكُلًّا ءَاتَيْنَا حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُۥدَ ٱلْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَٱلطَّيْرَ وَكُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ففهمناها سليمان ۚ وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما ۚ وسخرنا مع داوود الجبال يسبحن والطير ۚ وكنا فاعلين
verses.transliterated: fafahhamnāhā sulaymāna wakullan ātaynā ḥuk'man waʿil'man wasakharnā maʿa dāwūda l-jibāla yusabbiḥ'na wal-ṭayra wakunnā fāʿilīn
verses.english: We granted Solomon the correct understanding, though we endowed both of them with wisdom and knowledge. We committed the mountains to serve David in glorifying (GOD), as well as the birds. This is what we did.

1981.english: We endowed Solomon with the correct understanding, though we endowed both of them with wisdom and knowledge. And we subjugated the mountains to David; they submitted, and so did the birds. This is what we did.

1989.english: We granted Solomon the correct understanding, though we endowed both of them with wisdom and knowledge. We committed the mountains to glorify (God) and to serve David, as well as the birds. This is what we did.

verses.arabic: وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ شَٰكِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وعلمناه صنعة لبوس لكم لتحصنكم من بأسكم ۖ فهل أنتم شاكرون
verses.transliterated: waʿallamnāhu ṣanʿata labūsin lakum lituḥ'ṣinakum min basikum fahal antum shākirūn
verses.english: And we taught him the skill of making shields to protect you in war. Are you then thankful?

1981.english: And we taught him the manufacture of shields that protect you from each other's aggression. Would you be thankful?

1989.english: And we taught him the skill of making shields to protect you in war. Are you then thankful?

verses.arabic: وَلِسُلَيْمَٰنَ ٱلرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً تَجْرِى بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلَّتِى بَٰرَكْنَا فِيهَا وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولسليمان الريح عاصفة تجري بأمره إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها ۚ وكنا بكل شيء عالمين
verses.transliterated: walisulaymāna l-rīḥa ʿāṣifatan tajrī bi-amrihi ilā l-arḍi allatī bāraknā fīhā wakunnā bikulli shayin ʿālimīn
verses.english: For Solomon, we committed the wind gusting and blowing at his disposal. He could direct it as he wished, to whatever land he chose, and we blessed such land for him. We are fully aware of all things.

1981.english: For Solomon, we subjugated the winds, gusting and blowing at his command to the land that we blessed. We are fully aware of all things.

1989.english: For Solomon, we committed the wind gusting and blowing in his service. He could direct it as he wished, to whatever land he chose, and we blessed such land for him. We are fully aware of all things.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُۥ وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَٰفِظِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ومن الشياطين من يغوصون له ويعملون عملا دون ذلك ۖ وكنا لهم حافظين
verses.transliterated: wamina l-shayāṭīni man yaghūṣūna lahu wayaʿmalūna ʿamalan dūna dhālika wakunnā lahum ḥāfiẓīn
verses.english: And of the devils there were those who would dive for him (to harvest the sea), or do whatever else he commanded them to do. We committed them in his service.

1981.english: Also the devils were subjugated to dive for him, and do all kinds of work; we kept them in his service.

1989.english: And of the devils there were those who would dive for him (to harvest the sea), or do whatever else he commanded them to do. We kept them in his service.

verses.arabic: وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر وأنت أرحم الراحمين
verses.transliterated: wa-ayyūba idh nādā rabbahu annī massaniya l-ḍuru wa-anta arḥamu l-rāḥimīn
verses.english: And Job implored his Lord: "Adversity has befallen me, and, of all the merciful ones, You are the Most Merciful."
verses.subtitle: Job

1981.english: And when Job called upon his Lord, saying, "Adversity has afflicted me, and You are the most merciful,"
1981.subtitle: Job

1989.english: And Job implored his Lord: “Adversity has befallen me, and, of all the merciful ones, You are the Most Merciful.”
1989.subtitle: Job

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فاستجبنا له فكشفنا ما به من ضر ۖ وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة من عندنا وذكرى للعابدين
verses.transliterated: fa-is'tajabnā lahu fakashafnā mā bihi min ḍurrin waātaynāhu ahlahu wamith'lahum maʿahum raḥmatan min ʿindinā wadhik'rā lil'ʿābidīn
verses.english: We responded to him, relieved his adversity, and restored his family for him, even twice as much. That was a mercy from us, and a reminder for the worshipers.

1981.english: we answered his prayer, and relieved his adversity. We restored his family for him, and multiplied them, as mercy from us, and a reminder for the worshipers.

1989.english: We responded to him, relieved his adversity, and restored his family for him, and doubled them. That was a mercy from us, and a reminder for the worshipers.

verses.arabic: وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل ۖ كل من الصابرين
verses.transliterated: wa-is'māʿīla wa-id'rīsa wadhā l-kif'li kullun mina l-ṣābirīn
verses.english: Also, Ismail, Idrîs, Zal-Kifl; all were steadfast, patient.

1981.english: Similarly, Ishmael, Idris, and Dhal-kifl; each was steadfastly patient.
1981.subtitle: Many Prophets; One Message

1989.english: Also, Ismail, Idris, Zal-Kifl; all were steadfast, patient.

verses.arabic: وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا ۖ إنهم من الصالحين
verses.transliterated: wa-adkhalnāhum fī raḥmatinā innahum mina l-ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: We admitted them into our mercy, for they were righteous.

1981.english: We admitted them into our mercy, for they were righteous.

1989.english: We admitted them into our mercy, for they were righteous.

verses.arabic: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر عليه فنادى في الظلمات أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين
verses.transliterated: wadhā l-nūni idh dhahaba mughāḍiban faẓanna an lan naqdira ʿalayhi fanādā fī l-ẓulumāti an lā ilāha illā anta sub'ḥānaka innī kuntu mina l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: And Zan-Noon (Jonah, "the one with an 'N' in his name"), abandoned his mission in protest, thinking that we could not control him. He ended up imploring from the darkness (of the big fish's belly): "There is no god other than You. Be You glorified. I have committed a gross sin."
verses.subtitle: Jonah

1981.english: And when Dhan-noon (Jonah) left in anger, and thought that we could not reach him, he ended up calling from the darkness (of the fish): "There is no god except You; glory be to You; I was wrong indeed."

1989.english: And Zan-Noon (Jonah, “the one with an ‘N ’ in his name”), abandoned his mission in protest, thinking that we could not control him. He ended up imploring from the darkness (of the big fish’s belly): “There is no other god besides You. Be You glorified. I have committed an error.’
1989.subtitle: Jonah

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم ۚ وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين
verses.transliterated: fa-is'tajabnā lahu wanajjaynāhu mina l-ghami wakadhālika nunjī l-mu'minīn
verses.english: We responded to him, and saved him from the crisis; we thus save the believers.

1981.english: We then answered his prayer, and saved him from the disaster; we thus save the believers.

1989.english: We responded to him, and saved him from misery; we thus save the believers.

verses.arabic: وَزَكَرِيَّآ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وزكريا إذ نادى ربه رب لا تذرني فردا وأنت خير الوارثين
verses.transliterated: wazakariyyā idh nādā rabbahu rabbi lā tadharnī fardan wa-anta khayru l-wārithīn
verses.english: And Zachariah implored his Lord: "My Lord, do not keep me without an heir, though You are the best inheritor."
verses.subtitle: Zachariah and John

1981.english: And when Zechariah called upon his Lord: "My Lord, leave me not childless, though You are the ultimate inheritor,"

1989.english: And Zachariah implored his Lord: “My Lord, do not keep me without an heir, though You are the best inheritor.”
1989.subtitle: Zachariah and John

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فاستجبنا له ووهبنا له يحيى وأصلحنا له زوجه ۚ إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا ۖ وكانوا لنا خاشعين
verses.transliterated: fa-is'tajabnā lahu wawahabnā lahu yaḥyā wa-aṣlaḥnā lahu zawjahu innahum kānū yusāriʿūna fī l-khayrāti wayadʿūnanā raghaban warahaban wakānū lanā khāshiʿīn
verses.english: We responded to him and granted him John; we fixed his wife for him. That is because they used to hasten to work righteousness, and implored us in situations of joy, as well as fear. To us, they were reverent.
verses.footnote: The use of the plural tense throughout the Quran indicates participation of the angels. It is clear from 3:39 and from the Bible that the angels dealt with Zachariah extensively, as they gave him the good news about John. See Appendix 10.

1981.english: we answered his prayer, and granted him John; we fixed his wife for him. They used to hasten into righteous works, and turn to us in need, as well as in reverence; to us, they were humble.

1989.english: We* responded to him and granted him John; we fixed his wife for him. That is because they always hastened to work righteousness, and implored us in situations of joy, as well as fear. To us, they were reverent.
1989.footnote: The use of the plural tense throughout Quran indicates participation of the angels. For example, it is clear from 3:39 and from the Bible that the angels dealt with Zachariah extensively, as they gave him the good news about John. See Appendix 10.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِن رُّوحِنَا وَجَعَلْنَٰهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: والتي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين
verses.transliterated: wa-allatī aḥṣanat farjahā fanafakhnā fīhā min rūḥinā wajaʿalnāhā wa-ib'nahā āyatan lil'ʿālamīn
verses.english: As for the one who maintained her virginity, we blew into her from our spirit, and thus, we made her and her son a portent for the whole world.
verses.subtitle: Mary and Jesus

1981.english: And the one who guarded her chastity, we blew into her from the spirit, and we made her and her son a sign for the whole world.

1989.english: And (recall) the one who maintained her virginity, then we blew into her from our spirit. We rendered her and her son a sign for the whole world.
1989.subtitle: Mary and Jesus

verses.arabic: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً وَأَنَا۠ رَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُونِ
verses.arabicClean: إن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاعبدون
verses.transliterated: inna hādhihi ummatukum ummatan wāḥidatan wa-anā rabbukum fa-uʿ'budūn
verses.english: Your congregation is but one congregation, and I alone am your Lord; you shall worship Me alone.
verses.subtitle: One God / One Religion

1981.english: Such is your religion: one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.

1989.english: Such (are the messengers of) your congregation—one congregation—and I am your Lord; you shall worship Me alone.
1989.subtitle: One God/One Religion

verses.arabic: وَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَٰجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم ۖ كل إلينا راجعون
verses.transliterated: wataqaṭṭaʿū amrahum baynahum kullun ilaynā rājiʿūn
verses.english: However, they divided themselves into disputing religions. All of them will come back to us (for judgment).

1981.english: However, they divided themselves into different religions; all are returning to us.

1989.english: Unfortunately, they divided themselves into disputing factions. All of them will come back to us (for judgment).

verses.arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِۦ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ كَٰتِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فمن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا كفران لسعيه وإنا له كاتبون
verses.transliterated: faman yaʿmal mina l-ṣāliḥāti wahuwa mu'minun falā kuf'rāna lisaʿyihi wa-innā lahu kātibūn
verses.english: As for those who work righteousness, while believing, their work will not go to waste; we are recording it.

1981.english: Whoever works righteousness, while a believer, his works will never go in vain; we are recording them.

1989.english: As for those who work righteousness, while believing, their work will not go to waste; we are recording it.

verses.arabic: وَحَرَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون
verses.transliterated: waḥarāmun ʿalā qaryatin ahlaknāhā annahum lā yarjiʿūn
verses.english: It is forbidden for any community we had annihilated to return.

1981.english: Never will a community that we annihilated return back (to this world).

1989.english: It is forbidden for any community we had annihilated to return.

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُتِحَتْ يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ وَهُم مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā futiḥat yajūju wamajūju wahum min kulli ḥadabin yansilūn
verses.english: Not until Gog and Magog reappear, will they then return—they will come from every direction.
verses.subtitle: The End of the World
verses.footnote: By the year 2270 AD, thanks to God's mathematical miracle in the Quran (Appendix 1), America will be the heart of Submission, and billions around the globe will have believed in the Quran (9:33, 41:53, 48:28, 61:9). Gog and Magog (allegorical names of villainous communities), will be the only bastions of heathenism, and they will attack the submitters. That is when the world will end (15:87, 18:94, Appendix 25). Gog and Magog are mentioned in 18:94 & 21:96, 17 verses before the end of each sura; this may indicate the time of their appearance.

1981.english: Not until Gog and Magog are opened; that is when they will come from every direction.

1989.english: Not until Gog and Magog reappear,* will they then return—they will come from every direction.
1989.subtitle: The End of the World
1989.footnote: By the year 2270 AD, thanks to God’s mathematical miracle in the Quran (Appendix 1), America will be the heart of Islam, and billions around the globe will have believed in the Quran (9:33, 41:53, 48:28, 61:9). Gog and Magog, will be the only bastions of heathenism, and they will attack the Muslims. That is when the world will end (15:87, 18:94, Appendix 25). God has not yet revealed the identity of Gog and Magog.

verses.arabic: وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: واقترب الوعد الحق فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا بل كنا ظالمين
verses.transliterated: wa-iq'taraba l-waʿdu l-ḥaqu fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣatun abṣāru alladhīna kafarū yāwaylanā qad kunnā fī ghaflatin min hādhā bal kunnā ẓālimīn
verses.english: That is when the inevitable prophecy will come to pass, and the disbelievers will stare in horror: "Woe to us; we have been oblivious. Indeed, we have been wicked."

1981.english: The truthful promise comes to pass, and those who disbelieved in our revelations will look in horror: "Woe to us, we were totally heedless of this. Indeed, we were wrong."

1989.english: That is when the fulfillment of the truthful promise will approach. The disbelievers will stare in horror: “Woe to us. We were oblivious to this. In fact, we have been wicked.”

verses.arabic: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنتُمْ لَهَا وَٰرِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون
verses.transliterated: innakum wamā taʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi ḥaṣabu jahannama antum lahā wāridūn
verses.english: You and the idols you worship besides GOD will be fuel for Hell; this is your inevitable destiny.
verses.subtitle: The Hereafter

1981.english: Surely, you and the idols you set up besides God will be fuel for Gehenna; you will be thrown therein.

1989.english: You and the idols you worship besides GOD will be fuel for Hell; this is your inevitable destiny.
1989.subtitle: The Hereafter

verses.arabic: لَوْ كَانَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةً مَّا وَرَدُوهَا وَكُلٌّ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لو كان هؤلاء آلهة ما وردوها ۖ وكل فيها خالدون
verses.transliterated: law kāna hāulāi ālihatan mā waradūhā wakullun fīhā khālidūn
verses.english: If those were gods, they would not have ended up in Hell. All its inhabitants abide in it forever.

1981.english: If these were really gods, they would not have gone therein; they will abide therein forever.

1989.english: If these were gods, they would not have ended in Hell. They all abide therein forever.

verses.arabic: لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يَسْمَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لهم فيها زفير وهم فيها لا يسمعون
verses.transliterated: lahum fīhā zafīrun wahum fīhā lā yasmaʿūn
verses.english: They will sigh and groan therein, and they will have no access to any news.

1981.english: They wail loudly therein, and they will be isolated from hearing anything.

1989.english: They will sigh and groan therein, and they will have no access to anything, while they abide therein.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُم مِّنَّا ٱلْحُسْنَىٰٓ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون
verses.transliterated: inna alladhīna sabaqat lahum minnā l-ḥus'nā ulāika ʿanhā mub'ʿadūn
verses.english: As for those who deserved our magnificent rewards, they will be protected from it.

1981.english: As for those who have deserved our blessings, they will be protected therefrom.

1989.english: As for those who deserved beautiful rewards from us, they will be protected.

verses.arabic: لَا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَهَا وَهُمْ فِى مَا ٱشْتَهَتْ أَنفُسُهُمْ خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لا يسمعون حسيسها ۖ وهم في ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون
verses.transliterated: lā yasmaʿūna ḥasīsahā wahum fī mā ish'tahat anfusuhum khālidūn
verses.english: They will not hear its hissing. They will enjoy an abode where they can get everything they desire, forever.
verses.subtitle: The Righteous

1981.english: Not even its hissing will be heard by them, and they will abide forever in everything they desire.

1989.english: They will not hear its hissing. They will abide in everything they desire, forever.

verses.arabic: لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ ٱلْفَزَعُ ٱلْأَكْبَرُ وَتَتَلَقَّىٰهُمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ هَٰذَا يَوْمُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر وتتلقاهم الملائكة هذا يومكم الذي كنتم توعدون
verses.transliterated: lā yaḥzunuhumu l-fazaʿu l-akbaru watatalaqqāhumu l-malāikatu hādhā yawmukumu alladhī kuntum tūʿadūn
verses.english: The great horror will not worry them, and the angels will receive them joyfully: "This is your day, that has been promised to you."

1981.english: The great horror will not worry them, and the angels receive them, saying, "This is your day, that has been promised to you."

1989.english: The great horror will not worry them, for the angels will receive them joyfully: “This is your day, that has been promised to you.”

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ نَطْوِى ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَطَىِّ ٱلسِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُّعِيدُهُۥ وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا فَٰعِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: يوم نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب ۚ كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده ۚ وعدا علينا ۚ إنا كنا فاعلين
verses.transliterated: yawma naṭwī l-samāa kaṭayyi l-sijili lil'kutubi kamā badanā awwala khalqin nuʿīduhu waʿdan ʿalaynā innā kunnā fāʿilīn
verses.english: On that day, we will fold the heaven, like the folding of a book. Just as we initiated the first creation, we will repeat it. This is our promise; we will certainly carry it out.
verses.subtitle: The Day of Resurrection

1981.english: On that day, We will fold the heavens like the folding of a book. Then, as We initiated the first creation, We will initiate a new creation. This is a promise that We will carry out.

1989.english: On that day, we will fold the heaven, like the folding of a book. Just as we initiated the first creation, we will repeat it. This is our promise; we will certainly carry it out.
1989.subtitle: The Day of Resurrection

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱلذِّكْرِ أَنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون
verses.transliterated: walaqad katabnā fī l-zabūri min baʿdi l-dhik'ri anna l-arḍa yarithuhā ʿibādiya l-ṣāliḥūn
verses.english: We have decreed in the Psalms, as well as in other scriptures, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous worshipers.

1981.english: We already recorded in the Psalms, as We do in this message, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.

1989.english: We have decreed in the Psalms, as well as in other scripture, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous worshipers.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ فِى هَٰذَا لَبَلَٰغًا لِّقَوْمٍ عَٰبِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين
verses.transliterated: inna fī hādhā labalāghan liqawmin ʿābidīn
verses.english: This is a proclamation for people who are worshipers.

1981.english: This is a declaration for the people who worship.

1989.english: This is a proclamation for people who are worshipers.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين
verses.transliterated: wamā arsalnāka illā raḥmatan lil'ʿālamīn
verses.english: We have sent you out of mercy from us towards the whole world.

1981.english: We did not send you, except out of mercy towards the whole world.

1989.english: We have sent you (O Muhammad) out of mercy from us towards the whole world.

verses.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّمَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ فَهَلْ أَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قل إنما يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد ۖ فهل أنتم مسلمون
verses.transliterated: qul innamā yūḥā ilayya annamā ilāhukum ilāhun wāḥidun fahal antum mus'limūn
verses.english: Proclaim, "I have been given divine inspiration that your god is one god. Will you then submit?"

1981.english: Say, "It has been revealed to me that your God is one God; will you then submit to Him?"

1989.english: Proclaim, “I have been given divine inspiration that your god is one god. Will you then submit?”

verses.arabic: فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَقُلْ ءَاذَنتُكُمْ عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ وَإِنْ أَدْرِىٓ أَقَرِيبٌ أَم بَعِيدٌ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فإن تولوا فقل آذنتكم على سواء ۖ وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون
verses.transliterated: fa-in tawallaw faqul ādhantukum ʿalā sawāin wa-in adrī aqarībun am baʿīdun mā tūʿadūn
verses.english: If they turn away, then say, "I have warned you sufficiently, and I have no idea how soon or late (the retribution) will come to you.

1981.english: If they turn away, then say, "I have given you the announcement exactly as given to me, and I have no idea how soon or far is what is promised to you.

1989.english: If they turn away, then say, “I have warned you sufficiently, and I have no idea how soon or late (the retribution) will come to you.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهُۥ يَعْلَمُ ٱلْجَهْرَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْتُمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إنه يعلم الجهر من القول ويعلم ما تكتمون
verses.transliterated: innahu yaʿlamu l-jahra mina l-qawli wayaʿlamu mā taktumūn
verses.english: "He is fully aware of your public utterances, and He is fully aware of everything you conceal.

1981.english: "Only He knows your declared utterances, as well as whatever you conceal.

1989.english: “He is the only One who knows your public utterances, and He knows whatever you conceal.

verses.arabic: وَإِنْ أَدْرِى لَعَلَّهُۥ فِتْنَةٌ لَّكُمْ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين
verses.transliterated: wa-in adrī laʿallahu fit'natun lakum wamatāʿun ilā ḥīni
verses.english: "For all that I know, this world is a test for you, and a temporary enjoyment."

1981.english: "For all that I know, this is a test, and a temporary life for you."

1989.english: “I have no idea; this may be a test for you, and a temporary enjoyment.”

verses.arabic: قَٰلَ رَبِّ ٱحْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَرَبُّنَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب احكم بالحق ۗ وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi uḥ'kum bil-ḥaqi warabbunā l-raḥmānu l-mus'taʿānu ʿalā mā taṣifūn
verses.english: Say, "My Lord, Your judgment is the absolute justice. Our Lord is the Most Gracious; only His help is sought in the face of your claims."

1981.english: He said, "My Lord, your judgment is equitable. Our Lord most gracious is the helper against your claims."

1989.english: Say, “My Lord, You judge equitably. Our Lord is the Most Gracious; only His help is sought in the face of your claims.” -T — >

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَىْءٌ عَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم ۚ إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم
verses.transliterated: yāayyuhā l-nāsu ittaqū rabbakum inna zalzalata l-sāʿati shayon ʿaẓīmu
verses.english: O people, you shall reverence your Lord, for the quaking of the Hour is something horrendous.

1981.english: O People, observe your Lord, for the shock of the Hour is a tremendous thing.

1989.english: O people, reverence your Lord, for the quaking of the Hour is something horrendous.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَهَا تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَٰرَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ
verses.arabicClean: يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد
verses.transliterated: yawma tarawnahā tadhhalu kullu mur'ḍiʿatin ʿammā arḍaʿat wataḍaʿu kullu dhāti ḥamlin ḥamlahā watarā l-nāsa sukārā wamā hum bisukārā walākinna ʿadhāba l-lahi shadīdu
verses.english: The day you witness it, even a nursing mother will discard her infant, and a pregnant woman will abort her fetus. You will see the people staggering, as if they are intoxicated, even though they are not intoxicated. This is because GOD's retribution is so awesome.

1981.english: The day you see it, even a nursing mother will discard her infant, and the pregnant will abort her fetus. And you will see the people intoxicated, not from intoxicants, but because God's retribution is severe.

1989.english: The day you witness it, (it will be so horrendous that) a nursing mother will even discard her infant, and a pregnant woman will abort her fetus. And you will see the people staggering as if they are intoxicated, even though they are not intoxicated. But GOD’s retribution is awesome.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطَٰنٍ مَّرِيدٍ
verses.arabicClean: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ويتبع كل شيطان مريد
verses.transliterated: wamina l-nāsi man yujādilu fī l-lahi bighayri ʿil'min wayattabiʿu kulla shayṭānin marīdi
verses.english: Among the people, there are those who argue about GOD without knowledge, and follow every rebellious devil.

1981.english: Some people argue against God without knowledge, and follow every rebellious devil.

1989.english: Among the people, there are those who argue about GOD without knowledge, and follow every rebellious devil.

verses.arabic: كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ مَن تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُۥ يُضِلُّهُۥ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
verses.arabicClean: كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير
verses.transliterated: kutiba ʿalayhi annahu man tawallāhu fa-annahu yuḍilluhu wayahdīhi ilā ʿadhābi l-saʿīr
verses.english: It is decreed that anyone who allies himself with him, he will mislead him and guide him to the agony of Hell.

1981.english: It has been decreed that anyone who allies himself with him, he will mislead him, and guide him only to the agony of hell.

1989.english: It is decreed that anyone who allies himself with him, he will mislead him and guide him to the agony of Hell.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ مُّخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوٓا۟ أَشُدَّكُمْ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًٔا وَتَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ هَامِدَةً فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنۢبَتَتْ مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۭ بَهِيجٍ
verses.arabicClean: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا خلقناكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة لنبين لكم ۚ ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ۖ ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا ۚ وترى الأرض هامدة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج
verses.transliterated: yāayyuhā l-nāsu in kuntum fī raybin mina l-baʿthi fa-innā khalaqnākum min turābin thumma min nuṭ'fatin thumma min ʿalaqatin thumma min muḍ'ghatin mukhallaqatin waghayri mukhallaqatin linubayyina lakum wanuqirru fī l-arḥāmi mā nashāu ilā ajalin musamman thumma nukh'rijukum ṭif'lan thumma litablughū ashuddakum waminkum man yutawaffā waminkum man yuraddu ilā ardhali l-ʿumuri likaylā yaʿlama min baʿdi ʿil'min shayan watarā l-arḍa hāmidatan fa-idhā anzalnā ʿalayhā l-māa ih'tazzat warabat wa-anbatat min kulli zawjin bahīji
verses.english: O people, if you have any doubt about resurrection, (remember that) we created you from dust, and subsequently from a tiny drop, which turns into a hanging (embryo), then it becomes a fetus that is given life or deemed lifeless. We thus clarify things for you. We settle in the wombs whatever we will for a predetermined period. We then bring you out as infants, then you reach maturity. While some of you die young, others live to the worst age, only to find out that no more knowledge can be attained beyond a certain limit. Also, you look at a land that is dead, then as soon as we shower it with water, it vibrates with life and grows all kinds of beautiful plants.
verses.subtitle: Where Did We Come From?
verses.footnote: The Quran's mathematical miracle is based on the number 19. As it turns out, this number represents the Creator's signature on His creations. Thus, you and I have 209 bones in our bodies (209=19x11). The length of pregnancy for a full term fetus is 266 days (19x14) (Langman's Medical Embryology, T. W. Sadler, Page 88, 1985).

1981.english: O people, if you have any doubt concerning resurrection, then (reflect on this): We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clot, then from a fetus that is given life or deemed lifeless in order to show you. Then we settle in the wombs what we will for a specific period, then we bring you out as an infant, then you attain full maturity; some of you die, while others attain the oldest age, only to realize that this knowledge is limited. Also, you see the land lifeless, then we send down water, whereupon it moves with life, and produces all kinds of beautiful plants.
1981.subtitle: Do You Doubt Resurrection?

1989.english: O people, if you have any doubt about resurrection, (remember that) we created you from dust, and subsequently from a tiny drop, which turns into a hanging (embryo), then it becomes a fetus that is given life or deemed lifeless. We thus clarify things for you. We settle in the wombs whatever we will for a predetermined period.* We then bring you out as infants, then you reach maturity. While some of you die young, others live to the worst age, only to find out that no more knowledge can be attained beyond a certain limit. Also, you look at a land that is dead, then we shower it with water, and it vibrates with life and grows all kinds of beautiful plants.
1989.subtitle: Where Did We Come From?
1989.footnote: The Quran’s mathematical miracle is based on the number 19. As it turns out, this number represents the Creator’s signature on His creations. Thus, you and I have 209 bones in our bodies (209=19x11). The length of pregnancy for a full term fetus is 266 days (19x14) (Langman’s Medical Embryology, T. W. Sadler, Page 88, 1985). The Jewish Calendar must be adjusted once every 19years, because the sun, the moon, and the earth line up in the same relative position once every 19 years.

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُۥ يُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَأَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأنه يحيي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير
verses.transliterated: dhālika bi-anna l-laha huwa l-ḥaqu wa-annahu yuḥ'yī l-mawtā wa-annahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīru
verses.english: This proves that GOD is the Truth, and that He revives the dead, and that He is Omnipotent.

1981.english: This proves that God is the truth, and that He can resurrect the dead, and that He is omnipotent.

1989.english: This proves that GOD is the Truth, and that He revives the dead, and that He is Omnipotent.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
verses.arabicClean: وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور
verses.transliterated: wa-anna l-sāʿata ātiyatun lā rayba fīhā wa-anna l-laha yabʿathu man fī l-qubūr
verses.english: And that the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and that GOD resurrects those who are in the graves.

1981.english: And that the Hour is coming; there is no doubt about it, and God resurrects those in the graves.

1989.english: And that the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and that GOD resurrects those who are in the graves.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلَا هُدًى وَلَا كِتَٰبٍ مُّنِيرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير
verses.transliterated: wamina l-nāsi man yujādilu fī l-lahi bighayri ʿil'min walā hudan walā kitābin munīri
verses.english: Among the people there is the one who argues about GOD without knowledge, and without guidance, and without an enlightening scripture.
verses.subtitle: A Common Occurrence

1981.english: Yet, some people argue about God without knowledge, without guidance, and without an enlightening scripture.

1989.english: Among the people there is the one who argues about GOD without knowledge, and without guidance, and without an enlightening scripture.

verses.arabic: ثَانِىَ عِطْفِهِۦ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا خِزْىٌ وَنُذِيقُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
verses.arabicClean: ثاني عطفه ليضل عن سبيل الله ۖ له في الدنيا خزي ۖ ونذيقه يوم القيامة عذاب الحريق
verses.transliterated: thāniya ʿiṭ'fihi liyuḍilla ʿan sabīli l-lahi lahu fī l-dun'yā khiz'yun wanudhīquhu yawma l-qiyāmati ʿadhāba l-ḥarīq
verses.english: Arrogantly he strives to divert the people from the path of GOD. He thus incurs humiliation in this life, and we commit him on the Day of Resurrection to the agony of burning.

1981.english: Turning away in arrogance, he causes others to deviate from the path of God. He has deserved humiliation in this life, and we commit him on the day of resurrection to the agony of burning.

1989.english: Arrogantly he strives to divert people from the path of GOD. He thus incurs humiliation in this life, and we commit him on the Day of Resurrection to the agony of burning

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّٰمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
verses.arabicClean: ذلك بما قدمت يداك وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد
verses.transliterated: dhālika bimā qaddamat yadāka wa-anna l-laha laysa biẓallāmin lil'ʿabīd
verses.english: This is what your hands have sent ahead for you. GOD is never unjust towards the people.

1981.english: This is what your own hands have advanced for you; God is never unjust towards the creatures.

1989.english: This is what your hands have sent ahead for you. GOD is never unjust towards the people.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيْرٌ ٱطْمَأَنَّ بِهِۦ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْخُسْرَانُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
verses.arabicClean: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف ۖ فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به ۖ وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ۚ ذلك هو الخسران المبين
verses.transliterated: wamina l-nāsi man yaʿbudu l-laha ʿalā ḥarfin fa-in aṣābahu khayrun iṭ'ma-anna bihi wa-in aṣābathu fit'natun inqalaba ʿalā wajhihi khasira l-dun'yā wal-ākhirata dhālika huwa l-khus'rānu l-mubīn
verses.english: Among the people there is the one who worships GOD conditionally. If things go his way, he is content. But if some adversity befalls him, he makes an about-face. Thus, he loses both this life and the Hereafter. Such is the real loss.
verses.subtitle: Fair Weather Friends

1981.english: And there is the one who worships God conditionally; if something good happens to him, he is content, but when a tribulation afflicts him, he reverts. Thus, he loses both this life and the hereafter. This is the real loss.

1989.english: Among the people there is the one who worships GOD conditionally. If things go his way, he is content. But if some adversity befalls him, he makes an about-face. Thus, he loses both this life and the Hereafter. Such is the real loss.
1989.subtitle: Fair Weather Friends

verses.arabic: يَدْعُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُۥ وَمَا لَا يَنفَعُهُۥ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَٰلُ ٱلْبَعِيدُ
verses.arabicClean: يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه ۚ ذلك هو الضلال البعيد
verses.transliterated: yadʿū min dūni l-lahi mā lā yaḍurruhu wamā lā yanfaʿuhu dhālika huwa l-ḍalālu l-baʿīd
verses.english: He idolizes beside GOD what possesses no power to harm him or benefit him; such is the real straying.

1981.english: He idolizes besides God what neither harms him, nor benefits him. This is the farthest straying.

1989.english: He idolizes besides GOD what possesses no power to harm him or benefit him; this is the real loss.

verses.arabic: يَدْعُوا۟ لَمَن ضَرُّهُۥٓ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِۦ لَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ وَلَبِئْسَ ٱلْعَشِيرُ
verses.arabicClean: يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه ۚ لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير
verses.transliterated: yadʿū laman ḍarruhu aqrabu min nafʿihi labi'sa l-mawlā walabi'sa l-ʿashīr
verses.english: He idolizes what is more apt to harm him than benefit him. What a miserable lord! What a miserable companion!

1981.english: He idolizes one who is more likely to hurt him than benefit him; what a miserable master; what a miserable companion!

1989.english: He idolizes what is more apt to harm him than benefit him. What a miserable lord; what a miserable companion.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ جَنَّٰتٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ
verses.arabicClean: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ۚ إن الله يفعل ما يريد
verses.transliterated: inna l-laha yud'khilu alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru inna l-laha yafʿalu mā yurīd
verses.english: GOD admits those who believe and lead a righteous life into gardens with flowing streams. Everything is in accordance with GOD's will.

1981.english: As for those who believe and work righteousness, God admits them into gardens with flowing streams. God does what He wills.

1989.english: GOD admits those who believe and lead a righteous life into gardens with flowing streams. GOD does whatever He wills.

verses.arabic: مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ فَلْيَنظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُۥ مَا يَغِيظُ
verses.arabicClean: من كان يظن أن لن ينصره الله في الدنيا والآخرة فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ثم ليقطع فلينظر هل يذهبن كيده ما يغيظ
verses.transliterated: man kāna yaẓunnu an lan yanṣurahu l-lahu fī l-dun'yā wal-ākhirati falyamdud bisababin ilā l-samāi thumma l'yaqṭaʿ falyanẓur hal yudh'hibanna kayduhu mā yaghīẓ
verses.english: If anyone thinks that GOD cannot support him in this life and in the Hereafter, let him turn completely to (his Creator in) heaven, and sever (his dependence on anyone else). He will then see that this plan eliminates anything that bothers him.
verses.subtitle: Happiness Now, and Forever

1981.english: If any one thinks that God cannot support him in this life, as well as in the hereafter, let him turn totally to God and sever (his idolization towards anyone else). He will then find out that this plan eliminates his worries.
1981.subtitle: Relevance of Faith to This Life
1981.footnote: The problem with most people is that they do not realize the direct relevance of religion to their lives. The fact is that our happiness in this world, our success in all our worldly affairs, as well as our happiness in the eternal real life, depend on following God's law. The vast majority of people, unfortunately, are unaware that God runs every minute detail in this world (see 10:61-64).

1989.english: If anyone thinks that GOD cannot support him in this life and in the Hereafter, let him turn completely to (his creator in) heaven, and sever (his dependence on anyone else). He will then see that this plan eliminates anything that bothers him.
1989.subtitle: Happiness Now, and Forever

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِى مَن يُرِيدُ
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك أنزلناه آيات بينات وأن الله يهدي من يريد
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika anzalnāhu āyātin bayyinātin wa-anna l-laha yahdī man yurīd
verses.english: We have thus revealed clear revelations herein, then GOD guides whomever He wills.

1981.english: We thus reveal these clear revelations, then God guides whomever He wills.

1989.english: We thus revealed clear revelations, then GOD guides whomever He wills.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ
verses.arabicClean: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة ۚ إن الله على كل شيء شهيد
verses.transliterated: inna alladhīna āmanū wa-alladhīna hādū wal-ṣābiīna wal-naṣārā wal-majūsa wa-alladhīna ashrakū inna l-laha yafṣilu baynahum yawma l-qiyāmati inna l-laha ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdu
verses.english: Those who believe, those who are Jewish, the converts, the Christians, the Zoroastrians, and the idol worshipers, GOD is the One who will judge among them on the Day of Resurrection. GOD witnesses all things.
verses.subtitle: God: The Only Judge

1981.english: Those who believe, those who are Jewish, the converts, the Christians, the Magi, and the idol worshipers; God will judge them all on the day of resurrection. God is witnessing all things.

1989.english: Those who believe, those who are Jewish, the converts, the Christians, the Zoroastrians, and the idol worshipers, GOD is the One who will judge among them on the Day of Resurrection. GOD witnesses all things.
1989.subtitle: God: The Only Judge

verses.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ
verses.arabicClean: ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب وكثير من الناس ۖ وكثير حق عليه العذاب ۗ ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم ۚ إن الله يفعل ما يشاء ۩
verses.transliterated: alam tara anna l-laha yasjudu lahu man fī l-samāwāti waman fī l-arḍi wal-shamsu wal-qamaru wal-nujūmu wal-jibālu wal-shajaru wal-dawābu wakathīrun mina l-nāsi wakathīrun ḥaqqa ʿalayhi l-ʿadhābu waman yuhini l-lahu famā lahu min muk'rimin inna l-laha yafʿalu mā yashā
verses.english: Do you not realize that to GOD prostrates everyone in the heavens and the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the animals, and many people? Many others among the people are committed to doom. Whomever GOD shames, none will honor him. Everything is in accordance with GOD's will.

1981.english: Do you not realize that to God prostrate those in the heavens, and those in the earth, and the sun and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the animals, and many people? Other people are committed to doom. Whomever God commits to humiliation, you will find none to honor him. God does what He wills.

1989.english: Do you not realize that to GOD prostrates everyone in the heavens and the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the animals, and many people? Many others are committed to doom. Whomever GOD shames, none will honor him. GOD does whatever He wills.

verses.arabic: هَٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُوا۟ فِى رَبِّهِمْ فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارٍ يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم ۖ فالذين كفروا قطعت لهم ثياب من نار يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم
verses.transliterated: hādhāni khaṣmāni ikh'taṣamū fī rabbihim fa-alladhīna kafarū quṭṭiʿat lahum thiyābun min nārin yuṣabbu min fawqi ruūsihimu l-ḥamīm
verses.english: Here are two parties feuding with regard to their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, they will have clothes of fire tailored for them. Hellish liquid will be poured on top of their heads.
verses.subtitle: How Terrible is Hell!
verses.footnote: People who have insisted upon going to Hell will inevitably complain: 'Had we known how bad this is, we would have behaved differently.' They will be told that the horrors of Hell have been pointed out to them in the most graphic, though symbolic, terms. It should be noted that Heaven and Hell are almost invariably mentioned together in the Quran.

1981.english: Of the two opposing sides, with regard to their Lord, those who disbelieve have deserved garments of fire, and lava being poured on their heads.

1989.english: Here are two feuding parties with regard to their Lord. As for those who disbelieved, they will have clothes of fire tailored for them. Hellish liquid will be poured on top of their heads.
1989.subtitle: How Terrible is Hell!
1989.footnote: People who have insisted on going to Hell will inevitably complain: ‘Had we known how bad this is, we would have behaved differently. ’ They will be told that the horrors of Hell have been pointed out to them in the most graphic, though symbolic, terms. It should be noted that Heaven and Hell are almost invariably mentioned together in the Quran.

verses.arabic: يُصْهَرُ بِهِۦ مَا فِى بُطُونِهِمْ وَٱلْجُلُودُ
verses.arabicClean: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود
verses.transliterated: yuṣ'haru bihi mā fī buṭūnihim wal-julūd
verses.english: It will cause their insides to melt, as well as their skins.

1981.english: Even their insides melt therefrom, and their skins.
1981.footnote: These are allegorical descriptions of heaven and hell (see Appendix 4).

1989.english: It will cause their insides to melt, as well as their skins.
1989.footnote: People who have insisted on going to Hell will inevitably complain: ‘Had we known how bad this is, we would have behaved differently. ’ They will be told that the horrors of Hell have been pointed out to them in the most graphic, though symbolic, terms. It should be noted that Heaven and Hell are almost invariably mentioned together in the Quran.

verses.arabic: وَلَهُم مَّقَٰمِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولهم مقامع من حديد
verses.transliterated: walahum maqāmiʿu min ḥadīdi
verses.english: They will be confined in iron pots.

1981.english: They will be confined in iron cells.
1981.footnote: These are allegorical descriptions of heaven and hell (see Appendix 4).

1989.english: They will be confined in iron pots.
