verses.transliterated: waqāla alladhīna lā yarjūna liqāanā lawlā unzila ʿalaynā l-malāikatu aw narā rabbanā laqadi is'takbarū fī anfusihim waʿataw ʿutuwwan kabīra
verses.english: Those who do not expect to meet us said, "If only the angels could come down to us, or we could see our Lord (we would then believe)!" Indeed, they have committed a gross arrogance, and have produced a gross blasphemy.

1981.english: Those who are not mindful of meeting us would say, "How come no angels come down to us, nor do we see our Lord?" Indeed, they have uttered a gross blasphemy, and transgressed a gross transgression.

1989.english: Those who do not expect to meet us said, “If only the angels could come down to us, or we could see our Lord (we would then believe)!” Indeed, they have committed gross arrogance, and produced a gross blasphemy.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ لَا بُشْرَىٰ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا
verses.arabicClean: يوم يرون الملائكة لا بشرى يومئذ للمجرمين ويقولون حجرا محجورا
verses.transliterated: yawma yarawna l-malāikata lā bush'rā yawma-idhin lil'muj'rimīna wayaqūlūna ḥij'ran maḥjūra
verses.english: The day they see the angels, it will not be good news for the guilty; they will say, "Now, we are irreversibly confined."

1981.english: The day they see the angels, there will be no joy for the guilty. They will be told, "There is absolutely no other chance for you."

1989.english: The day they see the angels, it will not be good news for the guilty. They will say, “We are irreversibly confined.”

verses.arabic: وَقَدِمْنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ مِنْ عَمَلٍ فَجَعَلْنَٰهُ هَبَآءً مَّنثُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا
verses.transliterated: waqadim'nā ilā mā ʿamilū min ʿamalin fajaʿalnāhu habāan manthūra
verses.english: We will look at all the works they have done, and render them null and void.

1981.english: We will turn to the works they had done, and render them null and void.

1989.english: We will look at all the works they had done, and render them utterly useless.

verses.arabic: أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا
verses.transliterated: aṣḥābu l-janati yawma-idhin khayrun mus'taqarran wa-aḥsanu maqīla
verses.english: The dwellers of Paradise are far better on that day; they will hear better news.

1981.english: As for those who have deserved Paradise, they will be in a better position on that day, and will hear better words.

1989.english: The dwellers of Paradise are far better on that day; they will hear better news.

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِٱلْغَمَٰمِ وَنُزِّلَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ تَنزِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ويوم تشقق السماء بالغمام ونزل الملائكة تنزيلا
verses.transliterated: wayawma tashaqqaqu l-samāu bil-ghamāmi wanuzzila l-malāikatu tanzīla
verses.english: The heaven will break apart, into masses of clouds, and the angels will descend in multitudes.

1981.english: On that day, the heaven will break up, and through the fog, the angels will descend and descend.

1989.english: The heaven will break apart, into masses of clouds, and the angels will descend in multitudes.

verses.arabic: ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَكَانَ يَوْمًا عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ عَسِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن ۚ وكان يوما على الكافرين عسيرا
verses.transliterated: al-mul'ku yawma-idhin l-ḥaqu lilrraḥmāni wakāna yawman ʿalā l-kāfirīna ʿasīra
verses.english: All sovereignty on that day belongs to the Most Gracious. For the disbelievers, it will be a difficult day.

1981.english: All kingship on that day rightfully belongs to God most gracious. It will be a difficult day for the disbelievers.

1989.english: All kingship on that day belongs absolutely to the Most Gracious. For the disbelievers, it will be a difficult day.

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى ٱتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا
verses.transliterated: wayawma yaʿaḍḍu l-ẓālimu ʿalā yadayhi yaqūlu yālaytanī ittakhadhtu maʿa l-rasūli sabīla
verses.english: The day will come when the transgressor will bite his hands (in anguish) and say, "Alas, I wish I had followed the path with the messenger.
verses.subtitle: God's Messenger of the Covenant
verses.footnote: This verse refers also to God's Messenger of the Covenant whose name is mathematically coded in the Quran as "Rashad Khalifa." If you write down the gematrical value of "Rashad" (505), followed by the gematrical value of "Khalifa" (725), followed by this sura number (25), followed by verses 27, 28, 29, and 30, the final number (5057252527282930) is a multiple of 19 (see Appendices 2 & 26 for details). The prophet Muhammad will also make such a statement as in 25:30 on the Day of Judgment.

1981.english: On that day, the wicked will bite his hands and say, "Oh I wish I followed the path with the messenger.
1981.subtitle: Choose Your Friends Carefully

1989.english: The day will come when the transgressor will bite his hands (in anguish) and say, “Oh, I wish I had followed the path of the messenger.
1989.subtitle: God’s Messenger of the Covenant
1989.footnote: This verse refers also to God’s Messenger of the Covenant whose name is mathematically coded in the Quran as “Rashad Khalifa.” If you write down the gematrical value of “Rashad” (505), followed by the gematrical value of “Khalifa” (725), followed by this sura number (25), followed by verses 27, 28, 29, and 30, the final number (5057252527282930) is a multiple of 19 (see Appendices 2 & 26 for details). Additionally, Muhammad will make such a statement on the Day of Judgment.

verses.arabic: يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰ لَيْتَنِى لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلَانًا خَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: يا ويلتى ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا
verses.transliterated: yāwaylatā laytanī lam attakhidh fulānan khalīla
verses.english: "Alas, woe to me, I wish I did not take that person as a friend.

1981.english: "Oh, woe to me, I wish I never chose that person for a friend.

1989.english: “Oh, woe to me, I wish I did not take that person as a friend.
1989.footnote: This verse refers also to God’s Messenger of the Covenant whose name is mathematically coded in the Quran as “Rashad Khalifa.” If you write down the gematrical value of “Rashad” (505), followed by the gematrical value of “Khalifa” (725), followed by this sura number (25), followed by verses 27, 28, 29, and 30, the final number (5057252527282930) is a multiple of 19 (see Appendices 2 & 26 for details). Additionally, Muhammad will make such a statement on the Day of Judgment.

verses.arabic: لَّقَدْ أَضَلَّنِى عَنِ ٱلذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ جَآءَنِى وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ خَذُولً
verses.arabicClean: لقد أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني ۗ وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا
verses.transliterated: laqad aḍallanī ʿani l-dhik'ri baʿda idh jāanī wakāna l-shayṭānu lil'insāni khadhūla
verses.english: "He has led me away from the message after it came to me. Indeed, the devil lets down his human victims."

1981.english: "He has diverted me away from the message when it came to me. Indeed, the devil misleads, then abandons the human being."

1989.english: “He has led me away from the message after it came to me. Indeed, the devil lets down his human victims.”
1989.footnote: This verse refers also to God’s Messenger of the Covenant whose name is mathematically coded in the Quran as “Rashad Khalifa.” If you write down the gematrical value of “Rashad” (505), followed by the gematrical value of “Khalifa” (725), followed by this sura number (25), followed by verses 27, 28, 29, and 30, the final number (5057252527282930) is a multiple of 19 (see Appendices 2 & 26 for details). Additionally, Muhammad will make such a statement on the Day of Judgment.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلرَّسُولُ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِى ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ مَهْجُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وقال الرسول يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا
verses.transliterated: waqāla l-rasūlu yārabbi inna qawmī ittakhadhū hādhā l-qur'āna mahjūra
verses.english: The messenger said, "My Lord, my people have deserted this Quran."

1981.english: The messenger will say, "My Lord, my people have deserted this Quran."
1981.subtitle: Muhammad's Mission and Wish
1981.footnote: Muhammad's mission and real wish was to deliver the Quran, the whole Quran, and nothing but the Quran. The Muslims, however, fell in the same satanic trap as the Jews and invented the "**hadith**" and "**sunna**" as additional sources of jurisprudence that can be made to conform to the various traditions, customs, and superstitions. The Jewish Mishnah corresponds to "**hadith**" and the Gemara corresponds to "**sunna**." Many Muslim scholars and their followers today have gone as far as stating that "**hadith**" abrogates the Quran (see 24:1-2)! Hence, the prophet Muhammad's disappointment on the day of judgment, as stated in verse 30. It is extremely significant that the words of verse 31 are identical to those dealing with the inventors of "**hadith**" in 6:112.

1989.english: The messenger* said, “My Lord, my people have deserted this Quran.”
1989.footnote: This verse refers also to God’s Messenger of the Covenant whose name is mathematically coded in the Quran as “Rashad Khalifa.” If you write down the gematrical value of “Rashad” (505), followed by the gematrical value of “Khalifa” (725), followed by this sura number (25), followed by verses 27, 28, 29, and 30, the final number (5057252527282930) is a multiple of 19 (see Appendices 2 & 26 for details). Additionally, Muhammad will make such a statement on the Day of Judgment.

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِىٍّ عَدُوًّا مِّنَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ هَادِيًا وَنَصِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين ۗ وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika jaʿalnā likulli nabiyyin ʿaduwwan mina l-muj'rimīna wakafā birabbika hādiyan wanaṣīra
verses.english: We also set up against every prophet enemies from among the guilty. Your Lord suffices as a guide, a master.

1981.english: We thus appointed for every prophet enemies from among the guilty, and God suffices as guide and protector.
1981.footnote: Muhammad's mission and real wish was to deliver the Quran, the whole Quran, and nothing but the Quran. The Muslims, however, fell in the same satanic trap as the Jews and invented the "**hadith**" and "**sunna**" as additional sources of jurisprudence that can be made to conform to the various traditions, customs, and superstitions. The Jewish Mishnah corresponds to "**hadith**" and the Gemara corresponds to "**sunna**." Many Muslim scholars and their followers today have gone as far as stating that "**hadith**" abrogates the Quran (see 24:1-2)! Hence, the prophet Muhammad's disappointment on the day of judgment, as stated in verse 30. It is extremely significant that the words of verse 31 are identical to those dealing with the inventors of "**hadith**" in 6:112.

1989.english: We also set up against every prophet enemies from among the guilty. Your Lord suffices as a guide, and helper.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ وَرَتَّلْنَٰهُ تَرْتِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة ۚ كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ۖ ورتلناه ترتيلا
verses.transliterated: waqāla alladhīna kafarū lawlā nuzzila ʿalayhi l-qur'ānu jum'latan wāḥidatan kadhālika linuthabbita bihi fuādaka warattalnāhu tartīla
verses.english: Those who disbelieved said, "Why did not the Quran come through him all at once?" We have released it to you gradually, in order to fix it in your memory. We have recited it in a specific sequence.

1981.english: The disbelievers said, "How come the Quran was not revealed him all at once?" We thus released it gradually, in order to fix it in your memory.

1989.english: Those who disbelieved said, “Why did the Quran not come to him all at once?” We have released it to you gradually, in order to fix it in your memory. We have recited it in a specific sequence.

verses.arabic: وَلَا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْنَٰكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا
verses.transliterated: walā yatūnaka bimathalin illā ji'nāka bil-ḥaqi wa-aḥsana tafsīra
verses.english: Whatever argument they come up with, we provide you with the truth, and a better understanding.
verses.subtitle: God's Evidence is Overwhelming

1981.english: Whatever argument they come up with, we provide you with the truth, and a better argument.

1989.english: Whatever excuse they come up with, we provide you with the truth, and a better reply.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: الذين يحشرون على وجوههم إلى جهنم أولئك شر مكانا وأضل سبيلا
verses.transliterated: alladhīna yuḥ'sharūna ʿalā wujūhihim ilā jahannama ulāika sharrun makānan wa-aḍallu sabīla
verses.english: Those who are forcibly summoned to Hell are in the worst position; they are the farthest from the right path.

1981.english: They will be gathered forcibly into Gehenna, since they adopted a wicked stand, and strayed far away from the path.

1989.english: Those who are forcibly summoned to Hell are in the worst position; they are the farthest from the right path.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُۥٓ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ وَزِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلنا معه أخاه هارون وزيرا
verses.transliterated: walaqad ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba wajaʿalnā maʿahu akhāhu hārūna wazīra
verses.english: We have given Moses the scripture, and appointed his brother Aaron to be his assistant.

1981.english: We gave Moses the scripture, and appointed his brother Aaron as his deputy.
1981.subtitle: The Disbelievers Consistently Doomed

1989.english: We have given Moses the scripture, and appointed his brother Aaron to be his assistant.

verses.arabic: فَقُلْنَا ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَدَمَّرْنَٰهُمْ تَدْمِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: فقلنا اذهبا إلى القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فدمرناهم تدميرا
verses.transliterated: faqul'nā idh'habā ilā l-qawmi alladhīna kadhabū biāyātinā fadammarnāhum tadmīra
verses.english: We said, "Go, both of you, to the people who rejected our revelations," and subsequently, we utterly annihilated the rejectors.

1981.english: We dispatched them to people who subsequently rejected our revelations. Consequently, we utterly destroyed them.

1989.english: We said, “Go, both of you, to the people who rejected our revelations.” Subsequently, we utterly annihilated the rejectors.

verses.arabic: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُوا۟ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ ءَايَةً وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
verses.arabicClean: وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم وجعلناهم للناس آية ۖ وأعتدنا للظالمين عذابا أليما
verses.transliterated: waqawma nūḥin lammā kadhabū l-rusula aghraqnāhum wajaʿalnāhum lilnnāsi āyatan wa-aʿtadnā lilẓẓālimīna ʿadhāban alīma
verses.english: Similarly, when the people of Noah disbelieved the messengers, we drowned them, and we set them up as a sign for the people. We have prepared for the transgressors a painful retribution.

1981.english: Similarly, when Noah's people disbelieved the messengers, we drowned them and set them up as a lesson for the people. We prepare for the wicked painful retribution.

1989.english: Similarly, when the people of Noah disbelieved the messengers, we drowned them all, and we set them up as a sign for the people. We have prepared for the transgressors a painful retribution.

verses.arabic: وَعَادًا وَثَمُودَا۟ وَأَصْحَٰبَ ٱلرَّسِّ وَقُرُونًۢا بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ كَثِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا
verses.transliterated: waʿādan wathamūdā wa-aṣḥāba l-rasi waqurūnan bayna dhālika kathīra
verses.english: Also 'Ãd, Thamûd, the inhabitants of Al-Russ, and many generations between them.

1981.english: Also, 'Ad, Thamood, the inhabitants of Rass, and many other communities;

1989.english: Also Aad, Thamoud, the inhabitants of Al-Russ, and many generations between them.

verses.arabic: وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ ٱلْأَمْثَٰلَ وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وكلا ضربنا له الأمثال ۖ وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا
verses.transliterated: wakullan ḍarabnā lahu l-amthāla wakullan tabbarnā tatbīra
verses.english: To each of these groups, we delivered sufficient examples, before we annihilated them.

1981.english: we cited the examples for them, before we condemned and annihilated them.

1989.english: To each of these rebellious com munities we delivered sufficient examples, then we utterly annihilated them.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا۟ عَلَى ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوْءِ أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَرَوْنَهَا بَلْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أتوا على القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء ۚ أفلم يكونوا يرونها ۚ بل كانوا لا يرجون نشورا
verses.transliterated: walaqad ataw ʿalā l-qaryati allatī um'ṭirat maṭara l-sawi afalam yakūnū yarawnahā bal kānū lā yarjūna nushūra
verses.english: They have passed by the community that was showered with a miserable shower (Sodom). Did they not see it? The fact is, they never believed in resurrection.

1981.english: They had passed by the community (Sodom) that we showered with a miserable shower. It is not that they failed to see it; they simply disbelieved in resurrection.

1989.english: They have passed by the community that was showered with a miserable shower (Sodom). Did they not see it? The fact is, they never believed in resurrection.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْكَ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā ra-awka in yattakhidhūnaka illā huzuwan ahādhā alladhī baʿatha l-lahu rasūla
verses.english: When they saw you, they always ridiculed you: "Is this the one chosen by GOD to be a messenger?
verses.subtitle: Messengers Ridiculed

1981.english: And when these people see you, they ridicule you: "Is this the man whom God sent as messenger?

1989.english: When they saw you, they always ridiculed you: “Is this the one chosen by GOD to be a messenger?
1989.subtitle: Messengers Ridiculed

verses.arabic: إِن كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا عَنْ ءَالِهَتِنَا لَوْلَآ أَن صَبَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا وَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْعَذَابَ مَنْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها ۚ وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا
verses.transliterated: in kāda layuḍillunā ʿan ālihatinā lawlā an ṣabarnā ʿalayhā wasawfa yaʿlamūna ḥīna yarawna l-ʿadhāba man aḍallu sabīla
verses.english: "He almost diverted us from our gods, if it were not that we steadfastly persevered with them." They will certainly find out, when they see the retribution, who are the real strayers from the path.

1981.english: "He almost diverted us from our idols, if it were not that we steadfastly persevered." They will certainly find out, when they face the retribution, as to who really strayed from the path.

1989.english: “He almost diverted us from our gods, if it were not that we steadfastly revered them.” They will certainly find out, when they see the retribution, who are the real strayers from the path.

verses.arabic: أَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا
verses.transliterated: ara-ayta mani ittakhadha ilāhahu hawāhu afa-anta takūnu ʿalayhi wakīla
verses.english: Have you seen the one whose god is his own ego? Will you be his advocate?
verses.subtitle: The Ego as a god

1981.english: What about the one who idolizes his own ego? Can you do anything for him?

1989.english: Have you seen the one whose god is his own ego? Are you going to be his advocate?

verses.arabic: أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون ۚ إن هم إلا كالأنعام ۖ بل هم أضل سبيلا
verses.transliterated: am taḥsabu anna aktharahum yasmaʿūna aw yaʿqilūna in hum illā kal-anʿāmi bal hum aḍallu sabīla
verses.english: Do you think that most of them hear, or understand? They are just like animals; no, they are far worse.

1981.english: Do you suppose many of them hear or understand? Indeed, they are just like animals; nay, they are even worse.

1989.english: Do you think that most of them hear, or understand? They are just like animals; no, they are far worse.

verses.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنًا ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا
verses.transliterated: alam tara ilā rabbika kayfa madda l-ẓila walaw shāa lajaʿalahu sākinan thumma jaʿalnā l-shamsa ʿalayhi dalīla
verses.english: Have you not seen how your Lord designed the shadow? If He willed, He could have made it fixed, then we would have designed the sun accordingly.
verses.subtitle: Infinite Blessings From God

1981.english: Do you not see how your Lord designed the shadow? Had He willed, He could have made it constant. Then we would have designed the sun accordingly.

1989.english: Have you not seen how your Lord designed the shadow? If He willed, He could have made it fixed, and we would have designed the sun accordingly.
1989.subtitle: Infinite Blessings From God

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَٰهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا
verses.transliterated: thumma qabaḍnāhu ilaynā qabḍan yasīra
verses.english: But we designed it to move slowly.

1981.english: Then we would have withdrawn it towards us gradually.

1989.english: But we designed it to move slowly.

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا وجعل النهار نشورا
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī jaʿala lakumu al-layla libāsan wal-nawma subātan wajaʿala l-nahāra nushūra
verses.english: He is the One who designed the night to be a cover, and for you to sleep and rest. And He made the day a resurrection.

1981.english: And He is the one who made the night to cover you, and the sleep to provide you with rest; and He made the day a resurrection.

1989.english: And He is the One who designed the night to be a cover, and for you to sleep, to provide you with rest. He made the day a resurrection.

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي أرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته ۚ وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī arsala l-riyāḥa bush'ran bayna yaday raḥmatihi wa-anzalnā mina l-samāi māan ṭahūra
verses.english: He is the One who sends the winds with good omens of His mercy, and we send down from the sky pure water.

1981.english: And He is the one who sends the winds with good omen, as mercy from His hands, then we send down from the sky pure water.

1989.english: And He is the One who sends the winds with good omens of His mercy. And we send from the sky pure water.

verses.arabic: لِّنُحْۦِىَ بِهِۦ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا وَنُسْقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَٰمًا وَأَنَاسِىَّ كَثِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: لنحيي به بلدة ميتا ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاما وأناسي كثيرا
verses.transliterated: linuḥ'yiya bihi baldatan maytan wanus'qiyahu mimmā khalaqnā anʿāman wa-anāsiyya kathīra
verses.english: With it, we revive dead lands and provide drink for our creations—multitudes of animals and humans.

1981.english: With it, we revive dead land, and provide drink for our many creatures, both animals and humans.

1989.english: With it, we revive dead lands, and provide drink for our creations— multitudes of animals and humans.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَٰهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا۟ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
verses.arabicClean: ولقد صرفناه بينهم ليذكروا فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا
verses.transliterated: walaqad ṣarrafnāhu baynahum liyadhakkarū fa-abā aktharu l-nāsi illā kufūra
verses.english: We have distributed it among them in exact measure, that they may take heed. But most people insist upon disbelieving.

1981.english: We thus explain the Quran for them, that they may take heed, but most people insist upon disbelieving.

1989.english: We have distributed it among them in exact measure, that they may take heed. But most people insist upon disbelieving.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِى كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا
verses.transliterated: walaw shi'nā labaʿathnā fī kulli qaryatin nadhīra
verses.english: If we willed, we could have sent to every community a warner.

1981.english: If we will, we can send to every community a preacher.

1989.english: If we willed, we could have sent to every community a warner.

verses.arabic: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ وَجَٰهِدْهُم بِهِۦ جِهَادًا كَبِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: فلا تطع الكافرين وجاهدهم به جهادا كبيرا
verses.transliterated: falā tuṭiʿi l-kāfirīna wajāhid'hum bihi jihādan kabīra
verses.english: Therefore, do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with this, a great striving.

1981.english: Therefore, do not obey the disbelievers, and struggle against them with this Quran, a great struggle.

1989.english: Therefore, do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with this, a great striving.

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي مرج البحرين هذا عذب فرات وهذا ملح أجاج وجعل بينهما برزخا وحجرا محجورا
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī maraja l-baḥrayni hādhā ʿadhbun furātun wahādhā mil'ḥun ujājun wajaʿala baynahumā barzakhan waḥij'ran maḥjūra
verses.english: He is the One who merges the two seas; one is fresh and palatable, while the other is salty and undrinkable. And He separated them with a formidable, inviolable barrier (evaporation).

1981.english: And He is the one who merges the two seas; one is fresh and sweet, while the other is salty and repulsive. He places between them a barrier (evaporation) they can never break.

1989.english: And He is the One who merges the two seas; one is fresh and palatable, while the other is salty and undrinkable. And He separated them with a formidable, effective barrier (evaporation).

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَرًا فَجَعَلَهُۥ نَسَبًا وَصِهْرًا وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا ۗ وكان ربك قديرا
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī khalaqa mina l-māi basharan fajaʿalahu nasaban waṣih'ran wakāna rabbuka qadīra
verses.english: He is the One who created from water a human being, then made him reproduce through marriage and mating. Your Lord is Omnipotent.

1981.english: And He is the one who created from water a human being, then made him reproduce through mating. Your Lord is omnipotent.

1989.english: And He is the One who created from water a human being, then made him reproduce through marriage and mating. Your Lord is Omnipotent.

verses.arabic: وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ ظَهِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم ۗ وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا
verses.transliterated: wayaʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi mā lā yanfaʿuhum walā yaḍurruhum wakāna l-kāfiru ʿalā rabbihi ẓahīra
verses.english: Yet, they still set up beside GOD idols that cannot benefit them, nor harm them. Indeed, the disbeliever is an enemy of his Lord.

1981.english: Yet, they idolize besides Him what possesses no power to benefit them or harm them. Indeed, the disbeliever is an opponent of his Lord.
1981.subtitle: Do Not Idolize Muhammad

1989.english: Yet, they still set up besides GOD idols that cannot benefit them, nor harm them. Indeed, the disbeliever is an enemy of his Lord.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا
verses.transliterated: wamā arsalnāka illā mubashiran wanadhīra
verses.english: We have sent you (Rashad) as a deliverer of good news, as well as a warner.
verses.footnote: The gematrical value of "Rashad Khalifa" (1230), plus the sura and verse number (25+56) give a total of 1230+25+56=1311=19x69.

1981.english: We did not send you (O Muhammad) except as a mere bearer of good news, as well as a warner.

1989.english: We did not send you except as a deliverer of good news, as well as a warner.

verses.arabic: قُلْ مَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلًا
verses.arabicClean: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر إلا من شاء أن يتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا
verses.transliterated: qul mā asalukum ʿalayhi min ajrin illā man shāa an yattakhidha ilā rabbihi sabīla
verses.english: Say, "I do not ask you for any money. All I seek is to help you find the right path to your Lord, if this is what you choose."

1981.english: Say, "I am not asking you for any wage. All I ask is that those of you who so choose may follow the path to their Lord."

1989.english: Say, “I do not ask you for any money. All I seek is to help you find the right path to your Lord, if this is what you choose.”

verses.arabic: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْحَىِّ ٱلَّذِى لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِۦ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت وسبح بحمده ۚ وكفى به بذنوب عباده خبيرا
verses.transliterated: watawakkal ʿalā l-ḥayi alladhī lā yamūtu wasabbiḥ biḥamdihi wakafā bihi bidhunūbi ʿibādihi khabīra
verses.english: You shall put your trust in the One who is Alive—the One who never dies—and praise Him and glorify Him. He is fully Cognizant of His creatures' sins.
verses.subtitle: The Prophets and the Saints Are Dead

1981.english: You shall trust in the living God who never dies, and praise His glory. Your Lord is fully cognizant of His creatures' sins.
1981.subtitle: Muhammad Dies; God Does Not

1989.english: You shall put your trust in the One who is Alive; the One who never dies. You shall praise Him and glorify Him. He is fully Cognizant of His creatures’ sins.
1989.subtitle: The Prophets and the Saints Are Dead

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ فَسْـَٔلْ بِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش ۚ الرحمن فاسأل به خبيرا
verses.transliterated: alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā fī sittati ayyāmin thumma is'tawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi l-raḥmānu fasal bihi khabīra
verses.english: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, in six days, then assumed all authority. The Most Gracious; ask about Him those who are well founded in knowledge.

1981.english: He created the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, in six days, then ascended the throne. God most gracious; ask about Him those who know.

1989.english: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, in six days, then assumed all authority. The Most Gracious; ask about Him those who are well founded in knowledge.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ قَالُوا۟ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا ۩
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā qīla lahumu us'judū lilrraḥmāni qālū wamā l-raḥmānu anasjudu limā tamurunā wazādahum nufūra
verses.english: When they are told, "Fall prostrate before the Most Gracious," they say, "What is the Most Gracious? Shall we prostrate before what you advocate?" Thus, it only augments their aversion.
verses.subtitle: The Unappreciative Human

1981.english: Yet, when told, "You shall fall prostrate for God most gracious," they say, "Who is God most gracious? Shall we fall prostrate for the one you advocate?" It only increases their aversion.

1989.english: When they are told, “Fall prostrate before the Most Gracious,” they say, “What is the Most Gracious? Shall we prostrate before that which is advocated by you?” Thus, it only augments their aversion.
1989.subtitle: The Unappreciative Human

verses.arabic: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَٰجًا وَقَمَرًا مُّنِيرًا
verses.arabicClean: تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا
verses.transliterated: tabāraka alladhī jaʿala fī l-samāi burūjan wajaʿala fīhā sirājan waqamaran munīra
verses.english: Most blessed is the One who placed constellations in the sky, and placed in it a lamp, and a shining moon.

1981.english: Most exalted is the one who placed constellations in the sky, as well as a lamp and a lighted moon.

1989.english: Most blessed is the One who placed constellations in the sky, and placed therein a lamp, and a shining moon.

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُورًا
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī jaʿala al-layla wal-nahāra khil'fatan liman arāda an yadhakkara aw arāda shukūra
verses.english: He is the One who designed the night and the day to alternate: a sufficient proof for those who wish to take heed, or to be appreciative.

1981.english: And He is the one who designed the night and the day to alternate, for those who choose to take heed, or choose to be appreciative.

1989.english: And He is the One who designed the night and the day to alternate; a sign for those who wish to take heed, or to be appreciative. Traits o f the Righteous

verses.arabic: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلْجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا
verses.arabicClean: وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما
verses.transliterated: waʿibādu l-raḥmāni alladhīna yamshūna ʿalā l-arḍi hawnan wa-idhā khāṭabahumu l-jāhilūna qālū salāma
verses.english: The worshipers of the Most Gracious are those who tread the earth gently, and when the ignorant speak to them, they only utter peace.
verses.subtitle: Traits of the Righteous

1981.english: And for the servants of God most gracious who walk on earth humbly, and when the ignorant speak to them, they only utter peace.

1989.english: The worshipers of the Most Gracious are those who tread the earth gently, and when the ignorant speak to them, they only utter peace.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَٰمًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna yabītūna lirabbihim sujjadan waqiyāma
verses.english: In the privacy of the night, they meditate on their Lord, and fall prostrate.

1981.english: And who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.

1989.english: In the privacy of the night, they meditate on their Lord, and fall prostrate.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين يقولون ربنا اصرف عنا عذاب جهنم ۖ إن عذابها كان غراما
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā iṣ'rif ʿannā ʿadhāba jahannama inna ʿadhābahā kāna gharāma
verses.english: And they say, "Our Lord, spare us the agony of Hell; its retribution is horrendous.

1981.english: And who say, "Our Lord, spare us the agony of Gehenna; surely, its retribution is agonizing.

1989.english: And they say, “Our Lord, keep the agony of Hell away from us; its retribution is horrendous.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهَا سَآءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا
verses.arabicClean: إنها ساءت مستقرا ومقاما
verses.transliterated: innahā sāat mus'taqarran wamuqāma
verses.english: "It is the worst abode; the worst destiny."

1981.english: "It is a miserable abode; a miserable destiny."

1989.english: “It is the worst abode; the worst destiny.”

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا۟ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna idhā anfaqū lam yus'rifū walam yaqturū wakāna bayna dhālika qawāma
verses.english: When they give, they are neither extravagant, nor stingy; they give in moderation.

1981.english: And when they spend, they are neither extravagant, nor stingy; they are moderate.

1989.english: When they give, they are neither extravagant, nor stingy; they spend in moderation.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين لا يدعون مع الله إلها آخر ولا يقتلون النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ولا يزنون ۚ ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna lā yadʿūna maʿa l-lahi ilāhan ākhara walā yaqtulūna l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi walā yaznūna waman yafʿal dhālika yalqa athāma
verses.english: They never implore beside GOD any other god, nor do they kill any soul—for GOD has made life sacred—except in the course of justice. Nor do they commit adultery. Those who commit these offenses will have to pay.

1981.english: And they never set up besides God any idol, nor do they kill anyone except in the course of justice, nor do they commit adultery. Anyone who does these is wicked.

1989.english: And they never implore besides GOD any other god, nor do they kill any soul—for GOD has made life sacred— except in the course of justice. Nor do they commit adultery. Those who commit these offenses will have to pay.

verses.arabic: يُضَٰعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
verses.arabicClean: يضاعف له العذاب يوم القيامة ويخلد فيه مهانا
verses.transliterated: yuḍāʿaf lahu l-ʿadhābu yawma l-qiyāmati wayakhlud fīhi muhāna
verses.english: Retribution is doubled for them on the Day of Resurrection, and they abide therein humiliated.

1981.english: The retribution will be doubled for him on the day of resurrection; he abides therein in eternal humiliation.

1989.english: Retribution is doubled for them on the Day of Resurrection, and they abide therein humiliated.

verses.arabic: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَٰلِحًا فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ حَسَنَٰتٍ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا
verses.arabicClean: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل عملا صالحا فأولئك يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات ۗ وكان الله غفورا رحيما
verses.transliterated: illā man tāba waāmana waʿamila ʿamalan ṣāliḥan fa-ulāika yubaddilu l-lahu sayyiātihim ḥasanātin wakāna l-lahu ghafūran raḥīma
verses.english: Exempted are those who repent, believe, and lead a righteous life. GOD transforms their sins into credits. GOD is Forgiver, Most Merciful.

1981.english: As for those who repent, believe, and work righteousness, then God will change their sins into credits, for God is forgiving, merciful.

1989.english: Exempted are those who repent, believe, and lead a righteous life. GOD transforms their sins into credits. GOD is Forgiver, Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَإِنَّهُۥ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتَابًا
verses.arabicClean: ومن تاب وعمل صالحا فإنه يتوب إلى الله متابا
verses.transliterated: waman tāba waʿamila ṣāliḥan fa-innahu yatūbu ilā l-lahi matāba
verses.english: Those who repent and lead a righteous life, GOD redeems them; a complete redemption.

1981.english: Whoever repents and works righteousness, God redeems him a complete redemption.

1989.english: Those who repent and lead a righteous life return to GOD, and He will surely redeem them a complete redemption.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ ٱلزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا۟ بِٱللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا۟ كِرَامًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين لا يشهدون الزور وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna lā yashhadūna l-zūra wa-idhā marrū bil-laghwi marrū kirāma
verses.english: They do not bear false witness. When they encounter vain talk, they ignore it.
verses.subtitle: Additional Traits of the Righteous

1981.english: And they do not bear false witness, and when they encounter vain talk, they readily evade it.

1989.english: And they do not bear false witness. And when they encounter vain talk, they ignore it.
1989.subtitle: Additional Traits of the Righteous

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا۟ عَلَيْهَا صُمًّا وَعُمْيَانًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين إذا ذكروا بآيات ربهم لم يخروا عليها صما وعميانا
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna idhā dhukkirū biāyāti rabbihim lam yakhirrū ʿalayhā ṣumman waʿum'yāna
verses.english: When reminded of their Lord's revelations, they never react to them as if they were deaf and blind.

1981.english: And when they are reminded of their Lord's revelations, they do not turn deaf and blind.

1989.english: When reminded of their Lord’s revelations, they never react to them as if they were deaf and blind.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
verses.arabicClean: والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماما
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wadhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin wa-ij'ʿalnā lil'muttaqīna imāma
verses.english: And they say, "Our Lord, let our spouses and children be a source of joy for us, and keep us in the forefront of the righteous."

1981.english: And they say, "Our Lord, let our spouses and children be a source of happiness for us, and make us in the forefront of the righteous."

1989.english: And they say, “Our Lord, let our spouses and children be a source of joy for us, and keep us in the forefront of the righteous.”

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ٱلْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟ وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةً وَسَلَٰمًا
verses.arabicClean: أولئك يجزون الغرفة بما صبروا ويلقون فيها تحية وسلاما
verses.transliterated: ulāika yuj'zawna l-ghur'fata bimā ṣabarū wayulaqqawna fīhā taḥiyyatan wasalāma
verses.english: These are the ones who attain Paradise in return for their steadfastness; they are received therein with joyous greetings and peace.

1981.english: These are the ones who are rewarded the high ranks for their steadfastness; they will be received therein with greetings and peace.

1989.english: These are the ones who attain Paradise in return for their steadfastness; they are received therein with joyous greetings and peace.

verses.arabic: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا
verses.arabicClean: خالدين فيها ۚ حسنت مستقرا ومقاما
verses.transliterated: khālidīna fīhā ḥasunat mus'taqarran wamuqāma
verses.english: Eternally they abide therein; what a beautiful destiny; what a beautiful abode.

1981.english: Eternally they abide therein; what a beautiful abode and destiny!

1989.english: Eternally they abide therein; what a beautiful destiny; what a beautiful abode.

verses.arabic: قُلْ مَا يَعْبَؤُا۟ بِكُمْ رَبِّى لَوْلَا دُعَآؤُكُمْ فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامًۢا
verses.arabicClean: قل ما يعبأ بكم ربي لولا دعاؤكم ۖ فقد كذبتم فسوف يكون لزاما
verses.transliterated: qul mā yaʿba-u bikum rabbī lawlā duʿāukum faqad kadhabtum fasawfa yakūnu lizāma
verses.english: Say, "You attain value at my Lord only through your worship. But if you disbelieve, you incur the inevitable consequences."

1981.english: Say, "My Lord could care less about you, if it were not for your blasphemous allegations. Since you disbelieved, the retribution is inevitable."

1989.english: Say, “You attain value at my Lord only through your worship. But if you disbelieve, you incur the inevitable consequences.”

verses.arabic: طسٓمٓ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم طسم
verses.transliterated: tta-seen-meem
verses.english: T. S. M.
verses.footnote: See Appendix 1 for the significance of these previously mysterious letters.

1981.english: T.S.M.
1981.footnote: These letters, along with the Quranic initials that prefix 28 other suras are part of the Quran's miraculous numerical code. They prove that the Quran can never be man made; that it is the unaltered word of God (see Appendices 1 and 2).

1989.english: T. S. M.*
1989.footnote: See Appendix 1 for the significance of these previously mysterious letters.

verses.arabic: تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين
verses.transliterated: til'ka āyātu l-kitābi l-mubīn
verses.english: These (letters) constitute proofs of this clarifying scripture.

1981.english: These (letters) constitute the miracles of this profound scripture.
1981.footnote: This expression is used exclusively in conjunction with Quranic initials throughout the Quran (see 10:1, 12:1, 13:1, 15:1, 27:1, 28:2, 31:1).

1989.english: These (letters) are miracles of this clarifying scripture.

verses.arabic: لَعَلَّكَ بَٰخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: لعلك باخع نفسك ألا يكونوا مؤمنين
verses.transliterated: laʿallaka bākhiʿun nafsaka allā yakūnū mu'minīn
verses.english: You may blame yourself that they are not believers.

1981.english: You may blame yourself for their disbelief.

1989.english: You may blame yourself that they are not believers.

verses.arabic: إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَٰقُهُمْ لَهَا خَٰضِعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إن نشأ ننزل عليهم من السماء آية فظلت أعناقهم لها خاضعين
verses.transliterated: in nasha nunazzil ʿalayhim mina l-samāi āyatan faẓallat aʿnāquhum lahā khāḍiʿīn
verses.english: If we will, we can send from the sky a sign that forces their necks to bow.

1981.english: However, if we will, we can send to them a miracle from the sky that forces their necks to bow.

1989.english: If we will, we can send from the sky a miracle that forces their necks to bow. Humans Averse to New Reminders

verses.arabic: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما يأتيهم من ذكر من الرحمن محدث إلا كانوا عنه معرضين
verses.transliterated: wamā yatīhim min dhik'rin mina l-raḥmāni muḥ'dathin illā kānū ʿanhu muʿ'riḍīn
verses.english: Whenever a reminder from the Most Gracious comes to them, that is new, they turn away in aversion.
verses.subtitle: The Quran's Mathematical Code

1981.english: Whenever a new reminder comes to them from God most gracious, they turn away in aversion.
1981.footnote: The Quran's miraculous numerical code, discovered exclusively in the course of this very translation, is a perfect example of God's "new" reminders.

1989.english: Whenever a reminder from the Most Gracious comes to them, that is new they turn away in aversion.

verses.arabic: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا۟ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنۢبَٰٓؤُا۟ مَا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فقد كذبوا فسيأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون
verses.transliterated: faqad kadhabū fasayatīhim anbāu mā kānū bihi yastahziūn
verses.english: Since they disbelieved, they have incurred the consequences of their heedlessness.

1981.english: Since they chose to disbelieve, they will surely suffer the consequences.

1989.english: Since they disbelieved, they have incurred that which they used to mock.

verses.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم
verses.transliterated: awalam yaraw ilā l-arḍi kam anbatnā fīhā min kulli zawjin karīmi
verses.english: Have they not seen the earth, and how many kinds of beautiful plants we have grown thereon?

1981.english: Do they not see how many beautiful kinds of plants we have grown on earth?

1989.english: Have they not seen the earth, and how many kinds of beautiful plants we have grown thereon?

verses.arabic: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إن في ذلك لآية ۖ وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين
verses.transliterated: inna fī dhālika laāyatan wamā kāna aktharuhum mu'minīn
verses.english: This should be a sufficient proof for them, but most of them are not believers.

1981.english: This alone should be a lesson, but most of them are not believers.

1989.english: This should be a sign for them, but most of them are not believers.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم
verses.transliterated: wa-inna rabbaka lahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-raḥīm
verses.english: Most assuredly, your Lord is the Almighty, Most Merciful.

1981.english: Surely, your Lord is the almighty, the most merciful.

1989.english: Most assuredly, your Lord is the Almighty, Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ نادى ربك موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين
verses.transliterated: wa-idh nādā rabbuka mūsā ani i'ti l-qawma l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: Recall that your Lord called Moses: "Go to the transgressing people.
verses.subtitle: Moses

1981.english: Recall that your Lord called upon Moses, saying, "Go to the wicked people;
1981.subtitle: Moses

1989.english: Recall that your Lord called Moses: “Go to the transgressing people.
1989.subtitle: Moses

verses.arabic: قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قوم فرعون ۚ ألا يتقون
verses.transliterated: qawma fir'ʿawna alā yattaqūn
verses.english: "Pharaoh's people; perhaps they reform."

1981.english: "Pharaoh's people; would they not be righteous?"

1989.english: “Pharaoh’s people; will they reform?’

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب إني أخاف أن يكذبون
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi innī akhāfu an yukadhibūn
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, I fear lest they disbelieve me.

1981.english: He said, "My Lord, I fear lest they disbelieve me.

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, I fear lest they disbelieve me.

verses.arabic: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني فأرسل إلى هارون
verses.transliterated: wayaḍīqu ṣadrī walā yanṭaliqu lisānī fa-arsil ilā hārūn
verses.english: "I may lose my temper. My tongue gets tied; send for my brother Aaron.

1981.english: "I may also lose my temper, and my tongue may become tied. So send with me my brother Aaron.

1989.english: “I may lose my temper. My tongue gets tied; send my brother Aaron.

verses.arabic: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
verses.arabicClean: ولهم علي ذنب فأخاف أن يقتلون
verses.transliterated: walahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūn
verses.english: "Also, they consider me a fugitive; I fear lest they kill me."

1981.english: "They hold a grudge against me, and I fear that they may kill me."

1989.english: “Also, they consider me a fugitive; I fear lest they kill me.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال كلا ۖ فاذهبا بآياتنا ۖ إنا معكم مستمعون
verses.transliterated: qāla kallā fa-idh'habā biāyātinā innā maʿakum mus'tamiʿūn
verses.english: He said, "No, (they will not). Go with My proofs. We will be with you, listening.

1981.english: God said, "Do not worry; just go, the two of you. We will be with you, listening.

1989.english: He said, “No, (they will not). Go with My signs. We will be with you listening.

verses.arabic: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فأتيا فرعون فقولا إنا رسول رب العالمين
verses.transliterated: fatiyā fir'ʿawna faqūlā innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: "Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are messengers from the Lord of the universe.

1981.english: "Go to Pharaoh and tell him, 'We are sent by the Lord of the universe.'

1989.english: “Go to Pharaoh and say, ‘We are messengers from the Lord of the universe.’

verses.arabic: أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
verses.arabicClean: أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل
verses.transliterated: an arsil maʿanā banī is'rāīl
verses.english: " 'Let the Children of Israel go.' "

1981.english: "'Let the children of Israel go.'"

1989.english: “ ‘Let the Children of Israel go.’ ”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال ألم نربك فينا وليدا ولبثت فينا من عمرك سنين
verses.transliterated: qāla alam nurabbika fīnā walīdan walabith'ta fīnā min ʿumurika sinīn
verses.english: He said, "Did we not raise you from infancy, and you spent many years with us?

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "Did we not bring you up from infancy, and raised you among us for many years?"

1989.english: He said, “Did we not raise you as an infant, and you spent many years with us?

verses.arabic: وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت وأنت من الكافرين
verses.transliterated: wafaʿalta faʿlataka allatī faʿalta wa-anta mina l-kāfirīn
verses.english: "Then you committed the crime that you committed, and you were ungrateful."

1981.english: "Yet, you committed the crime that you committed, thus showing your thanklessness."

1989.english: “And you committed the crime that you committed, and you were ungrateful.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين
verses.transliterated: qāla faʿaltuhā idhan wa-anā mina l-ḍālīn
verses.english: He said, "Indeed, I did it when I was astray.

1981.english: Moses said, "So I did it, when I was astray.

1989.english: He said, “So I did it when I was astray.

verses.arabic: فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما وجعلني من المرسلين
verses.transliterated: fafarartu minkum lammā khif'tukum fawahaba lī rabbī ḥuk'man wajaʿalanī mina l-mur'salīn
verses.english: "Then I fled, when I feared you, and my Lord endowed me with wisdom and made me one of the messengers.

1981.english: "Then I fled because I feared you, then God bestowed upon me wisdom, and made me a messenger.

1989.english: “Then I fled, because I feared you, and my Lord endowed me with wisdom and made me one of the messengers.

verses.arabic: وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
verses.arabicClean: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل
verses.transliterated: watil'ka niʿ'matun tamunnuhā ʿalayya an ʿabbadtta banī is'rāīl
verses.english: "You are boasting that you did me a favor, while enslaving the Children of Israel!"

1981.english: "Is it any favor for me that you enslaved the children of Israel?"

1989.english: “And you are boasting that you did me a favor, while enslaving the Children of Israel!”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال فرعون وما رب العالمين
verses.transliterated: qāla fir'ʿawnu wamā rabbu l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: Pharaoh said, "What is the Lord of the universe?"

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "What is the Lord of the universe?"

1989.english: Pharaoh said, “What is the Lord of the universe?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ۖ إن كنتم موقنين
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā in kuntum mūqinīn
verses.english: He said, "The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them. You should be certain about this."

1981.english: Moses said, "The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, if you could only attain certainty."

1989.english: He said, “The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, if you have certainty.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُۥٓ أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال لمن حوله ألا تستمعون
verses.transliterated: qāla liman ḥawlahu alā tastamiʿūn
verses.english: He said to those around him, "Did you hear this?"

1981.english: He said to those around him, "Did you hear this?"

1989.english: He said to those around him, “Did you hear this?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbukum warabbu ābāikumu l-awalīn
verses.english: He said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your ancestors."

1981.english: Moses said, "Your Lord, and the Lord of your ancestors."

1989.english: He said, “Your Lord and the Lord of your ancestors.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال إن رسولكم الذي أرسل إليكم لمجنون
verses.transliterated: qāla inna rasūlakumu alladhī ur'sila ilaykum lamajnūnu
verses.english: He said, "Your messenger who is sent to you is crazy."

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "Your messenger who is sent to you is crazy."

1989.english: He said, “Your messenger who is sent to you is crazy.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب المشرق والمغرب وما بينهما ۖ إن كنتم تعقلون
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbu l-mashriqi wal-maghribi wamā baynahumā in kuntum taʿqilūn
verses.english: He said, "The Lord of the east and the west, and everything between them, if you understand."

1981.english: Moses said, "The Lord of the East and the West, and everything between them, if you could only understand."

1989.english: He said, “The Lord of the east and the west, and everything between them, if you understand.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين
verses.transliterated: qāla la-ini ittakhadhta ilāhan ghayrī la-ajʿalannaka mina l-masjūnīn
verses.english: He said, "If you accept any god, other than me, I will throw you in the prison."

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "If you accept any other god besides me, I will imprison you."

1989.english: He said, “If you accept any god, other than me, I will throw you in the prison.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَىْءٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: قال أولو جئتك بشيء مبين
verses.transliterated: qāla awalaw ji'tuka bishayin mubīni
verses.english: He said, "What if I show you something profound?"

1981.english: Moses said, "What if I showed you something profound?"

1989.english: He said, “What if I show you something profound?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال فأت به إن كنت من الصادقين
verses.transliterated: qāla fati bihi in kunta mina l-ṣādiqīn
verses.english: He said, "Then produce it, if you are truthful."

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "Then show us, if you are truthful."

1989.english: He said, “Then produce it, if you are truthful.”

verses.arabic: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين
verses.transliterated: fa-alqā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya thuʿ'bānun mubīnu
verses.english: He then threw his staff, whereupon it became a profound snake.

1981.english: He then threw down his staff, and it turned into a profound serpent.

1989.english: He then threw his staff, whereupon it became a profound snake.

verses.arabic: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين
verses.transliterated: wanazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāu lilnnāẓirīn
verses.english: And he took out his hand, and it was white to the beholders.

1981.english: And he took his hand out; it was white to the beholders.

1989.english: And he took out his hand, and it was white to the beholders.

verses.arabic: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال للملإ حوله إن هذا لساحر عليم
verses.transliterated: qāla lil'mala-i ḥawlahu inna hādhā lasāḥirun ʿalīmu
verses.english: He said to the elders around him, "This is an experienced magician.

1981.english: Pharaoh said to the people around him, "This man is an expert magician.

1989.english: He said to the elders around him, “This is an experienced magician.

verses.arabic: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم بسحره فماذا تأمرون
verses.transliterated: yurīdu an yukh'rijakum min arḍikum bisiḥ'rihi famādhā tamurūn
verses.english: "He wants to take you out of your land, with his magic. What do you suggest?"

1981.english: "He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic. What do you suggest?"

1989.english: “He wants to take you out of your land, with his magic. What do you suggest?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وابعث في المدائن حاشرين
verses.transliterated: qālū arjih wa-akhāhu wa-ib'ʿath fī l-madāini ḥāshirīn
verses.english: They said, "Respite him and his brother, and send summoners to every town.

1981.english: They said, "Respite him and his brother, and send delegates to every town.

1989.english: They said, “Respite him and his brother, and send summoners to every town.

verses.arabic: يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: يأتوك بكل سحار عليم
verses.transliterated: yatūka bikulli saḥḥārin ʿalīmi
verses.english: "Let them summon every experienced magician."

1981.english: "Let them summon every experienced magician."

1989.english: “Let them summon every experienced magician.”

verses.arabic: فَجُمِعَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَٰتِ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ
verses.arabicClean: فجمع السحرة لميقات يوم معلوم
verses.transliterated: fajumiʿa l-saḥaratu limīqāti yawmin maʿlūmi
verses.english: The magicians were gathered at the appointed time, on the appointed day.

1981.english: Thus, the magicians were gathered for the big day.

1989.english: The magicians were gathered at the appointed time, on the predetermined day.

verses.arabic: وَقِيلَ لِلنَّاسِ هَلْ أَنتُم مُّجْتَمِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقيل للناس هل أنتم مجتمعون
verses.transliterated: waqīla lilnnāsi hal antum muj'tamiʿūn
verses.english: The people were told: "Come one and all; let us gather together here.

1981.english: And the people were told, "Would you all gather?

1989.english: And the people were told: “Will you all come?

verses.arabic: لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: لعلنا نتبع السحرة إن كانوا هم الغالبين
verses.transliterated: laʿallanā nattabiʿu l-saḥarata in kānū humu l-ghālibīn
verses.english: "Maybe we will follow the magicians, if they are the winners."

1981.english: "Let us follow the magicians, when they end up winners."

1989.english: “Maybe we will follow the magicians, if they are the winners.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا۟ لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما جاء السحرة قالوا لفرعون أئن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين
verses.transliterated: falammā jāa l-saḥaratu qālū lifir'ʿawna a-inna lanā la-ajran in kunnā naḥnu l-ghālibīn
verses.english: When the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, "Do we get paid, if we are the winners?"

1981.english: Then, when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, "Do we get paid if we are the winners?"

1989.english: When the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, “Do we get paid, if we are the winners?”

verses.arabic: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال نعم وإنكم إذا لمن المقربين
verses.transliterated: qāla naʿam wa-innakum idhan lamina l-muqarabīn
verses.english: He said, "Yes indeed; you will even be close to me."

1981.english: He said, "Yes, and you become close to me."

1989.english: He said, “Yes; you will even be in my council.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون
verses.transliterated: qāla lahum mūsā alqū mā antum mul'qūn
verses.english: Moses said to them, "Throw what you are going to throw."

1981.english: Moses said to them, "Throw whatever you want to throw."

1989.english: Moses said to them “Throw what you are going to throw.”

verses.arabic: فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم وقالوا بعزة فرعون إنا لنحن الغالبون
verses.transliterated: fa-alqaw ḥibālahum waʿiṣiyyahum waqālū biʿizzati fir'ʿawna innā lanaḥnu l-ghālibūn
verses.english: They threw their ropes and sticks, and said, "By Pharaoh's majesty, we will be the victors."

1981.english: They then threw their ropes and sticks, saying, "By the majesty of Pharaoh, we will be the winners."

1989.english: They threw their ropes and sticks, and said, “In the name of Pharaoh’s majesty, we will be the winners.”

verses.arabic: فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فألقى موسى عصاه فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون
verses.transliterated: fa-alqā mūsā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya talqafu mā yafikūn
verses.english: Moses threw his staff, whereupon it swallowed what they fabricated.

1981.english: Moses then threw his staff, whereupon it swallowed what they fabricated.

1989.english: Moses then threw his staff, whereupoit swallowed what they fabricated.

verses.arabic: فَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فألقي السحرة ساجدين
verses.transliterated: fa-ul'qiya l-saḥaratu sājidīn
verses.english: The magicians fell prostrate.
verses.subtitle: The Experts See the Truth

1981.english: The magicians fell prostrate.

1989.english: The magicians fell prostrate.

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين
verses.transliterated: qālū āmannā birabbi l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: They said, "We believe in the Lord of the universe.

1981.english: They said, "We believe in the Lord of the universe.

1989.english: They said, “We believe in the Lord of the universe.

verses.arabic: رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: رب موسى وهارون
verses.transliterated: rabbi mūsā wahārūn
verses.english: "The Lord of Moses and Aaron."

1981.english: "The Lord of Moses and Aaron."

1989.english: “The Lord of Moses and Aaron.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم ۖ إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلسوف تعلمون ۚ لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم أجمعين
verses.transliterated: qāla āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu lakabīrukumu alladhī ʿallamakumu l-siḥ'ra falasawfa taʿlamūna la-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin wala-uṣallibannakum ajmaʿīn
verses.english: He said, "Did you believe with him before I give you permission? He must be your teacher, who taught you magic. You will surely find out. I will cut your hands and feet on alternate sides. I will crucify you all."

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "Did you believe him before I give you permission? He must be your leader who taught you magic. You will certainly find out; I will cut your hands and feet on alternate sides; I will crucify you all."

1989.english: He said, “Did you believe with him before I give you permission? He must be your master, who taught you magic. You will surely find out. I will cut your hands and feet on alternate sides. I will crucify you all.”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ لَا ضَيْرَ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا لا ضير ۖ إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون
verses.transliterated: qālū lā ḍayra innā ilā rabbinā munqalibūn
verses.english: They said, "This will not change our decision; to our Lord we will return.

1981.english: They said, "No harm done; we simply return to our Lord.

1989.english: They said, “We do not care. To our Lord we will return.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَآ أَن كُنَّآ أَوَّلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنا نطمع أن يغفر لنا ربنا خطايانا أن كنا أول المؤمنين
verses.transliterated: innā naṭmaʿu an yaghfira lanā rabbunā khaṭāyānā an kunnā awwala l-mu'minīn
verses.english: "We hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, especially that we are the first believers."

1981.english: "We hope that our Lord may forgive us our sins, since we are the first to believe."

1989.english: “We hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, especially that we are the first believers.”

verses.arabic: وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي إنكم متبعون
verses.transliterated: wa-awḥaynā ilā mūsā an asri biʿibādī innakum muttabaʿūn
verses.english: We inspired Moses: "Travel with My servants; you will be pursued."

1981.english: And we inspired Moses: "Move away with My servants; you will be pursued."

1989.english: We inspired Moses: “Travel with My servants; you will be pursued.”

verses.arabic: فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فأرسل فرعون في المدائن حاشرين
verses.transliterated: fa-arsala fir'ʿawnu fī l-madāini ḥāshirīn
verses.english: Pharaoh sent to the cities callers.

1981.english: Pharaoh sent delegates to the various towns;

1989.english: Pharaoh sent to the cities callers.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن هؤلاء لشرذمة قليلون
verses.transliterated: inna hāulāi lashir'dhimatun qalīlūn
verses.english: (Proclaiming,) "This is a small gang.

1981.english: announcing that these are a rebellious few;

1989.english: (Proclaiming,) “This is a small gang.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَآئِظُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإنهم لنا لغائظون
verses.transliterated: wa-innahum lanā laghāiẓūn
verses.english: "They are now opposing us.

1981.english: and that: "They are our opponents;

1989.english: “They are now opposing us.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَٰذِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإنا لجميع حاذرون
verses.transliterated: wa-innā lajamīʿun ḥādhirūn
verses.english: "Let us all beware of them."

1981.english: "beware of them."

1989.english: “Let us all beware of them.”

verses.arabic: فَأَخْرَجْنَٰهُم مِّن جَنَّٰتٍ وَعُيُونٍ
verses.arabicClean: فأخرجناهم من جنات وعيون
verses.transliterated: fa-akhrajnāhum min jannātin waʿuyūni
verses.english: Consequently, we deprived them of gardens and springs.
verses.subtitle: The Inevitable Retribution

1981.english: Consequently, we deprived them of their gardens and springs,

1989.english: Consequently, we deprived them of gardens and springs.

verses.arabic: وَكُنُوزٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: وكنوز ومقام كريم
verses.transliterated: wakunūzin wamaqāmin karīmi
verses.english: And treasures and an honorable position.

1981.english: the treasures and the great mansions.

1989.english: And treasures and an honorable position.

verses.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَٰهَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
verses.arabicClean: كذلك وأورثناها بني إسرائيل
verses.transliterated: kadhālika wa-awrathnāhā banī is'rāīl
verses.english: Then we made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel.

1981.english: We made the children of Israel inherit (the earth).

1989.english: Then we made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel.

verses.arabic: فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فأتبعوهم مشرقين
verses.transliterated: fa-atbaʿūhum mush'riqīn
verses.english: They pursued them towards the east.

1981.english: The Egyptians pursued them towards the East.

1989.english: They pursued them towards the east.

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما تراءى الجمعان قال أصحاب موسى إنا لمدركون
verses.transliterated: falammā tarāā l-jamʿāni qāla aṣḥābu mūsā innā lamud'rakūn
verses.english: When both parties saw each other, Moses' people said, "We will be caught."

1981.english: When the two groups could see each other, Moses' companions said, "We will get caught."

1989.english: When both parties saw each other, Moses’ people said, “We will be caught.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ كَلَّآ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
verses.arabicClean: قال كلا ۖ إن معي ربي سيهدين
verses.transliterated: qāla kallā inna maʿiya rabbī sayahdīn
verses.english: He said, "No way. My Lord is with me; He will guide me."

1981.english: He said, "No way; my Lord is with me; He will guide me."

1989.english: He said, “No way. My Lord is with me; He will guide me.”

verses.arabic: فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: فأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر ۖ فانفلق فكان كل فرق كالطود العظيم
verses.transliterated: fa-awḥaynā ilā mūsā ani iḍ'rib biʿaṣāka l-baḥra fa-infalaqa fakāna kullu fir'qin kal-ṭawdi l-ʿaẓīm
verses.english: We then inspired Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff," whereupon it parted. Each part was like a great hill.

1981.english: We then inspired Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff." Whereupon, it parted; each part like a great hill.

1989.english: We then inspired Moses: “Strike the sea with your staff,” whereupon it parted. Each part was like a great hill.

verses.arabic: وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأزلفنا ثم الآخرين
verses.transliterated: wa-azlafnā thamma l-ākharīn
verses.english: We then delivered them all.

1981.english: We let them pass through.

1989.english: We then delivered the rest.

verses.arabic: وَأَنجَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأنجينا موسى ومن معه أجمعين
verses.transliterated: wa-anjaynā mūsā waman maʿahu ajmaʿīn
verses.english: We thus saved Moses and all those who were with him.

1981.english: We delivered Moses and all those with him.

1989.english: We saved Moses and all of those who were with him.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين
verses.transliterated: thumma aghraqnā l-ākharīn
verses.english: And we drowned the others.

1981.english: And we drowned the others.

1989.english: And we drowned the others.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إن في ذلك لآية ۖ وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين
verses.transliterated: inna fī dhālika laāyatan wamā kāna aktharuhum mu'minīn
verses.english: This should be a sufficient proof, but most people are not believers.

1981.english: This should be a lesson, but most people are not to believe.

1989.english: This should be a lesson, but most people are not believers.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم
verses.transliterated: wa-inna rabbaka lahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-raḥīm
verses.english: Most assuredly, your Lord is the Almighty, Most Merciful.

1981.english: Surely, your Lord is the almighty, the merciful.

1989.english: Most assuredly, your Lord is the Almighty, Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
verses.arabicClean: واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم
verses.transliterated: wa-ut'lu ʿalayhim naba-a ib'rāhīm
verses.english: Narrate to them Abraham's history.
verses.subtitle: Abraham

1981.english: Recite for them the history of Abraham.
1981.subtitle: Abraham

1989.english: Narrate to them Abraham’s history.
1989.subtitle: Abraham

verses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما تعبدون
verses.transliterated: idh qāla li-abīhi waqawmihi mā taʿbudūn
verses.english: He said to his father and his people, "What is this you are worshiping?"

1981.english: He said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"

1989.english: He said to his father and his people, “What is this you are worshiping?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا نعبد أصناما فنظل لها عاكفين
verses.transliterated: qālū naʿbudu aṣnāman fanaẓallu lahā ʿākifīn
verses.english: They said, "We worship statues; we are totally devoted to them."

1981.english: They said, "We worship statues; we are totally devoted to them."

1989.english: They said, “We worship statues; we are devoted to them.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون
verses.transliterated: qāla hal yasmaʿūnakum idh tadʿūn
verses.english: He said, "Can they hear you when you implore?

1981.english: He said, "Do they hear you when you implore?

1989.english: He said, “Can they hear you when you implore?

verses.arabic: أَوْ يَنفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ
verses.arabicClean: أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون
verses.transliterated: aw yanfaʿūnakum aw yaḍurrūn
verses.english: "Can they benefit you, or harm you?"

1981.english: "Can they benefit or harm you?"

1989.english: “Can they benefit you, or harm you?”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ بَلْ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا بل وجدنا آباءنا كذلك يفعلون
verses.transliterated: qālū bal wajadnā ābāanā kadhālika yafʿalūn
verses.english: They said, "No; but we found our parents doing this."

1981.english: They said, "We found our parents doing this."

1989.english: They said, “No; but we found our parents doing this.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَفَرَءَيْتُم مَّا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال أفرأيتم ما كنتم تعبدون
verses.transliterated: qāla afara-aytum mā kuntum taʿbudūn
verses.english: He said, "Do you see these idols that you worship.

1981.english: He said, "Indeed, whatever you worship:

1989.english: He said, “Do you see these idols that you worship—

verses.arabic: أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمُ ٱلْأَقْدَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أنتم وآباؤكم الأقدمون
verses.transliterated: antum waābāukumu l-aqdamūn
verses.english: "You and your ancestors.

1981.english: "you and your parents before you;

1989.english: “you and your ancestors.

verses.arabic: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين
verses.transliterated: fa-innahum ʿaduwwun lī illā rabba l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: "I am against them, for I am devoted only to the Lord of the universe.

1981.english: "are enemies to me. I only worship the Lord of the universe.

1989.english: “I am opposed to them. I am only devoted to the Lord of the universe.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَنِى فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ
verses.arabicClean: الذي خلقني فهو يهدين
verses.transliterated: alladhī khalaqanī fahuwa yahdīn
verses.english: "The One who created me, and guided me.

1981.english: "The one who created me and guides me.

1989.english: “The One who created me, and guides me.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِى هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِى وَيَسْقِينِ
verses.arabicClean: والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhī huwa yuṭ'ʿimunī wayasqīn
verses.english: "The One who feeds me and waters me.

1981.english: "The one who feeds me and waters me.

1989.english: “The One who feeds me and waters me.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā mariḍ'tu fahuwa yashfīn
verses.english: "And when I get sick, He heals me.

1981.english: "When I get sick,* he is the one who heals me.

1989.english: “And when I get sick, He heals me.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِى يُمِيتُنِى ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ
verses.arabicClean: والذي يميتني ثم يحيين
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhī yumītunī thumma yuḥ'yīn
