1989.english: In fact, their knowledge about the Hereafter is confused. They even harbor doubts about it. They are totally heedless thereof.
1989.subtitle: Believing in the Hereafter: Great Obstacle for Most Disbelievers

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًا وَءَابَآؤُنَآ أَئِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال الذين كفروا أإذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا أئنا لمخرجون
verses.transliterated: waqāla alladhīna kafarū a-idhā kunnā turāban waābāunā a-innā lamukh'rajūn
verses.english: Those who disbelieved said, "After we turn into dust, and also our parents, do we get brought out?

1981.english: Those who disbelieve would say, "After becoming dust, do we and our ancestors come back to life?
1981.subtitle: Belief in the Hereafter: The Greatest Obstacle

1989.english: Those who disbelieved said, “After we turn into dust, and also our parents, do we get brought out?

verses.arabic: لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا هَٰذَا نَحْنُ وَءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبْلُ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: لقد وعدنا هذا نحن وآباؤنا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين
verses.transliterated: laqad wuʿid'nā hādhā naḥnu waābāunā min qablu in hādhā illā asāṭīru l-awalīn
verses.english: "We have been given the same promise in the past. These are nothing but tales from the past."

1981.english: "This was promised to us, and to our ancestors before us. This is but history from the past."

1989.english: “We have been given the same promise in the past. These are nothing but tales from the past.”

verses.arabic: قُلْ سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين
verses.transliterated: qul sīrū fī l-arḍi fa-unẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-muj'rimīn
verses.english: Say, "Roam the earth and note the consequences for the guilty."

1981.english: Say, "Travel the earth and note the consequences for the guilty."

1989.english: Say, “Roam the earth and note the consequences for the guilty.”

verses.arabic: وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُن فِى ضَيْقٍ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تكن في ضيق مما يمكرون
verses.transliterated: walā taḥzan ʿalayhim walā takun fī ḍayqin mimmā yamkurūn
verses.english: Do not grieve over them, and do not be annoyed by their scheming.

1981.english: Do not grieve over them, and do not be annoyed by their schemes.

1989.english: Do not grieve over them, and do not be annoyed by their scheming.

verses.arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين
verses.transliterated: wayaqūlūna matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīn
verses.english: They say, "When will that promise come to pass, if you are truthful?"

1981.english: They say, "Where is the doom you threaten, if you are truthful?"

1989.english: They say, “When will that promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”

verses.arabic: قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قل عسى أن يكون ردف لكم بعض الذي تستعجلون
verses.transliterated: qul ʿasā an yakūna radifa lakum baʿḍu alladhī tastaʿjilūn
verses.english: Say, "You are already suffering some of the retribution you challenge."

1981.english: Say, "You are already suffering some of the doom you ask for."

1989.english: Say, “You are already suffering some of the retribution you challenge.”

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن ربك لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون
verses.transliterated: wa-inna rabbaka ladhū faḍlin ʿalā l-nāsi walākinna aktharahum lā yashkurūn
verses.english: Your Lord is full of grace towards the people, but most of them are unappreciative.

1981.english: Indeed, your Lord is gracious towards the people, but most of them are not appreciative.

1989.english: Your Lord is full of grace towards the people, but most of them are unappreciative.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن ربك ليعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون
verses.transliterated: wa-inna rabbaka layaʿlamu mā tukinnu ṣudūruhum wamā yuʿ'linūn
verses.english: Your Lord fully knows what their chests hide, and what they declare.

1981.english: Your Lord is fully aware of whatever their hearts conceal, and whatever they declare.

1989.english: And your Lord fully knows what their chests hide, and what they declare.

verses.arabic: وَمَا مِنْ غَآئِبَةٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا فِى كِتَٰبٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: وما من غائبة في السماء والأرض إلا في كتاب مبين
verses.transliterated: wamā min ghāibatin fī l-samāi wal-arḍi illā fī kitābin mubīni
verses.english: There is nothing in the heavens and the earth that is hidden (from GOD); everything is in a profound record.

1981.english: There is nothing in the heaven and the earth that is not recorded in a manifest record.

1989.english: There is nothing in the heavens and the earth that is absent; everything is in a profound record.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ يَقُصُّ عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَكْثَرَ ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن هذا القرآن يقص على بني إسرائيل أكثر الذي هم فيه يختلفون
verses.transliterated: inna hādhā l-qur'āna yaquṣṣu ʿalā banī is'rāīla akthara alladhī hum fīhi yakhtalifūn
verses.english: This Quran settles many issues for the Children of Israel; issues that they are still disputing.

1981.english: This Quran informs the children of Israel about many things that they dispute.

1989.english: This Quran settles for the Children of Israel many issues that they are still disputing.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإنه لهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين
verses.transliterated: wa-innahu lahudan waraḥmatun lil'mu'minīn
verses.english: And most assuredly, it is a guide and mercy for the believers.

1981.english: It is a guide and mercy for the believers.

1989.english: And most assuredly, it is a guide and mercy for the believers.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِى بَيْنَهُم بِحُكْمِهِۦ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: إن ربك يقضي بينهم بحكمه ۚ وهو العزيز العليم
verses.transliterated: inna rabbaka yaqḍī baynahum biḥuk'mihi wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-ʿalīm
verses.english: Your Lord is the One who judges among them in accordance with His rules. He is the Almighty, the Omniscient.

1981.english: Your Lord is the one who will judge them according to His law. He is the almighty, the omniscient.

1989.english: Your Lord is the One who judges among them in accordance with His rules. He is the Almighty, the Omniscient.

verses.arabic: فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنَّكَ عَلَى ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلْمُبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: فتوكل على الله ۖ إنك على الحق المبين
verses.transliterated: fatawakkal ʿalā l-lahi innaka ʿalā l-ḥaqi l-mubīn
verses.english: Therefore, put your trust in GOD; you are following the manifest truth.

1981.english: Therefore, put your trust in God; you are following the manifest truth.

1989.english: Therefore, put your trust in GOD; you are following the manifest truth.

verses.arabic: إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين
verses.transliterated: innaka lā tus'miʿu l-mawtā walā tus'miʿu l-ṣuma l-duʿāa idhā wallaw mud'birīn
verses.english: You cannot make the dead, nor the deaf, hear the call, if they turn away.

1981.english: You can never make the dead hear, nor the deaf hearken when they turn around to flee.
1981.footnote: Note that Abraham attributed sickness to himself, and not to God. *(as printed — likely refers to 26:80)*

1989.english: You cannot make the dead, nor the deaf, hear the call, if they turn away.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَٰدِى ٱلْعُمْىِ عَن ضَلَٰلَتِهِمْ إِن تُسْمِعُ إِلَّا مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُم مُّسْلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما أنت بهادي العمي عن ضلالتهم ۖ إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون
verses.transliterated: wamā anta bihādī l-ʿum'yi ʿan ḍalālatihim in tus'miʿu illā man yu'minu biāyātinā fahum mus'limūn
verses.english: Nor can you guide the blind out of their straying. The only ones who will hear you are those who believe in our revelations, and decide to be submitters.

1981.english: Nor can you guide the blind astray. You can make none hear, except those who believe in our revelations, and decide to submit.

1989.english: Nor can you guide the blind out of their straying. The only ones who will hear are those who believe in our revelations, and decide to be Muslims. The Computer w m

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا وَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَآبَّةً مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ كَانُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا لَا يُوقِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا وقع القول عليهم أخرجنا لهم دابة من الأرض تكلمهم أن الناس كانوا بآياتنا لا يوقنون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā waqaʿa l-qawlu ʿalayhim akhrajnā lahum dābbatan mina l-arḍi tukallimuhum anna l-nāsa kānū biāyātinā lā yūqinūn
verses.english: At the right time, we will produce for them a creature, made of earthly materials, declaring that the people are not certain about our revelations.
verses.subtitle: The Computer Is The Creature
verses.footnote: (2+7+8+2 = 19) The computer was required to unveil the Quran's mathematical miracle, and it proved that most people have discarded God's message (see Appendices 1 & 19).

1981.english: Once they deserve the final judgment, we will produce for them a creature from the earth who will speak to them, saying that the people did not firmly believe in our scripture.
1981.footnote: Strong evidence points at "the computer" as the "creature" predicted in this verse. Through the decoding of the Quran's numerical miracle (see Appendix 1), the computer speaks to the world that this is God's message and that the people have discarded it.

1989.english: At the right time, we will produce for them a creature, made of earthly materials, declaring that the people are not certain about our revelations.
1989.footnote: (2+ 7+8+2 = 19) The computer was required to unveil the Quran’s mathematical miracle, and proved that most people have discarded God’s word (App 1).

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ فَوْجًا مِّمَّن يُكَذِّبُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا ممن يكذب بآياتنا فهم يوزعون
verses.transliterated: wayawma naḥshuru min kulli ummatin fawjan mimman yukadhibu biāyātinā fahum yūzaʿūn
verses.english: The day will come when we summon from every community some of those who did not believe in our proofs, forcibly.

1981.english: And the day will come when we summon from every community a group of those who rejected our revelations; they will totally submit.

1989.english: The day will come when we summon from every community some of those who did not believe in our revela tions, forcibly.

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُو قَالَ أَكَذَّبْتُم بِـَٔايَٰتِى وَلَمْ تُحِيطُوا۟ بِهَا عِلْمًا أَمَّاذَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا جاءوا قال أكذبتم بآياتي ولم تحيطوا بها علما أماذا كنتم تعملون
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā jāū qāla akadhabtum biāyātī walam tuḥīṭū bihā ʿil'man ammādhā kuntum taʿmalūn
verses.english: When they arrive, He will say, "You have rejected My revelations, before acquiring knowledge about them. Is this not what you did?"
verses.subtitle: Study the Quran's Mathematical Code

1981.english: Once they are assembled, God will say, "Did you not reject My scripture, even before examining it, or what is it that you did?"

1989.english: When they arrive, He will say, “You have rejected My revelations, before acquiring knowledge about them. Is this not what you did?”
1989.subtitle: Study the Quran’s Mathematical Code

verses.arabic: وَوَقَعَ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِم بِمَا ظَلَمُوا۟ فَهُمْ لَا يَنطِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ووقع القول عليهم بما ظلموا فهم لا ينطقون
verses.transliterated: wawaqaʿa l-qawlu ʿalayhim bimā ẓalamū fahum lā yanṭiqūn
verses.english: They will incur the requital for their wickedness; they will say nothing.

1981.english: They will then incur the final judgment, because of their wickedness, and they will utter nothing.

1989.english: They will incur the requital, due to their works; they will utter nothing.

verses.arabic: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا۟ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ألم يروا أنا جعلنا الليل ليسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا ۚ إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: alam yaraw annā jaʿalnā al-layla liyaskunū fīhi wal-nahāra mub'ṣiran inna fī dhālika laāyātin liqawmin yu'minūn
verses.english: Have they not seen that we made the night for their rest, and the day lighted? These should be sufficient proofs for people who believe.

1981.english: Did they not see how we designed the night for their rest, and the day lighted? This provides proofs for people who believe.

1989.english: Have they not seen that we made the night for their rest, and the day for work? This should provide signs for people who believe.

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ دَٰخِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ويوم ينفخ في الصور ففزع من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ۚ وكل أتوه داخرين
verses.transliterated: wayawma yunfakhu fī l-ṣūri fafaziʿa man fī l-samāwāti waman fī l-arḍi illā man shāa l-lahu wakullun atawhu dākhirīn
verses.english: On the day when the horn is blown, everyone in the heavens and the earth will be horrified, except those chosen by GOD. All will come before Him, forcibly.

1981.english: When the day comes and the horn is blown, horrified will be everyone in the heavens and the earth; but not those whom God wills. All will come to Him submissively.

1989.english: On the day when the horn is blown, everyone in the heavens and the earth will be horrified, except those chosen by GOD. All will come before Him, willingly or unwillingly.

verses.arabic: وَتَرَى ٱلْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً وَهِىَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ ٱلسَّحَابِ صُنْعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ إِنَّهُۥ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَفْعَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب ۚ صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء ۚ إنه خبير بما تفعلون
verses.transliterated: watarā l-jibāla taḥsabuhā jāmidatan wahiya tamurru marra l-saḥābi ṣun'ʿa l-lahi alladhī atqana kulla shayin innahu khabīrun bimā tafʿalūn
verses.english: When you look at the mountains, you think that they are standing still. But they are moving, like the clouds. Such is the manufacture of GOD, who perfected everything. He is fully Cognizant of everything you do.
verses.subtitle: Earth's Movement: A Scientific Miracle

1981.english: When you look at the mountains, you may think that they are standing still. But they are moving in the same manner as the clouds. Such is the creation of God, who perfected everything. Surely, He is fully cognizant of everything you do.
1981.subtitle: A Quranic Scientific Marvel

1989.english: When you look at the mountains, you think they are standing still. But they are moving, like the clouds. Such is the manufacture of GOD, who perfected everything. He is fully Cognizant of everything you do.
1989.subtitle: Earth’s Movement: Great Scientific Miracle

verses.arabic: مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهَا وَهُم مِّن فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ ءَامِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون
verses.transliterated: man jāa bil-ḥasanati falahu khayrun min'hā wahum min fazaʿin yawma-idhin āminūn
verses.english: Those who bring good works (in their records) will receive far better rewards, and they will be perfectly secure from the horrors of that day.
verses.subtitle: The Day of Judgment

1981.english: Those who work righteousness are repaid manyfold, and they are perfectly secure from the horror of that day.

1989.english: Those who bring good works (in their records) receive far better rewards. They will be perfectly secure from the horrors of that day.
1989.subtitle: The Day of Judgment

verses.arabic: وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِى ٱلنَّارِ هَلْ تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار هل تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون
verses.transliterated: waman jāa bil-sayi-ati fakubbat wujūhuhum fī l-nāri hal tuj'zawna illā mā kuntum taʿmalūn
verses.english: As for those who bring evil works, they will be forced into Hell. Do you not get requited for what you did?

1981.english: As for those who work evil, they will be forced into the hellfire. Are you not paid for what you used to do?

1989.english: As for those who bring evil works, they will be forced into Hell. Do you not get paid for what you did?

verses.arabic: إِنَّمَآ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ رَبَّ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْبَلْدَةِ ٱلَّذِى حَرَّمَهَا وَلَهُۥ كُلُّ شَىْءٍ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنما أمرت أن أعبد رب هذه البلدة الذي حرمها وله كل شيء ۖ وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين
verses.transliterated: innamā umir'tu an aʿbuda rabba hādhihi l-baldati alladhī ḥarramahā walahu kullu shayin wa-umir'tu an akūna mina l-mus'limīn
verses.english: I am simply commanded to worship the Lord of this town—He has made it a safe sanctuary—and He possesses all things. I am commanded to be a submitter.

1981.english: I was simply commanded to worship the Lord of this town, the town He made sacred. To Him belongs everything. I was commanded to be a Muslim (submitter).

1989.english: I am simply commanded to worship the Lord of this town—He has made it sacred—and He possesses all things. I am commanded to be a Muslim.

verses.arabic: وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَا۟ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ فَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَقُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأن أتلو القرآن ۖ فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ۖ ومن ضل فقل إنما أنا من المنذرين
verses.transliterated: wa-an atluwā l-qur'āna famani ih'tadā fa-innamā yahtadī linafsihi waman ḍalla faqul innamā anā mina l-mundhirīn
verses.english: And to recite the Quran. Whoever is guided is guided for his own good, and if they go astray, then say, "I am simply a warner."

1981.english: And (I was commanded) to read the Quran. Thus, whoever is guided is guided for his own good, and those who stray, tell them, "I am no more than a warner."

1989.english: And to recite the Quran. Whoever is guided is guided for his own good, and if they go astray, then say, “I am simply a warner.”

verses.arabic: وَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقل الحمد لله سيريكم آياته فتعرفونها ۚ وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون
verses.transliterated: waquli l-ḥamdu lillahi sayurīkum āyātihi fataʿrifūnahā wamā rabbuka bighāfilin ʿammā taʿmalūn
verses.english: And say, "Praise be to GOD; He will show you His proofs, until you recognize them. Your Lord is never unaware of anything you do."

1981.english: And say, "Praise God; He will show you His signs until you recognize them." Your Lord is never unaware of anything you do.

1989.english: And say, “Praise be to GOD; He will show you His signs, until you recognize them. Your Lord is never unaware of anything you do.”

verses.arabic: طسٓمٓ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم طسم
verses.transliterated: tta-seen-meem
verses.english: T. S. M.
verses.footnote: See Appendix 1 for details of the Quran's miraculous mathematical code, and the meaning or significance of these Quranic Initials.

1981.english: T.S.M.
1981.footnote: The meaning of these letters is explained in detail in Appendix 1.

1989.english: T. S. M.*
1989.footnote: See Appendix 1 for details of the Quran’s miraculous mathematical code, and the meaning or significance of these Quranic Initials.

verses.arabic: تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين
verses.transliterated: til'ka āyātu l-kitābi l-mubīn
verses.english: These (letters) constitute proofs of this profound book.

1981.english: These (letters) constitute miracles in this profound scripture.
1981.footnote: This verse informs us that the Quranic initials in verse 28:1, together with the Quranic initials in 28 other suras, represent miracles in this Quran. It is significant that this particular expression is used EXCLUSIVELY in conjunction with Quranic initials (see 10:1, 12:1, 13:1, 15:1, 26:2, 27:1, 31:2).

1989.english: These (letters) are miracles of this profound scripture.

verses.arabic: نَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكَ مِن نَّبَإِ مُوسَىٰ وَفِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: نتلو عليك من نبإ موسى وفرعون بالحق لقوم يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: natlū ʿalayka min naba-i mūsā wafir'ʿawna bil-ḥaqi liqawmin yu'minūn
verses.english: We recite to you herein some history of Moses and Pharaoh, truthfully, for the benefit of people who believe.

1981.english: We relate to you herein some history of Moses and Pharaoh; the truth for people who believe.

1989.english: We recite to you herein some history of Moses and Pharaoh, truthfully, for the benefit of people who believe.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إن فرعون علا في الأرض وجعل أهلها شيعا يستضعف طائفة منهم يذبح أبناءهم ويستحيي نساءهم ۚ إنه كان من المفسدين
verses.transliterated: inna fir'ʿawna ʿalā fī l-arḍi wajaʿala ahlahā shiyaʿan yastaḍʿifu ṭāifatan min'hum yudhabbiḥu abnāahum wayastaḥyī nisāahum innahu kāna mina l-muf'sidīn
verses.english: Pharaoh turned into a tyrant on earth, and discriminated against some people. He persecuted a helpless group of them, slaughtering their sons, while sparing their daughters. He was indeed wicked.

1981.english: Indeed, Pharaoh was a tyrant on earth, who divided the people into castes. He enslaved a group of them, slaughtering their sons and sparing their daughters. He was really wicked.

1989.english: Pharaoh turned into a tyrant on earth, and discriminated against some people. He persecuted a helpless group among them, slaughtering their sons and sparing their daughters. He was indeed wicked.

verses.arabic: وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتُضْعِفُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض ونجعلهم أئمة ونجعلهم الوارثين
verses.transliterated: wanurīdu an namunna ʿalā alladhīna us'tuḍ'ʿifū fī l-arḍi wanajʿalahum a-immatan wanajʿalahumu l-wārithīn
verses.english: We willed to compensate those who were oppressed on earth, and to turn them into leaders, and make them the inheritors.
verses.subtitle: God Compensates the Oppressed

1981.english: We wanted to rescue the oppressed, make them leaders, and make them the inheritors.

1989.english: We willed to make it up to those who were oppressed on earth, and to turn them into dignified people, and make them the inheritors.
1989.subtitle: God Helps the Oppressed

verses.arabic: وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنُرِىَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَحْذَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ونمكن لهم في الأرض ونري فرعون وهامان وجنودهما منهم ما كانوا يحذرون
verses.transliterated: wanumakkina lahum fī l-arḍi wanuriya fir'ʿawna wahāmāna wajunūdahumā min'hum mā kānū yaḥdharūn
verses.english: And to establish them on earth, and to give Pharaoh, Hãmãn, and their troops a taste of their own medicine.

1981.english: We wanted to establish them on earth, and to show Pharaoh, Haamaan, and their troops exactly what they feared.

1989.english: And to establish them on earth, and to give Pharaoh, Hamaan, and their troops a taste of the suffering they had inflicted upon others.

verses.arabic: وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأوحينا إلى أم موسى أن أرضعيه ۖ فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم ولا تخافي ولا تحزني ۖ إنا رادوه إليك وجاعلوه من المرسلين
verses.transliterated: wa-awḥaynā ilā ummi mūsā an arḍiʿīhi fa-idhā khif'ti ʿalayhi fa-alqīhi fī l-yami walā takhāfī walā taḥzanī innā rāddūhu ilayki wajāʿilūhu mina l-mur'salīn
verses.english: We inspired Moses' mother: "Nurse him, and when you fear for his life, throw him into the river without fear or grief. We will return him to you, and will make him one of the messengers."
verses.subtitle: Confidence in God

1981.english: We inspired Moses' mother, saying, "Keep on nursing him, and whenever you fear for his life, throw him into the river without any fear or worry. We will return him to you, and will make him one of the messengers."

1989.english: We inspired Moses’ mother: “Nurse him, and when you fear for his life, throw him into the river without fear or grief. We will return him to you, and will make him one of the messengers.”
1989.subtitle: Confidence in God

verses.arabic: فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
verses.arabicClean: فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا ۗ إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين
verses.transliterated: fal-taqaṭahu ālu fir'ʿawna liyakūna lahum ʿaduwwan waḥazanan inna fir'ʿawna wahāmāna wajunūdahumā kānū khāṭiīn
verses.english: Pharaoh's family picked him up, only to have him lead the opposition and to be a source of grief for them. That is because Pharaoh, Hãmãn, and their troops were transgressors.

1981.english: Pharaoh's people picked him up, only to become their enemy and a source of grief for them. That is because Pharaoh, Haamaan, and their troops were sinners.

1989.english: Pharaoh’s family picked him up, only to have him lead the opposition and to be a source of grief for them. That is because Pharaoh, Hamaan, and their troops were transgressors.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقالت امرأت فرعون قرت عين لي ولك ۖ لا تقتلوه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وهم لا يشعرون
verses.transliterated: waqālati im'ra-atu fir'ʿawna qurratu ʿaynin lī walaka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan wahum lā yashʿurūn
verses.english: Pharaoh's wife said, "This can be a joyous find for me and you. Do not kill him, for he may be of some benefit for us, or we may adopt him to be our son." They had no idea.
verses.subtitle: Inside the Lion's Den

1981.english: Pharaoh's wife said, "What a joy for me and you; do not kill him. He may be useful to us; we may even adopt him." They had no idea.

1989.english: Pharaoh’s wife said, “This can be a joyous find for me and you. Do not kill him. He may benefit us, or we may adopt him to be our son.” They had no idea.
1989.subtitle: Inside the Lion’s Den

verses.arabic: وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا ۖ إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها لتكون من المؤمنين
verses.transliterated: wa-aṣbaḥa fuādu ummi mūsā fārighan in kādat latub'dī bihi lawlā an rabaṭnā ʿalā qalbihā litakūna mina l-mu'minīn
verses.english: The mind of Moses' mother was growing so anxious that she almost gave away his identity. But we strengthened her heart, to make her a believer.

1981.english: Moses' mother's mind was getting so terrified that she almost gave away her relationship to him. But we strengthened her heart, in order to make her confident.

1989.english: The mind of Moses’ mother was growing so anxious that she almost gave away his identity. But we strengthened her heart, to make her a believer.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقالت لأخته قصيه ۖ فبصرت به عن جنب وهم لا يشعرون
verses.transliterated: waqālat li-ukh'tihi quṣṣīhi fabaṣurat bihi ʿan junubin wahum lā yashʿurūn
verses.english: She said to his sister, "Trace his path." She watched him from afar, while they did not perceive.

1981.english: She said to his sister, "Trace him." She watched him from afar, while they did not perceive.

1989.english: She said to his sister, “Trace his path.” She watched him from afar, while they did not perceive.

verses.arabic: وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وحرمنا عليه المراضع من قبل فقالت هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم وهم له ناصحون
verses.transliterated: waḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu faqālat hal adullukum ʿalā ahli baytin yakfulūnahu lakum wahum lahu nāṣiḥūn
verses.english: We forbade him from accepting all the nursing mothers. (His sister) then said, "I can show you a family that can raise him for you, and take good care of him."
verses.subtitle: The Infant Returned to His Mother

1981.english: Then we forbade for him all the nursing mothers. His sister said, "I know people who can raise him for you, and take good care of him."

1989.english: We forbade him from accepting all the nursing mothers. (His sister) then said, “I can show you a family that can raise him, and take good care of him.”
1989.subtitle: The Infant Returned to His Mother

verses.arabic: فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فرددناه إلى أمه كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: faradadnāhu ilā ummihi kay taqarra ʿaynuhā walā taḥzana walitaʿlama anna waʿda l-lahi ḥaqqun walākinna aktharahum lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: Thus, we restored him to his mother, in order to please her, remove her worries, and to let her know that GOD's promise is the truth. However, most of them do not know.

1981.english: We thus returned him to his mother, causing her to rejoice, and alleviating her grief. We let her know that God's promise is truth. However, most people do not know.

1989.english: Thus, we restored him to his mother, in order to please her, remove her worries, and to let her know that GOD’s promise is the truth. However, most of them do not know.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسْتَوَىٰٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًا وَعِلْمًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما بلغ أشده واستوى آتيناه حكما وعلما ۚ وكذلك نجزي المحسنين
verses.transliterated: walammā balagha ashuddahu wa-is'tawā ātaynāhu ḥuk'man waʿil'man wakadhālika najzī l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: When he reached maturity and strength, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the righteous.

1981.english: When he grew up and matured, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the righteous.

1989.english: When he reached maturity and strength, we endowed him with wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the righteous.

verses.arabic: وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّ مُّضِلٌّ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه ۖ فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه ۖ قال هذا من عمل الشيطان ۖ إنه عدو مضل مبين
verses.transliterated: wadakhala l-madīnata ʿalā ḥīni ghaflatin min ahlihā fawajada fīhā rajulayni yaqtatilāni hādhā min shīʿatihi wahādhā min ʿaduwwihi fa-is'taghāthahu alladhī min shīʿatihi ʿalā alladhī min ʿaduwwihi fawakazahu mūsā faqaḍā ʿalayhi qāla hādhā min ʿamali l-shayṭāni innahu ʿaduwwun muḍillun mubīnu
verses.english: Once he entered the city unexpectedly, without being recognized by the people. He found two men fighting; one was (a Hebrew) from his people, and the other was (an Egyptian) from his enemies. The one from his people called on him for help against his enemy. Moses punched him, killing him. He said, "This is the work of the devil; he is a real enemy, and a profound misleader."
verses.subtitle: Moses Commits Manslaughter

1981.english: Once he entered the city in disguise, and found two men fighting, one from his clan (Hebrew), the other from his enemy (Egyptian). The Hebrew implored him for help against the Egyptian. Moses punched the Egyptian, killing him. He said, "This is the devil's work; surely, he is an ardent, misleading, enemy."

1989.english: Once he entered the city unexpectedly, without being recognized by the people. He found two men fighting; one was (a Hebrew) from his people, and the other was (an Egyptian) from his enemies. The one from his people called on him for help against his enemy. Moses punched him, killing him. He said, “This is the work of the devil; he is an enemy, and a profound misleader.”
1989.subtitle: Moses Commits Manslaughter

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له ۚ إنه هو الغفور الرحيم
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī fa-igh'fir lī faghafara lahu innahu huwa l-ghafūru l-raḥīm
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, I have wronged my soul. Please forgive me," and He forgave him. He is the Forgiver, Most Merciful.

1981.english: Moses said, "Lord, I have wronged my soul; forgive me." God forgave him, for He is the forgiver, the merciful.

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, I have wronged my soul. Please forgive me,” and He forgave him. He is the Forgiver, Most Merciful.

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi bimā anʿamta ʿalayya falan akūna ẓahīran lil'muj'rimīn
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, in return for Your blessings upon me, I will never be a supporter of the guilty ones."

1981.english: Moses said, "Lord, You have indeed blessed me, and I pledge never to support the sinners."

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, in return for You blessings upon me, I will never be a supporter of the guilty ones.”

verses.arabic: فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه ۚ قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين
verses.transliterated: fa-aṣbaḥa fī l-madīnati khāifan yataraqqabu fa-idhā alladhī is'tanṣarahu bil-amsi yastaṣrikhuhu qāla lahu mūsā innaka laghawiyyun mubīnu
verses.english: In the morning, he was in the city, afraid and watchful. The one who sought his help yesterday, asked for his help again. Moses said to him, "You are really a troublemaker."

1981.english: The next morning he visited the city, fearful and watchful. The same Hebrew he had helped the day before implored him again for help. Moses said, "You are really a trouble maker."

1989.english: In the morning, he was in the city, afraid and watchful. The one who sought his help the day before, asked for his help again. Moses said to him, “You are really a troublemaker.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس ۖ إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين
verses.transliterated: falammā an arāda an yabṭisha bi-alladhī huwa ʿaduwwun lahumā qāla yāmūsā aturīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bil-amsi in turīdu illā an takūna jabbāran fī l-arḍi wamā turīdu an takūna mina l-muṣ'liḥīn
verses.english: Before he attempted to strike their common enemy, he said, "O Moses, do you want to kill me, as you killed the other man yesterday? Obviously, you wish to be a tyrant on earth; you do not wish to be righteous."
verses.subtitle: Moses' Crime Exposed

1981.english: And when he started to strike their common enemy, he said, "O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed another man yesterday? You really want to be a tyrant on earth, not a righteous person."

1989.english: Before he attempted to strike their common enemy, he said, “O Moses, do you want to kill me, as you killed the other man yesterday? Obviously, you wish to be a tyrant on earth; you do not wish to be righteous.”
1989.subtitle: Moses’ Crime Exposed

verses.arabic: وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين
verses.transliterated: wajāa rajulun min aqṣā l-madīnati yasʿā qāla yāmūsā inna l-mala-a yatamirūna bika liyaqtulūka fa-ukh'ruj innī laka mina l-nāṣiḥīn
verses.english: A man came running from the other side of the city, saying, "O Moses, the people are plotting to kill you. You better leave immediately. I am giving you good advice."

1981.english: A man came from the other side of the city, saying, "O Moses, the people are plotting to kill you; you better get out. This is my sincere advice to you."

1989.english: A man came running from the other side of the city, saying, “O Moses, the people are plotting to kill you. You better leave immediately; I am giving you good advice.”

verses.arabic: فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب ۖ قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين
verses.transliterated: fakharaja min'hā khāifan yataraqqabu qāla rabbi najjinī mina l-qawmi l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: He fled the city, afraid and watchful. He said, "My Lord, save me from the oppressive people."

1981.english: Moses fled, fearful and watchful, saying, "Save me, Lord, from the oppressive people."

1989.english: He fled the city, afraid and watchful. He said, “My Lord, save me from the oppressive people.”

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
verses.arabicClean: ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل
verses.transliterated: walammā tawajjaha til'qāa madyana qāla ʿasā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāa l-sabīl
verses.english: As he traveled towards Midyan, he said, "May my Lord guide me in the right path."
verses.subtitle: In Midyan

1981.english: As he headed towards Midyan, he said, "May my Lord guide me in the right path."

1989.english: As he traveled towards Midyan, he said, “May my Lord guide me to the right path.”

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان ۖ قال ما خطبكما ۖ قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء ۖ وأبونا شيخ كبير
verses.transliterated: walammā warada māa madyana wajada ʿalayhi ummatan mina l-nāsi yasqūna wawajada min dūnihimu im'ra-atayni tadhūdāni qāla mā khaṭbukumā qālatā lā nasqī ḥattā yuṣ'dira l-riʿāu wa-abūnā shaykhun kabīru
verses.english: When he reached Midyan's water, he found a crowd of people watering, and noticed two women waiting on the side. He said, "What is it that you need?" They said, "We are not able to water, until the crowd disperses, and our father is an old man."

1981.english: When he reached Midyan's water, he found a crowd watering, and noticed two women standing on the side. He said, "What is your problem?" They said, "We cannot water until the crowd disperses; our father is an old man."

1989.english: When he reached Midyan’s water, he found a crowd of people watering, and noticed two women being shoved and pushed. He said, “What is it that you want?” They said, “We are not able to water, until the crowd disperses, and our father is an old man.”

verses.arabic: فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير
verses.transliterated: fasaqā lahumā thumma tawallā ilā l-ẓili faqāla rabbi innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīru
verses.english: He watered for them, then turned to the shade, saying, "My Lord, whatever provision You send to me, I am in dire need for it."

1981.english: He watered for them, then turned to rest in the shade, saying, "Lord, I am in dire need for any provisions You may send me."

1989.english: He watered for them, then turned to the shade, saying, “My Lord, whatever provision you send to me, I surely need it.”

verses.arabic: فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا ۚ فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف ۖ نجوت من القوم الظالمين
verses.transliterated: fajāathu iḥ'dāhumā tamshī ʿalā is'tiḥ'yāin qālat inna abī yadʿūka liyajziyaka ajra mā saqayta lanā falammā jāahu waqaṣṣa ʿalayhi l-qaṣaṣa qāla lā takhaf najawta mina l-qawmi l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: Soon, one of the two women approached him, shyly, and said, "My father invites you to pay you for watering for us." When he met him, and told him his story, he said, "Have no fear. You have been saved from the oppressive people."

1981.english: Soon, one of the two women came to him walking shyly. She said, "My father invites you to pay you for watering us." When he went to him and told him his story, he said, "Do not worry, you are safe here from the oppressive people."

1989.english: Soon, one of the two women approached him, shyly, and said, “My father invites you to pay you for watering for us.” When he met him, and told him his story, he said, “Have no fear. You have been saved from the oppressive people.”

verses.arabic: قَالَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسْتَـْٔجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ
verses.arabicClean: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره ۖ إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين
verses.transliterated: qālat iḥ'dāhumā yāabati is'tajir'hu inna khayra mani is'tajarta l-qawiyu l-amīn
verses.english: One of the two women said, "O my father, hire him. He is the best one to hire, for he is strong and honest."
verses.subtitle: Moses Marries

1981.english: One of the women said, "Hire him father, for he is a good one to hire. He is strong and honest."

1989.english: One of the two women said, “O my father, hire him. He is the best one to hire; he is strong and honest.”
1989.subtitle: Moses Marries

verses.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ٱبْنَتَىَّ هَٰتَيْنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأْجُرَنِى ثَمَٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِندِكَ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج ۖ فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك ۖ وما أريد أن أشق عليك ۚ ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين
verses.transliterated: qāla innī urīdu an unkiḥaka iḥ'dā ib'natayya hātayni ʿalā an tajuranī thamāniya ḥijajin fa-in atmamta ʿashran famin ʿindika wamā urīdu an ashuqqa ʿalayka satajidunī in shāa l-lahu mina l-ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: He said, "I wish to offer one of my two daughters for you to marry, in return for working for me for eight pilgrimages; if you make them ten, it will be voluntary on your part. I do not wish to make this matter too difficult for you. You will find me, GOD willing, righteous."

1981.english: He said, "I wish to offer you one of my daughters in marriage, in return for your working for me eight pilgrimages (years). If you complete ten, it would be voluntary on your part. I do not want to be harsh on you. You will find me, God willing, fair."

1989.english: He said, “I wish that you marry one of my two daughters, in return for working for me for eight pilgrimages; if you make them ten, it will be voluntary on your part. I do not wish to make this matter too difficult for you. You will find me, GOD willing, righteous.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكَ أَيَّمَا ٱلْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ عَلَىَّ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ
verses.arabicClean: قال ذلك بيني وبينك ۖ أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي ۖ والله على ما نقول وكيل
verses.transliterated: qāla dhālika baynī wabaynaka ayyamā l-ajalayni qaḍaytu falā ʿud'wāna ʿalayya wal-lahu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīlu
verses.english: He said, "It is an agreement between me and you. Whichever period I fulfill, you will not be averse to either one. GOD is the guarantor of what we said."

1981.english: Moses said, "(I accept this agreement) between me and you. Whichever period I choose to fulfill will be acceptable to you. God attests to our agreement."

1989.english: He said, “It is an agreement between me and you. Whichever period I fulfill, you will not be averse to either one. GOD is the guarantor of what we said.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارًا قَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون
verses.transliterated: falammā qaḍā mūsā l-ajala wasāra bi-ahlihi ānasa min jānibi l-ṭūri nāran qāla li-ahlihi um'kuthū innī ānastu nāran laʿallī ātīkum min'hā bikhabarin aw jadhwatin mina l-nāri laʿallakum taṣṭalūn
verses.english: When he had fulfilled his obligation, he traveled with his family (towards Egypt). He saw from the slope of Mount Sinai a fire. He said to his family, "Stay here. I have seen a fire. Maybe I can bring to you news, or a portion of the fire to warm you."
verses.subtitle: Back to Egypt

1981.english: Moses fulfilled the interim, and as he traveled with his family, he noticed a fire at the slope of Mount Toor (Sinai). He said to his family, "Wait for me here. I just saw a fire; maybe I can bring news or some fire to warm you up."

1989.english: When he had fulfilled his obligation, he traveled with his family (towards Egypt). He saw from the slope of Mount Sinai a fire. He said to his family, “Stay here. I have seen a fire. Maybe I can bring to you news, or a portion of the fire to warm you.”
1989.subtitle: Back to Egypt

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ مِن شَٰطِئِ ٱلْوَادِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ فِى ٱلْبُقْعَةِ ٱلْمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين
verses.transliterated: falammā atāhā nūdiya min shāṭi-i l-wādi l-aymani fī l-buq'ʿati l-mubārakati mina l-shajarati an yāmūsā innī anā l-lahu rabbu l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: When he reached it, he was called from the edge of the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot where the burning bush was located: "O Moses, this is Me. GOD; Lord of the universe.
verses.subtitle: Moses Appointed

1981.english: When he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley, the bush was burning: "Moses, this is I, God, Lord of the universe.

1989.english: When he reached it, he was called from the edge of the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot where the burning bush was located: “O Moses, this is Me. GOD; Lord of the universe.”
1989.subtitle: Moses Appointed

verses.arabic: وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ وَلَّىٰ مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقْبِلْ وَلَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْءَامِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأن ألق عصاك ۖ فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب ۚ يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف ۖ إنك من الآمنين
verses.transliterated: wa-an alqi ʿaṣāka falammā raāhā tahtazzu ka-annahā jānnun wallā mud'biran walam yuʿaqqib yāmūsā aqbil walā takhaf innaka mina l-āminīn
verses.english: Throw down your staff. When he saw it moving like a demon, he turned around and fled. "O Moses, come back; do not be afraid. You are perfectly safe.

1981.english: "Then he was told to throw down his staff. When he saw it moving like a demon, he turned around and fled. "Moses, come back, and have no fear. You are perfectly safe.

1989.english: And: “Throw down your staff.” When he saw it moving like a demon, he turned around and fled. “O Moses, come back; do not be afraid. You are perfectly safe.

verses.arabic: ٱسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرَّهْبِ فَذَٰنِكَ بُرْهَٰنَانِ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب ۖ فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه ۚ إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين
verses.transliterated: us'luk yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin wa-uḍ'mum ilayka janāḥaka mina l-rahbi fadhānika bur'hānāni min rabbika ilā fir'ʿawna wamala-ihi innahum kānū qawman fāsiqīn
verses.english: Put your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without a blemish. Fold your wings and settle down from your fear. These are two proofs from your Lord, to be shown to Pharaoh and his elders; they have been wicked people.

1981.english: "Put your hand in your pocket; it will come out white, without a blemish. Gather your confidence, for these are only two of the proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his elders. They are wicked people."

1989.english: “Put your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without a blemish. Fold your wings and settle down from your fear. These are two proofs from your Lord, to be shown to Pharaoh and his elders; they are evil people.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
verses.arabicClean: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون
verses.transliterated: qāla rabbi innī qataltu min'hum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūn
verses.english: He said, "My Lord, I killed one of them, and I fear lest they kill me.

1981.english: Moses said, "Lord, I killed one of them, and I fear lest they kill me.

1989.english: He said, “My Lord, I killed one of them, and I fear lest they kill me.

verses.arabic: وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
verses.arabicClean: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني ۖ إني أخاف أن يكذبون
verses.transliterated: wa-akhī hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsil'hu maʿiya rid'an yuṣaddiqunī innī akhāfu an yukadhibūn
verses.english: Also, my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I. Send him with me as a helper to confirm and strengthen me. I fear lest they disbelieve me.

1981.english: "Also, my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I. Send him with me for support. I am afraid they may disbelieve me."

1989.english: “Also, my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I. Send him with me as a helper who will believe me. I fear lest they disbelieve me.”

verses.arabic: قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما ۚ بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون
verses.transliterated: qāla sanashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka wanajʿalu lakumā sul'ṭānan falā yaṣilūna ilaykumā biāyātinā antumā wamani ittabaʿakumā l-ghālibūn
verses.english: He said, "We will strengthen you with your brother, and we will provide you both with manifest authority. Thus, they will not be able to touch either one of you. With our miracles, the two of you, together with those who follow you, will be the victors."

1981.english: God said, "We will strengthen you with your brother, and provide you both with authority. They can never harm you. With our signs, you two and all those who follow you will be victorious."

1989.english: He said, “We will strengthen your arm with your brother, and we will provide you both with manifest authority. Thus, they will not be able to touch either one of you. With our miracles, the two of you, together with those who follow you, will be the victors.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍ قَالُوا۟ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُّفْتَرًى وَمَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِىٓ ءَابَآئِنَا ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين
verses.transliterated: falammā jāahum mūsā biāyātinā bayyinātin qālū mā hādhā illā siḥ'run muf'taran wamā samiʿ'nā bihādhā fī ābāinā l-awalīn
verses.english: When Moses went to them with our proofs, clear and profound, they said, "This is fabricated magic. We have never heard of this from our ancient ancestors."
verses.subtitle: Pharaoh's Arrogance

1981.english: When Moses went to them with our profound miracles, they said, "This is no more than fabricated magic. We have never heard of this since our ancient ancestors."

1989.english: When Moses went to them with our revelations, perfectly clear, they said, “This is fabricated magic. We have never heard of this since our ancient ancestors.”
1989.subtitle: Pharaoh’s Arrogance

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن جَآءَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ مِنْ عِندِهِۦ وَمَن تَكُونُ لَهُۥ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار ۖ إنه لا يفلح الظالمون
verses.transliterated: waqāla mūsā rabbī aʿlamu biman jāa bil-hudā min ʿindihi waman takūnu lahu ʿāqibatu l-dāri innahu lā yuf'liḥu l-ẓālimūn
verses.english: Moses said, "My Lord knows best who brought the guidance from Him, and who will be the ultimate victors. Surely, the transgressors never succeed."

1981.english: Moses said, "My Lord knows best who is bringing the true guidance from Him, and will be the ultimate winner. Surely, the wicked never succeed."

1989.english: Moses said, “My Lord knows best who brought the guidance from Him, and who will be the ultimate victors. Surely, the transgressors never succeed.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى فَأَوْقِدْ لِى يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجْعَل لِّى صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين
verses.transliterated: waqāla fir'ʿawnu yāayyuhā l-mala-u mā ʿalim'tu lakum min ilāhin ghayrī fa-awqid lī yāhāmānu ʿalā l-ṭīni fa-ij'ʿal lī ṣarḥan laʿallī aṭṭaliʿu ilā ilāhi mūsā wa-innī la-aẓunnuhu mina l-kādhibīn
verses.english: Pharaoh said, "O you elders, I have not known of any god for you other than me. Therefore, fire the adobe, O Hãmãn, in order to build a tower, that I may take a look at the god of Moses. I am sure that he is a liar."

1981.english: Pharaoh said, "O people, I never knew of any other god for you except me. Burn the clay, O Haamaan, and build a tower for me. Maybe I can take a look at the God of Moses. I think he is a liar."

1989.english: Pharaoh said, “O you elders, I have not known of any god for you other than me. Therefore, fire the adobe, O Hamaan, in order to build a tower, that I may take a look at the god of Moses. I believe that he is a liar.”

verses.arabic: وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ هُوَ وَجُنُودُهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْنَا لَا يُرْجَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون
verses.transliterated: wa-is'takbara huwa wajunūduhu fī l-arḍi bighayri l-ḥaqi waẓannū annahum ilaynā lā yur'jaʿūn
verses.english: Thus, he and his troops continued to commit arrogance on earth, without any right, and thought that they would not be returned to us.

1981.english: He and his troops were oppressive tyrants on earth. They were unjust, and totally mindless of their returning to us.

1989.english: Thus, he and his troops committed arrogance on earth, without any right; they thought that they would not be returned to us.

verses.arabic: فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم ۖ فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين
verses.transliterated: fa-akhadhnāhu wajunūdahu fanabadhnāhum fī l-yami fa-unẓur kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: Consequently, we punished him and his troops, by throwing them into the sea. Note the consequences for the transgressors.

1981.english: Consequently, we punished him and his troops, and threw them into the sea. Therefore, note the consequences for the wicked.

1989.english: Consequently, we punished him and his troops. We threw them into the sea. Therefore, note the consequences for the transgressors.

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِ وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ۖ ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalnāhum a-immatan yadʿūna ilā l-nāri wayawma l-qiyāmati lā yunṣarūn
verses.english: We made them imams who led their people to Hell. Furthermore, on the Day of Resurrection, they will have no help.

1981.english: We made them imams who lead their people to the hellfire, and on the day of resurrection, they will not be helped.

1989.english: We made them imams who led their people to Hell; on the Day of Resurrection, they will have no help.

verses.arabic: وَأَتْبَعْنَٰهُمْ فِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ هُم مِّنَ ٱلْمَقْبُوحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ۖ ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين
verses.transliterated: wa-atbaʿnāhum fī hādhihi l-dun'yā laʿnatan wayawma l-qiyāmati hum mina l-maqbūḥīn
verses.english: They incurred in this life condemnation, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be despised.

1981.english: We accursed them in this life, and on the day of resurrection they will be despised.

1989.english: They incurred in this life condemnation, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be despised. The Torah

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْقُرُونَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ بَصَآئِرَ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون
verses.transliterated: walaqad ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba min baʿdi mā ahlaknā l-qurūna l-ūlā baṣāira lilnnāsi wahudan waraḥmatan laʿallahum yatadhakkarūn
verses.english: We gave Moses the scripture—after having annihilated the previous generations, and after setting the examples through them—to provide enlightenment for the people, and guidance, and mercy, that they may take heed.
verses.subtitle: The Book of Moses
verses.footnote: The Torah is the collection of all the scriptures revealed to all the prophets of Israel, including the book of Moses. The Quran consistently states that Moses was given a book, or "the Statute Book." Nowhere in the Quran do we see that Moses was given "the Torah." Today's Old Testament, therefore, is the Torah (see 3:50, 5:46).

1981.english: We gave Moses the scripture, after destroying the previous generations, to serve as enlightenment for the people, and guidance and mercy, that they may take heed.

1989.english: We gave Moses the scripture—after having annihilated the previous generations, and after setting the examples through them— to provide enlightenment for the people, and guidance, and mercy, that they may take heed.

verses.arabic: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلْغَرْبِىِّ إِذْ قَضَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَمْرَ وَمَا كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين
verses.transliterated: wamā kunta bijānibi l-gharbiyi idh qaḍaynā ilā mūsā l-amra wamā kunta mina l-shāhidīn
verses.english: You were not present on the slope of the western mount, when we issued the command to Moses; you were not a witness.
verses.subtitle: Addressing God's Messenger of the Covenant
verses.footnote: The name of this messenger is confirmed mathematically: by placing the gematrical value of "Rashad Khalifa" (1230) next to the verse number (44), we get 123044=19x6476.

1981.english: You were not present at the Western slope when we gave Moses the commandments, nor were you a witness.

1989.english: You were not present on the west side, when we issued the command to Moses; you were not a witness.

verses.arabic: وَلَٰكِنَّآ أَنشَأْنَا قُرُونًا فَتَطَاوَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْعُمُرُ وَمَا كُنتَ ثَاوِيًا فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ تَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر ۚ وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين
verses.transliterated: walākinnā anshanā qurūnan fataṭāwala ʿalayhimu l-ʿumuru wamā kunta thāwiyan fī ahli madyana tatlū ʿalayhim āyātinā walākinnā kunnā mur'silīn
verses.english: But we established many generations, and, because of the length of time, (they deviated). Nor were you among the people of Midyan, reciting our revelations to them. But we did send messengers.

1981.english: We established many generations who received no scripture for a long time. Nor were you residing with the people of Midyan, reciting for them our revelations. But we did send messengers.

1989.english: But we established many generations, and, because of the length of time, (they deviated). Nor were you among the people of Midyan, reciting our revelations to them. But we did send messengers.

verses.arabic: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ إِذْ نَادَيْنَا وَلَٰكِن رَّحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوْمًا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون
verses.transliterated: wamā kunta bijānibi l-ṭūri idh nādaynā walākin raḥmatan min rabbika litundhira qawman mā atāhum min nadhīrin min qablika laʿallahum yatadhakkarūn
verses.english: Nor were you on the slope of Mount Sinai when we called (Moses). But it is mercy from your Lord, (towards the people,) in order to warn people who received no warner before you, that they may take heed.

1981.english: Nor were you at the slope of Al-Toor (Mount Sinai) when we called. This is indeed mercy from your Lord, that you may warn people who received no warner before you; perhaps they take heed.

1989.english: Nor were you on the slope of Mount Sinai when we called (Moses). But it is mercy from your Lord, (that we informed you,) in order to warn people who received no warner before you, that they may take heed.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْلَآ أَن تُصِيبَهُم مُّصِيبَةٌۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُوا۟ رَبَّنَا لَوْلَآ أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين
verses.transliterated: walawlā an tuṣībahum muṣībatun bimā qaddamat aydīhim fayaqūlū rabbanā lawlā arsalta ilaynā rasūlan fanattabiʿa āyātika wanakūna mina l-mu'minīn
verses.english: Thus, they cannot say, when a disaster strikes them as a consequence of their own deeds, "Our Lord, had You sent a messenger to us, we would have followed Your revelations, and would have been believers."
verses.subtitle: No Excuse

1981.english: Now, if a disaster strikes them because of their own deeds, they cannot say, "Our Lord, had You sent a messenger to us, we would have followed Your commandments, and would have been believers."

1989.english: Thus, they cannot say, when a disaster strikes them as a consequence of their own deeds, “Our Lord, had You sent a messenger to us, we would have followed Your commandments; we would have been believers.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ لَوْلَآ أُوتِىَ مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفُرُوا۟ بِمَآ أُوتِىَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ قَالُوا۟ سِحْرَانِ تَظَٰهَرَا وَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا بِكُلٍّ كَٰفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى ۚ أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل ۖ قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون
verses.transliterated: falammā jāahumu l-ḥaqu min ʿindinā qālū lawlā ūtiya mith'la mā ūtiya mūsā awalam yakfurū bimā ūtiya mūsā min qablu qālū siḥ'rāni taẓāharā waqālū innā bikullin kāfirūn
verses.english: Now that the truth has come to them from us, they said, "If only we could be given what was given to Moses!" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses in the past? They said, "Both (scriptures) are works of magic that copied one another." They also said, "We are disbelievers in both of them."
verses.subtitle: The Torah and The Quran

1981.english: However, when the truth came to them from us, they said, "If only we could see the same thing as that given to Moses (we will then believe)." Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses? They said, "(The Torah and the Quran are) two magics that support one another, and we reject them both."
1981.subtitle: Quran: God's Message to the World
1981.footnote: The Jews abandoned the Torah in favor of the Mishnah and Gemara, while the Muslims abandoned the Quran in favor of **Hadith** and **Sunna**.

1989.english: Now that the truth has come to them from us, they said, “If only we could be shown the same miracles as the miracles of Moses!” Did they not disbelieve in the miracles of Moses in the past? They said, “Both (scriptures) are works of magic that copied one another.” They also said, “We are disbelievers in both of them.”
1989.subtitle: The Torah and The Quran

verses.arabic: قُلْ فَأْتُوا۟ بِكِتَٰبٍ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ أَهْدَىٰ مِنْهُمَآ أَتَّبِعْهُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين
verses.transliterated: qul fatū bikitābin min ʿindi l-lahi huwa ahdā min'humā attabiʿ'hu in kuntum ṣādiqīn
verses.english: Say, "Then produce a scripture from GOD with better guidance than the two, so I can follow it, if you are truthful."

1981.english: Say, "Show me a book from God that provides more guidance than them. I will follow it, if you are truthful."

1989.english: Say, “Then produce a scripture from GOD with better guidance than the two, so I can follow it, if you are truthful.”

verses.arabic: فَإِن لَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لَكَ فَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّمَا يَتَّبِعُونَ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ بِغَيْرِ هُدًى مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ۚ ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله ۚ إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين
verses.transliterated: fa-in lam yastajībū laka fa-iʿ'lam annamā yattabiʿūna ahwāahum waman aḍallu mimmani ittabaʿa hawāhu bighayri hudan mina l-lahi inna l-laha lā yahdī l-qawma l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: If they fail to respond to you, then know that they follow only their own opinions. Who is farther astray than those who follow their own opinions, without guidance from GOD? GOD does not guide such wicked people.
verses.subtitle: God Sends His Teachings to us Through His Messengers

1981.english: If they fail to respond to you, then know that they only follow their own opinions. And who is more astray than one who follows his own opinions, without guidance from God. God does not guide the wicked.

1989.english: If they fail to respond to you, then know that they are just following their own opinions. Who is farther astray than those who follow their own opinions, without guidance from GOD? GOD does not guide such wicked people.
1989.subtitle: God Sends His Teachings to us Through His Messengers

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ وَصَّلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون
verses.transliterated: walaqad waṣṣalnā lahumu l-qawla laʿallahum yatadhakkarūn
verses.english: We have delivered the message to them, that they may take heed.
verses.subtitle: All True Believers Accept the Quran

1981.english: We have certainly delivered the message to them, that they may take heed.

1989.english: We have delivered the message to them, that they may take heed.
1989.subtitle: All True Believers Accept the Quran

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ هُم بِهِۦ يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: alladhīna ātaynāhumu l-kitāba min qablihi hum bihi yu'minūn
verses.english: Those whom we blessed with the previous scriptures will believe in this.

1981.english: Those who truly studied the previous scriptures will believe in this.

1989.english: Those whom we blessed with the previous scriptures will believe in this.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مُسْلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā yut'lā ʿalayhim qālū āmannā bihi innahu l-ḥaqu min rabbinā innā kunnā min qablihi mus'limīn
verses.english: When it is recited to them, they will say, "We believe in it. This is the truth from our Lord. Even before we heard of it, we were submitters."

1981.english: When (this Quran is) recited to them, they would say, "We believe that this is the truth from our Lord. We have been, according to it, Muslims."

1989.english: When it is recited to them, they will say, “We believe in it. This is the truth from our Lord. Even before we heard of it, we were Muslims.”

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟ وَيَدْرَءُونَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون
verses.transliterated: ulāika yu'tawna ajrahum marratayni bimā ṣabarū wayadraūna bil-ḥasanati l-sayi-ata wamimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūn
verses.english: To these we grant twice the reward, because they steadfastly persevere. They counter evil works with good works, and from our provisions to them, they give.
verses.subtitle: Twice the Reward for Christians & Jews Who Recognize the Truth

1981.english: These will be given double the recompense because of their steadfastness, and because they repel evil with righteousness, and from our provisions to them, they give to charity.

1989.english: To these we grant twice the reward, because of their steadfastness. They counter evil works with good works, and from our provisions to them, they give.
1989.subtitle: Twice the Reward for Christians and Jews Who Recognize the Truth

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱللَّغْوَ أَعْرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ وَقَالُوا۟ لَنَآ أَعْمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لَا نَبْتَغِى ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā samiʿū l-laghwa aʿraḍū ʿanhu waqālū lanā aʿmālunā walakum aʿmālukum salāmun ʿalaykum lā nabtaghī l-jāhilīn
verses.english: When they come across vain talk, they disregard it and say, "We are responsible for our deeds, and you are responsible for your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not wish to behave like the ignorant ones."

1981.english: And when they encounter vain talk, they ignore it, saying "We are responsible for our work, and you are responsible for your work. Peace be on you, we have no desire to befriend the ignorant."

1989.english: And when they come across vain talk, they disregard it and say, “We are responsible for our deeds, and you are responsible for your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not wish to behave like the ignorant ones.”

verses.arabic: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِى مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء ۚ وهو أعلم بالمهتدين
verses.transliterated: innaka lā tahdī man aḥbabta walākinna l-laha yahdī man yashāu wahuwa aʿlamu bil-muh'tadīn
verses.english: You cannot guide the ones you love. GOD is the only One who guides in accordance with His will, and in accordance with His knowledge of those who deserve the guidance.
verses.subtitle: Only God Guides

1981.english: You cannot guide those you love. God is the one who guides whomever He wills, for He is fully aware of those who deserve the guidance.
1981.subtitle: Only God Guides

1989.english: You cannot guide the ones you love. GOD is the only One who guides in accordance with His will, and in accordance with His knowledge of those who deserve the guidance.
1989.subtitle: Only God Guides

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوٓا۟ إِن نَّتَّبِعِ ٱلْهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفْ مِنْ أَرْضِنَآ أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَمًا ءَامِنًا يُجْبَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَٰتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ رِّزْقًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا ۚ أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: waqālū in nattabiʿi l-hudā maʿaka nutakhaṭṭaf min arḍinā awalam numakkin lahum ḥaraman āminan yuj'bā ilayhi thamarātu kulli shayin riz'qan min ladunnā walākinna aktharahum lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: They said, "If we follow your guidance, we will suffer persecution." Did we not establish for them a Sacred Sanctuary, to which all kinds of fruits are offered, as a provision from us? Indeed, most of them do not know.

1981.english: (The pagans also) said, "If we follow your guidance, we will be persecuted throughout the land." Did we not establish for them a sacred shrine that is perfectly secure, with all kinds of provisions donated to it from us? Indeed, most of them do not know.

1989.english: They said, “If we follow your guidance, we will suffer persecution.” Did we not establish for them a Sacred Sanctuary, to which all kinds of fruits are offered, as a provision from us? Indeed, most of them do not know.

verses.arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍۭ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا فَتِلْكَ مَسَٰكِنُهُمْ لَمْ تُسْكَن مِّنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا وَكُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها ۖ فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا ۖ وكنا نحن الوارثين
verses.transliterated: wakam ahlaknā min qaryatin baṭirat maʿīshatahā fatil'ka masākinuhum lam tus'kan min baʿdihim illā qalīlan wakunnā naḥnu l-wārithīn
verses.english: Many a community we annihilated for turning unappreciative of their lives. Consequently, here are their homes, nothing but uninhabited ruins after them, except a few. We were the inheritors.

1981.english: Many a community we destroyed when they turned unappreciative. Here are their ruins that were abandoned, except a few; we were the inheritors.

1989.english: Many a community we annihilated for turning unappreciative of their provisions. Thus, here are their homes, nothing but uninhabited ruins after them, except a few. We were the inheritors.

verses.arabic: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبْعَثَ فِىٓ أُمِّهَا رَسُولًا يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَمَا كُنَّا مُهْلِكِى ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا وَأَهْلُهَا ظَٰلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا ۚ وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون
verses.transliterated: wamā kāna rabbuka muh'lika l-qurā ḥattā yabʿatha fī ummihā rasūlan yatlū ʿalayhim āyātinā wamā kunnā muh'likī l-qurā illā wa-ahluhā ẓālimūn
verses.english: For your Lord never annihilates any community without sending a messenger in the midst thereof, to recite our revelations to them. We never annihilate any community, unless its people are wicked.

1981.english: Your Lord never destroys any community, unless He sends in the midst thereof a messenger who recites our revelations for them. We never destroy any community unless its people are wicked.

1989.english: For your Lord never annihilates any community without sending a messenger in the midst thereof, to recite our revelations to them. We never annihilate any community, unless its people are wicked.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَىْءٍ فَمَتَٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتُهَا وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها ۚ وما عند الله خير وأبقى ۚ أفلا تعقلون
verses.transliterated: wamā ūtītum min shayin famatāʿu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wazīnatuhā wamā ʿinda l-lahi khayrun wa-abqā afalā taʿqilūn
verses.english: Everything that is given to you is only the material of this life, and its vanity. What is with GOD is far better, and everlasting. Do you not understand?

1981.english: Whatever you possess is the material of this life, and its vanities. What God possesses is far better, and eternal; do you not understand?

1989.english: Everything that is given to you is only the material of this life, and its adorn ment. What is with GOD is far better, and everlasting. Do you not understand?

verses.arabic: أَفَمَن وَعَدْنَٰهُ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا فَهُوَ لَٰقِيهِ كَمَن مَّتَّعْنَٰهُ مَتَٰعَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين
verses.transliterated: afaman waʿadnāhu waʿdan ḥasanan fahuwa lāqīhi kaman mattaʿnāhu matāʿa l-ḥayati l-dun'yā thumma huwa yawma l-qiyāmati mina l-muḥ'ḍarīn
verses.english: Is one whom we promised a good promise that will surely come to pass, equal to one whom we provide with the temporary materials of this life, then suffers eternal doom on the Day of Resurrection?

1981.english: Is one whom we promised a good promise that is sure to come, equal to one who enjoys the temporary vanities of this life, then is forcibly gathered on the day of resurrection?

1989.english: Is one whom we promised a good promise that will surely come to pass, equal to one whom we provide with the materials of this life, then he incurs eternal doom on the Day of Resurrection?

verses.arabic: وَيَوْمَ يُنَادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآءِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون
verses.transliterated: wayawma yunādīhim fayaqūlu ayna shurakāiya alladhīna kuntum tazʿumūn
verses.english: The day will come when He calls upon them, saying, "Where are those idols you had set up beside Me?"
verses.subtitle: The Idols Disown Their Idolizers

1981.english: On that day, He will call upon them saying, "Where are those idols you set up besides Me?"

1989.english: The day will come when He calls upon them, saying, “Where are those idols you had set up besides Me?”
1989.subtitle: The Idols Disown Their Idolizers

verses.arabic: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ رَبَّنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أَغْوَيْنَآ أَغْوَيْنَٰهُمْ كَمَا غَوَيْنَا تَبَرَّأْنَآ إِلَيْكَ مَا كَانُوٓا۟ إِيَّانَا يَعْبُدُونَ
