verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنۢ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَٰهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalnā min bayni aydīhim saddan wamin khalfihim saddan fa-aghshaynāhum fahum lā yub'ṣirūn
verses.english: And we place a barrier in front of them, and a barrier behind them, and thus, we veil them; they cannot see.

1981.english: And we place a barrier in front of them and a barrier behind them, so they can never see.

1989.english: And we place a barrier in front of them, and a barrier behind them, and thus, we veil them; they cannot see.

verses.arabic: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: wasawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūn
verses.english: It is the same whether you warn them or not, they cannot believe.
verses.footnote: Everyone is already stamped as a believer or a disbeliever. See Appendix 14.

1981.english: Therefore, it is the same for them; whether you warn them or not, they will not believe.

1989.english: It is the same whether you warn them or not, they do not believe.*
1989.footnote: Everyone is already stamped as a believer or a disbeliever. See Appendix 14.

verses.arabic: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَخَشِىَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب ۖ فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم
verses.transliterated: innamā tundhiru mani ittabaʿa l-dhik'ra wakhashiya l-raḥmāna bil-ghaybi fabashir'hu bimaghfiratin wa-ajrin karīmi
verses.english: You will be heeded only by those who uphold this message, and reverence the Most Gracious—even when alone in their privacy. Give them good news of forgiveness and a generous recompense.

1981.english: You can only warn those who heed the message and reverence God most gracious in their privacy. Promise these forgiveness and a generous recompense.

1989.english: You will be heeded only by those who uphold this message, and reverence the Most Gracious in their privacy. Give them good news of forgiveness and a generous recompense.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمْ وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم ۚ وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين
verses.transliterated: innā naḥnu nuḥ'yī l-mawtā wanaktubu mā qaddamū waāthārahum wakulla shayin aḥṣaynāhu fī imāmin mubīni
verses.english: We will certainly revive the dead, and we have recorded everything they have done in this life, as well as the consequences that continue after their death. Everything we have counted in a profound record.

1981.english: We will surely resurrect the dead; we have recorded everything they had done in their life, as well as the post-mortem consequences. Everything is kept in a profound record.

1989.english: We will certainly revive the dead. We record everything they do during their life, as well as the consequences that continue after their death. Everything we have counted in a profound book.

verses.arabic: وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَآءَهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون
verses.transliterated: wa-iḍ'rib lahum mathalan aṣḥāba l-qaryati idh jāahā l-mur'salūn
verses.english: Cite for them the example of people in a community that received the messengers.
verses.subtitle: Rejecting The Messengers: A Tragic Human Trait
verses.footnote: God's messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

1981.english: Cite for them the example of a community who received the messengers.
1981.subtitle: Perennial Human Plague

1989.english: Cite for them the example of people in one community who received the messengers.
1989.subtitle: Rejecting The Messengers: A Tragic Human Trait
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ إِلَيْكُم مُّرْسَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون
verses.transliterated: idh arsalnā ilayhimu ith'nayni fakadhabūhumā faʿazzaznā bithālithin faqālū innā ilaykum mur'salūn
verses.english: When we sent to them two (messengers), they disbelieved them. We then supported them by a third. They said, "We are (GOD's) messengers to you."

1981.english: We sent to them two, and they disbelieved them, then we supported them with a third. They said, "We are messengers to you."

1989.english: When we sent to them two (messengers), they disbelieved them, then we supported them by a third. They said, “We are (God’s) messengers to you.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ مِن شَىْءٍ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون
verses.transliterated: qālū mā antum illā basharun mith'lunā wamā anzala l-raḥmānu min shayin in antum illā takdhibūn
verses.english: They said, "You are no more than human beings like us. The Most Gracious did not send down anything. You are liars."

1981.english: They said, "You are no more than mortals like us, and God most gracious did not reveal anything to you. You are liars."

1989.english: They said, “You are no more than human beings like us. The Most Gracious did not reveal anything. You are really liars.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون
verses.transliterated: qālū rabbunā yaʿlamu innā ilaykum lamur'salūn
verses.english: They said, "Our Lord knows that we have been sent to you.

1981.english: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you.

1989.english: They said, “Our Lord knows that we have been sent to vou.
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: وَمَا عَلَيْنَآ إِلَّا ٱلْبَلَٰغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
verses.arabicClean: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين
verses.transliterated: wamā ʿalaynā illā l-balāghu l-mubīn
verses.english: "Our sole mission is to deliver the message."

1981.english: "Our sole function is to deliver the profound message."

1989.english: “Our sole mission is to deliver the message.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهُوا۟ لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم ۖ لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم
verses.transliterated: qālū innā taṭayyarnā bikum la-in lam tantahū lanarjumannakum walayamassannakum minnā ʿadhābun alīmu
verses.english: They said, "We consider you bad omens. Unless you refrain, we will surely stone you, or afflict you with painful retribution."

1981.english: They said, "We consider you bad omen for us. Unless you refrain, we will surely stone you; you will suffer painful retribution at our hands."

1989.english: They said, “We consider you bad omens. Unless you refrain from this, we will surely stone you, or afflict you with painful retribution.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمْ أَئِن ذُكِّرْتُم بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّسْرِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا طائركم معكم ۚ أئن ذكرتم ۚ بل أنتم قوم مسرفون
verses.transliterated: qālū ṭāirukum maʿakum a-in dhukkir'tum bal antum qawmun mus'rifūn
verses.english: They said, "Your omen depends on your response, now that you have been reminded. Indeed, you are transgressing people."

1981.english: They said, "You are the bad omen for yourselves, now that you have been reminded. Indeed, you are transgressors."

1989.english: They said, “Your omen depends on you, now that you are reminded. You are transgressing people.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: وَجَآءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين
verses.transliterated: wajāa min aqṣā l-madīnati rajulun yasʿā qāla yāqawmi ittabiʿū l-mur'salīn
verses.english: A man came from the other end of the city, saying, "O my people, follow the messengers.

1981.english: A man came from the far side of the city saying, "O my people, follow the messengers.

1989.english: A man came running from the other end of the city, saying, “O my people, follow the messengers.
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون
verses.transliterated: ittabiʿū man lā yasalukum ajran wahum muh'tadūn
verses.english: "Follow those who do not ask you for any wage, and are guided.

1981.english: "Follow those who do not ask you for any wage; they are guided.

1989.english: “Follow those who do not ask you for any wage, and are guided.
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: وَمَا لِىَ لَآ أَعْبُدُ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون
verses.transliterated: wamā liya lā aʿbudu alladhī faṭaranī wa-ilayhi tur'jaʿūn
verses.english: "Why should I not worship the One who initiated me, and to Him is your ultimate return?

1981.english: "Why shouldn't I worship the one who created me, and to Him is your final return?

1989.english: “Why should I not worship the One who initiated me, and to Him is your ultimate return?
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدْنِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ بِضُرٍّ لَّا تُغْنِ عَنِّى شَفَٰعَتُهُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
verses.arabicClean: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون
verses.transliterated: a-attakhidhu min dūnihi ālihatan in yurid'ni l-raḥmānu biḍurrin lā tugh'ni ʿannī shafāʿatuhum shayan walā yunqidhūn
verses.english: "Shall I set up beside Him gods? If the Most Gracious willed any harm for me, their intercession cannot help me one bit, nor can they rescue me.

1981.english: "Shall I idolize besides Him idols that, if God most gracious willed any harm for me, their intercession will be useless, and they can never save me?

1989.english: “Shall I set up besides Him (power less) gods? If the Most Gracious willed any harm for me, their intercession will not help me one bit, nor can they rescue me.
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: إِنِّىٓ إِذًا لَّفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين
verses.transliterated: innī idhan lafī ḍalālin mubīni
verses.english: "In that case, I would be totally astray.

1981.english: "If I do this, I would be totally astray.

1989.english: “Then I would be totally astray.
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: إِنِّىٓ ءَامَنتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَٱسْمَعُونِ
verses.arabicClean: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون
verses.transliterated: innī āmantu birabbikum fa-is'maʿūn
verses.english: "I have believed in your Lord; please listen to me."

1981.english: "I have believed in your Lord; please listen to me."

1989.english: “I have believed in your Lord; please listen to me.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَٰلَيْتَ قَوْمِى يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قيل ادخل الجنة ۖ قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون
verses.transliterated: qīla ud'khuli l-janata qāla yālayta qawmī yaʿlamūn
verses.english: (At the time of his death) he was told, "Enter Paradise." He said, "Oh, I wish my people knew.
verses.subtitle: The Righteous Go Straight to Paradise
verses.footnote: The righteous do not really die; they simply move on to the same Paradise where Adam & Eve lived. They join the prophets, saints, and martyrs in an active and utopian life (see App. 17).

1981.english: He was told, "Enter paradise," and he said, "I wish my people knew,

1989.english: (At the time of his death) he was told, “Enter Paradise.” He said, “Oh, I wish my people knew—
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِى رَبِّى وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين
verses.transliterated: bimā ghafara lī rabbī wajaʿalanī mina l-muk'ramīn
verses.english: "That my Lord has forgiven me, and made me honorable."

1981.english: "how my Lord has forgiven me, and how he has honored me."

1989.english: “that my Lord has forgiven me, and made me honorable.”
1989.footnote: God’s messengers have proof, advocate God alone, and do not ask for money.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ مِن جُندٍ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين
verses.transliterated: wamā anzalnā ʿalā qawmihi min baʿdihi min jundin mina l-samāi wamā kunnā munzilīn
verses.english: We did not send down upon his people, after him, soldiers from the sky; we did not need to send them down.

1981.english: We did not send down troops from the sky against his people; we did not need to.

1989.english: We did not send down upon his people, after him, soldiers from the sky; we did not need to send them down.

verses.arabic: إِن كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَٰحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَٰمِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون
verses.transliterated: in kānat illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan fa-idhā hum khāmidūn
verses.english: All it took was one blow, whereupon they were stilled.

1981.english: All we needed was one blow, whereupon they became dead.

1989.english: All it took was one blow, whereupon they were stilled.

verses.arabic: يَٰحَسْرَةً عَلَى ٱلْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يا حسرة على العباد ۚ ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون
verses.transliterated: yāḥasratan ʿalā l-ʿibādi mā yatīhim min rasūlin illā kānū bihi yastahziūn
verses.english: How sorry is the people's condition! Every time a messenger went to them, they always ridiculed him.
verses.subtitle: Ridiculing The Messengers: A Tragic Human Trait
verses.footnote: If the messenger presents solid proof of messengership, advocates the worship of God alone, and does not ask us for money, why should we not believe? (see Appendix 2)

1981.english: How sorry is the condition of the people! Whenever a messenger comes to them, they ridicule him.

1989.english: How sorry is the people’s condition! Every time a messenger went to them, they always ridiculed him.
1989.subtitle: Ridiculing The Messengers: A Tragic Human Trait
1989.footnote: If the messenger presents solid proof of messengership, advocates the worship of God alone, and does not ask us for money, why should we not believe? (Appendix 2)

verses.arabic: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون
verses.transliterated: alam yaraw kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni annahum ilayhim lā yarjiʿūn
verses.english: Did they not see how many generations we annihilated before them, and how they never return to them?

1981.english: Do they not see how many generations we annihilated before them, and how they never return to them?

1989.english: Did they not see how many generations before them we annihilated, and how they never return to them?

verses.arabic: وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون
verses.transliterated: wa-in kullun lammā jamīʿun ladaynā muḥ'ḍarūn
verses.english: Every one of them will be summoned before us.

1981.english: All of them will be brought before us.

1989.english: Every one of them will be summoned before us.

verses.arabic: وَءَايَةٌ لَّهُمُ ٱلْأَرْضُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَٰهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون
verses.transliterated: waāyatun lahumu l-arḍu l-maytatu aḥyaynāhā wa-akhrajnā min'hā ḥabban famin'hu yakulūn
verses.english: One sign for them is the dead land: we revive it and produce from it grains for their food.
verses.subtitle: Signs of God

1981.english: A sign for them is the dead land that we revive and produce from it grains for their food.

1989.english: One sign for them is the dead land: we revive it and produce from it grains for their food.
1989.subtitle: Signs of God

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّٰتٍ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَٰبٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْعُيُونِ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalnā fīhā jannātin min nakhīlin wa-aʿnābin wafajjarnā fīhā mina l-ʿuyūn
verses.english: We grow in it gardens of date palms, and grapes, and we cause springs to gush out therein.

1981.english: And we create in it gardens of date palms and grapes, and we cause springs to gush out.

1989.english: And we grow in it gardens of date palms, and grapes. And we cause springs to gush out therein.

verses.arabic: لِيَأْكُلُوا۟ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم ۖ أفلا يشكرون
verses.transliterated: liyakulū min thamarihi wamā ʿamilathu aydīhim afalā yashkurūn
verses.english: This is to provide them with fruits, and to let them manufacture with their own hands whatever they need. Would they be thankful?

1981.english: This is to provide them with food from the fruits thereof, as well as what they cook with their hands. Would they be appreciative?

1989.english: This is to provide them with fruits, and to let them manufacture what they need. Would they be thankful?

verses.arabic: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: sub'ḥāna alladhī khalaqa l-azwāja kullahā mimmā tunbitu l-arḍu wamin anfusihim wamimmā lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: Glory be to the One who created all kinds of plants from the earth, as well as themselves, and other creations that they do not even know.

1981.english: Glorified be the One who created all kinds of plants, as well as the people, and things they do not know.

1989.english: Glory be to the One who created all kinds of plants from the earth, as well as themselves, and other creations that they do not even know.

verses.arabic: وَءَايَةٌ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُم مُّظْلِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون
verses.transliterated: waāyatun lahumu al-laylu naslakhu min'hu l-nahāra fa-idhā hum muẓ'limūn
verses.english: Another sign for them is the night: we remove the daylight therefrom, whereupon they are in darkness.

1981.english: Another sign for them is the night; we strip the day therefrom, whereupon they are in darkness.

1989.english: Another sign for them is the night: we remove the daylight therefrom, whereupon they are in darkness.

verses.arabic: وَٱلشَّمْسُ تَجْرِى لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَا ذَٰلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ۚ ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم
verses.transliterated: wal-shamsu tajrī limus'taqarrin lahā dhālika taqdīru l-ʿazīzi l-ʿalīm
verses.english: The sun sets into a specific location, according to the design of the Almighty, the Omniscient.

1981.english: And the sun running in a specific orbit. Such is the design of the almighty, the omniscient.

1989.english: And the sun sets into a specific location, according to the design of the Almighty, the Omniscient.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَٰهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَٱلْعُرْجُونِ ٱلْقَدِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم
verses.transliterated: wal-qamara qaddarnāhu manāzila ḥattā ʿāda kal-ʿur'jūni l-qadīm
verses.english: The moon we designed to appear in stages, until it becomes like an old curved sheath.

1981.english: And we designed the moon to appear in stages, until it reverts to a thin curve.

1989.english: And the moon we designed in stages, until it becomes like an old curved sheath.

verses.arabic: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنۢبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيْلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَكُلٌّ فِى فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار ۚ وكل في فلك يسبحون
verses.transliterated: lā l-shamsu yanbaghī lahā an tud'rika l-qamara walā al-laylu sābiqu l-nahāri wakullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn
verses.english: The sun is never to catch up with the moon—the night and the day never deviate—each of them is floating in its own orbit.

1981.english: The sun never catches up with the moon, nor does the night prematurely overtake the day. Each floats in its own orbit.

1989.english: The sun is never to catch up with the moon, nor does the night precede the day. Each of them is floating in its own orbit.

verses.arabic: وَءَايَةٌ لَّهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ
verses.arabicClean: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون
verses.transliterated: waāyatun lahum annā ḥamalnā dhurriyyatahum fī l-ful'ki l-mashḥūn
verses.english: Another sign for them is that we carried their ancestors on the loaded ark.
verses.subtitle: Invention of the First Ship

1981.english: Another sign for them is that we carried their ancestors in the loaded ark.

1989.english: Another sign for them is that we carried their forefathers on the loaded ark.
1989.subtitle: Invention of the First Ship

verses.arabic: وَخَلَقْنَا لَهُم مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ مَا يَرْكَبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون
verses.transliterated: wakhalaqnā lahum min mith'lihi mā yarkabūn
verses.english: Then created the same for them to ride in.

1981.english: Then we created similar vessels for them to ride.

1989.english: Then created the same for them to ride in.

verses.arabic: وَإِن نَّشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلَا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون
verses.transliterated: wa-in nasha nugh'riq'hum falā ṣarīkha lahum walā hum yunqadhūn
verses.english: If we willed, we could have drowned them, so that their screaming would not be heard, nor could they be saved.

1981.english: Whenever we will, we can drown them, without a chance to scream or get saved.

1989.english: If we willed, we could have drowned them, so that their screaming would not be heard, nor could they be saved.

verses.arabic: إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا وَمَتَٰعًا إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين
verses.transliterated: illā raḥmatan minnā wamatāʿan ilā ḥīni
verses.english: Instead, we shower them with mercy, and let them enjoy for awhile.

1981.english: It is mercy from us that we assign for them a predetermined life span.

1989.english: Instead, we shower them with mercy, and let them enjoy for awhile.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُوا۟ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā qīla lahumu ittaqū mā bayna aydīkum wamā khalfakum laʿallakum tur'ḥamūn
verses.english: Yet, when they are told, "Learn from your past, to work righteousness for your future, that you may attain mercy,"

1981.english: Yet, when told, "Beware of your past and future, that you may attain mercy,"

1989.english: Yet, when they are told, “Learn from your past, to work righteousness for your future that you may attain mercy,”

verses.arabic: وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ ءَايَةٍ مِّنْ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين
verses.transliterated: wamā tatīhim min āyatin min āyāti rabbihim illā kānū ʿanhā muʿ'riḍīn
verses.english: No matter what kind of proof is given to them from their Lord, they consistently disregard it.

1981.english: And when every kind of sign is presented to them from their Lord, they turn away in aversion.

1989.english: No matter what kind of sign is sent to them from their Lord, they consistently disregard it.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ أَنُطْعِمُ مَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُۥٓ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā qīla lahum anfiqū mimmā razaqakumu l-lahu qāla alladhīna kafarū lilladhīna āmanū anuṭ'ʿimu man law yashāu l-lahu aṭʿamahu in antum illā fī ḍalālin mubīni
verses.english: When they are told, "Give from GOD's provisions to you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Why should we give to those whom GOD could feed, if He so willed? You are really far astray."

1981.english: And when told, "Give to charity from God's provisions to you," the disbelievers would say to the believers, "Shall we feed those who are fed by God, if He so wills? You are completely wrong."

1989.english: And when they are told, “Give from GOD’s provisions to you,” those who disbelieved say to those who believed, “Why should we give to those whom GOD could feed, if He so willed? You are really far astray.”

verses.arabic: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين
verses.transliterated: wayaqūlūna matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīn
verses.english: They also challenge, "When will that promise come to pass, if you are truthful?"

1981.english: And they say, "When will that promise come to pass, if you are truthful?"

1989.english: They also challenged, “When will that promise come to pass, if you are truthful?”

verses.arabic: مَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَٰحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون
verses.transliterated: mā yanẓurūna illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan takhudhuhum wahum yakhiṣṣimūn
verses.english: All they see will be one blow that overwhelms them, while they dispute.

1981.english: All they see is one blow that strikes them as they feud.

1989.english: All they see will be one blow that overwhelms them, while they dispute.

verses.arabic: فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً وَلَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون
verses.transliterated: falā yastaṭīʿūna tawṣiyatan walā ilā ahlihim yarjiʿūn
verses.english: They will not even have time to make a will, nor will they be able to return to their people.

1981.english: They will not have a chance to utter a will, nor can they come back to their people.

1989.english: They will not even have time to make a will, nor will they return to their people.

verses.arabic: وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَإِذَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون
verses.transliterated: wanufikha fī l-ṣūri fa-idhā hum mina l-ajdāthi ilā rabbihim yansilūn
verses.english: The horn will be blown, whereupon they will rise from the grave and go to their Lord.

1981.english: And when the horn is blown, they scramble out of the graves to face their Lord.

1989.english: The horn will be blown, whereupon they will rise from the grave and go to their Lord.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا ۜ ۗ هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون
verses.transliterated: qālū yāwaylanā man baʿathanā min marqadinā hādhā mā waʿada l-raḥmānu waṣadaqa l-mur'salūn
verses.english: They will say, "Woe to us. Who resurrected us from our death? This is what the Most Gracious has promised. The messengers were right."

1981.english: They will then say, "Woe to us; who raised us from death? This is what God most gracious had promised. The messengers were right."

1989.english: They will say, “Woe to us. Who resurrected us from our death? This is what the Most Gracious has promised. The messengers were right.”

verses.arabic: إِن كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَٰحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ جَمِيعٌ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون
verses.transliterated: in kānat illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan fa-idhā hum jamīʿun ladaynā muḥ'ḍarūn
verses.english: All it will take is one blow, whereupon they are summoned before us.

1981.english: It takes only one blow, whereupon they are brought before us.

1989.english: All it takes is one blow, whereupon they are summoned before us.

verses.arabic: فَٱلْيَوْمَ لَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون
verses.transliterated: fal-yawma lā tuẓ'lamu nafsun shayan walā tuj'zawna illā mā kuntum taʿmalūn
verses.english: On that day, no soul will be wronged in the least. You will be paid precisely for whatever you did.

1981.english: On that day, no one will be wronged in the least. You are not repaid, except for what you have done.

1989.english: On that day, no soul will be wronged in the least. You will be paid precisely for whatever you did.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلْيَوْمَ فِى شُغُلٍ فَٰكِهُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون
verses.transliterated: inna aṣḥāba l-janati l-yawma fī shughulin fākihūn
verses.english: The dwellers of Paradise will be, on that day, happily busy.

1981.english: Those who deserved heaven on that day will be happily involved.
1981.subtitle: Heaven and Hell
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: The dwellers of Paradise will be, on that day, happily busy.

verses.arabic: هُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُهُمْ فِى ظِلَٰلٍ عَلَى ٱلْأَرَآئِكِ مُتَّكِـُٔونَ
verses.arabicClean: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون
verses.transliterated: hum wa-azwājuhum fī ẓilālin ʿalā l-arāiki muttakiūn
verses.english: They abide with their spouses in beautiful shade, enjoying comfortable furnishings.

1981.english: They, and their spouses, will enjoy the shade as they relax on their couches.
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: They abide with their spouses in beautiful shade, enjoying comfortable furnishings.

verses.arabic: لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةٌ وَلَهُم مَّا يَدَّعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون
verses.transliterated: lahum fīhā fākihatun walahum mā yaddaʿūn
verses.english: They will have fruits therein; they will have anything they wish.

1981.english: They will have fruits therein, and everything they wish.
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: They will have fruits therein; they will have anything they wish.

verses.arabic: سَلَٰمٌ قَوْلًا مِّن رَّبٍّ رَّحِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: سلام قولا من رب رحيم
verses.transliterated: salāmun qawlan min rabbin raḥīmi
verses.english: Greetings of peace from a Most Merciful Lord.

1981.english: Peace will be their greeting from the Lord most merciful.
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: Greetings of peace from a Most Merciful Lord.

verses.arabic: وَٱمْتَٰزُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون
verses.transliterated: wa-im'tāzū l-yawma ayyuhā l-muj'rimūn
verses.english: As for you, O guilty ones, you will be set aside.

1981.english: And be marked on that day, O you guilty.
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: As for you, O guilty ones, you will be set aside. The Other

verses.arabic: أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يَٰبَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان ۖ إنه لكم عدو مبين
verses.transliterated: alam aʿhad ilaykum yābanī ādama an lā taʿbudū l-shayṭāna innahu lakum ʿaduwwun mubīnu
verses.english: Did I not covenant with you, O Children of Adam, that you shall not worship the devil? That he is your most ardent enemy?
verses.subtitle: The Devil is the Other Alternative

1981.english: Did I not make a covenant with you, O children of Adam,* that you shall not worship the devil, for he is your ardent enemy?

1989.english: Did I not covenant with you, O Children of Adam, that you shall not worship the devil? That he is your most ardent enemy?

verses.arabic: وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وأن اعبدوني ۚ هذا صراط مستقيم
verses.transliterated: wa-ani uʿ'budūnī hādhā ṣirāṭun mus'taqīmu
verses.english: And that you shall worship Me alone? This is the right path.

1981.english: That you shall worship Me alone to remain on the right path?
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: That you shall worship Me alone? That this is the straight path?

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنكُمْ جِبِلًّا كَثِيرًا أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا ۖ أفلم تكونوا تعقلون
verses.transliterated: walaqad aḍalla minkum jibillan kathīran afalam takūnū taʿqilūn
verses.english: He has misled multitudes of you. Did you not possess any understanding?

1981.english: Indeed, he misled multitudes of you. Did you not possess any intelligence?
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: He has misled multitudes of you. Did you not possess any understanding?

verses.arabic: هَٰذِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون
verses.transliterated: hādhihi jahannamu allatī kuntum tūʿadūn
verses.english: This is the Hell that was promised for you.

1981.english: This is Gehenna that has been promised to you.
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: This is the Hell that was promised for you.

verses.arabic: ٱصْلَوْهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون
verses.transliterated: iṣ'lawhā l-yawma bimā kuntum takfurūn
verses.english: Today you will burn in it, as a consequence of your disbelief.

1981.english: Burn in it today, because of your disbelief.
1981.footnote: Heaven and hell are described in allegorical terms throughout Quran (see 2:25-26). The Quran is aimed at all levels of education, culture, and mental capacity. See Appendix 4.

1989.english: Today you will burn in it, as a consequence of your disbelief.

verses.arabic: ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَتَشْهَدُ أَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون
verses.transliterated: al-yawma nakhtimu ʿalā afwāhihim watukallimunā aydīhim watashhadu arjuluhum bimā kānū yaksibūn
verses.english: On that day we will seal their mouths; their hands and feet will bear witness to everything they had done.

1981.english: On that day, we will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to us, and their feet will testify about everything they had done.
1981.subtitle: The Video Tape
1981.footnote: God invented the video recorder in order to give us an idea how our hands and feet will testify on the day of judgment. See 42:21 and Appendix 10.

1989.english: On that day we will seal their mouths and their hands and feet will bear witness to everything they had done.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَطَمَسْنَا عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِهِمْ فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَٰطَ فَأَنَّىٰ يُبْصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون
verses.transliterated: walaw nashāu laṭamasnā ʿalā aʿyunihim fa-is'tabaqū l-ṣirāṭa fa-annā yub'ṣirūn
verses.english: If we will, we can veil their eyes and, consequently, when they seek the path, they will not see.

1981.english: Whenever we will, we cover up their eyes, so they miss the path by failing to see.

1989.english: If we will, we can veil their eyes and thus, when they seek the path, they will not see.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَمَسَخْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِهِمْ فَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ مُضِيًّا وَلَا يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون
verses.transliterated: walaw nashāu lamasakhnāhum ʿalā makānatihim famā is'taṭāʿū muḍiyyan walā yarjiʿūn
verses.english: If we will, we can freeze them in place; thus, they can neither move forward, nor go back.

1981.english: Whenever we will, we freeze them in the situation they choose; they can neither progress nor go back.

1989.english: If we will, we can freeze them in place; thus, they can neither move forward, nor go back.

verses.arabic: وَمَن نُّعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ أَفَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق ۖ أفلا يعقلون
verses.transliterated: waman nuʿammir'hu nunakkis'hu fī l-khalqi afalā yaʿqilūn
verses.english: Whomever we permit to live for a long time, we revert him to weakness. Do they not understand?

1981.english: Anyone we allow to survive long enough, we revert them to weakness. Do they not understand?

1989.english: Whomever we permit to live for a long time, we revert him to weakness. Do they not understand?

verses.arabic: وَمَا عَلَّمْنَٰهُ ٱلشِّعْرَ وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لَهُۥٓ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ وَقُرْءَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له ۚ إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين
verses.transliterated: wamā ʿallamnāhu l-shiʿ'ra wamā yanbaghī lahu in huwa illā dhik'run waqur'ānun mubīnu
verses.english: What we taught him (the messenger) was not poetry, nor is he (a poet). This is but a formidable proof, and a profound Quran.
verses.footnote: The word "Zikr" refers frequently to the Quran's great mathematical code, which is certainly not literary, nor poetry. Please check out 38:1,8; 15:6,9; 16:44; 21:2, 24; 26:5; & 36:11.

1981.english: We did not teach him (Muhammad) any poetry, nor should he. This is a profound message; a profound Quran.

1989.english: We did not teach him (the messenger) poetry, nor should he. This is but a reminder; a profound Quran.

verses.arabic: لِّيُنذِرَ مَن كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين
verses.transliterated: liyundhira man kāna ḥayyan wayaḥiqqa l-qawlu ʿalā l-kāfirīn
verses.english: To preach to those who are alive, and to expose the disbelievers.

1981.english: To warn those who are alive, and to condemn the disbelievers.

1989.english: To warn everyone alive, and to expose the disbelievers.

verses.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُم مِّمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَآ أَنْعَٰمًا فَهُمْ لَهَا مَٰلِكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون
verses.transliterated: awalam yaraw annā khalaqnā lahum mimmā ʿamilat aydīnā anʿāman fahum lahā mālikūn
verses.english: Have they not seen that we created for them, with our own hands, livestock that they own?

1981.english: Do they not realize that we created for them, with our hands, the livestock that they own?

1989.english: Have they not seen that we created for them, with our own hands, livestock that they own?

verses.arabic: وَذَلَّلْنَٰهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون
verses.transliterated: wadhallalnāhā lahum famin'hā rakūbuhum wamin'hā yakulūn
verses.english: And we subdued them for them; some they ride, and some they eat.

1981.english: We subdued the animals for them, so they ride some and eat some.

1989.english: And we subdued them for them; some of them they ride, and some they eat.

verses.arabic: وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا مَنَٰفِعُ وَمَشَارِبُ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب ۖ أفلا يشكرون
verses.transliterated: walahum fīhā manāfiʿu wamashāribu afalā yashkurūn
verses.english: They derive other benefits from them, as well as drinks. Would they not be appreciative?

1981.english: They derive various benefits therefrom, as well as drinks. Would they not be thankful?

1989.english: They derive other benefits from them, as well as drinks. Would they not be appreciative?

verses.arabic: وَٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ءَالِهَةً لَّعَلَّهُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون
verses.transliterated: wa-ittakhadhū min dūni l-lahi ālihatan laʿallahum yunṣarūn
verses.english: They set up beside GOD other gods, perhaps they can be of help to them!
verses.subtitle: Powerless Idols

1981.english: Yet, they set up idols besides God to be of help to them.
1981.subtitle: Your Idols Can Never Help You
1981.footnote: Muhammad, Jesus, Mary, the saints, and all the idols possess no power to benefit or harm anyone. See 6:50, 7:188, 10:49, 11:31, 60:4, 72:21 and Appendix 7.

1989.english: They set up besides GOD other gods, perhaps they help them!
1989.subtitle: Powerless Idols

verses.arabic: لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُمْ جُندٌ مُّحْضَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون
verses.transliterated: lā yastaṭīʿūna naṣrahum wahum lahum jundun muḥ'ḍarūn
verses.english: On the contrary, they cannot help them; they end up serving them as devoted soldiers.

1981.english: But they can never help; instead, they become subjugated soldiers of their idols.
1981.footnote: Muhammad, Jesus, Mary, the saints, and all the idols possess no power to benefit or harm anyone. See 6:50, 7:188, 10:49, 11:31, 60:4, 72:21 and Appendix 7.

1989.english: On the contrary, they cannot help them; they end up serving them as devoted soldiers.

verses.arabic: فَلَا يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلا يحزنك قولهم ۘ إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون
verses.transliterated: falā yaḥzunka qawluhum innā naʿlamu mā yusirrūna wamā yuʿ'linūn
verses.english: Therefore, do not be saddened by their utterances. We are fully aware of everything they conceal and everything they declare.

1981.english: Do not be saddened by their utterances. We are fully aware of everything they conceal and everything they declare.

1989.english: Therefore, do not be saddened by their utterances. We are fully aware of everything they conceal and everything they declare.

verses.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين
verses.transliterated: awalam yara l-insānu annā khalaqnāhu min nuṭ'fatin fa-idhā huwa khaṣīmun mubīnu
verses.english: Does the human being not see that we created him from a tiny drop, then he turns into an ardent enemy?

1981.english: Does the human being realize that we created him from a tiny drop, then he turns into a defiant opponent?

1989.english: Does the human being not see that we created him from a tiny drop, then he turns into a profound enemy'

verses.arabic: وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًا وَنَسِىَ خَلْقَهُۥ قَالَ مَن يُحْىِ ٱلْعِظَٰمَ وَهِىَ رَمِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه ۖ قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم
verses.transliterated: waḍaraba lanā mathalan wanasiya khalqahu qāla man yuḥ'yī l-ʿiẓāma wahiya ramīmu
verses.english: He raises a question to us—while forgetting his initial creation—"Who can resurrect the bones after they had rotted?"

1981.english: He asks us a question, forgetting his initial creation, and says, "Who can resurrect the bones after having decayed?"

1989.english: And he posed a question to us, while forgetting his own creation: “Who can resurrect the bones after they had rotted?”

verses.arabic: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة ۖ وهو بكل خلق عليم
verses.transliterated: qul yuḥ'yīhā alladhī ansha-ahā awwala marratin wahuwa bikulli khalqin ʿalīmu
verses.english: Say, "The One who initiated them in the first place will resurrect them. He is fully aware of every creation."

1981.english: Say, "Resurrecting them will be the One who initiated them the first time. Of every creation, He is fully aware."

1989.english: Say, “The One who initiated them in the first place will resurrect them. He is fully aware of every creation.”

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلْأَخْضَرِ نَارًا فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون
verses.transliterated: alladhī jaʿala lakum mina l-shajari l-akhḍari nāran fa-idhā antum min'hu tūqidūn
verses.english: He is the One who creates for you, from the green trees, fuel which you burn for light.

1981.english: He is the One who turns the green trees into fuel for you.

1989.english: He is the One who creates for you, from the green trees, fuel which you burn for light.

verses.arabic: أَوَلَيْسَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلْخَلَّٰقُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم ۚ بلى وهو الخلاق العليم
verses.transliterated: awalaysa alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa biqādirin ʿalā an yakhluqa mith'lahum balā wahuwa l-khalāqu l-ʿalīm
verses.english: Is not the One who created the heavens and the earth able to recreate the same? Yes indeed; He is the Creator, the Omniscient.

1981.english: Is it not possible for the One who created the heavens and the earth to create them again? Yes indeed, He is the creator, the omniscient.

1989.english: Is not the One who created the heavens and the earth able to recreate the same? Yes indeed; He is the Creator, the Omniscient.

verses.arabic: إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيْـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
verses.arabicClean: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون
verses.transliterated: innamā amruhu idhā arāda shayan an yaqūla lahu kun fayakūn
verses.english: All He needs to do to carry out any command is say to it, "Be," and it is.

1981.english: His only command to have anything done, is to say, "Be," and it is.

1989.english: All He needs to do to carry out any command is say to it, “Be,” and it is.

verses.arabic: فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون
verses.transliterated: fasub'ḥāna alladhī biyadihi malakūtu kulli shayin wa-ilayhi tur'jaʿūn
verses.english: Therefore, glory be to the One in whose hand is the sovereignty over all things, and to Him you will be returned.
verses.footnote: It is noteworthy that the gematrical value of "Rashad" (505), plus the gematrical value of "Khalifa" (725), plus the sura number (36), plus the number of verses (83), produces a total that is a multiple of 19 (505+725+36+83=1349=19x71). Also, Sura 36 is number 19 among the 29 initialed suras.

1981.english: Therefore, glorified be the One who possesses the kingship over all things, and to Him you ultimately return.

1989.english: Therefore, glory be to the One in whose hand is the kingship over all things, and to Him you will be returned. >

verses.arabic: وَٱلصَّٰٓفَّٰتِ صَفًّا
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والصافات صفا
verses.transliterated: wal-ṣāfāti ṣaffa
verses.english: The arrangers in columns.

1981.english: By the angels who will arrange the people in columns.

1989.english: By the arrangers in columns.

verses.arabic: فَٱلزَّٰجِرَٰتِ زَجْرًا
verses.arabicClean: فالزاجرات زجرا
verses.transliterated: fal-zājirāti zajra
verses.english: The blamers of those to be blamed.

1981.english: And gather them together.

1989.english: And the blamers of those to be blamed.

verses.arabic: فَٱلتَّٰلِيَٰتِ ذِكْرًا
verses.arabicClean: فالتاليات ذكرا
verses.transliterated: fal-tāliyāti dhik'ra
verses.english: The reciters of the messages.

1981.english: And those who recite the message.

1989.english: And the reciters of the messages.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ إِلَٰهَكُمْ لَوَٰحِدٌ
verses.arabicClean: إن إلهكم لواحد
verses.transliterated: inna ilāhakum lawāḥidu
verses.english: Your god is only one.

1981.english: Your God is one.

1989.english: Your god is only one.

verses.arabic: رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ
verses.arabicClean: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق
verses.transliterated: rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā warabbu l-mashāriq
verses.english: The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, and Lord of the easts.
verses.footnote: Every heavenly body rises on the planet earth, and sets. Every rise is called "east."

1981.english: The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, and Lord of the easts.

1989.english: The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, and Lord of the easts.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ
verses.arabicClean: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب
verses.transliterated: innā zayyannā l-samāa l-dun'yā bizīnatin l-kawākib
verses.english: We have adorned the lowest heaven with adorning planets.
verses.footnote: We live in the innermost and smallest universe. The jinns are confined to this universe.

1981.english: We have adorned the lowest heaven* with the shining planets.
1981.footnote: See Appendix 5. Our immediate universe, with all the countless billions of stars and planets, is the smallest and innermost of seven heavens.

1989.english: We have adorned the lowest heaven with beautiful stars.

verses.arabic: وَحِفْظًا مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَٰنٍ مَّارِدٍ
verses.arabicClean: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد
verses.transliterated: waḥif'ẓan min kulli shayṭānin māridi
verses.english: We guarded it from every evil devil.

1981.english: And sealed it against every rebellious devil.
1981.footnote: The outer limit of our heaven is not penetrable by anything except the angels.

1989.english: And guarded it from every evil devil.

verses.arabic: لَّا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلَإِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
verses.arabicClean: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب
verses.transliterated: lā yassammaʿūna ilā l-mala-i l-aʿlā wayuq'dhafūna min kulli jānibi
verses.english: They cannot spy on the High Society; they get bombarded from every side.

1981.english: Thus, they cannot spy on the high society; they get shot from every side.

1989.english: They cannot spy on the high society; they get shot from every side.

verses.arabic: دُحُورًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ وَاصِبٌ
verses.arabicClean: دحورا ۖ ولهم عذاب واصب
verses.transliterated: duḥūran walahum ʿadhābun wāṣibu
verses.english: They have been condemned; they have incurred an eternal retribution.

1981.english: They will be defeated, then suffer eternal retribution.

1989.english: They are doomed; they have incurred an eternal retribution.

verses.arabic: إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ ٱلْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُۥ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ
verses.arabicClean: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب
verses.transliterated: illā man khaṭifa l-khaṭfata fa-atbaʿahu shihābun thāqibu
verses.english: If any of them ventures to charge the outer limits, he gets struck with a fierce projectile.

1981.english: Any of them that charges into the outer limit is followed by a piercing projectile.

1989.english: If any of them ventures to charge the outer limits, he gets struck with a fierce projectile.

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُم مِّن طِينٍ لَّازِبٍۭ
verses.arabicClean: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا ۚ إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب
verses.transliterated: fa-is'taftihim ahum ashaddu khalqan am man khalaqnā innā khalaqnāhum min ṭīnin lāzibi
verses.english: Ask them, "Are they more difficult to create, or the other creations?" We created them from wet mud.

1981.english: Ask the people then; are they more powerful than some of our creations? We created them from soft clay.

1989.english: Ask them, “Are they more difficult to create, or our other creations?” We created them from wet mud.

verses.arabic: بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: بل عجبت ويسخرون
verses.transliterated: bal ʿajib'ta wayaskharūn
verses.english: While you are awed, they mock.

1981.english: While you marvel, they ridicule.

1989.english: While you are awed, they mock.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ لَا يَذْكُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā dhukkirū lā yadhkurūn
verses.english: When reminded, they take no heed.

1981.english: When they are reminded, they take no heed.

1989.english: When reminded, they take no heed.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْا۟ ءَايَةً يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā ra-aw āyatan yastaskhirūn
verses.english: When they see proof, they ridicule it.

1981.english: Whenever they see a miracle, they resort to mockery.

1989.english: When they see proof, they ridicule it.

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين
verses.transliterated: waqālū in hādhā illā siḥ'run mubīnu
verses.english: They say, "This is obviously magic!

1981.english: They say, "This is only magic.

1989.english: They say, “This is obviously magic!

verses.arabic: أَءِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا وَعِظَٰمًا أَءِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون
verses.transliterated: a-idhā mit'nā wakunnā turāban waʿiẓāman a-innā lamabʿūthūn
verses.english: "After we die and become dust and bones, do we get resurrected?

1981.english: "After we die and turn to dust and bones, are we resurrected?

1989.english: “After we die and become dust and bones, do we get resurrected?

verses.arabic: أَوَءَابَآؤُنَا ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أوآباؤنا الأولون
verses.transliterated: awaābāunā l-awalūn
verses.english: "Even our ancient ancestors?"

1981.english: "Even our old ancestors?"

1989.english: “Even our ancient ancestors?”

verses.arabic: قُلْ نَعَمْ وَأَنتُمْ دَٰخِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قل نعم وأنتم داخرون
verses.transliterated: qul naʿam wa-antum dākhirūn
verses.english: Say, "Yes, you will be forcibly summoned."

1981.english: Say, "Yes, you will be forced."

1989.english: Say, “Yes, you will be forced.”

verses.arabic: فَإِنَّمَا هِىَ زَجْرَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ فَإِذَا هُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم ينظرون
verses.transliterated: fa-innamā hiya zajratun wāḥidatun fa-idhā hum yanẓurūn
verses.english: All it takes is one nudge, whereupon they (stand up) looking.

1981.english: It will be one nudge, whereupon they get up, looking.

1989.english: All it takes is one nudge, whereupon they (stand up) looking.

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا هَٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا يا ويلنا هذا يوم الدين
verses.transliterated: waqālū yāwaylanā hādhā yawmu l-dīn
verses.english: They will say, "Woe to us; this is the Day of Judgment."

1981.english: They will say, "Woe to us; this is the day of judgment."

1989.english: They will say, “Woe to us; this is the Day of Judgment.”

verses.arabic: هَٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تُكَذِّبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: هذا يوم الفصل الذي كنتم به تكذبون
verses.transliterated: hādhā yawmu l-faṣli alladhī kuntum bihi tukadhibūn
verses.english: This is the day of decision that you used to disbelieve in.

1981.english: This is the day of decision, that you used to deny.

1989.english: This is the day of decision that you used to disbelieve in.

verses.arabic: ٱحْشُرُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ وَأَزْوَٰجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْبُدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم وما كانوا يعبدون
verses.transliterated: uḥ'shurū alladhīna ẓalamū wa-azwājahum wamā kānū yaʿbudūn
verses.english: Summon the transgressors, and their spouses, and the idols they worshiped

1981.english: Gather the wicked, and their spouses, and the idols.

1989.english: Summon the transgressors, and their spouses, and the idols they worshiped—

verses.arabic: مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: من دون الله فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم
verses.transliterated: min dūni l-lahi fa-ih'dūhum ilā ṣirāṭi l-jaḥīm
verses.english: beside GOD, and guide them to the path of Hell.

1981.english: That they set up besides God. Lead them to the path of hell.

1989.english: besides GOD; guide them to the path of Hell.

verses.arabic: وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُم مَّسْـُٔولُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقفوهم ۖ إنهم مسئولون
verses.transliterated: waqifūhum innahum masūlūn
verses.english: Stop them, and ask them:

1981.english: Stop them, and ask,

1989.english: Stop them, and ask them:

verses.arabic: مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَنَاصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ما لكم لا تناصرون
verses.transliterated: mā lakum lā tanāṣarūn
verses.english: "Why do you not help one another?"

1981.english: Why do you not help one another?

1989.english: “Why do you not help one another?”

1981.footnote: Immediately after resurrection and the manifested physical appearance of the almighty God and the angels, all people will be automatically stratified into four ranks, the highest being the closest to God. These four initial ranks are the high heaven, the lower heaven, the purgatory, and hell. Eventually, God's mercy will merge the purgatory into the lower heaven. The three final groups will be separated by barriers. The inhabitants of any rank can only move downward to visit lower rank(s), but no one will be able to move upward beyond his rank. verses.english: This is what every worker should work for.

1981.english: This is what everyone should strive for.

1989.english: This is what every worker should work for.

verses.arabic: أَذَٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُّزُلًا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
verses.arabicClean: أذلك خير نزلا أم شجرة الزقوم
verses.transliterated: adhālika khayrun nuzulan am shajaratu l-zaqūm
verses.english: Is this a better destiny, or the tree of bitterness?

1981.english: Is this better, or the tree of bitterness?

1989.english: Is this a better destiny, or the tree of bitterness?

verses.arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰهَا فِتْنَةً لِّلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنا جعلناها فتنة للظالمين
verses.transliterated: innā jaʿalnāhā fit'natan lilẓẓālimīn
verses.english: We have rendered it a punishment for the transgressors.

1981.english: We have made it a retribution for the wicked.

1989.english: We have rendered it a test for the transgressors.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِىٓ أَصْلِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم
verses.transliterated: innahā shajaratun takhruju fī aṣli l-jaḥīm
verses.english: It is a tree that grows in the heart of Hell.

1981.english: It is a tree that grows at the bottom of hell.

1989.english: It is a tree that grows in the heart of Hell.

verses.arabic: طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُۥ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ
verses.arabicClean: طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين
verses.transliterated: ṭalʿuhā ka-annahu ruūsu l-shayāṭīn
verses.english: Its flowers look like the devils' heads.

1981.english: Its fruits like the heads of devils.

1989.english: Its flowers are like the devils’ heads.

verses.arabic: فَإِنَّهُمْ لَءَاكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِـُٔونَ مِنْهَا ٱلْبُطُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون
verses.transliterated: fa-innahum laākilūna min'hā famāliūna min'hā l-buṭūn
verses.english: They will eat from it until their bellies are filled up.

1981.english: They eat therefrom until their bellies are full.

1989.english: They will eat from it until their bellies are full.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْبًا مِّنْ حَمِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم
verses.transliterated: thumma inna lahum ʿalayhā lashawban min ḥamīmi
verses.english: Then they will top it with a hellish drink.

1981.english: Then they will add a drink of lava.

1989.english: Then top it with a hellish drink.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لَإِلَى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم
verses.transliterated: thumma inna marjiʿahum la-ilā l-jaḥīm
verses.english: Then they will return to Hell.

1981.english: Then they return to hell.

1989.english: Then they return to Hell.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْا۟ ءَابَآءَهُمْ ضَآلِّينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنهم ألفوا آباءهم ضالين
verses.transliterated: innahum alfaw ābāahum ḍāllīn
verses.english: They found their parents astray.
verses.subtitle: They Followed Their Parents Blindly

1981.english: They had found their parents astray.
1981.subtitle: Do Not Blindly Follow Your Parents

1989.english: They found their parents astray.
1989.subtitle: They Followed Their Parents Blindly

verses.arabic: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فهم على آثارهم يهرعون
verses.transliterated: fahum ʿalā āthārihim yuh'raʿūn
verses.english: And they blindly followed in their footsteps.

1981.english: And readily followed their footsteps.

1989.english: And blindly followed their footsteps.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ أَكْثَرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد ضل قبلهم أكثر الأولين
verses.transliterated: walaqad ḍalla qablahum aktharu l-awalīn
verses.english: Most of the previous generations have strayed in the same manner.

1981.english: The majority of previous generations were similarly astray.

1989.english: Most of the previous generations also strayed in the same manner.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا فِيهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أرسلنا فيهم منذرين
verses.transliterated: walaqad arsalnā fīhim mundhirīn
verses.english: We have sent to them warners.

1981.english: We had sent to them warners.

1989.english: We have sent to them warners.

verses.arabic: فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين
verses.transliterated: fa-unẓur kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-mundharīn
verses.english: Note the consequences for those who have been warned.

1981.english: Note the final end for those who were warned.

1989.english: Note the consequences for those who have been warned.

verses.arabic: إِلَّا عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إلا عباد الله المخلصين
verses.transliterated: illā ʿibāda l-lahi l-mukh'laṣīn
verses.english: Only GOD's servants who are absolutely devoted to Him alone (are saved).

1981.english: Only the devoted servants of God are saved.

1989.english: Only GOD’s servants who are absolutely devoted to Him alone (are saved).

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ نَادَىٰنَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد نادانا نوح فلنعم المجيبون
verses.transliterated: walaqad nādānā nūḥun falaniʿ'ma l-mujībūn
verses.english: Thus, Noah called upon us, and we were the best responders.
verses.subtitle: Noah

1981.english: Noah implored us, and we are the best responders.
1981.subtitle: Noah and Abraham

1989.english: Thus, Noah called upon us, and we were the best responders.
1989.subtitle: Noah

verses.arabic: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: ونجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم
verses.transliterated: wanajjaynāhu wa-ahlahu mina l-karbi l-ʿaẓīm
verses.english: We saved him and his family from the great disaster.

1981.english: We saved him and his family from the great disaster.

1989.english: We saved him and his family from the great disaster.

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلنا ذريته هم الباقين
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalnā dhurriyyatahu humu l-bāqīn
verses.english: We made his companions the survivors.

1981.english: We made him and his family the survivors.

1989.english: We made his progeny the survivors.

verses.arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين
verses.transliterated: wataraknā ʿalayhi fī l-ākhirīn
verses.english: And we preserved his history for subsequent generations.

1981.english: And preserved his history for the later generations.

1989.english: And we preserved his history for subsequent generations.

verses.arabic: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: سلام على نوح في العالمين
verses.transliterated: salāmun ʿalā nūḥin fī l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: Peace be upon Noah among the peoples.

1981.english: Peace be upon Noah, throughout history.

1989.english: Peace be upon Noah throughout history.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين
verses.transliterated: innā kadhālika najzī l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: We thus reward the righteous.

1981.english: We thus reward the pious.

1989.english: We thus reward the pious.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين
verses.transliterated: innahu min ʿibādinā l-mu'minīn
verses.english: He is one of our believing servants.

1981.english: He was one of our believing servants.

1989.english: He is one of our believing servants.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين
verses.transliterated: thumma aghraqnā l-ākharīn
verses.english: We drowned all the others.

1981.english: We drowned the others.

1989.english: We drowned all the others.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ لَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن من شيعته لإبراهيم
verses.transliterated: wa-inna min shīʿatihi la-ib'rāhīm
verses.english: Among his followers was Abraham.
verses.subtitle: Abraham

1981.english: Similar to him was Abraham.

1989.english: Among his followers was Abraham.
1989.subtitle: Abraham

verses.arabic: إِذْ جَآءَ رَبَّهُۥ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم
verses.transliterated: idh jāa rabbahu biqalbin salīmi
verses.english: He came to his Lord wholeheartedly.

1981.english: He came to his Lord wholeheartedly.

1989.english: He came to his Lord wholeheartedly.

verses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ماذا تعبدون
verses.transliterated: idh qāla li-abīhi waqawmihi mādhā taʿbudūn
verses.english: He said to his father and his people, "What are you worshiping?

1981.english: He said to his father and his people, "What is this you worship?

1989.english: He said to his father and his people “What are you worshiping?

verses.arabic: أَئِفْكًا ءَالِهَةً دُونَ ٱللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أئفكا آلهة دون الله تريدون
verses.transliterated: a-if'kan ālihatan dūna l-lahi turīdūn
verses.english: "Is it these fabricated gods, instead of GOD, that you want?

1981.english: "Is it false gods, besides God, that you want?

1989.english: “Is it these fabricated gods besides GOD that you want?

verses.arabic: فَمَا ظَنُّكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فما ظنكم برب العالمين
verses.transliterated: famā ẓannukum birabbi l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: "What do you think of the Lord of the universe?"

1981.english: "Do you not think of the Lord of the universe?"

1989.english: “What do you think of the Lord of the universe?”

verses.arabic: فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةً فِى ٱلنُّجُومِ
verses.arabicClean: فنظر نظرة في النجوم
verses.transliterated: fanaẓara naẓratan fī l-nujūm
verses.english: He looked carefully at the stars.

1981.english: He looked at the stars.

1989.english: He looked carefully at the stars.

verses.arabic: فَقَالَ إِنِّى سَقِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: فقال إني سقيم
verses.transliterated: faqāla innī saqīmu
verses.english: Then he gave up and said, "I am tired of this!"

1981.english: Then said, "I give up."

1989.english: He gave up: “I am tired of this!”

verses.arabic: فَتَوَلَّوْا۟ عَنْهُ مُدْبِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فتولوا عنه مدبرين
verses.transliterated: fatawallaw ʿanhu mud'birīn
verses.english: They turned away from him.

1981.english: They ignored him.

1989.english: But they turned away from him.

verses.arabic: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِهِمْ فَقَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فراغ إلى آلهتهم فقال ألا تأكلون
verses.transliterated: farāgha ilā ālihatihim faqāla alā takulūn
verses.english: He then turned on their idols, saying, "Would you like to eat?

1981.english: He went to their idols saying, "Would you like to eat?

1989.english: He turned on their idols, saying, “Would you like to eat?

verses.arabic: مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَنطِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ما لكم لا تنطقون
verses.transliterated: mā lakum lā tanṭiqūn
verses.english: "Why do you not speak?"

1981.english: "Why don't you answer me?"

1989.english: “Why do you not speak?”

verses.arabic: فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًۢا بِٱلْيَمِينِ
verses.arabicClean: فراغ عليهم ضربا باليمين
verses.transliterated: farāgha ʿalayhim ḍarban bil-yamīn
verses.english: He then destroyed them.

1981.english: He then destroyed them.

1989.english: He then destroyed them completely

verses.arabic: فَأَقْبَلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ
verses.arabicClean: فأقبلوا إليه يزفون
verses.transliterated: fa-aqbalū ilayhi yaziffūn
verses.english: They went to him in a great rage.

1981.english: They came to him furious.

1989.english: They went to him in great anger.

verses.arabic: قَالَ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال أتعبدون ما تنحتون
verses.transliterated: qāla ataʿbudūna mā tanḥitūn
verses.english: He said, "How can you worship what you carve?

1981.english: He said, "How could you worship what you carve?

1989.english: He said, “How can you worship what you carve?

verses.arabic: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والله خلقكم وما تعملون
verses.transliterated: wal-lahu khalaqakum wamā taʿmalūn
verses.english: "When GOD has created you, and everything you make!"

1981.english: "While God created you and everything you make."

1989.english: “When GOD has created you, and everything you make!”

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ ٱبْنُوا۟ لَهُۥ بُنْيَٰنًا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِى ٱلْجَحِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا ابنوا له بنيانا فألقوه في الجحيم
verses.transliterated: qālū ib'nū lahu bun'yānan fa-alqūhu fī l-jaḥīm
verses.english: They said, "Let us build a great fire, and throw him into it."

1981.english: They said, "Build a great fire for him."

1989.english: They said, “Let us build a profound fire, and throw him into it.”

verses.arabic: فَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأسفلين
verses.transliterated: fa-arādū bihi kaydan fajaʿalnāhumu l-asfalīn
verses.english: They schemed against him, but we made them the losers.

1981.english: They wanted to hurt him; but we made them the losers.

1989.english: They schemed against him, but we made them the losers.

verses.arabic: وَقَالَ إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
verses.arabicClean: وقال إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين
verses.transliterated: waqāla innī dhāhibun ilā rabbī sayahdīn
verses.english: He said, "I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."

1981.english: He said, "I will turn to my Lord; He will guide me.

1989.english: He said, “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.”

verses.arabic: رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: رب هب لي من الصالحين
verses.transliterated: rabbi hab lī mina l-ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: "My Lord, grant me righteous children."

1981.english: "My Lord, grant me righteous children."

1989.english: “My Lord, grant me righteous children.”

verses.arabic: فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: فبشرناه بغلام حليم
verses.transliterated: fabasharnāhu bighulāmin ḥalīmi
verses.english: We gave him good news of a good child.

1981.english: We promised him a clement son.
1981.footnote: This is Ishmael. According to the Bible (Genesis 16:16, 21:1-5, and 22:1-3), Ishmael was Abraham's only son for fourteen years. Isaac comes later in 37:112.

1989.english: We gave him good news of a clement child.

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما بلغ معه السعي قال يا بني إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك فانظر ماذا ترى ۚ قال يا أبت افعل ما تؤمر ۖ ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين
verses.transliterated: falammā balagha maʿahu l-saʿya qāla yābunayya innī arā fī l-manāmi annī adhbaḥuka fa-unẓur mādhā tarā qāla yāabati if'ʿal mā tu'maru satajidunī in shāa l-lahu mina l-ṣābirīn
verses.english: When he grew enough to work with him, he said, "My son, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you. What do you think?" He said, "O my father, do what you are commanded to do. You will find me, GOD willing, patient."
verses.subtitle: Satanic Dream
verses.footnote: The Most Merciful never advocates evil (7:28). As with Job, Satan claimed that Abraham loved his son too much, and was permitted to put Abraham to that severe test.

1981.english: When he grew up and started to accompany him, he said, "My son, I see in a vision that I must sacrifice you. What do you think?" He said, "Father, do whatever is enjoined upon you. You will find me, God willing, patient."

1989.english: When he grew enough to work with him, he said, “My son, I see in a dream that I must sacrifice you. What do you think?” He said, “O my father, do what you are commanded to do. You will find me, GOD willing, patient.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: فلما أسلما وتله للجبين
verses.transliterated: falammā aslamā watallahu lil'jabīn
verses.english: They both submitted, and he put his forehead down (to sacrifice him).

1981.english: When they both submitted, and he turned him down on his forehead,

1989.english: They both submitted, and he put his forehead down (to sacrifice him).

verses.arabic: وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم
verses.transliterated: wanādaynāhu an yāib'rāhīm
verses.english: We called him: "O Abraham.
verses.subtitle: God Intervenes to Save Abraham and Ismail

1981.english: We called him, "O Abraham!

1989.english: We called him, “O Abraham.

verses.arabic: قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قد صدقت الرؤيا ۚ إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين
verses.transliterated: qad ṣaddaqta l-ru'yā innā kadhālika najzī l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: "You have believed the dream." We thus reward the righteous.

1981.english: "You have fulfilled the vision." We thus reward the pious.

1989.english: “You have believed your own dream.” We thus reward the pious.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ
verses.arabicClean: إن هذا لهو البلاء المبين
verses.transliterated: inna hādhā lahuwa l-balāu l-mubīn
verses.english: That was an exacting test indeed.

1981.english: It was indeed an exacting test.

1989.english: That was an exacting trial.

verses.arabic: وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: وفديناه بذبح عظيم
verses.transliterated: wafadaynāhu bidhib'ḥin ʿaẓīmi
verses.english: We ransomed (Ismail) by substituting an animal sacrifice.

1981.english: We ransomed him with a great offering.

1989.english: We ransomed (Ismail) by substituting an animal sacrifice.

verses.arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين
verses.transliterated: wataraknā ʿalayhi fī l-ākhirīn
verses.english: And we preserved his history for subsequent generations.

1981.english: And preserved his history for the following generations.

1989.english: And we preserved his history for subsequent generations.

verses.arabic: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
verses.arabicClean: سلام على إبراهيم
verses.transliterated: salāmun ʿalā ib'rāhīm
verses.english: Peace be upon Abraham.

1981.english: Peace be upon Abraham.

1989.english: Peace be upon Abraham.

verses.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: كذلك نجزي المحسنين
verses.transliterated: kadhālika najzī l-muḥ'sinīn
verses.english: We thus reward the righteous.

1981.english: We thus reward the pious.

1989.english: We thus reward the righteous.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين
verses.transliterated: innahu min ʿibādinā l-mu'minīn
verses.english: He is one of our believing servants.

1981.english: He was one of our believing servants.

1989.english: He is one of our believing servants.

verses.arabic: وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وبشرناه بإسحاق نبيا من الصالحين
verses.transliterated: wabasharnāhu bi-is'ḥāqa nabiyyan mina l-ṣāliḥīn
verses.english: Then we gave him the good news about the birth of Isaac, to be one of the righteous prophets.
verses.subtitle: Birth of Isaac

1981.english: We gave him the good news of Isaac, to be a righteous prophet.

1989.english: Then we gave him the good news about the birth of Isaac, to be one of the righteous prophets.

verses.arabic: وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌ وَظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: وباركنا عليه وعلى إسحاق ۚ ومن ذريتهما محسن وظالم لنفسه مبين
verses.transliterated: wabāraknā ʿalayhi waʿalā is'ḥāqa wamin dhurriyyatihimā muḥ'sinun waẓālimun linafsihi mubīnu
verses.english: We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants, some are righteous, and some are wicked transgressors.

1981.english: We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants some are pious and some are wicked.

1989.english: We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants, some are righteous, and some are transgressors.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد مننا على موسى وهارون
verses.transliterated: walaqad manannā ʿalā mūsā wahārūn
verses.english: We also blessed Moses and Aaron.
verses.subtitle: Moses and Aaron

1981.english: We also blessed Moses and Aaron.
1981.subtitle: Moses and Aaron

1989.english: We blessed Moses and Aaron.
1989.subtitle: Moses and Aaron

verses.arabic: وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُمَا وَقَوْمَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: ونجيناهما وقومهما من الكرب العظيم
verses.transliterated: wanajjaynāhumā waqawmahumā mina l-karbi l-ʿaẓīm
verses.english: We delivered them and their people from the great disaster.

1981.english: We delivered them and their people from the great disaster.
