verses.transliterated: in yasha yus'kini l-rīḥa fayaẓlalna rawākida ʿalā ẓahrihi inna fī dhālika laāyātin likulli ṣabbārin shakūri
verses.english: If He willed, He could have stilled the winds, leaving them motionless on top of the water. These are proofs for those who are steadfast, appreciative.

1981.english: If He wills, He can halt the winds, leaving them standing still. These are signs for everyone who is steadfast, appreciative.

1989.english: If He willed, He could have stilled the winds, leaving them motionless on top of the water. These are signs for those who are steadfast, appreciative.

verses.arabic: أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِمَا كَسَبُوا۟ وَيَعْفُ عَن كَثِيرٍ
verses.arabicClean: أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا ويعف عن كثير
verses.transliterated: aw yūbiq'hunna bimā kasabū wayaʿfu ʿan kathīri
verses.english: He can annihilate them, as a consequence of their own works. Instead, He overlooks many (of their sins).

1981.english: Or, He may cause them to drown as a consequence of their deeds; but He overlooks much.

1989.english: Or He could have annihilated them as a consequence of their own works. Instead, He overlooks many (of their sins).

verses.arabic: وَيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِىٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا مَا لَهُم مِّن مَّحِيصٍ
verses.arabicClean: ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من محيص
verses.transliterated: wayaʿlama alladhīna yujādilūna fī āyātinā mā lahum min maḥīṣi
verses.english: Those who argue against our proofs will find out that they have no basis.

1981.english: Those who dispute our revelations will find out that they have no basis.

1989.english: Those who argue against our signs should know that they have no basis.

verses.arabic: فَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَىْءٍ فَمَتَٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا ۖ وما عند الله خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون
verses.transliterated: famā ūtītum min shayin famatāʿu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wamā ʿinda l-lahi khayrun wa-abqā lilladhīna āmanū waʿalā rabbihim yatawakkalūn
verses.english: Whatever you are given is no more than temporary material of this life. What GOD possesses is far better and everlasting, for those who believe and trust in their Lord.

1981.english: Whatever you possess is the temporary material of this life. What God possesses is far better and everlasting, for those who believe and trust in their Lord.

1989.english: Whatever you are given is no more than temporary material of this world What GOD reserves is far better anc everlasting, for those who believe and trust in their Lord.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُوا۟ هُمْ يَغْفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna yajtanibūna kabāira l-ith'mi wal-fawāḥisha wa-idhā mā ghaḍibū hum yaghfirūn
verses.english: They avoid gross sins and vice, and when angered they forgive.
verses.subtitle: Traits of the Believers

1981.english: And they avoid gross evil and sins, and whenever provoked, they forgive.

1989.english: They avoid gross sins and vice, and when angered they forgive.
1989.subtitle: Traits of the Believers

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُوا۟ لِرَبِّهِمْ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَمْرُهُمْ شُورَىٰ بَيْنَهُمْ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذين استجابوا لربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna is'tajābū lirabbihim wa-aqāmū l-ṣalata wa-amruhum shūrā baynahum wamimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūn
verses.english: They respond to their Lord by observing the Contact Prayers (Salat). Their affairs are decided after due consultation among themselves, and from our provisions to them they give (to charity).

1981.english: They respond to their Lord, and observe the **salat** prayers. Their affairs are decided by consensus among them, and from our provisions to them they donate.

1989.english: And they respond to their Lord by observing the contact prayers (Salat), and by deciding their affairs on the basis of consultation among themselves, and from our provisions to them they give (to charity).

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْبَغْىُ هُمْ يَنتَصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna idhā aṣābahumu l-baghyu hum yantaṣirūn
verses.english: When gross injustice befalls them, they stand up for their rights.

1981.english: When injustice befalls them, they defend themselves until victory.

1989.english: When injustice befalls them, they stand up for their rights.

verses.arabic: وَجَزَٰٓؤُا۟ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِّثْلُهَا فَمَنْ عَفَا وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَجْرُهُۥ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها ۖ فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله ۚ إنه لا يحب الظالمين
verses.transliterated: wajazāu sayyi-atin sayyi-atun mith'luhā faman ʿafā wa-aṣlaḥa fa-ajruhu ʿalā l-lahi innahu lā yuḥibbu l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: Although the just requital for an injustice is an equivalent retribution, those who pardon and maintain righteousness are rewarded by GOD. He does not love the unjust.

1981.english: They counter aggression with an equivalent response. However, those who pardon and conciliate receive a better reward from God; God is never unjust.

1989.english: Although the requital for an evil work is an equivalent retribution, those who pardon and maintain righteousness are rewarded by GOD. He does not love the unjust.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَنِ ٱنتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِۦ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مَا عَلَيْهِم مِّن سَبِيلٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولمن انتصر بعد ظلمه فأولئك ما عليهم من سبيل
verses.transliterated: walamani intaṣara baʿda ẓul'mihi fa-ulāika mā ʿalayhim min sabīli
verses.english: Certainly, those who stand up for their rights, when injustice befalls them, are not committing any error.

1981.english: If one avenges an injustice, he shall not be blamed.

1989.english: Certainly, those who stand up for their rights, when injustice befalls them, are not committing any error.

verses.arabic: إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ وَيَبْغُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق ۚ أولئك لهم عذاب أليم
verses.transliterated: innamā l-sabīlu ʿalā alladhīna yaẓlimūna l-nāsa wayabghūna fī l-arḍi bighayri l-ḥaqi ulāika lahum ʿadhābun alīmu
verses.english: The wrong ones are those who treat the people unjustly, and resort to aggression without provocation. These have incurred a painful retribution.

1981.english: To be blamed are those who inflict injustice upon the people and resort to aggression without provocation. These have deserved painful retribution.

1989.english: Committing errors are those who treat the people unjustly, and resort to aggression without provocation. These have incurred a painful retribution.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ
verses.arabicClean: ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور
verses.transliterated: walaman ṣabara waghafara inna dhālika lamin ʿazmi l-umūr
verses.english: Resorting to patience and forgiveness reflects a true strength of character.

1981.english: If one resorts to patience and forgiveness, this reflects true strength.

1989.english: However, maintaining patience and forgiveness reflects a strength of character.

verses.arabic: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن وَلِىٍّ مِّنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَتَرَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ يَقُولُونَ هَلْ إِلَىٰ مَرَدٍّ مِّن سَبِيلٍ
verses.arabicClean: ومن يضلل الله فما له من ولي من بعده ۗ وترى الظالمين لما رأوا العذاب يقولون هل إلى مرد من سبيل
verses.transliterated: waman yuḍ'lili l-lahu famā lahu min waliyyin min baʿdihi watarā l-ẓālimīna lammā ra-awū l-ʿadhāba yaqūlūna hal ilā maraddin min sabīli
verses.english: Whomever GOD sends astray will never find any other lord, and you will see such transgressors, when they see the retribution, saying, "Can we get another chance?"

1981.english: Whomever God misguides will find no protector, and you will see them, as they face the retribution saying, "Can we get another chance?"

1989.english: Whomever GOD sends astray will never find another protector, and you will see such transgressors, when they see the retribution, saying, “Can we get another chance?”

verses.arabic: وَتَرَىٰهُمْ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا خَٰشِعِينَ مِنَ ٱلذُّلِّ يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِىٍّ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ أَلَآ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِى عَذَابٍ مُّقِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: وتراهم يعرضون عليها خاشعين من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي ۗ وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ۗ ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم
verses.transliterated: watarāhum yuʿ'raḍūna ʿalayhā khāshiʿīna mina l-dhuli yanẓurūna min ṭarfin khafiyyin waqāla alladhīna āmanū inna l-khāsirīna alladhīna khasirū anfusahum wa-ahlīhim yawma l-qiyāmati alā inna l-ẓālimīna fī ʿadhābin muqīmi
verses.english: You will see them facing it, humiliated and debased, and looking, yet trying to avoid looking. Those who believed will proclaim: "The real losers are those who lost their souls and their families on the Day of Resurrection. The transgressors have deserved an everlasting retribution."

1981.english: You will see them facing it humiliated and debased; looking and trying to evade it. Those who believed will say, "The real losers are those who lost their souls and their families on the day of resurrection. Indeed, the wicked have deserved eternal retribution."

1989.english: You will see them facing it, humiliated and debased, and looking but trying to avoid looking. Those who believed will proclaim: “The real losers are those who lost their souls and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Certainly, the transgressors have incurred an eternal retribution.”

verses.arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لَهُم مِّنْ أَوْلِيَآءَ يَنصُرُونَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن سَبِيلٍ
verses.arabicClean: وما كان لهم من أولياء ينصرونهم من دون الله ۗ ومن يضلل الله فما له من سبيل
verses.transliterated: wamā kāna lahum min awliyāa yanṣurūnahum min dūni l-lahi waman yuḍ'lili l-lahu famā lahu min sabīli
verses.english: There will be no allies to help them against GOD. Whomever GOD sends astray can never be guided.

1981.english: They will have no allies to support them against God. Whomever God misguides will find no path.

1989.english: They will find no allies to help them against GOD. Whomever GOD sends astray can never be guided.

verses.arabic: ٱسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِرَبِّكُم مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِىَ يَوْمٌ لَّا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَكُم مِّن مَّلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّكِيرٍ
verses.arabicClean: استجيبوا لربكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله ۚ ما لكم من ملجإ يومئذ وما لكم من نكير
verses.transliterated: is'tajībū lirabbikum min qabli an yatiya yawmun lā maradda lahu mina l-lahi mā lakum min malja-in yawma-idhin wamā lakum min nakīri
verses.english: You shall respond to your Lord before a day comes which is decreed inevitable by GOD. There will be no refuge for you on that day, nor an advocate.

1981.english: You shall respond to your Lord, before a day comes which is inevitable. You will have no refuge on that day, nor could you deny anything.

1989.english: You shall respond to your Lord before a day comes which is made inevitable by GOD. There will be no refuge for you on that day, nor an advocate.

verses.arabic: فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا۟ فَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا إِنْ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا ٱلْبَلَٰغُ وَإِنَّآ إِذَآ أَذَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً فَرِحَ بِهَا وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَإِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ كَفُورٌ
verses.arabicClean: فإن أعرضوا فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا ۖ إن عليك إلا البلاغ ۗ وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها ۖ وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور
verses.transliterated: fa-in aʿraḍū famā arsalnāka ʿalayhim ḥafīẓan in ʿalayka illā l-balāghu wa-innā idhā adhaqnā l-insāna minnā raḥmatan fariḥa bihā wa-in tuṣib'hum sayyi-atun bimā qaddamat aydīhim fa-inna l-insāna kafūru
verses.english: If they turn away, we did not send you as their guardian. Your sole mission is delivering the message. When we shower the human beings with mercy, they become proud, and when adversity afflicts them, as a consequence of their own deeds, the human beings turn into disbelievers.
verses.subtitle: Sole Mission of the Messenger

1981.english: If they turn away, we have not sent you as their guardian. Your sole mission is to deliver this message. Whenever we endow the humans with mercy from us, they turn joyful, but when adversity befalls them, as a consequence of their own deeds, they turn unappreciative.
1981.subtitle: Sole Function Of The Messenger

1989.english: If they turn away, we did not send you as their guardian. Your sole mission is delivering the message. When we shower the human being with mercy, he becomes proud, and when adversity afflicts him, as a consequence of his own deeds, the human being turns unappreciative.

verses.arabic: لِّلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَٰثًا وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ
verses.arabicClean: لله ملك السماوات والأرض ۚ يخلق ما يشاء ۚ يهب لمن يشاء إناثا ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور
verses.transliterated: lillahi mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi yakhluqu mā yashāu yahabu liman yashāu ināthan wayahabu liman yashāu l-dhukūr
verses.english: To GOD belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills, granting daughters to whomever He wills, and granting sons to whomever He wills.

1981.english: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills. He grants whomever He wills daughters and grants whomever He wills sons.

1989.english: To GOD belongs the kingship of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills, granting daughters to whomever He wills, and granting sons to whomever He wills.

verses.arabic: أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَانًا وَإِنَٰثًا وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيمًا إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ
verses.arabicClean: أو يزوجهم ذكرانا وإناثا ۖ ويجعل من يشاء عقيما ۚ إنه عليم قدير
verses.transliterated: aw yuzawwijuhum dhuk'rānan wa-ināthan wayajʿalu man yashāu ʿaqīman innahu ʿalīmun qadīru
verses.english: Or, He may have the males and the females marry each other, then render whomever He wills sterile. He is Omniscient, Omnipotent.

1981.english: He may have the males and the females get married, yet keep them sterile. He is omniscient, omnipotent.

1989.english: Or, He may have the males and the females marry each other, then render whomever He wills sterile. He is Omniscient, Omnipotent.

verses.arabic: وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْيًا أَوْ مِن وَرَآئِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِىَ بِإِذْنِهِۦ مَا يَشَآءُ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِىٌّ حَكِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء ۚ إنه علي حكيم
verses.transliterated: wamā kāna libasharin an yukallimahu l-lahu illā waḥyan aw min warāi ḥijābin aw yur'sila rasūlan fayūḥiya bi-idh'nihi mā yashāu innahu ʿaliyyun ḥakīmu
verses.english: No human being can communicate with GOD except through inspiration, or from behind a barrier, or by sending a messenger through whom He reveals what He wills. He is the Most High, Most Wise.
verses.subtitle: How God Communicates With Us

1981.english: It is not possible for a human to communicate with God except through inspiration, or behind a barrier, or through a messenger to whom He reveals whatever He wills. He is most high, wise.
1981.subtitle: God Communicates With Us

1989.english: No human being can communicate with GOD except through inspiration, or from behind a barrier, or by His sending of a messenger through whom He reveals what He wills. He is the Most High, Most Wise.
1989.subtitle: How God Communicates With Us

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِى مَا ٱلْكِتَٰبُ وَلَا ٱلْإِيمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِن جَعَلْنَٰهُ نُورًا نَّهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِىٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ۚ ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا ۚ وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika awḥaynā ilayka rūḥan min amrinā mā kunta tadrī mā l-kitābu walā l-īmānu walākin jaʿalnāhu nūran nahdī bihi man nashāu min ʿibādinā wa-innaka latahdī ilā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmi
verses.english: Thus, we inspired to you a revelation proclaiming our commandments. You had no idea about the scripture, or faith. Yet, we made this a beacon to guide whomever we choose from among our servants. Surely, you guide in a straight path.

1981.english: We thus revealed to you an inspiration from us declaring our commandments. Previously, you had no idea what the scripture was, or what faith was. But we made this scripture a beacon to guide whomever we will. Indeed, you guide to a straight path.

1989.english: We inspired to you a revelation proclaiming our commandments—you had no idea about the scripture, or faith—and we made it a beacon to guide whomever we choose from among our servants. Surely, you guide to a straight path.

verses.arabic: صِرَٰطِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَلَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلْأُمُورُ
verses.arabicClean: صراط الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ۗ ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور
verses.transliterated: ṣirāṭi l-lahi alladhī lahu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi alā ilā l-lahi taṣīru l-umūr
verses.english: The path of GOD, to whom belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth. Absolutely, all matters are controlled by GOD.

1981.english: This is the path of God, who possesses everything in the heavens and the earth. To God all matters ultimately return.

1989.english: The path of GOD, to whom belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth. Absolutely, all matters are controlled by GOD. s

verses.arabic: حمٓ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حم
verses.transliterated: hha-meem
verses.english: H. M.
verses.footnote: See Footnote 40:1. The frequency of occurrence of the letters "H" (Hã) and "M" (Mîm) in the seven H.M.-initialed suras is 292, and 1855, respectively. This adds up to 2147, or 19x113.

1981.english: H. M.
1981.footnote: See footnote 40:1.

1989.english: H. M.*
1989.footnote: See Footnote 40:1. The frequency of occurrence of the letter “H ” (Haa) in tht seven Haa-initialed suras is 292, while the letter “M ” (Meem) occurs 1855 times in the seven suras. This adds up to a total of 2147, or 19x113. See Appendix 1 for the details.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: والكتاب المبين
verses.transliterated: wal-kitābi l-mubīn
verses.english: And the enlightening scripture.

1981.english: And this manifest scripture.

1989.english: And the profound scripture.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَٰهُ قُرْءَٰنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون
verses.transliterated: innā jaʿalnāhu qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan laʿallakum taʿqilūn
verses.english: We have rendered it an Arabic Quran, that you may understand.
verses.footnote: Arabic is the most efficient language, especially in expressing commandments, statutes and exacting laws. Hence the revelation of the Quran in Arabic for the clear understanding of all peoples, regardless of their tongues. See Appendix 4 for the details.

1981.english: We have made it an Arabic Quran, that you may understand.
1981.footnote: The word "you" in this verse refers to all the people on earth, regardless of their language. Careful research, involving most major languages on earth, has revealed that Arabic is the most suitable language for writing statutes. See Appendix 3 for details.

1989.english: We have rendered it an Arabic Quran, that you may understand.*
1989.footnote: Arabic is the most efficient language, especially in expressing commandments., statutes and exacting laws. Hence the revelation of the Quran in Arabic for the clear understanding of all peoples, regardless of their tongues. See Appendix 4 for the details.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُۥ فِىٓ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِىٌّ حَكِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم
verses.transliterated: wa-innahu fī ummi l-kitābi ladaynā laʿaliyyun ḥakīmu
verses.english: It is preserved with us in the original master, honorable and full of wisdom.

1981.english: It is recorded with us in the master record, honorable and full of wisdom.

1989.english: It is preserved with us in the original master, honorable and full of wisdom

verses.arabic: أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحًا أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْمًا مُّسْرِفِينَ
verses.arabicClean: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين
verses.transliterated: afanaḍribu ʿankumu l-dhik'ra ṣafḥan an kuntum qawman mus'rifīn
verses.english: Should we just ignore the fact that you have transgressed the limits?
verses.footnote: This refers to our original sin as detailed in the Introduction and Appendix 7.

1981.english: Shall we simply ignore the fact that you are transgressors?

1989.english: Should we just ignore the fact that you have transgressed?

verses.arabic: وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن نَّبِىٍّ فِى ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وكم أرسلنا من نبي في الأولين
verses.transliterated: wakam arsalnā min nabiyyin fī l-awalīn
verses.english: We have sent many a prophet to the previous generations.
verses.subtitle: The Plan for Redemption

1981.english: We sent many a prophet to previous generations.

1989.english: Many a prophet we have sent to the previous generations.

verses.arabic: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن نَّبِىٍّ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما يأتيهم من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزئون
verses.transliterated: wamā yatīhim min nabiyyin illā kānū bihi yastahziūn
verses.english: Every time a prophet went to them, they ridiculed him.

1981.english: Whenever a prophet went to them, they ridiculed him.

1989.english: Every time a prophet went to them, they ridiculed him.

verses.arabic: فَأَهْلَكْنَآ أَشَدَّ مِنْهُم بَطْشًا وَمَضَىٰ مَثَلُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فأهلكنا أشد منهم بطشا ومضى مثل الأولين
verses.transliterated: fa-ahlaknā ashadda min'hum baṭshan wamaḍā mathalu l-awalīn
verses.english: Consequently, we annihilated people who were even more powerful than these. We thus set the examples from the previous communities.

1981.english: Consequently, we annihilated stronger people than these, and this is a lesson from the past.

1989.english: Consequently, we annihilated people who were even more powerful than these. We thus set the examples from the previous communities.

verses.arabic: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم
verses.transliterated: wala-in sa-altahum man khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa layaqūlunna khalaqahunna l-ʿazīzu l-ʿalīm
verses.english: If you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth," they would say, "The Almighty, the Omniscient has created them."

1981.english: If you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth," they would say, "The almighty, the omniscient."
1981.subtitle: Worshipping God Not Enough
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: If you asked them, “Who created the heavens and the earth,” they would say, “The Almighty, the Omniscient has created them.”

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون
verses.transliterated: alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa mahdan wajaʿala lakum fīhā subulan laʿallakum tahtadūn
verses.english: He is the One who made the earth habitable for you, and created for you roads therein, that you may follow the right way.

1981.english: He is the one who made the earth for your habitation and established for you roads therein, that you may be guided.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: He is the One who made the earth habitable for you, and created for you roads therein, that you may be guided.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِى نَزَّلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۢ بِقَدَرٍ فَأَنشَرْنَا بِهِۦ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا ۚ كذلك تخرجون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhī nazzala mina l-samāi māan biqadarin fa-ansharnā bihi baldatan maytan kadhālika tukh'rajūn
verses.english: He is the One who sends down from the sky water, in exact measure, to revive dead lands therewith. Similarly, you will be resurrected.

1981.english: He is the one who sends down water from the sky, in exact measure, and revives dead land therewith. You will thus be raised.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: And He is the One who sends down from the sky water, in exact measure, to revive dead lands therewith. Similarly, you will be resurrected.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْفُلْكِ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhī khalaqa l-azwāja kullahā wajaʿala lakum mina l-ful'ki wal-anʿāmi mā tarkabūn
verses.english: He is the One who created all kinds, in pairs (male and female), and He created for you ships and livestock to ride.

1981.english: He is the one who created all kinds, and made the ships, as well as certain animals for you to ride.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: And He is the One who created all kinds, in pairs (male and female). And He created for you ships and livestock to ride.

verses.arabic: لِتَسْتَوُۥا۟ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِۦ ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ إِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَتَقُولُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُۥ مُقْرِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين
verses.transliterated: litastawū ʿalā ẓuhūrihi thumma tadhkurū niʿ'mata rabbikum idhā is'tawaytum ʿalayhi wataqūlū sub'ḥāna alladhī sakhara lanā hādhā wamā kunnā lahu muq'rinīn
verses.english: As you rest on top of them, you shall appreciate such a blessing from your Lord, and say, "Glory be to the One who subdued this for us. We could not have controlled them by ourselves.

1981.english: As you mount their backs, you shall appreciate the blessings of your Lord and say, "Glory be to the one who subdued this for us; we could not subdue it ourselves.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: As you rest on top of them, you shall appreciate this blessing from your Lord, and say, “Glory be to the One who subdued this for us. We could not have controlled them by ourselves.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون
verses.transliterated: wa-innā ilā rabbinā lamunqalibūn
verses.english: "We ultimately return to our Lord."

1981.english: "We ultimately return to our Lord."
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: “We ultimately return to our Lord.”

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلُوا۟ لَهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِهِۦ جُزْءًا إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَكَفُورٌ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا ۚ إن الإنسان لكفور مبين
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalū lahu min ʿibādihi juz'an inna l-insāna lakafūrun mubīnu
verses.english: They even assigned for Him a share from His own creation! Surely, the human being is profoundly unappreciative.
verses.subtitle: Angels As Daughters: A Blasphemy

1981.english: Yet, they set up idols from among His servants. Indeed, the human being is unappreciative.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: They even assigned for Him a share from His own creation! Surely, the human being is profoundly unappreciative.
1989.subtitle: Angels As Daughters: A Blasphemy

verses.arabic: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ بَنَاتٍ وَأَصْفَىٰكُم بِٱلْبَنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: أم اتخذ مما يخلق بنات وأصفاكم بالبنين
verses.transliterated: ami ittakhadha mimmā yakhluqu banātin wa-aṣfākum bil-banīn
verses.english: Has He chosen from among His creations daughters for Himself, while blessing you with sons?

1981.english: Others claim that He chose daughters among His creation, while giving them sons.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: Has He chosen from among His creations daughters for Himself, while blessing you with sons?

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِمَا ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ مَثَلًا ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُۥ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإذا بشر أحدهم بما ضرب للرحمن مثلا ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم
verses.transliterated: wa-idhā bushira aḥaduhum bimā ḍaraba lilrraḥmāni mathalan ẓalla wajhuhu mus'waddan wahuwa kaẓīmu
verses.english: When one of them is given news (of a daughter) as they claimed for the Most Gracious, his face is darkened with misery and anger!

1981.english: Yet, when one of them is given news that he has begotten a daughter, his face becomes darkened with misery.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: When one of them is given news (of a daughter) as they claimed for the Most Gracious, his face is darkened with misery; he becomes despondent.

verses.arabic: أَوَمَن يُنَشَّؤُا۟ فِى ٱلْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِى ٱلْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: أومن ينشأ في الحلية وهو في الخصام غير مبين
verses.transliterated: awaman yunasha-u fī l-ḥil'yati wahuwa fī l-khiṣāmi ghayru mubīni
verses.english: (They say,) "What is good about an offspring that is brought up to be beautiful, and cannot help in war?"

1981.english: For the girl is brought up to be beautiful, not to help him in war.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: (They say,) “What is good about an offspring which is brought up to be beautiful, and cannot help in war?”

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلُوا۟ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَٰدُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ إِنَٰثًا أَشَهِدُوا۟ خَلْقَهُمْ سَتُكْتَبُ شَهَٰدَتُهُمْ وَيُسْـَٔلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا ۚ أشهدوا خلقهم ۚ ستكتب شهادتهم ويسألون
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalū l-malāikata alladhīna hum ʿibādu l-raḥmāni ināthan ashahidū khalqahum satuk'tabu shahādatuhum wayus'alūn
verses.english: They claimed that the angels, who are servants of the Most Gracious, are females! Have they witnessed their creation? Their claims are recorded, and they will be asked.

1981.english: They claimed that the angels, who are servants of God most gracious, are females. Did they ever witness their creation? Their blasphemy will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: They claimed that the angels, who are creations of the Most Gracious, are females! Have they witnessed their creation? Their claims will be recorded, and they will be questioned.

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ مَا عَبَدْنَٰهُم مَّا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم ۗ ما لهم بذلك من علم ۖ إن هم إلا يخرصون
verses.transliterated: waqālū law shāa l-raḥmānu mā ʿabadnāhum mā lahum bidhālika min ʿil'min in hum illā yakhruṣūn
verses.english: They even said, "If the Most Gracious willed, we would not have worshiped them." They have no basis for such a claim; they only conjecture.
verses.footnote: The idol worshipers cannot blame God for their idolatry, since we have absolute freedom of choice to worship God alone, or not.

1981.english: They also said, "If it is the will of God most gracious, we would not idolize them." Indeed, they have no basis for idol worship; they only invent.
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: They also said, “If the Most Gracious willed, we would not have worshiped them.” They certainly have no basis for such a claim. They only conjecture.*
1989.footnote: The idol worshipers cannot blame God for their idolatry, since we have absolute freedom of choice to worship God alone, or not.

verses.arabic: أَمْ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُمْ كِتَٰبًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦ فَهُم بِهِۦ مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم آتيناهم كتابا من قبله فهم به مستمسكون
verses.transliterated: am ātaynāhum kitāban min qablihi fahum bihi mus'tamsikūn
verses.english: Have we given them a book before this, and they are upholding it?

1981.english: Did we give them any scripture that advocates idol worship?
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: Have we given them a book before this, that they are upholding?

verses.arabic: بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون
verses.transliterated: bal qālū innā wajadnā ābāanā ʿalā ummatin wa-innā ʿalā āthārihim muh'tadūn
verses.english: The fact is: they said, "We found our parents carrying on certain practices, and we are following in their footsteps."
verses.subtitle: Inherited Traditions Condemned

1981.english: What they said was, "We found our parents doing this, and we simply followed their footsteps."
1981.subtitle: Do Not Follow Your Parents Blindly
1981.footnote: See footnote 41:14.

1989.english: Instead, they said, “We found our parents carrying on certain practices, and we are following in their footsteps.”

verses.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِى قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون
verses.transliterated: wakadhālika mā arsalnā min qablika fī qaryatin min nadhīrin illā qāla mut'rafūhā innā wajadnā ābāanā ʿalā ummatin wa-innā ʿalā āthārihim muq'tadūn
verses.english: Invariably, when we sent a warner to any community, the leaders of that community would say, "We found our parents following certain practices, and we will continue in their footsteps."

1981.english: Thus, whenever we sent a warner to any community, the leaders said, "We found our parents following a religion, and we are following their footsteps."

1989.english: Invariably, when we sent a warner to a community, the leaders therein said, “We found our parents following certain practices, and we will continue in their footsteps.”

verses.arabic: قَٰلَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُم بِأَهْدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمْ عَلَيْهِ ءَابَآءَكُمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: قال أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم ۖ قالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون
verses.transliterated: qāla awalaw ji'tukum bi-ahdā mimmā wajadttum ʿalayhi ābāakum qālū innā bimā ur'sil'tum bihi kāfirūn
verses.english: (The messenger) would say, "What if I brought to you better guidance than what you inherited from your parents?" They would say, "We are disbelievers in the message you brought."

1981.english: The messenger would say, "What if I showed you better guidance than that of your parents?" They said, "We reject whatever you bring."

1989.english: He would say, “What if I brought to you better guidance than what you inherited from your parents?” They would say, “We are disbelievers in the message you brought.”

verses.arabic: فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فانتقمنا منهم ۖ فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين
verses.transliterated: fa-intaqamnā min'hum fa-unẓur kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-mukadhibīn
verses.english: Consequently, we requited them. Note the consequences for the rejectors.

1981.english: Consequently, we punished them. Note the consequences for the rejectors.

1989.english: Therefore, we requited them; note the consequences for the rejectors.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّنِى بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء مما تعبدون
verses.transliterated: wa-idh qāla ib'rāhīmu li-abīhi waqawmihi innanī barāon mimmā taʿbudūn
verses.english: Abraham said to his father and his people, "I disown what you worship.
verses.subtitle: Abraham's Example

1981.english: Abraham said to his father and his people, "I disown your idols.

1989.english: Abraham said to his father and his people, “I disown what you worship.

verses.arabic: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى فَإِنَّهُۥ سَيَهْدِينِ
verses.arabicClean: إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين
verses.transliterated: illā alladhī faṭaranī fa-innahu sayahdīn
verses.english: "Only the One who initiated me can guide me."

1981.english: "I worship only the one who created me and guides me."

1989.english: “Only the One who created me can guide me.”

verses.arabic: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةًۢ بَاقِيَةً فِى عَقِبِهِۦ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وجعلها كلمة باقية في عقبه لعلهم يرجعون
verses.transliterated: wajaʿalahā kalimatan bāqiyatan fī ʿaqibihi laʿallahum yarjiʿūn
verses.english: This example (of Abraham) was rendered an everlasting lesson for subsequent generations; perhaps they redeem their souls.

1981.english: His example is set up for those who come after him, that they may return.
1981.footnote: The lesson of Abraham is prominently detailed throughout the Quran. He grew up in an idol-worshipping community, and without receiving any education, he looked at the universe around him and discovered God (see 6:75-79). Similarly, no one has any excuse for not discovering and worshipping God alone. Like Abraham, we are all born with the knowledge of God as a natural instinct. (See 7:172).

1989.english: After him, He made this example (of Abraham) an everlasting lesson for subsequent generations, that they may redeem themselves.

verses.arabic: بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَءَابَآءَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: بل متعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين
verses.transliterated: bal mattaʿtu hāulāi waābāahum ḥattā jāahumu l-ḥaqu warasūlun mubīnu
verses.english: Indeed, I have given these people and their ancestors sufficient chances, then the truth came to them, and a clarifying messenger.

1981.english: I have allowed these people and their parents to enjoy themselves until the truth came to them, and a clarifying messenger.

1989.english: Indeed, I have given these people and their forefathers sufficient chances, then the truth came to them, and a clarifying messenger.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما جاءهم الحق قالوا هذا سحر وإنا به كافرون
verses.transliterated: walammā jāahumu l-ḥaqu qālū hādhā siḥ'run wa-innā bihi kāfirūn
verses.english: When the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers therein."

1981.english: But when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we reject it."

1989.english: When the truth came to them, they said, “This is magic, and we are disbelievers therein.”

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم
verses.transliterated: waqālū lawlā nuzzila hādhā l-qur'ānu ʿalā rajulin mina l-qaryatayni ʿaẓīmi
verses.english: They said, "If only this Quran was sent down through another man from the two communities (Mecca or Yathrib) who is prominent!"
verses.subtitle: Muhammad Ridiculed

1981.english: They said, "How come this Quran was not revealed through a prominent man from either town?"
1981.subtitle: God Chooses His Messenger

1989.english: They said, “If only this Quran was sent down through another man from the two communities (Mecca or Yathrib) who is prominent!”
1989.subtitle: Muhammad Ridiculed

verses.arabic: أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَٰتٍ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضًا سُخْرِيًّا وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أهم يقسمون رحمت ربك ۚ نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ۚ ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا ۗ ورحمت ربك خير مما يجمعون
verses.transliterated: ahum yaqsimūna raḥmata rabbika naḥnu qasamnā baynahum maʿīshatahum fī l-ḥayati l-dun'yā warafaʿnā baʿḍahum fawqa baʿḍin darajātin liyattakhidha baʿḍuhum baʿḍan sukh'riyyan waraḥmatu rabbika khayrun mimmā yajmaʿūn
verses.english: Are they the ones who assign your Lord's mercy? We have assigned their shares in this life, raising some of them above others in ranks, in order to let them serve one another. The mercy from your Lord is far better than any material they may hoard.

1981.english: Are they the ones who distribute the mercy of your Lord? We assign to them shares in this life, raising some of them above others, in order to use the services of one another. However, the mercy from your Lord is far better than any materials they hoard.

1989.english: Are they the ones who assign your Lord’s mercy? We have assigned their shares in this life, raising some of them above others in ranks, in order to let them serve one another. However, the mercy from your Lord is far better than any material they may hoard.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْلَآ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سقفا من فضة ومعارج عليها يظهرون
verses.transliterated: walawlā an yakūna l-nāsu ummatan wāḥidatan lajaʿalnā liman yakfuru bil-raḥmāni libuyūtihim suqufan min fiḍḍatin wamaʿārija ʿalayhā yaẓharūn
verses.english: If it were not that all the people might become one (disbelieving) congregation, we would have granted everyone who disbelieves in the Most Gracious mansions with silver roofs, and stairs upon which they could climb.
verses.subtitle: Materials of This World: All That The Disbelievers Get

1981.english: If it were not that all the people may become disbelievers, we would have granted every disbeliever a mansion with silver roofs and tall stairs.
1981.subtitle: The Materials Of This World Are Nil

1989.english: If it were not that all the people might become one (disbelieving) congregation, we would have granted everyone who disbelieves in the Most Gracious mansions with silver roofs, and stairs upon which they could climb.
1989.subtitle: Materials of This World: All That The Disbelievers Get

verses.arabic: وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْوَٰبًا وَسُرُرًا عَلَيْهَا يَتَّكِـُٔونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولبيوتهم أبوابا وسررا عليها يتكئون
verses.transliterated: walibuyūtihim abwāban wasururan ʿalayhā yattakiūn
verses.english: Their mansions would have impressive gates, and luxurious furnishings.

1981.english: Any many gates and luxurious furniture.

1989.english: And gates for their mansions, and luxurious furnishings.

verses.arabic: وَزُخْرُفًا وَإِن كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وزخرفا ۚ وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا ۚ والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين
verses.transliterated: wazukh'rufan wa-in kullu dhālika lammā matāʿu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wal-ākhiratu ʿinda rabbika lil'muttaqīn
verses.english: Also many ornaments. All these are the temporary materials of this lowly life. The Hereafter—at your Lord—is far better for the righteous.

1981.english: And numerous vanities. All these are the materials of this world. But the hereafter is reserved at your Lord for the righteous.

1989.english: And many vanities. All these are the temporary materials of this lowly life. The Hereafter, at your Lord, is far better for the righteous. Awareness of Our Invisible Companions*

verses.arabic: وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُۥ شَيْطَٰنًا فَهُوَ لَهُۥ قَرِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين
verses.transliterated: waman yaʿshu ʿan dhik'ri l-raḥmāni nuqayyiḍ lahu shayṭānan fahuwa lahu qarīnu
verses.english: Anyone who disregards the message of the Most Gracious, we appoint a devil to be his constant companion.
verses.subtitle: Invisible, Devilish, Companions
verses.footnote: Each one of us has a representative of Satan as a constant companion (App. 7).

1981.english: Anyone who neglects the message of God most gracious, we appoint a devil to be his constant companion.
1981.footnote: Those who neglect the Quran in favor of "**hadith**" and/or "**sunna**" (which are lies attributed to the prophet), believe that they are rightly guided. (see Appendices 11, 15, 16, and 17.)

1989.english: Anyone who disregards the message of the Most Gracious, we appoint a devil to be his constant companion.*
1989.footnote: Each one of us has a representative of Satan as a constant companion, within the same body. Unless we convert our companions, they continue to be devils (App. 7).

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإنهم ليصدونهم عن السبيل ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون
verses.transliterated: wa-innahum layaṣuddūnahum ʿani l-sabīli wayaḥsabūna annahum muh'tadūn
verses.english: Such companions will divert them from the path, yet make them believe that they are guided.

1981.english: Then the devils keep them away from the path, and make them think that they are guided.
1981.footnote: Those who neglect the Quran in favor of "**hadith**" and/or "**sunna**" (which are lies attributed to the prophet), believe that they are rightly guided. (see Appendices 11, 15, 16, and 17.)

1989.english: Such companions will divert them from the path. Yet, they make them believe that they are guided.
1989.footnote: Each one of us has a representative of Satan as a constant companion, within the same body. Unless we convert our companions, they continue to be devils (App. 7).

verses.arabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يَٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرِينُ
verses.arabicClean: حتى إذا جاءنا قال يا ليت بيني وبينك بعد المشرقين فبئس القرين
verses.transliterated: ḥattā idhā jāanā qāla yālayta baynī wabaynaka buʿ'da l-mashriqayni fabi'sa l-qarīn
verses.english: When he comes before us he will say, "Oh I wish you were as far from me as the two easts. What a miserable companion!"
verses.footnote: The "easts" imply the locations of sunrise, moonrise, and the rising of heavenly bodies.

1981.english: Then, when they come to us, each will say to his devil, "I wish you were as far from me as the distance between the two easts. What a miserable companion!"

1989.english: Then, when he comes to us he will say, “Oh I wish you were as far from me as the distance between the two easts. What a miserable companion!”
1989.footnote: Each one of us has a representative of Satan as a constant companion, within the same body. Unless we convert our companions, they continue to be devils (App. 7).

verses.arabic: وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِى ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولن ينفعكم اليوم إذ ظلمتم أنكم في العذاب مشتركون
verses.transliterated: walan yanfaʿakumu l-yawma idh ẓalamtum annakum fī l-ʿadhābi mush'tarikūn
verses.english: It will not console you on that day, as transgressors, that both of you will share in the retribution.

1981.english: On that day, there will be no consolation in being together in hell.

1989.english: It will not console you on that day, since you have transgressed, that both of you will share in the retribution. Addressing the Messenger
1989.footnote: Each one of us has a representative of Satan as a constant companion, within the same body. Unless we convert our companions, they continue to be devils (App. 7).

verses.arabic: أَفَأَنتَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ أَوْ تَهْدِى ٱلْعُمْىَ وَمَن كَانَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: أفأنت تسمع الصم أو تهدي العمي ومن كان في ضلال مبين
verses.transliterated: afa-anta tus'miʿu l-ṣuma aw tahdī l-ʿum'ya waman kāna fī ḍalālin mubīni
verses.english: Can you make the deaf hear; can you make the blind see, or those who are far astray?
verses.subtitle: God's Messenger of the Covenant

1981.english: You cannot make the deaf hear, nor can you guide the blind, nor can you guide those who are totally astray.

1989.english: Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and the wicked strayers?

verses.arabic: فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فإما نذهبن بك فإنا منهم منتقمون
verses.transliterated: fa-immā nadhhabanna bika fa-innā min'hum muntaqimūn
verses.english: Whether we let you die before it or not, we will surely requite them.

1981.english: Whether we let you die before it or not, we will sooner or later punish them.

1989.english: Whether we let you die before it or not, we will surely punish them.

verses.arabic: أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ ٱلَّذِى وَعَدْنَٰهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِم مُّقْتَدِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أو نرينك الذي وعدناهم فإنا عليهم مقتدرون
verses.transliterated: aw nuriyannaka alladhī waʿadnāhum fa-innā ʿalayhim muq'tadirūn
verses.english: Or, we may show you (the retribution) we promised for them. We are in full control over them.

1981.english: We may let you see the doom we promised them. We are in total control over them.

1989.english: And we may show you (the retribution) we promised for them. We are in full control over them.

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَمْسِكْ بِٱلَّذِىٓ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك ۖ إنك على صراط مستقيم
verses.transliterated: fa-is'tamsik bi-alladhī ūḥiya ilayka innaka ʿalā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmi
verses.english: You shall steadfastly preach what is revealed to you; you are in the right path.
verses.footnote: The sum of the gematrical value of "Rashad Khalifa" (1230) plus 43 is 1273, 19x67.

1981.english: Therefore, you shall uphold what is revealed to you, for you are in the right path.

1989.english: Therefore, you shall steadfastly uphold what we have given you; you are in the right path.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ وَسَوْفَ تُسْـَٔلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك ۖ وسوف تسألون
verses.transliterated: wa-innahu ladhik'run laka waliqawmika wasawfa tus'alūn
verses.english: This is a message for you and your people; all of you will be questioned.

1981.english: This is a message for you and your people, for which you will be answerable.

1989.english: This is a message for you and your people, and you will be questioned.

verses.arabic: وَسْـَٔلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ءَالِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون
verses.transliterated: wasal man arsalnā min qablika min rusulinā ajaʿalnā min dūni l-raḥmāni ālihatan yuʿ'badūn
verses.english: Check the messengers we sent before you: "Have we ever appointed any other gods—beside the Most Gracious—to be worshiped?"

1981.english: Study the history of all the messengers before you; did we ever allow any idols to be set up besides God most gracious?

1989.english: Ask all those messengers that we sent before you: “Have we set up besides the Most Gracious other gods to be worshiped?”

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَإِي۟هِۦ فَقَالَ إِنِّى رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فقال إني رسول رب العالمين
verses.transliterated: walaqad arsalnā mūsā biāyātinā ilā fir'ʿawna wamala-ihi faqāla innī rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīn
verses.english: For example, we sent Moses with our proofs to Pharaoh and his elders, proclaiming: "I am a messenger from the Lord of the universe."

1981.english: For example, we sent Moses with our miracles to Pharaoh and his people saying, "I am sent by the Lord of the universe."
1981.subtitle: The Lesson From Moses

1989.english: For example, we sent Moses with our miracles to Pharaoh and his elders, saying, “I am a messenger from the Lord of the universe.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَضْحَكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما جاءهم بآياتنا إذا هم منها يضحكون
verses.transliterated: falammā jāahum biāyātinā idhā hum min'hā yaḍḥakūn
verses.english: When he showed them our proofs, they laughed at them.

1981.english: When he showed them our miracles, they laughed at them.

1989.english: When he showed them our miracles, they laughed at them.

verses.arabic: وَمَا نُرِيهِم مِّنْ ءَايَةٍ إِلَّا هِىَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا وَأَخَذْنَٰهُم بِٱلْعَذَابِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها ۖ وأخذناهم بالعذاب لعلهم يرجعون
verses.transliterated: wamā nurīhim min āyatin illā hiya akbaru min ukh'tihā wa-akhadhnāhum bil-ʿadhābi laʿallahum yarjiʿūn
verses.english: Every sign we showed them was bigger than the one before it. We afflicted them with the plagues, perhaps they repent.
verses.subtitle: Moses and Pharaoh

1981.english: Every sign we showed them was greater than the previous one; as we afflicted them with plagues, that they may return.

1989.english: Every sign we showed them was even bigger than the previous one, and we afflicted them with the plagues, perhaps they repent.
1989.subtitle: Moses and Pharaoh

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهْتَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا يا أيه الساحر ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك إننا لمهتدون
verses.transliterated: waqālū yāayyuha l-sāḥiru ud'ʿu lanā rabbaka bimā ʿahida ʿindaka innanā lamuh'tadūn
verses.english: They said, "O you magician, implore your Lord on our behalf, since you have an agreement with Him (to relieve this plague); we will then be guided."

1981.english: They said, "O you magician, call upon your Lord to relieve our plagues; we will then follow the guidance."

1989.english: They said, “O magician, implore your Lord on our behalf, since you are closer to Him (to relieve this plague)-, we will then be guided.”

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما كشفنا عنهم العذاب إذا هم ينكثون
verses.transliterated: falammā kashafnā ʿanhumu l-ʿadhāba idhā hum yankuthūn
verses.english: But as soon as we relieved their affliction, they reverted.

1981.english: But when we relieved their plagues, they broke their vows.

1989.english: But as soon as we relieved their affliction, they reverted.

verses.arabic: وَنَادَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فِى قَوْمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَلَيْسَ لِى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِىٓ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ونادى فرعون في قومه قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي ۖ أفلا تبصرون
verses.transliterated: wanādā fir'ʿawnu fī qawmihi qāla yāqawmi alaysa lī mul'ku miṣ'ra wahādhihi l-anhāru tajrī min taḥtī afalā tub'ṣirūn
verses.english: Pharaoh announced to his people, "O my people, do I not possess the kingship over Egypt, and these flowing rivers belong to me? Do you not see?

1981.english: Pharaoh announced, "O my people, do I not possess the kingdom of Egypt and these rivers flow beneath me? Do you not see?"

1989.english: Pharaoh announced to his people, “O my people, do I not possess the kingship of Egypt, and these rivers are flowing under me? Do you not see?

verses.arabic: أَمْ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
verses.arabicClean: أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين ولا يكاد يبين
verses.transliterated: am anā khayrun min hādhā alladhī huwa mahīnun walā yakādu yubīn
verses.english: "Which one is better; me or that one who is lowly and can hardly speak?

1981.english: "Which one is better, me or this one who is lowly and can hardly speak?

1989.english: “Which one is better; me or that one who is lowly and can hardly speak?

verses.arabic: فَلَوْلَآ أُلْقِىَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلولا ألقي عليه أسورة من ذهب أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين
verses.transliterated: falawlā ul'qiya ʿalayhi aswiratun min dhahabin aw jāa maʿahu l-malāikatu muq'tarinīn
verses.english: "How come he does not possess a treasure of gold; how come the angels do not accompany him?"

1981.english: "Why does he not receive a treasure of gold or bring the angels with him as assistants?"

1989.english: “Why does he not possess a treasure of gold, or bring the angels to work with him?”

verses.arabic: فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فاستخف قومه فأطاعوه ۚ إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين
verses.transliterated: fa-is'takhaffa qawmahu fa-aṭāʿūhu innahum kānū qawman fāsiqīn
verses.english: He thus fooled his people, and they obeyed him; they were wicked people.

1981.english: Pharaoh thus duped his people and made them obey him; they were wicked.

1989.english: He thus fooled his people, and they obeyed him; for they were wicked people.

verses.arabic: فَلَمَّآ ءَاسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم أجمعين
verses.transliterated: falammā āsafūnā intaqamnā min'hum fa-aghraqnāhum ajmaʿīn
verses.english: When they persisted in opposing us, we punished them and drowned them all.

1981.english: Because they opposed us, we avenged and drowned them all.

1989.english: When they persisted in fighting us, we punished them and drowned them all.

verses.arabic: فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ سَلَفًا وَمَثَلًا لِّلْءَاخِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فجعلناهم سلفا ومثلا للآخرين
verses.transliterated: fajaʿalnāhum salafan wamathalan lil'ākhirīn
verses.english: We rendered them a precedent and an example for the others.

1981.english: We set them up as examples for the others.

1989.english: We rendered them an example and a lesson for the others. Another Example From History

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدون
verses.transliterated: walammā ḍuriba ub'nu maryama mathalan idhā qawmuka min'hu yaṣiddūn
verses.english: When the son of Mary was cited as an example, your people disregarded it.
verses.subtitle: Jesus: Another Example

1981.english: And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, your people rebelled.

1989.english: And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, your people immediately rejected it.

verses.arabic: وَقَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلًۢا بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هو ۚ ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا ۚ بل هم قوم خصمون
verses.transliterated: waqālū aālihatunā khayrun am huwa mā ḍarabūhu laka illā jadalan bal hum qawmun khaṣimūn
verses.english: They said, "Is it better to worship our gods, or to worship him?" They said this only to argue with you. Indeed, they are people who have joined the opposition.

1981.english: They said, "Which is better, worshipping our idols, or worshipping Jesus (as the Christians do)?" They used his example to argue with you. Indeed, they are contentious.
1981.footnote: The Muslims who deviated from Quran and advocated other sources of law, such as the invented "**hadith**" and/or "**sunna**," are not any better than those who idolize Jesus, as stated in this verse. Deviating from the Quran constitutes disobedience of the prophet and idolizing him against his will (see 25:30-31).

1989.english: They said, “Is it better to worship our gods, or to worship him?” They said this only to argue with you. Indeed, they are people in opposition.

verses.arabic: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُ مَثَلًا لِّبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
verses.arabicClean: إن هو إلا عبد أنعمنا عليه وجعلناه مثلا لبني إسرائيل
verses.transliterated: in huwa illā ʿabdun anʿamnā ʿalayhi wajaʿalnāhu mathalan libanī is'rāīl
verses.english: He was no more than a servant whom we blessed, and we sent him as an example for the Children of Israel.

1981.english: Jesus is no more than a servant whom we blessed. We made him an example for the children of Israel.

1989.english: He was no more than a human servant whom we blessed, and we rendered him a lesson for the Children of Israel.

verses.arabic: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُم مَّلَٰٓئِكَةً فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولو نشاء لجعلنا منكم ملائكة في الأرض يخلفون
verses.transliterated: walaw nashāu lajaʿalnā minkum malāikatan fī l-arḍi yakhlufūn
verses.english: If we willed, we could have made you angels who colonize and reproduce on earth.

1981.english: Had we willed, we could have sent angels to reside with you on earth.

1989.english: If we willed, we could have made you angels colonizing the earth.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ فَلَا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا وَٱتَّبِعُونِ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإنه لعلم للساعة فلا تمترن بها واتبعون ۚ هذا صراط مستقيم
verses.transliterated: wa-innahu laʿil'mun lilssāʿati falā tamtarunna bihā wa-ittabiʿūni hādhā ṣirāṭun mus'taqīmu
verses.english: He is to serve as a marker for knowing the end of the world, so you can no longer harbor any doubt about it. You shall follow Me; this is the right path.
verses.subtitle: Jesus and the End of the World
verses.footnote: As detailed in Appendix 25, the End of the World is given in the Quran, and the birth date of Jesus provided one of the significant signs that the calculations are correct. We learn that the world will end in the year 2280 (19x120) after the birth of Jesus (see 47:18). Additionally, both the lunar year (1710) & the solar year (2280) are divisible by 570 (19x30), the number of years from the birth of Jesus to the birth of Muhammad. Thus, the birth date of Jesus is a marker.

1981.english: He was sent to provide you with knowledge relevant to the Hour, "You shall not be doubtful, and follow me; this is a straight path.

1989.english: He is to serve as a sign for knowing the end of the world.* You shall harbor no doubts about it, and follow me. This is the right path.
1989.footnote: As detailed in Appendix 25, the End of the World is given in the Quran, and the birthdate of Jesus provided one of the significant signs that the calculations are correct. We learn that the world will end in the year 2280 (19x120) after the birth of Jesus. See 47:18. Additionally, both the lunar year (1710) & the solar year (2280) are divisible by 570 (19x30), the number of years from the birth of Jesus to the birth of Muhammad.

verses.arabic: وَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: ولا يصدنكم الشيطان ۖ إنه لكم عدو مبين
verses.transliterated: walā yaṣuddannakumu l-shayṭānu innahu lakum ʿaduwwun mubīnu
verses.english: Let not the devil repel you; he is your most ardent enemy.

1981.english: "Let not the devil repel you; for he is your ardent enemy."

1989.english: Let not the devil repel you; he is your most ardent enemy.

verses.arabic: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ عِيسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
verses.arabicClean: ولما جاء عيسى بالبينات قال قد جئتكم بالحكمة ولأبين لكم بعض الذي تختلفون فيه ۖ فاتقوا الله وأطيعون
verses.transliterated: walammā jāa ʿīsā bil-bayināti qāla qad ji'tukum bil-ḥik'mati wali-ubayyina lakum baʿḍa alladhī takhtalifūna fīhi fa-ittaqū l-laha wa-aṭīʿūn
verses.english: When Jesus went with the proofs, he said, "I bring to you wisdom, and to clarify some of the matters in which you dispute. You shall reverence GOD and obey me.

1981.english: When Jesus came with miracles, he said, "I bring you wisdom and clarifications of some disputes. Beware of God, and obey me.

1989.english: When Jesus came with the miracles, he said, “I bring to you wisdom, and clarification of some matters in which you dispute. You shall reverence GOD and obey me.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: إن الله هو ربي وربكم فاعبدوه ۚ هذا صراط مستقيم
verses.transliterated: inna l-laha huwa rabbī warabbukum fa-uʿ'budūhu hādhā ṣirāṭun mus'taqīmu
verses.english: "GOD is my Lord and your Lord, you shall worship Him alone. This is the right path."

1981.english: "God is my Lord and your Lord; you shall worship Him. This is a straight path."

1989.english: “GOD is my Lord and your Lord, you shall worship Him alone. This is the right path.”

verses.arabic: فَٱخْتَلَفَ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ مِنۢ بَيْنِهِمْ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم ۖ فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم
verses.transliterated: fa-ikh'talafa l-aḥzābu min baynihim fawaylun lilladhīna ẓalamū min ʿadhābi yawmin alīmi
verses.english: The opponents disputed among themselves. Woe to those who transgress from the retribution of a painful day.

1981.english: But the various parties disputed among themselves. Therefore, woe to the wrongdoers from the retribution of a painful day.

1989.english: The parties disputed among themselves. Woe to those who trans gressed from the retribution of a painful day.

verses.arabic: هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ أَن تَأْتِيَهُم بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: هل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون
verses.transliterated: hal yanẓurūna illā l-sāʿata an tatiyahum baghtatan wahum lā yashʿurūn
verses.english: Are they waiting for the Hour (Day of Judgment) to come to them suddenly when they least expect it?

1981.english: Are they waiting until their end comes suddenly when they least expect it?

1989.english: Are they waiting for the Hour to come to them suddenly when they least expect it?

verses.arabic: ٱلْأَخِلَّآءُ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين
verses.transliterated: al-akhilāu yawma-idhin baʿḍuhum libaʿḍin ʿaduwwun illā l-mutaqīn
verses.english: The close friends on that day will become enemies of one another, except for the righteous.

1981.english: The close friends on that day will become enemies, except for the righteous.

1989.english: The close friends on that day will become enemies of one another, except for the righteous.

verses.arabic: يَٰعِبَادِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ وَلَآ أَنتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون
verses.transliterated: yāʿibādi lā khawfun ʿalaykumu l-yawma walā antum taḥzanūn
verses.english: O My servants, you will have no fear on that day, nor will you grieve.
verses.subtitle: The Righteous

1981.english: O My servants, do not worry about anything today; nor shall you grieve.

1989.english: O My servants, you will suffer no fear on that day, nor will you grieve.
1989.subtitle: The Righteous

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُوا۟ مُسْلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين آمنوا بآياتنا وكانوا مسلمين
verses.transliterated: alladhīna āmanū biāyātinā wakānū mus'limīn
verses.english: They are the ones who believed in our revelations, and were submitters.

1981.english: They believed in our revelations and totally submitted.

1989.english: They believed in our revelations, and totally submitted.

verses.arabic: ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ أَنتُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُكُمْ تُحْبَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ادخلوا الجنة أنتم وأزواجكم تحبرون
verses.transliterated: ud'khulū l-janata antum wa-azwājukum tuḥ'barūn
verses.english: Enter Paradise, together with your spouses, and rejoice.

1981.english: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, and rejoice.

1989.english: Enter Paradise, together with your spouses, and rejoice.

verses.arabic: يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِم بِصِحَافٍ مِّن ذَهَبٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ وَفِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ ٱلْأَنفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ ٱلْأَعْيُنُ وَأَنتُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يطاف عليهم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب ۖ وفيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين ۖ وأنتم فيها خالدون
verses.transliterated: yuṭāfu ʿalayhim biṣiḥāfin min dhahabin wa-akwābin wafīhā mā tashtahīhi l-anfusu wataladhu l-aʿyunu wa-antum fīhā khālidūn
verses.english: Offered to them will be golden trays and cups, and they will find everything the hearts desire and the eyes wish for. You live therein forever.

1981.english: Trays made of gold will be passed around for them, and cups. They will have anything their souls desire or their eyes wish. They abide therein forever.

1989.english: Offered to them will be golden trays and cups of everything the hearts desire and the eyes wish for. You live therein forever.

verses.arabic: وَتِلْكَ ٱلْجَنَّةُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُورِثْتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وتلك الجنة التي أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون
verses.transliterated: watil'ka l-janatu allatī ūrith'tumūhā bimā kuntum taʿmalūn
verses.english: Such is the Paradise that you inherit, in return for your works.

1981.english: This is Paradise that you inherit because of your works.

1989.english: Such is the Paradise that you inherit, in return for your works.

verses.arabic: لَكُمْ فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةٌ كَثِيرَةٌ مِّنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لكم فيها فاكهة كثيرة منها تأكلون
verses.transliterated: lakum fīhā fākihatun kathīratun min'hā takulūn
verses.english: You will have in it all kinds of fruits, from which you eat.

1981.english: You will have many fruits therein from which you eat.

1989.english: You will have in it all kinds of fruits, from which you eat.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ فِى عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون
verses.transliterated: inna l-muj'rimīna fī ʿadhābi jahannama khālidūn
verses.english: Surely, the guilty will abide in the retribution of Gehenna forever.

1981.english: As for the guilty, they will abide forever in hell.

1989.english: Surely, the guilty will abide in the retribution of Gehenna forever.

verses.arabic: لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون
verses.transliterated: lā yufattaru ʿanhum wahum fīhi mub'lisūn
verses.english: Never will the retribution be commuted for them; they will be confined therein.

1981.english: They will never be reprieved and will be confined therein.

1989.english: Never will it be commuted for them; they will be confined therein.

verses.arabic: وَمَا ظَلَمْنَٰهُمْ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.arabicClean: وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين
verses.transliterated: wamā ẓalamnāhum walākin kānū humu l-ẓālimīn
verses.english: It is not us who wronged them; it is they who wronged their own souls.

1981.english: It is not us who wronged them; it is they who wronged themselves.

1989.english: It is not us who wronged them; it is they who wronged their own souls.

verses.arabic: وَنَادَوْا۟ يَٰمَٰلِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ قَالَ إِنَّكُم مَّٰكِثُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك ۖ قال إنكم ماكثون
verses.transliterated: wanādaw yāmāliku liyaqḍi ʿalaynā rabbuka qāla innakum mākithūn
verses.english: They will implore: "O Mãlek, let your Lord finish us off." He will say, "You are staying forever.

1981.english: They will call, "O Malik (guardian of hell), let your Lord finish us." But he will say, "You will last forever.

1989.english: They will implore: “O Maalek, let your Lord finish us off.” He will say, “You are staying.

verses.arabic: لَقَدْ جِئْنَٰكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ لِلْحَقِّ كَٰرِهُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لقد جئناكم بالحق ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون
verses.transliterated: laqad ji'nākum bil-ḥaqi walākinna aktharakum lil'ḥaqqi kārihūn
verses.english: "We have given you the truth, but most of you hate the truth."
verses.subtitle: They Hate The Truth

1981.english: "We have given you the truth, but most of you disliked the truth."

1989.english: “We have given you the truth, but most of you hate the truth.”
1989.subtitle: They Hate The Truth

verses.arabic: أَمْ أَبْرَمُوٓا۟ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّا مُبْرِمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم أبرموا أمرا فإنا مبرمون
verses.transliterated: am abramū amran fa-innā mub'rimūn
verses.english: Have they schemed some scheme? We too are scheming.

1981.english: Have they planned a certain plan? We also plan. Did they think that we could not hear their secret conspiracies?

1989.english: Have they schemed a scheme? We too are scheming.

verses.arabic: أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لَا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَىٰهُم بَلَىٰ وَرُسُلُنَا لَدَيْهِمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم يحسبون أنا لا نسمع سرهم ونجواهم ۚ بلى ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون
verses.transliterated: am yaḥsabūna annā lā nasmaʿu sirrahum wanajwāhum balā warusulunā ladayhim yaktubūn
verses.english: Do they think that we do not hear their secrets and conspiracies? Yes indeed; our messengers are with them, recording.

1981.english: Indeed, our messengers are with them, recording.

1989.english: Do they think that we do not hear their secrets and conspiracies? Yes indeed; our messengers are with them, recording.

verses.arabic: قُلْ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْعَٰبِدِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين
verses.transliterated: qul in kāna lilrraḥmāni waladun fa-anā awwalu l-ʿābidīn
verses.english: Proclaim: "If the Most Gracious did have a son, I would still be the foremost worshiper."

1981.english: Say, "If God most gracious had a son, I will be the first to believe."
1981.footnote: If God indeed had a son, who would object? It simply happens to be an untruth, and a blasphemy.

1989.english: Proclaim: “If the Most Gracious did have a son, I would be the first to worship Him (anyway).”

verses.arabic: سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
verses.arabicClean: سبحان رب السماوات والأرض رب العرش عما يصفون
verses.transliterated: sub'ḥāna rabbi l-samāwāti wal-arḍi rabbi l-ʿarshi ʿammā yaṣifūn
verses.english: Be He glorified; He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord with the great dominion, far above their claims.

1981.english: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the throne; He is high above their claims.

1989.english: Be He glorified; He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord with the great dominion, far above their claims.

verses.arabic: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون
verses.transliterated: fadharhum yakhūḍū wayalʿabū ḥattā yulāqū yawmahumu alladhī yūʿadūn
verses.english: Let them blunder and play until they meet their day that is awaiting them.

1981.english: Let them blunder and play, until they meet the day that is promised to them.

1989.english: Let them blunder and play until they meet their day that is awaiting them.

verses.arabic: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَٰهٌ وَفِى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَٰهٌ وَهُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: وهو الذي في السماء إله وفي الأرض إله ۚ وهو الحكيم العليم
verses.transliterated: wahuwa alladhī fī l-samāi ilāhun wafī l-arḍi ilāhun wahuwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm
verses.english: He is the only One who is a deity in the heaven and a deity on earth. He is the Most Wise, the Omniscient.

1981.english: He is the one God in the heaven and the one God on earth; He is the wise, the omniscient.

1989.english: He is the only god in the heaven and the only god on earth, and He is the Most Wise, the Omniscient.

verses.arabic: وَتَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَعِندَهُۥ عِلْمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وتبارك الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وعنده علم الساعة وإليه ترجعون
verses.transliterated: watabāraka alladhī lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā waʿindahu ʿil'mu l-sāʿati wa-ilayhi tur'jaʿūn
verses.english: Most Exalted is the One who possesses all sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them. With Him is the knowledge about the Hour (end of the world), and to Him you will be returned.

1981.english: Most exalted is the one who possesses the dominion of the heavens and the earth and everything between them. Only He knows when the Hour will come. To Him you ultimately return.

1989.english: Most Exalted is the One who possesses the kingship of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them. With Him is the knowledge about the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.

verses.arabic: وَلَا يَمْلِكُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةَ إِلَّا مَن شَهِدَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولا يملك الذين يدعون من دونه الشفاعة إلا من شهد بالحق وهم يعلمون
verses.transliterated: walā yamliku alladhīna yadʿūna min dūnihi l-shafāʿata illā man shahida bil-ḥaqi wahum yaʿlamūn
verses.english: None of those whom they idolize beside Him possess any power to intercede, unless their intercession coincides with the truth, and they fully know.

1981.english: The idols they set up besides Him possess no power to intercede, unless their intercession coincides with the truth, and unless they are aware thereof.
1981.subtitle: There Will Be No Intercession
1981.footnote: See Appendix 7 for details.

1989.english: None of those whom they idolize besides Him possess any power to intercede, unless their intercession coincides with the truth, and they are aware thereof.

verses.arabic: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُ فَأَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله ۖ فأنى يؤفكون
verses.transliterated: wala-in sa-altahum man khalaqahum layaqūlunna l-lahu fa-annā yu'fakūn
verses.english: If you asked them who created them, they would say, "GOD." Why then did they deviate?

1981.english: Ironically, when you ask them who created them, they would say, "God." Why then did they deviate?
1981.footnote: See footnote 23:84.

1989.english: If you asked them who created them, they would say, “GOD.” Why then did they deviate?

verses.arabic: وَقِيلِهِۦ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوْمٌ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وقيله يا رب إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: waqīlihi yārabbi inna hāulāi qawmun lā yu'minūn
verses.english: It will be proclaimed: "O my Lord, these people do not believe."

1981.english: They will be declared as disbelievers.

1989.english: It is proclaimed: “O my Lord, these people do not believe.”

verses.arabic: فَٱصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ وَقُلْ سَلَٰمٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فاصفح عنهم وقل سلام ۚ فسوف يعلمون
verses.transliterated: fa-iṣ'faḥ ʿanhum waqul salāmun fasawfa yaʿlamūn
verses.english: You shall disregard them and say, "Peace;" they will surely find out.

1981.english: Therefore, disregard them and say, "Peace," for they will eventually find out.

1989.english: Disregard them and say, “Peace;” they will surely find out.

verses.arabic: حمٓ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حم
verses.transliterated: hha-meem
verses.english: H. M.

1981.english: H. M.
1981.footnote: See footnote 40:1.

1989.english: H. M.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُبِينِ
verses.arabicClean: والكتاب المبين
verses.transliterated: wal-kitābi l-mubīn
verses.english: And this enlightening scripture.

1981.english: And this profound scripture.

1989.english: And this profound scripture.

verses.arabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ
verses.arabicClean: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة ۚ إنا كنا منذرين
verses.transliterated: innā anzalnāhu fī laylatin mubārakatin innā kunnā mundhirīn
verses.english: We have sent it down in a blessed night, for we are to warn.

1981.english: We have revealed the Quran in a blessed night, that we may warn.
1981.footnote: The Quran was revealed into Muhammad's heart all at once (see 2:185, 17:1, 53:1-18, and 97:1), and released through his mouth over a period of 23 years (see 17:106).
