1981.english: I have not created the jinns and the humans except to worship Me alone.
1981.footnote: The whole idea behind creating us is to show the angels that a creature who never sees God is capable of reaching God and worshipping Him alone. When one of the angels, namely satan, entertained rebellious ideas despite the fact that he saw God and knew well that He was the absolute master, God decided to show the angels that a creature who never sees God is capable of worshipping God alone (See Appendix 6).

1989.english: 1 did not create the jinns and the humans except to worship Me alone.
1989.subtitle: The Purpose of Our Existence

verses.arabic: مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ
verses.arabicClean: ما أريد منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون
verses.transliterated: mā urīdu min'hum min riz'qin wamā urīdu an yuṭ'ʿimūn
verses.english: I need no provisions from them, nor do I need them to feed Me.

1981.english: I do not need any provision from them, nor do I need them to feed Me.

1989.english: 1 need no provisions from them, nor do I need them to feed Me.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ
verses.arabicClean: إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين
verses.transliterated: inna l-laha huwa l-razāqu dhū l-quwati l-matīn
verses.english: GOD is the Provider, the Possessor of all power, the Supreme.

1981.english: God is the one who provides; the one who possesses all power, the omnipotent.

1989.english: GOD is the Provider, the Possessor of all power, the Supreme.

verses.arabic: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ذَنُوبًا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَٰبِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
verses.arabicClean: فإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم فلا يستعجلون
verses.transliterated: fa-inna lilladhīna ẓalamū dhanūban mith'la dhanūbi aṣḥābihim falā yastaʿjilūn
verses.english: The transgressors have incurred the same fate as their previous counterparts; they should not challenge.

1981.english: Those who commit evil will be doomed like their previous counterparts were doomed. Therefore, they should not hasten to challenge our doom.

1989.english: The transgressors have incurred the same fate as their previous counterparts; they should not challenge.

verses.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن يَوْمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فويل للذين كفروا من يومهم الذي يوعدون
verses.transliterated: fawaylun lilladhīna kafarū min yawmihimu alladhī yūʿadūn
verses.english: Woe to those who disbelieved from the day that is awaiting them.

1981.english: Woe to those who disbelieve, from the day that is promised to them.

1989.english: Woe to those who disbelieved from the day that is awaiting them.

verses.arabic: وَٱلطُّورِ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والطور
verses.transliterated: wal-ṭūr
verses.english: Mt. Sinai.

1981.english: By Mount Sinai.

1989.english: Mt. Sinai.

verses.arabic: وَكِتَٰبٍ مَّسْطُورٍ
verses.arabicClean: وكتاب مسطور
verses.transliterated: wakitābin masṭūri
verses.english: The recorded scripture.

1981.english: And the scripture that is recorded.

1989.english: The recorded scripture.

verses.arabic: فِى رَقٍّ مَّنشُورٍ
verses.arabicClean: في رق منشور
verses.transliterated: fī raqqin manshūri
verses.english: Published in books.

1981.english: And published on paper.

1989.english: Published in books.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْمَعْمُورِ
verses.arabicClean: والبيت المعمور
verses.transliterated: wal-bayti l-maʿmūr
verses.english: The frequented Shrine.

1981.english: By the frequented shrine.

1989.english: The frequented Shrine.

verses.arabic: وَٱلسَّقْفِ ٱلْمَرْفُوعِ
verses.arabicClean: والسقف المرفوع
verses.transliterated: wal-saqfi l-marfūʿ
verses.english: The exalted ceiling.

1981.english: With its high ceiling.

1989.english: The exalted ceiling.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ
verses.arabicClean: والبحر المسجور
verses.transliterated: wal-baḥri l-masjūr
verses.english: The sea that is set aflame.

1981.english: By the vast ocean.

1989.english: The sea that is set aflame.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَٰقِعٌ
verses.arabicClean: إن عذاب ربك لواقع
verses.transliterated: inna ʿadhāba rabbika lawāqiʿu
verses.english: Your Lord's requital is unavoidable.

1981.english: The retribution from your Lord is a reality.

1989.english: Your Lord’s requital is unavoidable.

verses.arabic: مَّا لَهُۥ مِن دَافِعٍ
verses.arabicClean: ما له من دافع
verses.transliterated: mā lahu min dāfiʿi
verses.english: No force in the universe can stop it.

1981.english: Nothing can stop it.

1989.english: No force in the universe can stop it.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْرًا
verses.arabicClean: يوم تمور السماء مورا
verses.transliterated: yawma tamūru l-samāu mawra
verses.english: The day will come when the sky will violently thunder.

1981.english: That is the day when the heaven will violently thunder.

1989.english: The day will come when the sky will violently thunder.

verses.arabic: وَتَسِيرُ ٱلْجِبَالُ سَيْرًا
verses.arabicClean: وتسير الجبال سيرا
verses.transliterated: watasīru l-jibālu sayra
verses.english: The mountains will be wiped out.

1981.english: The mountains will be erased.

1989.english: The mountains will be wiped out.

verses.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فويل يومئذ للمكذبين
verses.transliterated: fawaylun yawma-idhin lil'mukadhibīn
verses.english: Woe on that day to the disbelievers—

1981.english: Woe on that day to the rejectors.

1989.english: Woe on that day to the disbelievers—

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: الذين هم في خوض يلعبون
verses.transliterated: alladhīna hum fī khawḍin yalʿabūn
verses.english: who are in their blundering, heedless.

1981.english: Who are heedless and playing.

1989.english: who are in their blundering, heedless.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
verses.arabicClean: يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا
verses.transliterated: yawma yudaʿʿūna ilā nāri jahannama daʿʿa
verses.english: They will be herded into Gehenna, forcibly.

1981.english: On that day, they will be herded to the fire of hell.

1989.english: They will be herded into Gehenna, forcibly.

verses.arabic: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: هذه النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون
verses.transliterated: hādhihi l-nāru allatī kuntum bihā tukadhibūn
verses.english: This is the Fire in which you used to disbelieve.

1981.english: This is the fire that you used to deny.

1989.english: This is the Fire in which you used to disbelieve.

verses.arabic: أَفَسِحْرٌ هَٰذَآ أَمْ أَنتُمْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أفسحر هذا أم أنتم لا تبصرون
verses.transliterated: afasiḥ'run hādhā am antum lā tub'ṣirūn
verses.english: Is this magic, or do you not see?

1981.english: Is this magic, or do you not see?

1989.english: Is this magic, or do you not see?

verses.arabic: ٱصْلَوْهَا فَٱصْبِرُوٓا۟ أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: اصلوها فاصبروا أو لا تصبروا سواء عليكم ۖ إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون
verses.transliterated: iṣ'lawhā fa-iṣ'birū aw lā taṣbirū sawāon ʿalaykum innamā tuj'zawna mā kuntum taʿmalūn
verses.english: Suffer the burning. Whether you are patient or impatient, it will be the same for you. This is the just requital for what you did.

1981.english: Burn therein, whether you can or cannot stand it, you have no other choice. You are paying for what you did.

1989.english: Suffer the burning. Whether you are patient or impatient, it will be the same for you. This is the just requital for what you did.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ
verses.arabicClean: إن المتقين في جنات ونعيم
verses.transliterated: inna l-mutaqīna fī jannātin wanaʿīmi
verses.english: The righteous have deserved gardens and bliss.

1981.english: As for the righteous, they have deserved gardens of bliss.

1989.english: The righteous have deserved gardens and bliss.

verses.arabic: فَٰكِهِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
verses.arabicClean: فاكهين بما آتاهم ربهم ووقاهم ربهم عذاب الجحيم
verses.transliterated: fākihīna bimā ātāhum rabbuhum wawaqāhum rabbuhum ʿadhāba l-jaḥīm
verses.english: They enjoy what their Lord has reserved for them; their Lord has spared them the retribution of Hell.

1981.english: They enjoy what their Lord bestows upon them. Their Lord has spared them the agony of hell.

1989.english: They enjoy what their Lord has reserved for them; their Lord has spared them the retribution of Hell.

verses.arabic: كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما كنتم تعملون
verses.transliterated: kulū wa-ish'rabū hanīan bimā kuntum taʿmalūn
verses.english: Eat and drink happily, in return for your works.

1981.english: Eat and drink with blessings, in return for what you did.

1989.english: Eat and drink happily, in return for your works.

verses.arabic: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: متكئين على سرر مصفوفة ۖ وزوجناهم بحور عين
verses.transliterated: muttakiīna ʿalā sururin maṣfūfatin wazawwajnāhum biḥūrin ʿīni
verses.english: They relax on luxurious furnishings, and we match them with beautiful spouses.

1981.english: They relax on rows of furnishings, and we join with them magnificent spouses.
1981.footnote: See Appendix 4, detailing these allegorical descriptions of heaven and hell.

1989.english: They relax on luxurious furnishings, and we match them with beautiful spouses.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَمَآ أَلَتْنَٰهُم مِّنْ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَىْءٍ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ
verses.arabicClean: والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء ۚ كل امرئ بما كسب رهين
verses.transliterated: wa-alladhīna āmanū wa-ittabaʿathum dhurriyyatuhum biīmānin alḥaqnā bihim dhurriyyatahum wamā alatnāhum min ʿamalihim min shayin kullu im'ri-in bimā kasaba rahīnu
verses.english: For those who believed, and their children also followed them in belief, we will have their children join them. We never fail to reward them for any work. Every person is paid for what he did.

1981.english: Those who believed and whose children followed them in belief, we will reunite them with their children. We never deprive them of any work they had done. Every person is ransomed in accordance with his work.

1989.english: For those who believed, and their children also followed them in belief, we will have their children join them. We never fail to reward them for any work. Every person is paid for what he did.

verses.arabic: وَأَمْدَدْنَٰهُم بِفَٰكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وأمددناهم بفاكهة ولحم مما يشتهون
verses.transliterated: wa-amdadnāhum bifākihatin walaḥmin mimmā yashtahūn
verses.english: We will supply them with fruits and meats that they love.

1981.english: We supply them with fruits and meats that they desire.

1989.english: We will supply them with fruits and meats that they love.

verses.arabic: يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا لَّا لَغْوٌ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: يتنازعون فيها كأسا لا لغو فيها ولا تأثيم
verses.transliterated: yatanāzaʿūna fīhā kasan lā laghwun fīhā walā tathīmu
verses.english: They will enjoy drinks that are never polluted, and never sinful to drink.

1981.english: They will share drinks that never run out and are never polluted.

1989.english: They will enjoy drinks that are never polluted, and never sinful to drink.

verses.arabic: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمَانٌ لَّهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَّكْنُونٌ
verses.arabicClean: ويطوف عليهم غلمان لهم كأنهم لؤلؤ مكنون
verses.transliterated: wayaṭūfu ʿalayhim ghil'mānun lahum ka-annahum lu'lu-on maknūnu
verses.english: Serving them will be servants like protected pearls.

1981.english: Serving them will be servants like precious pearls.

1989.english: Serving them will be servants like protected pearls.

verses.arabic: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون
verses.transliterated: wa-aqbala baʿḍuhum ʿalā baʿḍin yatasāalūn
verses.english: They will meet each other and reminisce among themselves.

1981.english: They will converse with each other.

1989.english: They will meet each other and reminisce among themselves.

verses.arabic: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِىٓ أَهْلِنَا مُشْفِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قالوا إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين
verses.transliterated: qālū innā kunnā qablu fī ahlinā mush'fiqīn
verses.english: They will say, "We used to be kind and humble among our people.

1981.english: They will say, "We used to be humble among our people.

1989.english: They will say, “We used to be kind and humble among our people.

verses.arabic: فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
verses.arabicClean: فمن الله علينا ووقانا عذاب السموم
verses.transliterated: famanna l-lahu ʿalaynā wawaqānā ʿadhāba l-samūm
verses.english: "GOD has blessed us, and has spared us the agony of ill winds.

1981.english: "Then God showered us with His blessings and spared us the agony of ill winds.

1989.english: “GOD has blessed us, and has spared us the agony of ill winds.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.arabicClean: إنا كنا من قبل ندعوه ۖ إنه هو البر الرحيم
verses.transliterated: innā kunnā min qablu nadʿūhu innahu huwa l-baru l-raḥīm
verses.english: "We used to implore Him; He is the Most Kind, Most Merciful."

1981.english: "We used to implore Him; He is the benign, the merciful."

1989.english: “We used to implore Him; He is the Most Kind, Most Merciful.”

verses.arabic: فَذَكِّرْ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ
verses.arabicClean: فذكر فما أنت بنعمت ربك بكاهن ولا مجنون
verses.transliterated: fadhakkir famā anta biniʿ'mati rabbika bikāhinin walā majnūni
verses.english: You shall remind the people. With your Lord's blessings upon you, you are neither a soothsayer, nor crazy.
verses.subtitle: The Messenger

1981.english: Therefore, you shall continue to remind the people, for you are never doubtful about your Lord's message, nor are you crazy.

1989.english: You shall remind the people. With your Lord’s blessings upon you, you are neither a soothsayer, nor crazy.
1989.subtitle: The Messenger

verses.arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرٌ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِۦ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ
verses.arabicClean: أم يقولون شاعر نتربص به ريب المنون
verses.transliterated: am yaqūlūna shāʿirun natarabbaṣu bihi rayba l-manūn
verses.english: They may say, "He is a poet; let us just wait until he is dead."

1981.english: They may say, "He is a poet; let us just ignore him until he is dead."

1989.english: They may say, “He is a poet; let us just wait until he is dead.”

verses.arabic: قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا۟ فَإِنِّى مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
verses.arabicClean: قل تربصوا فإني معكم من المتربصين
verses.transliterated: qul tarabbaṣū fa-innī maʿakum mina l-mutarabiṣīn
verses.english: Say, "Go on waiting; I will wait along with you."

1981.english: Say, "Keep on waiting; I am waiting along with you."

1989.english: Say, “Go on waiting; I will wait along with you.”

verses.arabic: أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلَٰمُهُم بِهَٰذَآ أَمْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا ۚ أم هم قوم طاغون
verses.transliterated: am tamuruhum aḥlāmuhum bihādhā am hum qawmun ṭāghūn
verses.english: Is it their dreams that dictate their behavior, or are they naturally wicked?

1981.english: Is it their dreams that lead them to this, or is it wickedness?

1989.english: Is it their dreams that dictate their behavior, or are they naturally wicked?

verses.arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُۥ بَل لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم يقولون تقوله ۚ بل لا يؤمنون
verses.transliterated: am yaqūlūna taqawwalahu bal lā yu'minūn
verses.english: Do they say, "He made it all up?" Instead, they are simply disbelievers.

1981.english: Do they say that he made this up? They simply cannot believe.

1989.english: Do they say, “He made it all up?” Instead, they are simply disbelievers.

verses.arabic: فَلْيَأْتُوا۟ بِحَدِيثٍ مِّثْلِهِۦٓ إِن كَانُوا۟ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.arabicClean: فليأتوا بحديث مثله إن كانوا صادقين
verses.transliterated: falyatū biḥadīthin mith'lihi in kānū ṣādiqīn
verses.english: Let them produce a Hadith like this, if they are truthful.
verses.subtitle: "Mohammedans" Challenge God and Produce Hadith

1981.english: Let them show us a **hadith** (narration) like this, if they are truthful.

1989.english: Let them produce a Hadith like this, if they are truthful.
1989.subtitle: “Mohammedans” Challenge God and Produce Hadith

verses.arabic: أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم خلقوا من غير شيء أم هم الخالقون
verses.transliterated: am khuliqū min ghayri shayin am humu l-khāliqūn
verses.english: Were they created from nothing? Are they the creators?

1981.english: Were they created out of nothing? Could they be the creators?

1989.english: Were they created from nothing? Are they the creators?

verses.arabic: أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم خلقوا السماوات والأرض ۚ بل لا يوقنون
verses.transliterated: am khalaqū l-samāwāti wal-arḍa bal lā yūqinūn
verses.english: Did they create the heavens and the earth? Indeed, they have no certainty.

1981.english: Did they create the heavens and the earth? Indeed, they are never certain.

1989.english: Did they create the heavens and the earth? Indeed, they have no certainty.

verses.arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمْ خَزَآئِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْمُصَۣيْطِرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم عندهم خزائن ربك أم هم المصيطرون
verses.transliterated: am ʿindahum khazāinu rabbika am humu l-muṣayṭirūn
verses.english: Do they possess the treasures of your Lord? Are they in control?

1981.english: Do they possess the treasures of your Lord? Are they in control?

1989.english: Do they possess the treasures of your Lord? Are they in control?

verses.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُم بِسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
verses.arabicClean: أم لهم سلم يستمعون فيه ۖ فليأت مستمعهم بسلطان مبين
verses.transliterated: am lahum sullamun yastamiʿūna fīhi falyati mus'tamiʿuhum bisul'ṭānin mubīni
verses.english: Do they climb a ladder that enables them to listen? Let their listeners show their proof.

1981.english: Do they have a stairway that enables them to listen to us? Let their listener show his evidence.

1989.english: Do they climb a ladder that enables them to listen? Let their listeners show their proof.

verses.arabic: أَمْ لَهُ ٱلْبَنَٰتُ وَلَكُمُ ٱلْبَنُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم له البنات ولكم البنون
verses.transliterated: am lahu l-banātu walakumu l-banūn
verses.english: Does He have daughters, while you have sons?

1981.english: Does God have daughters, while you have sons?

1989.english: Does He have daughters, while you have sons?

verses.arabic: أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون
verses.transliterated: am tasaluhum ajran fahum min maghramin muth'qalūn
verses.english: Are you asking them for any wage, and they are burdened thereby?

1981.english: Are you asking them for a wage, so they are burdened thereby?

1989.english: Are you asking them for any wage, and they are burdened thereby?

verses.arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون
verses.transliterated: am ʿindahumu l-ghaybu fahum yaktubūn
verses.english: Do they know the future, and have it recorded?

1981.english: Do they know the future and record it?

1989.english: Do they know the future, and have it recorded?

verses.arabic: أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْدًا فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْمَكِيدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم يريدون كيدا ۖ فالذين كفروا هم المكيدون
verses.transliterated: am yurīdūna kaydan fa-alladhīna kafarū humu l-makīdūn
verses.english: Are they plotting and scheming? The disbelievers' schemes backfire against them.

1981.english: Is it obstruction that they seek? The disbelievers only hinder themselves.

1989.english: Are they plotting and scheming? The disbelievers’ schemes backfire against them.

verses.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلَٰهٌ غَيْرُ ٱللَّهِ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أم لهم إله غير الله ۚ سبحان الله عما يشركون
verses.transliterated: am lahum ilāhun ghayru l-lahi sub'ḥāna l-lahi ʿammā yush'rikūn
verses.english: Do they have another god besides GOD? GOD be glorified, far above having partners.

1981.english: Do they have a god other than God? God be glorified, over and above any idols they set up.

1989.english: Do they have another god besides GOD? GOD be glorified, far above having partners.

verses.arabic: وَإِن يَرَوْا۟ كِسْفًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ سَاقِطًا يَقُولُوا۟ سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإن يروا كسفا من السماء ساقطا يقولوا سحاب مركوم
verses.transliterated: wa-in yaraw kis'fan mina l-samāi sāqiṭan yaqūlū saḥābun markūmu
verses.english: When they see masses falling from the sky, they will say, "Piled clouds!"

1981.english: When they see masses about to fall from the sky, they would say, "Dense clouds."

1989.english: When they see masses falling from the sky, they will say, “Piled clouds!”

verses.arabic: فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ
verses.arabicClean: فذرهم حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي فيه يصعقون
verses.transliterated: fadharhum ḥattā yulāqū yawmahumu alladhī fīhi yuṣ'ʿaqūn
verses.english: Disregard them until they meet the day in which they are struck.

1981.english: Therefore, disregard them until they meet their day of doom.

1989.english: Disregard them until they meet the day in which they are struck.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: يوم لا يغني عنهم كيدهم شيئا ولا هم ينصرون
verses.transliterated: yawma lā yugh'nī ʿanhum kayduhum shayan walā hum yunṣarūn
verses.english: On that day, their schemes will not protect them, nor will they be helped.

1981.english: On that day, their schemes will never help them; nothing will protect them.

1989.english: On that day, their schemes will not protect them, nor will they be helped

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ عَذَابًا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وإن للذين ظلموا عذابا دون ذلك ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون
verses.transliterated: wa-inna lilladhīna ẓalamū ʿadhāban dūna dhālika walākinna aktharahum lā yaʿlamūn
verses.english: Those who transgress suffer retribution here, but most of them do not know.

1981.english: The wicked actually suffer retribution in this life, without realizing it.

1989.english: Those who transgress suffer retribution here, but most of them do not know.

verses.arabic: وَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
verses.arabicClean: واصبر لحكم ربك فإنك بأعيننا ۖ وسبح بحمد ربك حين تقوم
verses.transliterated: wa-iṣ'bir liḥuk'mi rabbika fa-innaka bi-aʿyuninā wasabbiḥ biḥamdi rabbika ḥīna taqūm
verses.english: You shall steadfastly persevere in carrying out your Lord's command—you are in our eyes—and glorify and praise your Lord when you get up.

1981.english: You shall steadfastly persevere in preaching the message of your Lord. You are in our eyes. And praise the glory of your Lord when you get up.

1989.english: You shall steadfastly persevere in carrying out your Lord’s command—you are in our eyes—and glorify and praise your Lord when you get up.

verses.arabic: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًٔا
verses.arabicClean: وما لهم به من علم ۖ إن يتبعون إلا الظن ۖ وإن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا
verses.transliterated: wamā lahum bihi min ʿil'min in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-inna l-ẓana lā yugh'nī mina l-ḥaqi shaya
verses.english: They had no knowledge about this; they only conjectured. Conjecture is no substitute for the truth.

1981.english: They have no basis for such a claim; they only follow conjecture. Conjecture is no substitute for the truth.

1989.english: They had no knowledge about this; they only conjectured. Conjecture is no substitute for the truth.

verses.arabic: فَأَعْرِضْ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا
verses.arabicClean: فأعرض عن من تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا
verses.transliterated: fa-aʿriḍ ʿan man tawallā ʿan dhik'rinā walam yurid illā l-ḥayata l-dun'y
verses.english: You shall disregard those who turn away from our message, and become preoccupied with this worldly life.
verses.subtitle: Choose Your Friends Carefully

1981.english: Therefore, stay away from those who disregard our message and seek only the material of this world.

1989.english: You shall disregard those who turn away from our message, and become preoccupied with this worldly life.
1989.subtitle: Choose Your Friends Carefully

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: ذلك مبلغهم من العلم ۚ إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى
verses.transliterated: dhālika mablaghuhum mina l-ʿil'mi inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bimani ih'tad
verses.english: This is the extent of their knowledge. Your Lord is fully aware of those who strayed away from His path, and He is fully aware of those who are guided.

1981.english: This is the extent of their knowledge. Your Lord is fully aware of those who deviate from His path, and He is fully aware of those who are guided.

1989.english: This is the extent of their knowledge. Your Lord is fully aware of those who strayed away from His path, and He is fully aware of those who are guided.

verses.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔوا۟ بِمَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَيَجْزِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ بِٱلْحُسْنَى
verses.arabicClean: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ليجزي الذين أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى
verses.transliterated: walillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi liyajziya alladhīna asāū bimā ʿamilū wayajziya alladhīna aḥsanū bil-ḥus'n
verses.english: To GOD belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth. He will requite those who commit evil for their works, and will reward the righteous for their righteousness.

1981.english: To God belongs everything in the heavens and the earth. He will requite the evildoers only for their deeds, and reward the righteous manyfold.

1989.english: To GOD belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth. He will requite those who commit evil for their works, and will reward the righteous for their righteousness.

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
verses.arabicClean: الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش إلا اللمم ۚ إن ربك واسع المغفرة ۚ هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم ۖ فلا تزكوا أنفسكم ۖ هو أعلم بمن اتقى
verses.transliterated: alladhīna yajtanibūna kabāira l-ith'mi wal-fawāḥisha illā l-lamama inna rabbaka wāsiʿu l-maghfirati huwa aʿlamu bikum idh ansha-akum mina l-arḍi wa-idh antum ajinnatun fī buṭūni ummahātikum falā tuzakkū anfusakum huwa aʿlamu bimani ittaq
verses.english: They avoid gross sins and transgressions, except for minor offenses. Your Lord's forgiveness is immense. He has been fully aware of you since He initiated you from the earth, and while you were embryos in your mothers' bellies. Therefore, do not exalt yourselves; He is fully aware of the righteous.

1981.english: For the righteous avoid gross sins and transgressions, except minor offenses, and your Lord is full of forgiveness. He is fully aware of you. He is the one who created you from the earth, then reproduced you as embryos in your mothers' wombs. Therefore, you do not need to exalt yourselves; He is fully aware of the righteous.

1989.english: They avoid gross sins and transgressions, except for minor offenses. Your Lord’s forgiveness is immense. He has been fully aware of you since He initiated you from the earth, and while you were embryos in your mothers’ bellies. Therefore, do not exalt yourselves; He is fully aware of the righteous.

verses.arabic: أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ
verses.arabicClean: أفرأيت الذي تولى
verses.transliterated: afara-ayta alladhī tawall
verses.english: Have you noted the one who turned away?

1981.english: What about the one who turns away?

1989.english: Have you noted the one who turned away?

verses.arabic: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰٓ
verses.arabicClean: وأعطى قليلا وأكدى
verses.transliterated: wa-aʿṭā qalīlan wa-akd
verses.english: Rarely did he give to charity, and then very little.

1981.english: Who rarely gives to charity, and then complains?

1989.english: Rarely did he give to charity, and then very little.

verses.arabic: أَعِندَهُۥ عِلْمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَىٰٓ
verses.arabicClean: أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى
verses.transliterated: aʿindahu ʿil'mu l-ghaybi fahuwa yar
verses.english: Did he possess knowledge of the future? Could he see it?

1981.english: Does he possess knowledge of the future; does he see?

1989.english: Did he possess knowledge of the future? Could he see it?

verses.arabic: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِى صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى
verses.transliterated: am lam yunabba bimā fī ṣuḥufi mūs
verses.english: Was he not informed of the teachings in the scripture of Moses?

1981.english: Did he not know about Moses' scripture?

1989.english: Was he not informed of the teachings in the scripture of Moses?

verses.arabic: وَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلَّذِى وَفَّىٰٓ
verses.arabicClean: وإبراهيم الذي وفى
verses.transliterated: wa-ib'rāhīma alladhī waff
verses.english: And Abraham who fulfilled?

1981.english: And Abraham who fulfilled?

1989.english: And Abraham who fulfilled?

verses.arabic: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى
verses.transliterated: allā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'r
verses.english: No soul bears the sins of another soul.

1981.english: (They taught) that no burdened soul can bear the burdens of another.

1989.english: No soul bears the sins of another soul.

verses.arabic: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
verses.transliterated: wa-an laysa lil'insāni illā mā saʿ
verses.english: Every human being is responsible for his own works.

1981.english: And that every human being is responsible for what he does.

1989.english: Every human being is responsible for his own works.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُۥ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأن سعيه سوف يرى
verses.transliterated: wa-anna saʿyahu sawfa yur
verses.english: And everyone's works will be shown.

1981.english: And that everything he does will be witnessed.

1989.english: And everyone’s works will be shown.

verses.arabic: ثُمَّ يُجْزَىٰهُ ٱلْجَزَآءَ ٱلْأَوْفَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: ثم يجزاه الجزاء الأوفى
verses.transliterated: thumma yuj'zāhu l-jazāa l-awf
verses.english: Then they will be paid fully for such works.

1981.english: Then he is fully repaid therefor.

1989.english: Then they will be paid fully for such works.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى
verses.transliterated: wa-anna ilā rabbika l-muntah
verses.english: To your Lord is the final destiny.

1981.english: And that to your Lord is the final destiny.

1989.english: To your Lord is the final destiny.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى
verses.transliterated: wa-annahu huwa aḍḥaka wa-abk

1981.english: And that He is the one who makes you happy or miserable.

1989.english: He is the One who makes you laugh or cry.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا
verses.arabicClean: وأنه هو أمات وأحيا
verses.transliterated: wa-annahu huwa amāta wa-aḥy
verses.english: He is the One who controls death and life.

1981.english: And that He is the one who controls death and life.

1989.english: He is the One who controls death and life.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّهُۥ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأنه خلق الزوجين الذكر والأنثى
verses.transliterated: wa-annahu khalaqa l-zawjayni l-dhakara wal-unth
verses.english: He is the One who created the two kinds, male and female—
verses.subtitle: The Husband Determines The Baby's Gender

1981.english: And that He is the one who created both kinds, male and female,

1989.english: He is the One who created the two kinds, male and female—
1989.subtitle: The Husband Determines The Baby’s Gender

verses.arabic: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: من نطفة إذا تمنى
verses.transliterated: min nuṭ'fatin idhā tum'n

1981.english: from a drop of semen.

1989.english: from a tiny drop of semen.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى
verses.transliterated: wa-anna ʿalayhi l-nashata l-ukh'r
verses.english: He will effect the recreation.

1981.english: And that He will effect the recreation.

1989.english: He will effect the recreation.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى
verses.transliterated: wa-annahu huwa aghnā wa-aqn
verses.english: He is the One who makes you rich or poor.

1981.english: And that He is the one who makes you rich or poor.

1989.english: He is the One who makes you rich or poor.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّهُۥ هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلشِّعْرَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأنه هو رب الشعرى
verses.transliterated: wa-annahu huwa rabbu l-shiʿ'r
verses.english: He is the Lord of the galaxies.

1981.english: And that He is the Lord of the glowing star.

1989.english: He is the Lord of the galaxies.

verses.arabic: وَأَنَّهُۥٓ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا ٱلْأُولَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وأنه أهلك عادا الأولى
verses.transliterated: wa-annahu ahlaka ʿādan l-ūl
verses.english: He is the One who annihilated ancient 'Ãd.

1981.english: And that He is the one who annihilated ancient 'Aad.

1989.english: He is the One who annihilated ancient ‘Aad.

verses.arabic: وَثَمُودَا۟ فَمَآ أَبْقَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وثمود فما أبقى
verses.transliterated: wathamūdā famā abq
verses.english: And wiped out Thamûd.

1981.english: Also Thamood; He wiped them out.

1989.english: And wiped out Thamoud.

verses.arabic: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: وقوم نوح من قبل ۖ إنهم كانوا هم أظلم وأطغى
verses.transliterated: waqawma nūḥin min qablu innahum kānū hum aẓlama wa-aṭgh

1981.english: Before that, He annihilated Noah's people. They were more wicked and more sinning.

1989.english: Also the people of Noah before that; they were evil transgressors.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: والمؤتفكة أهوى
verses.transliterated: wal-mu'tafikata ahw
verses.english: The evil communities (of Sodom and Gomorrah) were the lowliest.

1981.english: And He destroyed the sinners (of Sodom and Gomorrah).

1989.english: The evil communities (of Sodom and Gomorrah) were the lowliest.

verses.arabic: فَغَشَّىٰهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ
verses.arabicClean: فغشاها ما غشى
verses.transliterated: faghashāhā mā ghash
verses.english: Consequently, they utterly vanished.

1981.english: They were completely overwhelmed.

1989.english: Consequently, they utterly vanished.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارَىٰ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربك تتمارى
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbika tatamār
verses.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1989.english: Which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: هَٰذَا نَذِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنُّذُرِ ٱلْأُولَىٰٓ
verses.arabicClean: هذا نذير من النذر الأولى
verses.transliterated: hādhā nadhīrun mina l-nudhuri l-ūl
verses.english: This is a warning like the older ones.

1981.english: This is a warning like the previous warnings.

1989.english: This is a warning like the older ones.

verses.arabic: أَزِفَتِ ٱلْءَازِفَةُ
verses.arabicClean: أزفت الآزفة
verses.transliterated: azifati l-āzifat
verses.english: The inevitable is imminent.

1981.english: The inevitable has drawn near.

1989.english: The inevitable is imminent.

verses.arabic: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
verses.arabicClean: ليس لها من دون الله كاشفة
verses.transliterated: laysa lahā min dūni l-lahi kāshifatu
verses.english: None besides GOD can relieve it.

1981.english: No one besides God can relieve it.

1989.english: None besides GOD can relieve it.

verses.arabic: أَفَمِنْ هَٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ
verses.arabicClean: أفمن هذا الحديث تعجبون
verses.transliterated: afamin hādhā l-ḥadīthi taʿjabūn
verses.english: Are you questioning this matter?

1981.english: Are you wondering about this message?

1989.english: Are you questioning this matter?

verses.arabic: وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وتضحكون ولا تبكون
verses.transliterated: wataḍḥakūna walā tabkūn
verses.english: Are you laughing, instead of crying?

1981.english: Are you laughing, instead of crying?

1989.english: Are you laughing, instead of crying?

verses.arabic: وَأَنتُمْ سَٰمِدُونَ
verses.arabicClean: وأنتم سامدون
verses.transliterated: wa-antum sāmidūn
verses.english: Are you insisting on your ways?

1981.english: Are you stubborn?

1989.english: Are you insisting on your ways?

verses.arabic: فَٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ وَٱعْبُدُوا۟
verses.arabicClean: فاسجدوا لله واعبدوا ۩
verses.transliterated: fa-us'judū lillahi wa-uʿ'bud
verses.english: You shall fall prostrate before GOD, and worship.

1981.english: You shall fall prostrate before God, as you worship.

1989.english: You shall fall prostrate before GOD, and worship.

verses.arabic: ٱقْتَرَبَتِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر
verses.transliterated: iq'tarabati l-sāʿatu wa-inshaqqa l-qamar
verses.english: The Hour has come closer, and the moon has split.
verses.footnote: This important sign of the approaching end of the world came to pass in 1969 when humans landed on the moon and brought pieces of the moon to earth. At the same time, God's mathematical Miracle of the Quran was being gradually unveiled. Traditional Muslims opposed it, since it exposed the fallacy of their practices (App. 25).

1981.english: When the Hour approaches, the moon will split.
1981.footnote: As frequently observed, the Quranic language is often in the past tense, indicating a prediction that is sure to come, or rather, an event that actually took place and was witnessed only by God, the only witness of our future. The storytellers, who were unfamiliar with the Quranic linguistics, invented numerous stories about a miracle performed by Muhammad, whereby he allegedly caused the moon to split. The flagrant contradictions among these stories testify to the false nature of **hadith**. The most "reliable" book of **hadith**, namely Bukhari, reports two versions of the alleged miracle, one in Mecca and one in Mina. In another book of **hadith**, it is reported that one-half of the moon fell down and was found in the courtyard of Ali's house!!! The violation of the moon already took place by the landing of the humans in 1969. See also 44:10.

1989.english: The Hour has come closer, and the moon has split.*
1989.footnote: This important sign of the approaching end of the world came to pass in 1969 when humans landed on the moon and brought pieces of the moon to earth. At the same time, God’s mathematical Miracle of the Quran was being gradually unveiled. Traditional Muslims opposed it, since it exposed the fallacy of their practices (App. 25).

verses.arabic: وَإِن يَرَوْا۟ ءَايَةً يُعْرِضُوا۟ وَيَقُولُوا۟ سِحْرٌ مُّسْتَمِرٌّ
verses.arabicClean: وإن يروا آية يعرضوا ويقولوا سحر مستمر
verses.transliterated: wa-in yaraw āyatan yuʿ'riḍū wayaqūlū siḥ'run mus'tamirru
verses.english: Then they saw a miracle; but they turned away and said, "Old magic."

1981.english: Yet, whenever they see a sign, they turn away saying, "This is real magic."

1989.english: Then they saw a miracle; but they turned away and said, “Old magic.”

verses.arabic: وَكَذَّبُوا۟ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓا۟ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ
verses.arabicClean: وكذبوا واتبعوا أهواءهم ۚ وكل أمر مستقر
verses.transliterated: wakadhabū wa-ittabaʿū ahwāahum wakullu amrin mus'taqirru
verses.english: They disbelieved, followed their opinions, and adhered to their old traditions.

1981.english: They disbelieve and follow their own opinions and what they could physically sense.

1989.english: They disbelieved, followed their opinions, and adhered to their old traditions.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَنۢبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد جاءهم من الأنباء ما فيه مزدجر
verses.transliterated: walaqad jāahum mina l-anbāi mā fīhi muz'dajaru
verses.english: Sufficient warnings have been delivered to alert them.

1981.english: They have received enough knowledge to set them straight.

1989.english: Sufficient warnings have been delivered to alert them.

verses.arabic: حِكْمَةٌۢ بَٰلِغَةٌ فَمَا تُغْنِ ٱلنُّذُرُ
verses.arabicClean: حكمة بالغة ۖ فما تغن النذر
verses.transliterated: ḥik'matun bālighatun famā tugh'ni l-nudhur
verses.english: Great wisdom; but all the warnings have been in vain.

1981.english: Great wisdom (has come to them), but the warnings seem to be useless.

1989.english: Great wisdom; but all the warnings have been in vain.

verses.arabic: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ يَدْعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَىْءٍ نُّكُرٍ
verses.arabicClean: فتول عنهم ۘ يوم يدع الداع إلى شيء نكر
verses.transliterated: fatawalla ʿanhum yawma yadʿu l-dāʿi ilā shayin nukuri
verses.english: Ignore them; the day will come when the caller will announce a terrible disaster.

1981.english: Therefore, leave them alone. The day will come when the caller calls them to something terrible.

1989.english: Ignore them; the day will come when the caller will announce a terrible disaster.

verses.arabic: خُشَّعًا أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ
verses.arabicClean: خشعا أبصارهم يخرجون من الأجداث كأنهم جراد منتشر
verses.transliterated: khushaʿan abṣāruhum yakhrujūna mina l-ajdāthi ka-annahum jarādun muntashiru
verses.english: With their eyes humiliated, they come out of the graves like scattered locusts.

1981.english: Their eyes will be humbled as they come out of the graves, like swarms of locusts.

1989.english: With their eyes humiliated, they come out of the graves like scattered locusts.

verses.arabic: مُّهْطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِ يَقُولُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ
verses.arabicClean: مهطعين إلى الداع ۖ يقول الكافرون هذا يوم عسر
verses.transliterated: muh'ṭiʿīna ilā l-dāʿi yaqūlu l-kāfirūna hādhā yawmun ʿasiru
verses.english: As they respond to the caller, the disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."

1981.english: Obeying the caller, the disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."

1989.english: As they respond to the caller, the disbelievers will say, “This is a difficult day.”

verses.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُوا۟ عَبْدَنَا وَقَالُوا۟ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ
verses.arabicClean: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح فكذبوا عبدنا وقالوا مجنون وازدجر
verses.transliterated: kadhabat qablahum qawmu nūḥin fakadhabū ʿabdanā waqālū majnūnun wa-uz'dujir
verses.english: The people of Noah disbelieved before them. They disbelieved our servant and said, "Crazy!" He was persecuted.

1981.english: Before them, the people of Noah have disbelieved. They disbelieved our servant and said, "Crazy." He was rejected.

1989.english: The people of Noah disbelieved before them. They disbelieved our servant and said, “Crazy!” He was persecuted.

verses.arabic: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَغْلُوبٌ فَٱنتَصِرْ
verses.arabicClean: فدعا ربه أني مغلوب فانتصر
verses.transliterated: fadaʿā rabbahu annī maghlūbun fa-intaṣi
verses.english: He implored his Lord, "I am oppressed; grant me victory."

1981.english: He implored his Lord, "I have been humiliated; give me victory."

1989.english: He implored his Lord, “I am oppressed; grant me victory.”

verses.arabic: فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَآءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ففتحنا أبواب السماء بماء منهمر
verses.transliterated: fafataḥnā abwāba l-samāi bimāin mun'hamiri
verses.english: We then opened the gates of the sky, pouring water.

1981.english: Whereupon, we opened the gates of the sky, pouring water.

1989.english: We then opened the gates of the sky, pouring water.

verses.arabic: وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا فَٱلْتَقَى ٱلْمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ
verses.arabicClean: وفجرنا الأرض عيونا فالتقى الماء على أمر قد قدر
verses.transliterated: wafajjarnā l-arḍa ʿuyūnan fal-taqā l-māu ʿalā amrin qad qudir
verses.english: And we caused springs to gush out of the earth. The waters met to effect a predetermined decision.

1981.english: Springs gushed out from the earth. The waters met according to predetermined judgment.

1989.english: And we caused springs to gush out of the earth. The waters met to effect a predetermined decision. The Ark

verses.arabic: وَحَمَلْنَٰهُ عَلَىٰ ذَاتِ أَلْوَٰحٍ وَدُسُرٍ
verses.arabicClean: وحملناه على ذات ألواح ودسر
verses.transliterated: waḥamalnāhu ʿalā dhāti alwāḥin wadusuri
verses.english: We carried him on a watercraft made of logs and ropes.
verses.subtitle: The Ark

1981.english: We carried him on (a craft) of wood and nails.

1989.english: We carried him on a watercraft made of logs and ropes.

verses.arabic: تَجْرِى بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
verses.arabicClean: تجري بأعيننا جزاء لمن كان كفر
verses.transliterated: tajrī bi-aʿyuninā jazāan liman kāna kufir
verses.english: It ran under our watchful eyes; a reward for one who was rejected.

1981.english: It ran under our watchful eyes, as a reward for the rejected messenger.

1989.english: It ran under our watchful eyes; a reward for one who was rejected.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَٰهَآ ءَايَةً فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد تركناها آية فهل من مدكر
verses.transliterated: walaqad taraknāhā āyatan fahal min muddakiri
verses.english: We have set it up as a lesson. Does any of you wish to learn?

1981.english: We set it up as a lesson; is there anyone who wishes to learn?

1989.english: We have set it up as a lesson. Does any of you wish to learn?

verses.arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: فكيف كان عذابي ونذر
verses.transliterated: fakayfa kāna ʿadhābī wanudhur
verses.english: How terrible was My retribution after the warnings!

1981.english: How (terrible) was My retribution and warnings?

1989.english: How terrible was My retribution after the warnings!

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر
verses.transliterated: walaqad yassarnā l-qur'āna lildhik'ri fahal min muddakiri
verses.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

1981.english: We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who wishes to learn?
1981.footnote: See Appendix 17.

1989.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

verses.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: كذبت عاد فكيف كان عذابي ونذر
verses.transliterated: kadhabat ʿādun fakayfa kāna ʿadhābī wanudhur
verses.english: Ãd disbelieved. Consequently, how terrible was My retribution after the warnings.

1981.english: 'Aad disbelieved; how (terrible) was My retribution and warnings?

1989.english: Aad disbelieved. Consequently, how terrible was My retribution after the warnings.

verses.arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِى يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ
verses.arabicClean: إنا أرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في يوم نحس مستمر
verses.transliterated: innā arsalnā ʿalayhim rīḥan ṣarṣaran fī yawmi naḥsin mus'tamirri
verses.english: We sent upon them violent winds, on a day of continuous misery.

1981.english: We sent upon them violent wind, on a day of continuous misery.

1989.english: We sent upon them violent winds, on a day of continuous misery.

verses.arabic: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: تنزع الناس كأنهم أعجاز نخل منقعر
verses.transliterated: tanziʿu l-nāsa ka-annahum aʿjāzu nakhlin munqaʿiri
verses.english: It tossed the people around as if they were decayed palm tree trunks.

1981.english: It tossed the people as if they were decaying palm trees.

1989.english: It tossed the people around as if they were decayed palm tree trunks.

verses.arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: فكيف كان عذابي ونذر
verses.transliterated: fakayfa kāna ʿadhābī wanudhur
verses.english: How terrible was My retribution after the warnings!

1981.english: How (terrible) was My retribution and warnings?

1989.english: How terrible was My retribution after the warnings!

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر
verses.transliterated: walaqad yassarnā l-qur'āna lildhik'ri fahal min muddakiri
verses.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

1981.english: We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who wishes to learn?

1989.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

verses.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: كذبت ثمود بالنذر
verses.transliterated: kadhabat thamūdu bil-nudhur
verses.english: Thamûd rejected the warnings.

1981.english: Thamood rejected the warnings.

1989.english: Thamoud rejected the warnings.

verses.arabic: فَقَالُوٓا۟ أَبَشَرًا مِّنَّا وَٰحِدًا نَّتَّبِعُهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذًا لَّفِى ضَلَٰلٍ وَسُعُرٍ
verses.arabicClean: فقالوا أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه إنا إذا لفي ضلال وسعر
verses.transliterated: faqālū abasharan minnā wāḥidan nattabiʿuhu innā idhan lafī ḍalālin wasuʿuri
verses.english: They said, "Shall we follow one of us; a human being? We will then go astray, then end up in Hell.

1981.english: They said, "Shall we follow a man like us? We will then be wrong and stupid.

1989.english: They said, “Shall we follow one of us; a human being? We will then go astray, then end up in Hell.

verses.arabic: أَءُلْقِىَ ٱلذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنۢ بَيْنِنَا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ
verses.arabicClean: أألقي الذكر عليه من بيننا بل هو كذاب أشر
verses.transliterated: a-ul'qiya l-dhik'ru ʿalayhi min bayninā bal huwa kadhābun ashiru
verses.english: "Did the message come down to him, instead of us? He is a flagrant liar."

1981.english: "Was he chosen out of all of us to receive the message? He is a flagrant liar."

1989.english: “Did the message come down to him, instead of us? He is a flagrant liar.”

verses.arabic: سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَدًا مَّنِ ٱلْكَذَّابُ ٱلْأَشِرُ
verses.arabicClean: سيعلمون غدا من الكذاب الأشر
verses.transliterated: sayaʿlamūna ghadan mani l-kadhābu l-ashir
verses.english: They will find out tomorrow who the flagrant liar is.

1981.english: They will find out tomorrow who the flagrant liar is.

1989.english: They will find out tomorrow who the flagrant liar is.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا۟ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَّهُمْ فَٱرْتَقِبْهُمْ وَٱصْطَبِرْ
verses.arabicClean: إنا مرسلو الناقة فتنة لهم فارتقبهم واصطبر
verses.transliterated: innā mur'silū l-nāqati fit'natan lahum fa-ir'taqib'hum wa-iṣ'ṭabi
verses.english: We are sending the camel as a test for them. Watch them and be patient.

1981.english: We sent the camel as a test for them. Just watch them and be patient.

1989.english: We are sending the camel as a test for them. Watch them and be patient.

verses.arabic: وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌۢ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُّحْتَضَرٌ
verses.arabicClean: ونبئهم أن الماء قسمة بينهم ۖ كل شرب محتضر
verses.transliterated: wanabbi'hum anna l-māa qis'matun baynahum kullu shir'bin muḥ'taḍaru
verses.english: Inform them that the water shall be divided among them; (the camel) shall be allowed to drink on her designated day.

1981.english: Tell them that the water shall be shared between them at specific times.

1989.english: Inform them that the water shall be divided among them; (the camel) shall be allowed to drink on her designated day.

verses.arabic: فَنَادَوْا۟ صَاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ
verses.arabicClean: فنادوا صاحبهم فتعاطى فعقر
verses.transliterated: fanādaw ṣāḥibahum fataʿāṭā faʿaqar
verses.english: But they persuaded their friend to kill (the camel), and he obliged.

1981.english: They consulted their leader, and after receiving the message, he slaughtered (the camel).

1989.english: But they persuaded their friend to kill (the camel), and he obliged.

verses.arabic: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: فكيف كان عذابي ونذر
verses.transliterated: fakayfa kāna ʿadhābī wanudhur
verses.english: Consequently, how terrible was My retribution! They have been warned.

1981.english: How (terrible) was My retribution and warnings.

1989.english: Consequently, how terrible was My retribution! They have been warned.

verses.arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً وَٰحِدَةً فَكَانُوا۟ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ
verses.arabicClean: إنا أرسلنا عليهم صيحة واحدة فكانوا كهشيم المحتظر
verses.transliterated: innā arsalnā ʿalayhim ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan fakānū kahashīmi l-muḥ'taẓir
verses.english: We sent upon them one blow, whereupon they became like harvested hay.

1981.english: We sent upon them one strike, whereupon they became like harvested hay.

1989.english: We sent upon them one blow, whereupon they became like harvested hay.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر
verses.transliterated: walaqad yassarnā l-qur'āna lildhik'ri fahal min muddakiri
verses.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

1981.english: We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who wishes to learn?

1989.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

verses.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍۭ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: كذبت قوم لوط بالنذر
verses.transliterated: kadhabat qawmu lūṭin bil-nudhur
verses.english: The people of Lot rejected the warnings.

1981.english: The people of Lot rejected the warnings.

1989.english: The people of Lot rejected the warnings.

verses.arabic: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حَاصِبًا إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطٍ نَّجَّيْنَٰهُم بِسَحَرٍ
verses.arabicClean: إنا أرسلنا عليهم حاصبا إلا آل لوط ۖ نجيناهم بسحر
verses.transliterated: innā arsalnā ʿalayhim ḥāṣiban illā āla lūṭin najjaynāhum bisaḥari
verses.english: We showered them with rocks. Only Lot's family was saved at dawn.

1981.english: We showered them with rocks, except Lot's family; we saved them at dawn.

1989.english: We showered them with rocks. Only Lot’s family was saved at dawn.

verses.arabic: نِّعْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَن شَكَرَ
verses.arabicClean: نعمة من عندنا ۚ كذلك نجزي من شكر
verses.transliterated: niʿ'matan min ʿindinā kadhālika najzī man shakar
verses.english: We blessed him and his family; we thus reward the appreciative.

1981.english: That was a blessing from us. We thus reward the appreciative.

1989.english: We blessed him and his family; we thus reward the appreciative.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَنذَرَهُم بَطْشَتَنَا فَتَمَارَوْا۟ بِٱلنُّذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أنذرهم بطشتنا فتماروا بالنذر
verses.transliterated: walaqad andharahum baṭshatanā fatamāraw bil-nudhur
verses.english: He warned them about our requital, but they ridiculed the warnings.

1981.english: He had warned them of our strike, but they doubted the warnings.

1989.english: He warned them about our requital, but they ridiculed the warnings.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيْفِهِۦ فَطَمَسْنَآ أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد راودوه عن ضيفه فطمسنا أعينهم فذوقوا عذابي ونذر
verses.transliterated: walaqad rāwadūhu ʿan ḍayfihi faṭamasnā aʿyunahum fadhūqū ʿadhābī wanudhur
verses.english: They negotiated with him about his guests; we blinded them. Suffer My retribution; you have been warned.

1981.english: They negotiated with him about his guests; we had blinded their eyes. They have deserved My retribution and warnings.

1989.english: They negotiated with him about his guests; we blinded them. Suffer My retribution; you have been warned.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُم بُكْرَةً عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد صبحهم بكرة عذاب مستقر
verses.transliterated: walaqad ṣabbaḥahum buk'ratan ʿadhābun mus'taqirru
verses.english: Early the next morning, a devastating retribution struck them.

1981.english: On the following morning, they were hit by devastating retribution.

1989.english: Early the next morning, a devastating retribution struck them.

verses.arabic: فَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ
verses.arabicClean: فذوقوا عذابي ونذر
verses.transliterated: fadhūqū ʿadhābī wanudhur
verses.english: Suffer My retribution; you have been warned.

1981.english: They have deserved My retribution and warnings.

1989.english: Suffer My retribution; you have been warned.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر
verses.transliterated: walaqad yassarnā l-qur'āna lildhik'ri fahal min muddakiri
verses.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

1981.english: We have made the Quran easy to remember; is there anyone who wishes to learn?

1989.english: We made the Quran easy to learn. Does any of you wish to learn?

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ ٱلنُّذُرُ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد جاء آل فرعون النذر
verses.transliterated: walaqad jāa āla fir'ʿawna l-nudhur
verses.english: Pharaoh's people were warned.

1981.english: Pharaoh's people received the warnings.

1989.english: Pharaoh’s people were warned.

verses.arabic: كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذْنَٰهُمْ أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: كذبوا بآياتنا كلها فأخذناهم أخذ عزيز مقتدر
verses.transliterated: kadhabū biāyātinā kullihā fa-akhadhnāhum akhdha ʿazīzin muq'tadiri
verses.english: They rejected all our signs. Consequently, we requited them as an Almighty, Omnipotent should.

1981.english: They rejected all our signs and, consequently, we punished them as an almighty, omnipotent can punish.

1989.english: They rejected all our signs. Consequently, we requited them as an Almighty, Omnipotent should.

verses.arabic: أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكُمْ أَمْ لَكُم بَرَآءَةٌ فِى ٱلزُّبُرِ
verses.arabicClean: أكفاركم خير من أولئكم أم لكم براءة في الزبر
verses.transliterated: akuffārukum khayrun min ulāikum am lakum barāatun fī l-zubur
verses.english: Are your disbelievers better than those disbelievers? Have you been absolved by the scripture?

1981.english: Are your disbelievers any better than those? Did you receive a pardon in the scriptures?

1989.english: Are your disbelievers better than those disbelievers? Have you been absolved by the scripture?

verses.arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ
verses.arabicClean: أم يقولون نحن جميع منتصر
verses.transliterated: am yaqūlūna naḥnu jamīʿun muntaṣiru
verses.english: Perhaps they think, "We will be the winners."

1981.english: Do they say, "We will be victorious?"

1989.english: Perhaps they think, “We will be the winners.”

verses.arabic: سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ
verses.arabicClean: سيهزم الجمع ويولون الدبر
verses.transliterated: sayuh'zamu l-jamʿu wayuwallūna l-dubur
verses.english: All of them will be defeated; they will turn around and flee.

1981.english: Indeed, they will be defeated; they will flee.

1989.english: All of them will be defeated; they will turn around and flee.

verses.arabic: بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
verses.arabicClean: بل الساعة موعدهم والساعة أدهى وأمر
verses.transliterated: bali l-sāʿatu mawʿiduhum wal-sāʿatu adhā wa-amarr
verses.english: The Hour is awaiting them, and the Hour is far worse and more painful.

1981.english: The Hour awaits them. The Hour will be far worse and more devastating.

1989.english: The Hour is awaiting them, and the Hour is far worse and more painful.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ وَسُعُرٍ
verses.arabicClean: إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر
verses.transliterated: inna l-muj'rimīna fī ḍalālin wasuʿuri
verses.english: Certainly, the guilty are astray, and will end up in Hell.

1981.english: The guilty ones are in total loss and stupidity.

1989.english: Certainly, the guilty are astray, and will end up in Hell.

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِى ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُوا۟ مَسَّ سَقَرَ
verses.arabicClean: يوم يسحبون في النار على وجوههم ذوقوا مس سقر
verses.transliterated: yawma yus'ḥabūna fī l-nāri ʿalā wujūhihim dhūqū massa saqar
verses.english: They will be dragged into the hellfire, forcibly. Suffer the agony of retribution.

1981.english: The day will come when they are dragged into the hellfire forcibly. They have deserved the agony of retribution.

1989.english: They will be dragged into the hellfire, forcibly. Suffer the agony of retribution.

verses.arabic: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَٰهُ بِقَدَرٍ
verses.arabicClean: إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر
verses.transliterated: innā kulla shayin khalaqnāhu biqadari
verses.english: Everything we created is precisely measured.

1981.english: We have created everything in exact measure.

1989.english: Everything we created is precisely measured.

verses.arabic: وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلَّا وَٰحِدَةٌ كَلَمْحٍۭ بِٱلْبَصَرِ
verses.arabicClean: وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر
verses.transliterated: wamā amrunā illā wāḥidatun kalamḥin bil-baṣar
verses.english: Our commands are done within the blink of an eye.

1981.english: Whatever we will is done within the blink of an eye.

1989.english: Our commands are done within the blink of an eye.

verses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَآ أَشْيَاعَكُمْ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
verses.arabicClean: ولقد أهلكنا أشياعكم فهل من مدكر
verses.transliterated: walaqad ahlaknā ashyāʿakum fahal min muddakiri
verses.english: We annihilated your counterparts. Does any of you wish to learn?

1981.english: We have destroyed your counterparts; is there anyone who wishes to learn?

1989.english: We annihilated your counterparts. Does any of you wish to learn?

verses.arabic: وَكُلُّ شَىْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِى ٱلزُّبُرِ
verses.arabicClean: وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر
verses.transliterated: wakullu shayin faʿalūhu fī l-zubur
verses.english: Everything they did is recorded in the scriptures.

1981.english: Everything they did is recorded in the scriptures.

1989.english: Everything they did is recorded in the scriptures.

verses.arabic: وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ
verses.arabicClean: وكل صغير وكبير مستطر
verses.transliterated: wakullu ṣaghīrin wakabīrin mus'taṭaru
verses.english: Everything, small or large, is written down.

1981.english: Everything, small or large, is written down.

1989.english: Everything, small or large, is written down.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍ وَنَهَرٍ
verses.arabicClean: إن المتقين في جنات ونهر
verses.transliterated: inna l-mutaqīna fī jannātin wanahari
verses.english: Surely, the righteous have deserved gardens and rivers.

1981.english: The righteous have deserved gardens and streams.

1989.english: Surely, the righteous have deserved gardens and rivers.

verses.arabic: فِى مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍۭ
verses.arabicClean: في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر
verses.transliterated: fī maqʿadi ṣid'qin ʿinda malīkin muq'tadiri
verses.english: In a position of honor, at an Omnipotent King.

1981.english: They occupy an honorable position, at the omnipotent King.

1989.english: In a position of honor, at an Omnipotent King.

verses.arabic: ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ
verses.arabicClean: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الرحمن
verses.transliterated: al-raḥmān
verses.english: The Most Gracious.

1981.english: God most gracious.

1989.english: The Most Gracious.

verses.arabic: عَلَّمَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ
verses.arabicClean: علم القرآن
verses.transliterated: alimul alqur'aan
verses.english: Teacher of the Quran.

1981.english: The one who teaches the Quran.
1981.footnote: The Quran is a book unlike any other book; every aspect of it is surrounded by invisible forces. Our creator teaches us that the Quran is attainable exclusively by those who sincerely seek the knowledge therein. The insincere are hopelessly barred from getting one word correctly out of Quran (see 17:45-46, 18:57, and 56:79). In direct opposition to Quran, those who idolize the prophet claim that we need the "hadith" in order to teach us the Quran. The Quran clearly state that only God is the teacher of Quran (see 41:44 and 75:19). The inventors and followers of "hadith" are defying the Quran's consistent assertion that our source of religious knowledge shall be the Quran, the whole Quran, and nothing but the Quran. See Appendix 15.

1989.english: Teacher of the Quran.

verses.arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ
verses.arabicClean: خلق الإنسان
verses.transliterated: khalaqa l-insān
verses.english: Creator of the human beings.

1981.english: The one who created the human being.

1989.english: Creator of the human beings.

verses.arabic: عَلَّمَهُ ٱلْبَيَانَ
verses.arabicClean: علمه البيان
verses.transliterated: almahu alabayaana
verses.english: He taught them how to distinguish.

1981.english: The one who taught him how to distinguish (right from wrong).

1989.english: He taught them how to distinguish.

verses.arabic: ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ
verses.arabicClean: الشمس والقمر بحسبان
verses.transliterated: al-shamsu wal-qamaru biḥus'bāni
verses.english: The sun and the moon are perfectly calculated.

1981.english: The sun and the moon created as timing devices.

1989.english: The sun and the moon are perfectly calculated.

verses.arabic: وَٱلنَّجْمُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ
verses.arabicClean: والنجم والشجر يسجدان
verses.transliterated: wal-najmu wal-shajaru yasjudān
verses.english: The stars and the trees prostrate.

1981.english: The stars and the trees prostrate.

1989.english: The stars and the trees prostrate.

verses.arabic: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
verses.arabicClean: والسماء رفعها ووضع الميزان
verses.transliterated: wal-samāa rafaʿahā wawaḍaʿa l-mīzān
verses.english: He constructed the sky and established the law.

1981.english: He raised the heaven and established the balance.

1989.english: He constructed the sky and established the law.

verses.arabic: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْمِيزَانِ
verses.arabicClean: ألا تطغوا في الميزان
verses.transliterated: allā taṭghaw fī l-mīzān
verses.english: You shall not transgress the law.

1981.english: You shall not transgress when you weigh.

1989.english: You shall not transgress the law.

verses.arabic: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا۟ ٱلْمِيزَانَ
verses.arabicClean: وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان
verses.transliterated: wa-aqīmū l-wazna bil-qis'ṭi walā tukh'sirū l-mīzān
verses.english: You shall establish justice; do not violate the law.

1981.english: You shall be equitable when you weigh; do not cheat when you trade.

1989.english: You shall establish justice; do not violate the law.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ
verses.arabicClean: والأرض وضعها للأنام
verses.transliterated: wal-arḍa waḍaʿahā lil'anām
verses.english: He created the earth for all creatures.

1981.english: He made the earth for all the people.

1989.english: He created the earth for all creatures

verses.arabic: فِيهَا فَٰكِهَةٌ وَٱلنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ ٱلْأَكْمَامِ
verses.arabicClean: فيها فاكهة والنخل ذات الأكمام
verses.transliterated: fīhā fākihatun wal-nakhlu dhātu l-akmām
verses.english: In it there are fruits, and date palms with their hanging fruit.
verses.footnote: Compare the spaceship Earth's renewable systems and reproducing astronauts, with the most sophisticated spaceships that we launch into space. God be glorified.

1981.english: With fruits and palms with sheaths.

1989.english: In it there are fruits, and date palms with their hanging fruit.*
1989.footnote: Compare the spaceship Earth's renewable systems and reproducing astronauts, with the most sophisticated spaceships that we launch into space. God be glorified.

verses.arabic: وَٱلْحَبُّ ذُو ٱلْعَصْفِ وَٱلرَّيْحَانُ
verses.arabicClean: والحب ذو العصف والريحان
verses.transliterated: wal-ḥabu dhū l-ʿaṣfi wal-rayḥān
verses.english: Also grains and the spices.

1981.english: With food grains and flowers.

1989.english: Also grains and the spices.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: (O humans and jinns,) which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?
1981.footnote: This sura is specifically directed to the two kinds of creatures who possess the freedom of choice, namely the humans and the jinns.

1989.english: (O humans and jinns,) which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن صَلْصَٰلٍ كَٱلْفَخَّارِ
verses.arabicClean: خلق الإنسان من صلصال كالفخار
verses.transliterated: khalaqa l-insāna min ṣalṣālin kal-fakhār
verses.english: He created the human from aged clay, like the potter's clay.

1981.english: He created the human from clay like the potter's.

1989.english: He created the human from aged clay, like the potter’s clay.

verses.arabic: وَخَلَقَ ٱلْجَآنَّ مِن مَّارِجٍ مِّن نَّارٍ
verses.arabicClean: وخلق الجان من مارج من نار
verses.transliterated: wakhalaqa l-jāna min mārijin min nāri
verses.english: And created the jinns from blazing fire.

1981.english: And created the jinns from blazing fire.

1989.english: And created the jinns from blazing fire.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: (O humans and jinns,) which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?

1989.english: (O humans and jinns,) which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ
verses.arabicClean: رب المشرقين ورب المغربين
verses.transliterated: rabbu l-mashriqayni warabbu l-maghribayn
verses.english: Lord of the two easts and the two wests.

1981.english: Lord of the two easts and the two wests.

1989.english: Lord of the two easts and the two wests.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?

1989.english: Which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ
verses.arabicClean: مرج البحرين يلتقيان
verses.transliterated: maraja l-baḥrayni yaltaqiyān
verses.english: He separates the two seas where they meet.

1981.english: He separates the fresh water from the salt water.

1989.english: He separates the two seas where they meet.

verses.arabic: بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَّا يَبْغِيَانِ
verses.arabicClean: بينهما برزخ لا يبغيان
verses.transliterated: baynahumā barzakhun lā yabghiyān
verses.english: A barrier is placed between them, to prevent them from transgressing.

1981.english: Between them is a barrier they cannot surmount.
1981.footnote: See footnote 25:53.

1989.english: A barrier is placed between them, to prevent them from transgressing.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?

1989.english: Which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا ٱللُّؤْلُؤُ وَٱلْمَرْجَانُ
verses.arabicClean: يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان
verses.transliterated: yakhruju min'humā l-lu'lu-u wal-marjān
verses.english: Out of both of them you get pearls and coral.

1981.english: From the two seas, you extract pearls and coral.

1989.english: Out of both of them you get pearls and coral.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?

1989.english: Which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: وَلَهُ ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْمُنشَـَٔاتُ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ كَٱلْأَعْلَٰمِ
verses.arabicClean: وله الجوار المنشآت في البحر كالأعلام
verses.transliterated: walahu l-jawāri l-munshaātu fī l-baḥri kal-aʿlām
verses.english: He gave you ships that roam the sea like flags.

1981.english: He controls the ships that roam the sea like flags.

1989.english: He gave you ships that roam the sea like flags.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?

1989.english: Which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ
verses.arabicClean: كل من عليها فان
verses.transliterated: kullu man ʿalayhā fāni
verses.english: Everyone on earth perishes.

1981.english: Everyone on earth will perish.

1989.english: Everyone on earth perishes.

verses.arabic: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلَٰلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ
verses.arabicClean: ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام
verses.transliterated: wayabqā wajhu rabbika dhū l-jalāli wal-ik'rām
verses.english: Only the presence of your Lord lasts. Possessor of Majesty and Honor.

1981.english: Only the presence of your Lord will continue; He is the possessor of majesty and honor.

1989.english: Only the presence of your Lord lasts. Possessor of Majesty and Honor.

verses.arabic: فَبِأَىِّ ءَالَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ
verses.arabicClean: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان
verses.transliterated: fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibān
verses.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you deny?

1981.english: Which of your Lord's marvels can you two deny?

1989.english: Which of your Lord’s marvels can you deny?

verses.arabic: يَسْـَٔلُهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأْنٍ
verses.arabicClean: يسأله من في السماوات والأرض ۚ كل يوم هو في شأن
verses.transliterated: yasaluhu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi kulla yawmin huwa fī shani
verses.english: Imploring Him is everyone in the heavens and the earth. Every day He is in full control.

1981.english: Everyone in the heavens and the earth implore Him. Everyday He is in full control.

1981.english: Below these two gardens, there will be two lower gardens.
1981.subtitle: The Lower Heaven
1981.footnote: There will be a high heaven, which is closest to God, and below it a lower heaven, then hell, which is the farthest from God. Note how the allegorical description of the high heaven is represented by "flowing" water, while the lower heaven's water needs pumping; the high heaven contains all kinds of fruits, while the lower heaven contains a limited number of fruits; the spouses in the high heaven are with the inhabitants, while those in the lower heaven have to go looking for spouses. verses.arabic: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَٰقِعِ ٱلنُّجُومِ
verses.arabicClean: فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم
verses.transliterated: falā uq'simu bimawāqiʿi l-nujūm
verses.english: I swear by the positions of the stars.
verses.subtitle: Only the Sincere Can Understand the Quran
verses.footnote: Our universe, the smallest and innermost of seven universes, contains a billion galaxies, a billion trillion stars, spanning billions of light years. These uncountable decillions of heavenly bodies maintain their orbits in a divinely controlled precision. The more we learn, the more we realize how awesome this oath is. See Appendix 6.

1981.english: I swear by the positions of the stars.
1981.subtitle: The Honorable Quran

1989.english: I swear by the positions of the stars.
1989.subtitle: Only the Sincere Can Understand the Quran
1989.footnote: Our universe, the smallest and innermost of seven universes, contains a billion galaxies, a billion trillion stars, spanning billions of light years. These uncountable decillions of heavenly bodies maintain their orbits in a divinely controlled precision. The more we learn, the more we realize how awesome this oath is. See Appendix 6.

verses.arabic: وَإِنَّهُۥ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم
verses.transliterated: wa-innahu laqasamun law taʿlamūna ʿaẓīmu
verses.english: This is an oath, if you only knew, that is awesome.

1981.english: And it is an awesome oath, if you only knew.

1989.english: This is an oath, if you only knew, that is awesome.*
1989.footnote: Our universe, the smallest and innermost of seven universes, contains a billion galaxies, a billion trillion stars, spanning billions of light years. These uncountable decillions of heavenly bodies maintain their orbits in a divinely controlled precision. The more we learn, the more we realize how awesome this oath is. See Appendix 6.

verses.arabic: إِنَّهُۥ لَقُرْءَانٌ كَرِيمٌ
verses.arabicClean: إنه لقرآن كريم
verses.transliterated: innahu laqur'ānun karīmu
verses.english: This is an honorable Quran.

1981.english: This is an honorable Quran.

1989.english: This is an honorable Quran.

verses.arabic: فِى كِتَٰبٍ مَّكْنُونٍ
verses.arabicClean: في كتاب مكنون
verses.transliterated: fī kitābin maknūni
verses.english: In a protected book.

1981.english: In a perfectly preserved book.

1989.english: In a protected book.

verses.arabic: لَّا يَمَسُّهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلْمُطَهَّرُونَ
verses.arabicClean: لا يمسه إلا المطهرون
verses.transliterated: lā yamassuhu illā l-muṭaharūn
verses.english: None can grasp it except the sincere.
verses.footnote: The insincere who are not satisfied with the Quran alone are divinely prevented from understanding the Quran. This concept is repeated throughout the Quran (17:45, 18:57). Consequently, they cannot understand this verse. For example, compare this translation of 7:3, 17:46, 41:44, & 56:79 with other translations.

1981.english: None can touch it, except the righteous.
1981.footnote: The Quran is by no means a regular book. Only the sincere seekers of the truth will be allowed to understand it (see 41:44). The insincere will be prevented from acquiring any knowledge from the Quran (see 17:46, 18:57, and Appendix 17). In fact, those who are prevented by God from learning the Quran claim that this verse means that no one can physically "touch" the Quran unless he satisfies certain ablution requirements. Obviously, this distortion is a clever satanic plot to prevent people from studying God's message to them. Our salvation is in reading, studying, and heeding the Quran.

1989.english: None can grasp it except the sincere.*
1989.footnote: The insincere who are not satisfied with the Quran alone are divinely prevented from understanding the Quran. This concept is repeated throughout the Quran (17:45, 18:57).
